description-station-hydrometry: Multiple peak flow rating across period of record however higher flood estimates are based on two ratings, QHigh1983 and QHigh1994, applied as upper segments to regular low to medium flow ratings. QHigh1983 is based on gaugings up to 2.980m (measured flow of 90.7 cumecs) and then simple extrapolation. QHigh1994 is based on gaugings up to 2.954m (measured flow of 85.4 cumecs) and then further informed by hydraulic modelling, providing some confidence in the flow estimate of higher events. The cause of the shift of the flood control between QHigh1983 an QHigh1994 is currently not understood and based on gauging evidence alone. Small amounts of bypassing occur on left bank during extreme flows.
description-flow-record: Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2023 (WINFAP Files v12).
description-catchment: Gently undulating, relatively low lying catchment. Impermeable metamorphic Lower Dalradian formations overlain with Boulder Clay and morainic drift. Intrusion of ORS in the NW. Largely agricultural with some forest cover. No significant catchment changes known.
description-flow-regime: Likely influence of agricultural drainage/abstraction on low flows. Superficial deposits dampen the responsiveness of the catchment.

name: Don at Parkhill
description-summary: Velocity area station; the lowest station on the Don.
description-general: Velocity area station, about 37m wide section. Lowest gauging station on the Don.
description-station-hydrometry: Cableway rated with natural control. Weed growth a problem during summer half-year. Complex low flow rating history. Peak flow rating derived from current meter gaugings up to 3.7m (2.2QMED) and simple extrapolation beyond. One peak flow rating applied to the whole record.
description-flow-record: Flow records for 1969-86 reprocessed in 1987; significant revisions in high and low flow range.
description-catchment: Mountainous headwaters, mainly snowy in winter. Mainly Dalradian metamorphics with large amounts of basic intrusives and small pockets of Old Red Sandstone. Responsiveness dampened by superficial deposits. High moorland, forestry, pastoral and arable in lower valleys. Notable floodplains, mainly in the lower reaches. No major catchment changes, but increased urbanisation in Inverurie.
description-flow-regime: Natural regime.

name: Don at Haughton
description-summary: Velocity area station, catchment drains the eastern Cairngorms.
description-general: Velocity area station; about 40m wide.
description-station-hydrometry: Cableway rated, natural control. Levels can be affected by ice and weed. Minor bypassing only at the highest flood flows >5.0m (2002 and 2016). Peak flow rating revised in 2020 and derived from gaugings up to 4.8m and flood plain modelling up to 6.0m. However, there is lower confidence in flow estimates pre 01/01/1984 as there is a ten year period with no gaugings. Two peak flow ratings across period of record.
description-flow-record: All pre-1984 flows are flagged as estimated in the SEPA database and post-1984 flows for events above 5m stage should be treated with caution. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in August 2021 (WINFAP Files v10) and in August 2024 (WINFAP Files v13).
description-catchment: Mountainous headwaters, often snowy in winter. Mainly Dalradian metamorphics with large amounts of basic intrusives and a small pocket of ORS. High moorland, forestry, pastoral and arable in lower valleys. No significant catchment changes known.
description-flow-regime: Natural regime. Slow rising river, responsiveness dampened by superficial deposits.

name: Don at Bridge of Alford
description-summary: Velocity area station, one of four stations on the River Don. Culfork is the most upstream, then Alford, with Haughton and Parkhill further downstream.
description-general: Velocity area station, one of four stations on the River Don. Culfork is the most upstream, then Alford, with Haughton and Parkhill further downstream.
description-station-hydrometry: Cableway rated. Stable natural control with slight changes to lower sections of ratings every couple of years since flows began in 1973. Rating derived from current meter and ADCP gaugings from cableway up to 2.7m. Peak flow rating extrapolated up to 5.0m using multiple cross sections and 1D and 2D modelling. A single peak flow rating is applied to the entire record.
description-flow-record: Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2019 (WINFAP Files v8).
description-catchment: Upland catchment. Mountainous headwaters, often snowy in winter. Mainly Dalradian metamorphics, some older basic intrusives and a small pocket of ORS. High moorland, forestry, hill grazing and some arable in the valley bottom. No significant catchment changes known.
description-flow-regime: Natural regime. Responsiveness dampened by superficial deposits.

name: Urie at Pitcaple
description-summary: Velocity area station replace 11801.
description-general: Velocity area station about 16m wide. Station replaced 11801. Removed from Peak Flow Dataset in August 2021 (WINFAP Files v10).
description-station-hydrometry: Natural control and cableway rated. Good low flow performance. Some bypassing occurs at high flows (water shortcuts the meander immediately upstream and joins the river downstream of gauging station). Rating derived from current meter gaugings up to 1.8m, extended up to 3.25m on survey/model points and extrapolated from 3.4m. Gaugings pre-1988 are referenced to different datum - not used for current rating. Data removed from peak flows dataset due to uncertainty of whole record.
description-flow-record: 1984 minimum flow c0.6 cumecs. Pre-1988 flows calculated from staff gauge readings (high flows truncated at a gauge reading of 1m) - intermittent.
description-catchment: Bedrock predominantly metamorphic. Moorland headwaters, substantial areas of mixed and arable farming below; forestry. Minimal floodplains. No significant catchment changes known.
description-flow-regime: Natural regime, no abstractions. Responsiveness dampened by superficial deposits.

name: Don at Mill of Newe
description-summary: Velocity area station gauging a rural catchment. Closed in 1994.
description-general: Velocity-area station with complex weir of unorthodox design. Principally a low flow station. Closed on 9/6/94.
description-station-hydrometry: No cableway and no suitable locations for high flow gaugings. Structure retains control in all conditions. Small flow towards disused hydro-electric power plant bypasses weir. Weir traps in central fish pass frequently adjusted, often resulting in need to recalibrate.
description-flow-record: NA
description-catchment: Complex metamorphic geology; dissected plateau with peaks to 600-700m and steep slopes. Granite in S. Some forestry on lower ground; remainder rough grazing.
description-flow-regime: NA

name: Don at Culfork
description-summary: Velocity area station gauging a natural upland catchment.
description-general: Velocity area station.
description-station-hydrometry: No cableway. High flows gauged from bridge on river bend immediately u/s.
description-flow-record: Low flows in winter months can be caused by persistent low temperatures, e.g. Feb 2009.
description-catchment: Upland catchment (mostly 600-800 m) dissected by fast-flowing tributaries. Little or no floodplain in main river valley. Complex metamorphic geology (impermeable bedrock with some superficial deposits). Land use is mostly heath with some forestry.
description-flow-regime: Natural flows.

name: Dee at Woodend
description-summary: Velocity area station providing the longest record of flow on the Dee. Series encompasses early data from Cairnton.
description-general: Velocity area station; about 60m wide section. Flow records for Woodend are an amalgamation from two different stations. Present station (built in 1972) replaced earlier station (Cairnton, located approx. 1 mile downstream from Woodend at an abstraction point - some daily staff readings from 1911, continuous flow records from 1929, chart records from 1934) on same reach. Current meter measurements at Woodend initiated by Capt. McClean. Cairnton continued operating until the end of 1984.
description-station-hydrometry: Cableway rated, fairly stable natural control. Winter low flows can also be elevated by ice. From 1929, rating for Cairnton derived by correlation with current meter measurements at Woodend. From 1934 Woodend used for calculating flows at Cairnton, both stations fitted with chart recorders. From 1972, rating at Woodend derived from current meter gaugings up to 3.0m (about QMED), simple extrapolation beyond. Multiple peak flow ratings across period of record.
description-flow-record: Major floods in 1937, 1951 and 2015. Occasional isolated low flow in winter months e.g. Jan 1960, thought to be due to frozen catchment. Winter low flows can also be elevated by ice, in some cases flows have been reprocessed to correct for this, e.g. Dec 2009. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in August 2025 (WINFAP Files v14).
description-catchment: Mountainous headwaters, often snowy in winter. Dalradian and Moinian metamorphics along most of valley, flanked by igneous intrusives. Responsiveness slightly dampened by superficial deposits. Mountain, moorland; forestry, with pastoral and some arable in valley bottom. No significant catchment changes known.
description-flow-regime: Natural regime. No regulation, little natural storage (but significant snow in headwaters), minor abstractions.

name: Dee at Park
description-summary: Velocity area station, the most downstream on the Dee.
description-general: Velocity area station; section about 50m wide.
description-station-hydrometry: Cableway rated, unstable natural control causing frequent changes in low and medium flow ratings. Rating derived from current meter gaugings up to 4m (1.2QMED), simple extrapolation beyond. Peak flow ratings revised in 2025. Three peak flow ratings across period of record.
description-flow-record: Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in August 2026 (WINFAP Files v15).
description-catchment: Mountainous headwaters, often snowy in winter. Dalradian and Moinian metamorphics along most of valley, flanked by igneous intrusives. Mountain, moorland, forestry landuse with, pastoral and some arable in valley bottom. No significant catchment changes known.
description-flow-regime: Responsiveness slightly dampened by superficial deposits. Abstraction for PWS of approximately 0.7 cumec between Woodend (12001) and Park (accounts for almost 10% of Q95 flow).

name: Dee at Polhollick
description-summary: Velocity area station on the middle reaches of the Dee.
description-general: Velocity area station, about 52m wide section.
description-station-hydrometry: Cableway rated with natural control. Winter river levels may increase due to ice formation, and this can result in erroneous flows. Where possible, estimated daily mean flows have been substituted. Ratings derived from current meter gaugings up to 2.3m with simple extrapolation beyond. Three peak flow ratings across period of record.
description-flow-record: Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2023 (WINFAP Files v12) and in August 2024 (WINFAP Files v13).
description-catchment: Upland catchment with mountainous headwaters, snowy in winter. Bedrock Dalradian and Moinian metamorphics with basic intrusions. Mountain, moorland, pasture, and forestry landuse. No significant catchment changes known.
description-flow-regime: Natural flow regime.

name: Girnock Burn at Littlemill
description-summary: Velocity area station gauging a natural upland catchment. Station closed in 2011.
description-general: Velocity area station. Transferred to NERPB in July 1994. No records of earlier ratings or gaugings. Important catchment for fishery research. Station closed during 2011.
description-station-hydrometry: Rated by wading.
description-flow-record: Magnitude of Sept 1995 flood under review. Winter low flows can be elevated by ice, in some cases flows have been reprocessed to correct for this, e.g. Dec 2009.
description-catchment: Upland catchment. Bedrock Dalradian and older basic intrusive rocks mostly overlain by superficial deposits. Landuse moorland and pastoral with some forestry.
description-flow-regime: Natural flow regime.

name: Muick at Invermuick
description-summary: Velocity area station draining the south west Cairngorms and flowing into the Dee just downstream of 12003.
description-general: Velocity area station, about 20m wide.
description-station-hydrometry: Cableway rated, natural control. Problems with silting in well (until 1980) and ice in cold winters (flows may be estimated). Rating derived from current meter gaugings up to 1.7m (measured at 72 cumecs) with simple extrapolation beyond. One peak flow rating applied to entire record. There is a side channel just downstream of gauging station that can periodically be blocked by members of the public to deepen the pool and then it inevitably gets knocked down by the fisheries board. This can necessitate rating adjustments at the lower end. The station is on the River Muick just before it joins the River Dee at Ballater. There is potential backing up from either a downstream bridge or from the River Dee itself during extreme events. The current high flow rating does not account for this. With future investigation, there may be potential to further refine flood estimates.
description-flow-record: Flows in 1976 invalid due to blocked pipe. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2023 (WINFAP Files v12).
description-catchment: Upland catchment with mountainous headwaters, often snowy in winter. Bedrock Dalradian intrusive basics with more than half overlain by superficial deposits. Landuse pastoral and mountain moorland; some forestry and lochs. Forestry operations developed in the catchment.
description-flow-regime: Flow regime influenced by upstream Lochs. Natural with no abstrations up until around March 2020 when a hydro scheme was installed upstream of the station. However, all water is returned upstream of the station and no water is diverted from the catchment.

name: Gairn at Invergairn
description-summary: Velocity area station gauging catchment with natural regime, although flows can be affected by frozen catchment.
description-general: Velocity area station with cableway; about 15m wide section.
description-station-hydrometry: Semi-natural section control includes rubble from an early gabion control that was broken up soon after its construction by the spate of 15/11/1978. The rock and boulder strewn, turbulent highland river is not conducive to accurate low flow estimation. The channel is bounded on either side by approximately 2m high embankments which are largely lined with trees. Frozen catchment conditions can result in notable low flows such as on 22/01/1985. There is low confidence in flood estimations above around 50 cumecs, which are based on simple extrapolation above the highest gauging in the respective period of each rating. Additionally, the flow calibration of larger events is potentially compromised by possible backing up from the River Dee confluence 1km downstream. The channel flood control has shifted on four occasions (1981, 1995, 2015 and 2022) and four peak flow ratings reflect these states up to the flood of 18/11/2022. This extreme flood in 2022 caused a very significant change to channel control and there is currently no flood calibration and hence peak flow data beyond this date.
description-flow-record: Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in August 2026 (WINFAP Files v15).
description-catchment: Upland catchment with mountainous headwaters often snowy in winter. Some Dalradian metamorphics, mainly granite intrusive. Half of catchment overlain by superficial deposits. Landuse pastoral and mountain moorland; some forestry. No significant catchment changes known. Catchment rainfall may be underestimated.
description-flow-regime: Natural regime.

name: Dee at Mar Lodge
description-summary: Velocity area station, the highest on the Dee.
description-general: Velocity area station, about 45m wide. Highest gauging station on the Dee.
description-station-hydrometry: Cableway rated, unstable natural control. Prolonged cold spells cause a considerable drop in flow and on rare occasions ice formation on the control requires estimation of flow. River well contained, no bypassing. Rating derived from current meter gaugings up to 2.3m (about QMED), simple extrapolation beyond. No out of bank surveys have been undertaken at this site by either SEPA or any external contractors. However, recent work by consultants following flooding from Storm Frank (Dec 2015) has suggested modelling should be undertaken to account of out of bank flow at this site as some water bypassed the station flowing through trees on the left-hand bank on the Mar Lodge estate. This may have an impact on subsequent high flow rating reviews but as of 30/10/17 this information is not available. One peak flow rating applied up to 14/08/14, where the channel profile changed significantly during the remnants of hurricane Bertha. The rating is being re-calibrated and no peak flow estimates are currently available post 14/08/14.
description-flow-record: December 1989 flows estimated due to ice formation. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in October 2018 (WINFAP Files v7).
description-catchment: Upland catchment with mountainous headwaters, often snowy in winter. Dalradian and Moinian metamorphic and granite mountains. Nearly half overlain by superficial deposits. Mountainous with moorland and some forestry. No significant catchment changes known. Catchment rainfall may be significantly underestimated.
description-flow-regime: Natural regime.

name: Feugh at Heugh Head
description-summary: Velocity area station in rugged mountainous catchment. Low flows affected by abstraction for PWS.
description-general: Velocity area station, about 20m wide.
description-station-hydrometry: Station has cableway and natural control. Flows may be influenced by a fishing jetty a short distance d/s from gauging station. Rating derived from current meter gaugings up to 3.4m (about QMED), simple extrapolation beyond. One peak flow rating has been applied to the entire record. A cableway allows high flow gaugings. There are large man-made stepping stones upstream of cableway that are thought to be a factor in the station control. Downstream its a natural open channel with the exception of a fishing groyne downstream of station that is influential on low flows. Rating derived from current meter gaugings up to 3.4m (about QMED), simple extrapolation beyond. One peak flow rating has been applied to the entire record.
description-flow-record: Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in October 2018 (WINFAP Files v7).
description-catchment: Rugged topography. Mountainous headwaters, often snowy in winter. Developed largely on granites and metamorphics with almost complete superficial deposit cover. Mostly moorland and upland pasture. Some forest cover due to afforestation in Glen Dye.
description-flow-regime: Flashy response. Abstraction (at Charr, PWS for Stonehaven) accounts for <5% of Q95 flow. Off-line storage reservoir installed in early 1990s with connection back to the river, which might have an influence on flows.

name: Water of Dye at Charr
description-summary: Compound critical depth flume gauging a responsive, upland catchment with a largely natural regime. Station closed 2021-04-01 due to difficulties maintaining site.
description-general: Compound critical-depth flume (constructed by Grampian Regional Council, repaired in 1983).
description-station-hydrometry: Large capacity flume, flows >30 cumecs estimated or truncated. July 2008, modifications for fisheries carried out - centre of flume narrowed, hence low flow relationship altered significantly.
description-flow-record: Mixed flow series comprising lengthy runs of naturalised and gauged flows. Incomplete chart records from 1963. Peak flows from Aug 1990 only. Station closed 2021.
description-catchment: Rugged upland catchment with moorland (exclusively), developed principally on granite; overlain by superficial deposits.
description-flow-regime: Very responsive regime - natural apart from PWS abstraction (for Stonehaven), an export of approx. 0.05 cumecs (around 5% of mean runoff), significant at low flows.

name: Bervie at Inverbervie
description-summary: Velocity area station on the low-lying north east coast of Scotland.
description-general: Velocity area station, about 10m wide.
description-station-hydrometry: Cableway rated. De-stabilised artificial control replaced by gabions in 1989. Extreme floods above about 2m bypass the station (via the rb floodplain; water spills onto the road and collects in a depression, probably just evaporates and infiltrates). Rating derived from current meter gaugings up to 1.8m (1.1 QMED), simple extrapolation beyond. Two peak flow ratings have been applied to the record.
description-flow-record: NA
description-catchment: Low-lying catchment. Bedrock of mixed permeability with ORS; almost entirely covered with superficial deposits. Arable landuse in valley, pastoral on hills and some forestry. No significant catchment changes known.
description-flow-regime: Natural flow regime.

name: Luther Water at Luther Bridge
description-summary: Velocity area station gauging a steep rural catchment.
description-general: Velocity area station 10m wide. Stable bedrock control at low flows.
description-station-hydrometry: Cableway present. Situation not ideal due to bend u/s and island d/s, but stage-discharge relation is regularly reviewed using routine gaugings.
description-flow-record: NA
description-catchment: Upper third of catchment is fairly steep (Grampian Mountains), the rest has moderate slopes. Majority of the catchment is on ORS, the remainder is metamorphic. Almost the entire catchment is covered by superficial deposits. Land use is forest (approx. half) and rough grazing at higher levels with arable and cattle elsewhere.
description-flow-regime: NA

name: South Esk at Stannochy Bridge
description-summary: NA
description-general: NA
description-station-hydrometry: NA
description-flow-record: NA
description-catchment: NA
description-flow-regime: NA

name: Prosen Water at Prosen Bridge
description-summary: Velocity area station gauging a natural, mountainous catchment.
description-general: Velocity area station 16m wide. Fairly stable rock and boulder control.
description-station-hydrometry: Cableway present. Gauged up to approx. 80 cumecs.
description-flow-record: Notably low winter flows, e.g. Dec 1995, due to extreme low temperatures.
description-catchment: Metamorphic bedrock; approx. half overlain by superficial deposits. Mountainous with rough grazing and forest cover.
description-flow-regime: Usually has significant spring snowmelt. Natural regime.

name: Lunan Water at Kirkton Mill
description-summary: Velocity area station gauging a rural catchment, some influences on flow regime due to abstraction.
description-general: Velocity area station 6m wide. Control at low and medium flows is unstable gravel bed.
description-station-hydrometry: Cableway present.
description-flow-record: NA
description-catchment: A moderately sloping catchment typically rising to 250m. Bedrock is divided in almost equal proportions between ORS and igneous rocks almost all of which is overlain by superficial deposits. Land use is pasture and arable with some forest cover.
description-flow-regime: Agricultural abstraction of approx. 0.16 cumecs can influence summer low flows.

name: North Esk at Logie Mill
description-summary: Compound crump weir gauging the south east Grampian Mountains.
description-general: Compound Crump profile fibreglass weir, width 41m. Station added to peak flows dataset in August 2026 (WINFAP Files v15).
description-station-hydrometry: Compound crump weir acts as the control for low to medium flows. Weir prone to damage during high flow events resulting in changes to the stage-discharge relationship. New ratings required for the duration of repair work and on completion of works as weir not always returned to pre-damaged state. Rating calibrated on gaugings up to SG 3.485m, 475 cumecs (approx. 1.3 QMED). Flows are extrapolated beyond the validated limit but with low confidence. High flows are largely contained; however, this prevents gaugings during large events due to station becoming inaccessible. Flood embankments are also known to breach during extremes > SG 4m (e.g. 2015, 2020, 2022, 2023). Limited gauging range and unknown stage-discharge relationship during extremes limits Peak Flow status to QMED.
description-flow-record: Daily flows of limited precision (based on single stage readings) from 1/76 to 4/83 derived from two nearby sites; high flows overestimated. Naturalised monthly flows available 1976-87.
description-catchment: Drains south-east flank of Grampians. Steeply sloping apart from lower third. Bedrock is mostly ORS, the remainder being igneous and metamorphic; most of which is overlain by superficial deposits. Rough grazing on open moorland; cattle and arable at lower levels.
description-flow-regime: Usually has significant spring snowmelt. Minor abstractions for PWS and irrigation.

name: South Esk at Brechin
description-summary: Velocity area station gauging a long, narrow catchment. Replaces 13003.
description-general: Velocity area station 20m wide. Supersedes 13003, Stannochy Bridge (1979-82), 3km u/s.
description-station-hydrometry: Cableway present. High flows can cut off access to the cableway. Control washed away during December 2012 event. Flood protection scheme constructed 2015 - May 2016.
description-flow-record: NA
description-catchment: A long narrow catchment draining the SE flank of the Grampians. The upper two thirds are steeply sloping. Land use is a mix of rough grazing on open moorland, forestry and, at lower levels, arable. The lower half lies on ORS, the remainder is metamorphic; two thirds of which is overlain by superficial deposits.
description-flow-regime: Summer flows can be affected by agricultural abstractions, approx 0.16 cumecs. Usually has significant spring snowmelt.

name: West Water at Dalhouse Bridge
description-summary: Velocity area station gauging a predominantly mountainous catchment.
description-general: Velocity area station 20m wide.
description-station-hydrometry: Unstable gravel control which until 1990 was affected by abstraction of gravel by farmers. Cableway present.
description-flow-record: NA
description-catchment: Predominantly mountainous catchment. Largely impermeable bedrock with significant superficial deposits. Limited forestry. Rough grazing. Uplands are peaty and flat. Valley sides are steep.
description-flow-regime: Flows are natural. Significant spring snowmelt is common.

name: Brothock Water at Arbroath
description-summary: Velocity area station opened for Arbroath flood warning scheme.
description-general: Station opened as part of Arbroath flood warning scheme, launched winter 1993/94. Station is located on straight reach, immediately u/s of road bridge.
description-station-hydrometry: Bed is a vegetated mix of sand and gravel, with high flows controlled by bridge. Debris thrown from bridge causes rating problems.
description-flow-record: NA
description-catchment: A gently-sloping, low-lying catchment, with fertile soils supporting a variety of crops and some forestry. Minor agricultural abstractions. Bedrock mostly ORS with some lavas and tuffs, almost entirely overlain by superficial deposits.
description-flow-regime: NA

name: South Esk at Gella Bridge
description-summary: Velocity area station gauging a natural upland catchment.
description-general: Velocity area station located on straight reach between bridges. Bed and control are mixture of large boulders, sand and bedrock. Opened in Dec 1990 as part of South Esk Flood Warning Scheme. Old arched bridge on upstream side of station started to collapse in Aug 2007. It was demolished shortly after, but the vertical walls remain which are higher than the top of ramp (2.3m), therefore not impacting the rating. Station added to peak flows dataset in August 2025 (WINFAP Files v14).
description-station-hydrometry: Cableway rated, fairly stable natural control. Station located on reach between bridges, contained to 2.3m on right bank, and significantly higher on left bank. No bypassing of station. Ratings revised in 2024 which allowed inclusion in the peak flow dataset. Confident in flows up to 2.22m up to Jan 2016, and then only up to 1.9m from then onwards.
description-flow-record: Highest peaks in Dec 2015 (3.03m), Oct 2023 (2.51m) and Nov 2022 (2.4m). New high flow rating created after Dec 2015 flow, likely due to deposition under the downstream bridge.
description-catchment: Upland catchment. Bedrock predominantly Dalradian metamorphics over 50% of which is overlain by superficial deposits. Predominantly mountainous with grassland (long and narrow valley supporting rough grazing), and some forest.
description-flow-regime: Natural flows. Usually experiences significant spring snowmelt.

name: Colliston Burn at Colliston
description-summary: Velocity area station opened for flood warning in Arbroath.
description-general: Velocity area station installed in Oct 1993 as part of flood warning scheme for Arbroath. Tipping bucket raingauge installed at site in Oct 1994.
description-station-hydrometry: NA
description-flow-record: High flows in Sept and Nov 2009 currently under review. Flows from Aug 2004 reprocessed in 2012.
description-catchment: Bedrock ORS, a locally important aquifer, with Boulder Clay cover. Low lying catchment of subdued relief supporting agriculture. Entirely rural.
description-flow-regime: Irrigation borehole upstream can influence low flows, e.g. summer 1994, 1996, 2005, 2022, 2025.

name: Eden at Kemback
description-summary: Velocity area station in a low-lying coastal catchment. Flows affected by abstractions and effluent returns.
description-general: Velocity area station, about 15m wide.
description-station-hydrometry: Cableway present. High flow control is downstream bridge. Low flow control is natural bar 30m d/s from hut. Bypassing occurs on the lb in the very highest floods above 2.1m, but not considered to be significant at the levels recorded. At higher levels then there is the potential for significant bypassing. Summer weed growth necessitates frequent revisions to the rating. Ratings derived from current meter gaugings up to 2.1m (about 1.1 to 1.3QMED) for each rating, simple extrapolation beyond. Recent rating review in 2003. Four peak flow ratings cover period of record.
description-flow-record: NA
description-catchment: A gently sloping and low-lying catchment between the Tay and Forth estuaries. Mixed bedrock geology; ORS along the central valley, igneous to the north, some igneous plus Carboniferous Limestone and sandstone to the south. Land use is mainly arable, grassland, and woodland. No significant catchment changes known.
description-flow-regime: Abstractions for irrigation; gw abstractions and effluent returns and small reservoirs in the headwaters.

name: Dighty Water at Balmossie Mill
description-summary: Velocity area station gauging a predominantly low-lying catchment.
description-general: Velocity Area station 9m wide. Station added to peak flows dataset in August 2024 (WINFAP Files v13).
description-station-hydrometry: Cableway removed 1999. Summer weed growth necessitates frequent revisions to the stage-discharge relationship. High flow gaugings up to 29.4 cumecs. Potential backing up from bridge at extreme high flows. All flows contained. Multiple peak flow ratings across period of record.
description-flow-record: Peak flows held from 2008 pending consolidation of earlier ratings.
description-catchment: Gently sloping and low-lying catchment except for the far N and W edges which drain S flank of Sidlaw Hills (up to 450m). Bedrock predominantly Devonian S'st, mostly overlain by superficial deposits. Lower part of catchment urban (Dundee), the rest mainly arable, with grassland and some forest.
description-flow-regime: Very flashy.

name: Motray Water at St Michaels
description-summary: Velocity area station gauging a low lying catchment in North East Scotland.
description-general: Velocity area station, 4m wide.
description-station-hydrometry: Control is kerbstones at low flow, channel at medium flow and bridge at high flow. Kerb weir rebuilt in Nov 1995, station recalibrated. No cableway, gauged from bridge.
description-flow-record: Abstractions and discharges from sand and gravel workings cause cyclical pattern, particularly apparent at low flows, e.g. autumn 1986 and summer-autumn 2003.
description-catchment: Low-lying catchment. Bedrock ORS and igneous; two thirds of which is overlain by superficial deposits. Arable and rough grazing; some woodland.
description-flow-regime: Abstractions for irrigation.

name: Monikie Burn at Panbride
description-summary: Velocity area station gauging a low lying catchment. Station closed in 1992.
description-general: Velocity area station, 2.5m wide. Railway sleepers form the low flow control. Station opened for spray irrigation monitoring. Closed 12/1992 due to scour below railway sleeper control.
description-station-hydrometry: Gauged by wading to bankfull (about 1m). There are problems with weed growth.
description-flow-record: Data may be of limited value.
description-catchment: Low undulating catchment on ORS. Mainly used for arable farming.
description-flow-regime: Small recreational reservoirs (formerly for PWS) affect flow when being cleaned out. Agricultural abstractions can reduce flow to zero.

name: Craigmill Burn at Craigmill
description-summary: Velocity area station gauging a lowland catchment in North East Scotland. Station closed in 2010.
description-general: Velocity area station, 5m wide. Station closed during 2010.
description-station-hydrometry: Kerb weir control constructed Oct 1996 in attempt to make more sensitive at low flows; previously unstable silt and gravel control. No cableway. Calibrated to 0.7m (medium flow). Fairly slow flows. Weed growth is a problem.
description-flow-record: NA
description-catchment: Lowland catchment. Bedrock predominantly ORS; almost entirely overlain by superficial deposits. Land use mainly arable, grassland and forest.
description-flow-regime: Abstractions for irrigation. Recreational reservoirs (formerly PWS; 2 u/s + 2 irrigation lagoons) affect flows when being cleaned out. Transfer between reservoirs is common practice.

name: Eden at Strathmiglo
description-summary: Velocity area station gauging a lowland catchment; some minor artificial influences.
description-general: Velocity area station.
description-station-hydrometry: All but highest flows contained; by-passing is very minor. Sand/cobble bed with grassy island providing control; growth of vegetation necessitates seasonal recalibration.
description-flow-record: NA
description-catchment: Lowland catchment with gentle hills rising to the N and the steeper Lomonds to the S. Mixed bedrock of ORS and various igneous types, most of which is overlain by superficial deposits. Landuse is predominantly arable agriculture at lower levels, and grazing (some improved land) with some forest.
description-flow-regime: Strathmiglo STW effluent (minor) bypasses station.

name: Motray Water at Kilmany
description-summary: Velocity area station opened for irrigation monitoring. Station closed in 2010.
description-general: Station established to monitor spray irrigation abstractions in fertile area of NE Fife. Station closed during 2010.
description-station-hydrometry: Banks to 1.5m will contain all flows; cobble bed is rather uneven but stable. A wooden footbridge u/s allows measurement of high flows >2.1 cumecs.
description-flow-record: NA
description-catchment: Lowland catchment. Bedrock intermediate/basic extrusives of Devonian/ORS age; approx. 50% overlain by superficial deposits. Fertile soils support a variety of crops at lower levels with grassland elsewhere.
description-flow-regime: Abstractions for irrigation are mainly at a single point and produce marked steps in the hydrograph.

name: Isla at Forter
description-summary: Compound flume, suffers from gravel accumulation.
description-general: Compound standing-wave flume, 4km NNW of Kirkton of Glenisla.
description-station-hydrometry: Substantial and variable gravel accumulation - could impact on station calibration; may explain notably high mean runoff.
description-flow-record: NA
description-catchment: NA
description-flow-regime: NA

name: Newton Burn at Newton
description-summary: Compound sharp-edged weir gauging a responsive catchment. Closed in 1968.
description-general: A compound sharp-edged weir with three crests; about 16m wide overall. 2km above the confluence with the River Isla.
description-station-hydrometry: Hydrometric performance uncertain.
description-flow-record: NA
description-catchment: NA
description-flow-regime: Responsive regime. Import of water from a neighbouring catchment influences the water balance.

name: Tay at Caputh
description-summary: Velocity area station gauging a catchment with steep, mountainous headwaters. 62% of the catchment controlled for HEP.
description-general: Velocity area station, about 95m wide. Original station (with bridge control) was moved u/s in 1975. Flows at the old station were all contained.
description-station-hydrometry: Cableway present, span 120m. Natural control. Bypassing occurs mostly on the left bank at levels above 3.15m - new temporary channel created in 1993 flood. Peak flow ratings derived from current meter gaugings up to 5.3m (about 2.3QMED), simple extrapolation beyond. Data transfer from old site and hydraulic re-construction also used for the highest floods. Peak flow ratings reviewed in 2003.
description-flow-record: Twice daily stage readings from July 1937, continuous recording from October 1951. Monthly naturalised data available 1973-1987. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in October 2018 (WINFAP Files v7).
description-catchment: Steep, mountainous headwaters, often snowy in winter. Bedrock mostly metamorphics and granites with more than half overlain by superficial deposits. Landuse mountains and moorland, rough grazing and forestry. Upstream of Dunkeld there are agricultural floodbanks within a reach spanning some 15km including the confluence of the Upper Tay with River Tummel.
description-flow-regime: 62% of catchment controlled for HEP; developed from 1930s to 1957 - reservoirs and water transfers throughout the Tay and Tummel catchments. Net water import. Substantial surface storage; numerous lochs, largest are Ericht, Rannoch, Tummel and Tay.

name: Inzion at Loch of Lintrathen
description-summary: Compound sharp-edged weir situated above the Loch of Linthrathen.
description-general: Compound sharp-edged weir about 9m wide situated 265m above the Loch of Linthrathen.
description-station-hydrometry: NA
description-flow-record: Incomplete series but daily flows for 1927-38.
description-catchment: NA
description-flow-regime: NA

name: Melgan at Loch of Lintrathen
description-summary: Compound sharp-crested weir, above Loch Lintrathan.
description-general: Compound sharp-crested weir, 11.8m wide about 700m above Loch Lintrathan.
description-station-hydrometry: Hydrometric performance uncertain.
description-flow-record: Incomplete record; early flows from 1927. All flows bar the summer of 1968 pre-date the construction of u/s impounding reservoir.
description-catchment: NA
description-flow-regime: NA

name: Tay at Ballathie
description-summary: Velocity area station, the most downstream on the Tay. Station has the highest gauged daily flow in the UK.
description-general: Velocity area station with cableway; 90m wide. The most d/s station on the Tay which records the highest gauged daily flow in the UK.
description-station-hydrometry: Control is bed slope and channel cross-section. To date all flows have been contained. Two ratings derived from current meter gaugings up to 5.413m (06/12/15, measured at 1447 cumecs), simple extrapolation beyond. Some hydraulic re-constructions analysis undertaken to estimate highest floods.
description-flow-record: Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2020 (WINFAP Files v9).
description-catchment: Mountainous headwater catchment, often snowy in winter. Catchment is mostly steep (mountains and moorland), exceptions are lower valleys. Bedrock mainly metamorphics and granite, but the lower catchment (Isla Valley) is ORS. Over half of the catchment is overlain by superficial deposits (mostly Boulder Clay). Landuse is mainly rough grazing and forestry. Several large lochs in catchment (Ericht, Tummel, Tay and Rannoch).
description-flow-regime: Since end of 1957, 1980 sq.km (43%) controlled for hydro-electric power. From the mid 1990s there may be an influence on flood frequency lower down the Tay due to change in hydro-electric power management of levels to accommodate greater storage for flood water. Some control prior to this. 73 sq.km controlled for water supply. Significant winter snow cover.

name: Tay at Pitnacree
description-summary: Velocity area station on the upper Tay. Part of the catchment controlled for HEP.
description-general: Velocity area station, about 90m wide.
description-station-hydrometry: Cableway present until May 2023. Control is unstable gravel bed. All flows contained. Three peak flow ratings across period of record derived from current meter gaugings; rating QHigh1959 from gaugings up to 2.6m (about 1.3QMED). The station was moved from the left bank to the right bank on 01/07/1975 and a new datum was established. The switch to rating QHigh1975 accommodates this datum change. QHigh1975 is based on gaugings up to 3.5m (about 1.5QMED), and a modelled point for the peak of the event on 17/1/1993.
description-flow-record: Naturalised monthly flows available from 1973 to 1987. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2023 (WINFAP Files v12).
description-catchment: Mountainous headwaters, often snowy in winter. Most of the catchment is steep. Bedrock almost entirely metamorphic; half overlain by superficial deposits. Land use mainly moorland, rough grazing and forestry. Contains Loch Tay - the largest natural standing water body in greater Tay catchment.
description-flow-regime: 293 sq.km (25% of catchment) controlled for hydro-electric power but no further development post-1960.

name: Dean Water at Cookston
description-summary: Velocity area station. Flows affected by abstraction at low flows and imports from the Isla catchment.
description-general: Velocity area station, about 10m wide.
description-station-hydrometry: Cableway present. Control is a road bridge. All flows contained to date. Summer weed growth is a problem during low flows. No high flow gauging since 1988. Peak flow ratings from current meter gauging; Rating 1 from gaugings up to 2m (about 1.2 QMED), Rating 2 from gaugings up to 2m (about QMED), simple extrapolation beyond.
description-flow-record: Naturalised monthly flows available 1973-87. August - December 1973 flows missing due to faulty equipment.
description-catchment: Low-lying and gently sloping catchment except for the South which drains the northern flank of the Sidlaw Hills. Bedrock almost entirely ORS; largely overlain by superficial deposits. Land use mainly arable and predominantly rural, but urbanised (Forfar) around head of main channel. No significant catchment changes known.
description-flow-regime: Slow reacting - flattish peaks. Attenuation at the top end of catchment in Forfar Loch area. Reversal of flow back up into Forfar Loch under extreme flows. Industrial and agricultural abstractions in low flows and in the lower parts agricultural embankments. The town of Forfar discharges treated effluent into Forfar Loch in the upper catchment; this is an import from the Isla River.

name: Isla at Wester Cardean
description-summary: Velocity area station gauging a mountainous catchment, significantly influenced by upstream impounding reservoirs.
description-general: Velocity area station, about 25m wide. Removed from Peak Flow Dataset in August 2021 (WINFAP Files v10).
description-station-hydrometry: Cableway present. Until 1994 an island downstream of the station was high flow control. Island was removed in 1994 by landowner, hence control is now unstable for high flows and backing up occurs which can affect the rating. Bypassing occurs at levels above 3.3m from about 2km u/s - flows bypass on the right bank bend via meadow by overtopping of levees. Ratings derived from current meter gaugings up to 2.7m, simple extrapolation beyond. Data removed from peak flows dataset due to low confidence in flood estimates due to unstable control, hysteresis and bypassing.
description-flow-record: Naturalised monthly flows available from 1973-1985. High flow data post-1994 is of poor quality due to unstable control and bypassing at the station.
description-catchment: Mountainous headwaters, often snowy in winter. Catchment lies on southern edge of Grampians rising above 1000m and has mainly steep slopes. Southern part of the catchment is sandstone, the remainder is metamorphic and igneous. More than half of the catchment is overlain by superficial deposits. Landuse predominantly rough grazing and forestry in uplands, cattle and arable in lowlands. No significant catchment changes known.
description-flow-regime: Significantly influenced by impounding reservoir system of Loch of Lintrathen and Blackwater Reservoirs (supply for Dundee). Appreciable net export. This provides public water supply, industrial and agricultural abstractions.

name: Lyon at Comrie Bridge
description-summary: Velocity area station gauging a steeply sloping catchment with hydro-electric power storage.
description-general: Velocity area station 40m wide. Upgraded from pressure recorder (installed 1972, start of peak flows) to full network status in 1983. Station added to peak flows dataset in October 2018 (WINFAP Files v7).
description-station-hydrometry: 170 sq km controlled for hydro-electric power (major development 1951-59) storage in Lochs Lyon, An Daimh and Stronuich. Hydro-power diversions greatly reduce catchment runoff. Flows affected by ice during cold winters. Multiple peak flow ratings across period of record.
description-flow-record: Peak stage and flows pre-1981 are taken from SEPA black summary books and charts, no rating is available for this period. Twice-daily ramp readings: 6/37 to 9/72. 'Weekly' nature of time-series prior to 1973. Naturalised monthly flows available from 1973-87.
description-catchment: Steeply sloping catchment (Grampian mountains). Bedrock metamorphic (schist, quartzite and marble) with approx. Half overlain by superficial deposits. Land use rough grazing and forestry.
description-flow-regime: 170 sq. km controlled for hydro-electric power(major development 1951-59) storage in Lochs Lyon, An Daimh and Stronuich. Hydro-power diversions greatly reduce catchment runoff.

name: Tummel at Pitlochry
description-summary: Velocity area station gauging a catchment entirely controlled for HEP.
description-general: Velocity area station below Faskally Dam. Used for flood warning. Original site 15804 Balinluig (1720 sq.km) moved 8km u/s to 15012 Port-na-craig (1649 sq.km) in 1978. Port-na-craig formally superseded by Pitlochry (1670 sq.km) 700m d/s on 11/4/95 but station number 15012 retained.
description-station-hydrometry: Cableway present. Control scoured by Jan 1993 flood, low flow levels thence below inlet pipe.
description-flow-record: Naturalised monthly flows from 1973-87. Data 9/9/93-11/4/95 estimated from Pitlochry 15045.
description-catchment: Most of catchment is steeply sloping (Grampians >1000m). Bedrock predominantly impermeable, metamorphic, with more than half by superficial deposits. Landuse mainly rough grazing and forestry.
description-flow-regime: Entire catchment controlled for HEP; major storage in Lochs Ericht, Rannoch, Tummel and Faskally. Flows maintained above approx. 19 cumecs.

name: Almond at Almondbank
description-summary: Velocity area station draining the south east Grampians. Station is the lowest tributary on the Tay above the tidal limit.
description-general: Control and bank instability and various engineering works have impacted the performance since 2008. From around 2008 there was bank erosion on the right bank opposite the stilling well hut and there was further washing out of the old stone mill weir that is located downstream of station and downstream confluence of East Pow. Flood protection works (phase 1) were on going from circa 2010 to repair bank erosion and weir. Weir was rebuilt to include fish pass. Flood Protection work ongoing since 2016 (phase 2).
description-station-hydrometry: Cableway present. Natural control. Channel affected by ice during prolonged periods of low temperature. Weir downstream could be control for high flows. Ratings derived from current meter gaugings up to 2.3m (about 1.1QMED), simple extrapolation beyond. Several ratings across period of record.
description-flow-record: Daily read gauge boards from January 1955 to January 1973. Naturalised monthly flows available from 1973-1985. December 1971/Jan 1972 flows removed from the NRFA; December 2009/January 2010 and December 2010 flows considered suspect due to ice formation. 1993 highest flow checked by slope area method. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in October 2018 (WINFAP Files v7).
description-catchment: Mountainous, often snowy in winter. Long, narrow, steeply sloping catchment draining Glen Almond in southeast of Grampians. Two thirds of bedrock is metamorphic the remainder is sandstone. Over half of the catchment is overlain by superficial deposits. Land use is heather moor, rough grazing in upper parts with some cattle in the lower, some forest cover. Hydro-electric power schemes have developed within the catchment.
description-flow-regime: Very flashy. 30 sq.km controlled for HEP. Minor abstraction from Fendoch Burn for water supply - affecting only low and medium flows.

name: Ardle at Kindrogan
description-summary: Velocity area station gauging a mountainous catchment.
description-general: Velocity area station 14m wide.
description-station-hydrometry: All flows contained. High flows gauged from bridge d/s. Boulder and gravel control.
description-flow-record: Extreme low temperatures can cause ice build up and hence erroneous flow values, e.g. Dec 2001 - Jan 2002.
description-catchment: Mountainous steep catchment on metamorphic rock with some l'st outcrops, half is overlain by superficial deposits. Landuse mainly rough grazing with some forestry.
description-flow-regime: Natural flows.

name: Almond at Newton Bridge
description-summary: Velocity area station gauging a mainly natural catchment, some area controlled for HEP.
description-general: Velocity area station 15m wide.
description-station-hydrometry: Cableway present. Stable control of gravel and small stones.
description-flow-record: Control and channel may be affected by ice during prolonged periods of low temperature (Dec 2009-Mar 2010 and Dec 2010 flows considered suspect).
description-catchment: Steep mountainous catchment on metamorphic rock, a third overlain by superficial deposits. Land use mostly rough grazing; some forestry.
description-flow-regime: 30 sq.km controlled for hydro-electric power otherwise natural regime - very flashy.

name: Tay at Kenmore
description-summary: Velocity area station in the upper Tay, 2km d/s from Loch Tay.
description-general: Velocity area station, about 60m wide.
description-station-hydrometry: Cableway present. Natural control. All flows contained to date. Strong winds over Loch Tay (2km upstream) can affect flows. Current ratings derived from current meter gaugings. Flow estimates above the highest gauging are based on simple extrapolation. Multiple peak flow ratings across period of record.
description-flow-record: Daily gaugeboard readings 1959-1974. Naturalised monthly flows available 1974-1985. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in August 2021 (WINFAP Files v10) and in August 2024 (WINFAP Files v13).
description-catchment: The catchment is in the Grampians (rising up to >1200m) and is steeply sloping except for the valley bottom. Mountainous, often snowy in winter. Bedrock almost all metamorphic; half overlain by superficial deposits. Land use rough grazing with forest. Catchment contains Loch Tay (16 miles long, 1.5miles wide) and some smaller lochs upstream. Hydro-electric power schemes have developed in the catchment.
description-flow-regime: Slow reacting regime. 120 sq km of the catchment is controlled for hydroelectric power. Water imported from Lyon catchment since 1958 - evident in water balance. Water exported to Loch Earn catchment since 1958.

name: Braan at Ballinloan
description-summary: Velocity area station gauging a most upland catchment. Replaced by 15023.
description-general: Velocity area station. Superseded by d/s 15023 (area difference 13 km2).
description-station-hydrometry: NA
description-flow-record: NA
description-catchment: Mostly upland catchment with impermeable bedrock, and some superficial deposits of mixed permeability. Land use: heath, forest, grasslands.
description-flow-regime: Responsive regime.

name: Lyon at Moar
description-summary: Velocity area station gauging a Highland catchment with responsive regime. Station closed in 1958.
description-general: River section 2km u/s of Meggernie Castle.
description-station-hydrometry: NA
description-flow-record: All but the 1958 flows predate Breadalbane hydro-electric power project.
description-catchment: Very wet Highland catchment.
description-flow-regime: Very responsive regime.

name: Lunan Burn at Mill Bank
description-summary: Velocity area station gauging a rural hilly catchment in North East Scotland. Downgraded to level only in April 2021.
description-general: Velocity area station, 7.5m wide.
description-station-hydrometry: No cableway. Stable cobbled bed control (old ford) under a bridge; bridge is high flow control. Not gauged at very high flows.
description-flow-record: Equipment failure results in gaps in the record e.g. Oct-Nov 2009. Downgraded to level only in April 2021.
description-catchment: Undulating hilly catchment to about 400m. Mixed permeability bedrock with two thirds overlain by superficial deposits. Mixed arable farming and rough grazing with natural woodlands. Five small natural lochs in the catchment.
description-flow-regime: Minor abstractions for irrigation.

name: Braan at Hermitage
description-summary: Velocity area station gauging a natural catchment in the Grampians. Replacement for 15017.
description-general: Velocity area station, 30m wide. Supersedes Ballinloan (15017) 5km u/s (197 sq.km). Station added to peak flows dataset in August 2021 (WINFAP Files v10).
description-station-hydrometry: Cableway present. Flows fully contained, gauged to the median annual flood, approx 120 cumecs. The low flow control, a derelict stone weir, is sometimes altered by children. Site prone to ice issues during periods of low temperatures.
description-flow-record: Dec 2010 flows severely affected by ice and should be treated with caution.
description-catchment: Catchment is in the Grampians (rising up to > 800m) and has steep or moderate slopes. Metamorphic bedrock geology with just over half overlain by superficial deposits. Mainly open moorland with rough grazing; some forestry.
description-flow-regime: Flows are natural.

name: Dochart at Killin
description-summary: Velocity area station gauging a mountainous catchment. Some exports of flow for HEP.
description-general: Velocity area station, 35m wide.
description-station-hydrometry: Cableway present. Stable bedrock control; sharp fall in bed level d/s of station, culminating in the Dochart Falls. Flows contained to median annual flood, greater flows extend onto l.b. floodplain, over 1 in 50 flows extend over both banks.
description-flow-record: Extreme low temperatures can cause ice build up and hence erroneous flows, e.g. Jan 1982.
description-catchment: A mountainous, steeply sloping catchment. Bedrock predominantly metamorphic over half of is overlain by superficial deposits. Land use mainly rough grazing on open moorland with some forestry at the head of the catchment and along the valley bottom. Adjacent to the IH experimental Balquhidder catchments.
description-flow-regime: Some exports to the Loch Lyon system for HEP.

name: Ericht at Craighall
description-summary: Velocity area station gauging a natural catchment. Ice build up can occur at the station.
description-general: Velocity area station, 46m wide. Stable bedrock control. Station added to peak flows dataset in August 2024 (WINFAP Files v13).
description-station-hydrometry: Cableway present. All flows contained, rating curve well defined. Multiple peak flow ratings across period of record.
description-flow-record: Extreme low temperatures can cause ice build up and hence erroneous flow values, e.g. Dec 2001 - Jan 2002.
description-catchment: Mountainous steeply sloping catchment. Mostly impermeable bedrock, metamorphic, two thirds overlain by superficial deposits. Land use mainly rough grazing with some forestry.
description-flow-regime: Flows are natural.

name: Garry Burn at Loakmill
description-summary: Velocity area station; flows are subject to significant abstraction for irrigation.
description-general: Velocity area station; 4m wide.
description-station-hydrometry: No cableway; high flows gauged from bridge. Low flow control formed from sleepers in a Flat V configuration; bridge is high flow control. Fully gauged.
description-flow-record: NA
description-catchment: Moderately sloping catchment rising to 400m. Bedrock metamorphic and ORS; largely overlain by superficial deposits. Land use mixed farming, forest.
description-flow-regime: Significant abstractions for irrigation.

name: Ordie Burn at Luncarty
description-summary: Velocity area station gauging a rural catchment in North East Scotland. Downgraded to level only in October 2021.
description-general: Velocity area station 7m wide.
description-station-hydrometry: Cableway present until 1996. Old mill weir 1.5m high provides a stable control at all flows; the weir offtake has been closed off. Notch cut into the weir to allow fish passage during February 2006. Fully rated. Major bank erosion noted after high flows in January 2011.
description-flow-record: Downgraded to level only in October 2021.
description-catchment: Moderately sloping catchment rising to 450m. Bedrock metamorphic and ORS; mostly overlain by superficial deposits. Land use mixed farming, some forest cover.
description-flow-regime: NA

name: Alyth Burn at Pitcrocknie
description-summary: Velocity area station gauging a small catchment in the East Grampians.
description-general: Continuous recorder replaced a post gauge in 1991. Ceased recording 31/12/94. Data used for spray irrigation monitoring and pollution control purposes.
description-station-hydrometry: Low flow control (ford) removed 1993, making stability and accuracy of data less reliable. High flow control 50m d/s thought to be quite stable.
description-flow-record: NA
description-catchment: Catchment drains a narrow valley between the Ericht and Isla in the East Grampians. Bedrock old red standstone, some extrusives, and Dalradian metamorphics. Land use arable, grazing and forestry.
description-flow-regime: PWS for Alyth derives from outside the catchment and enters burn via STW immediately d/s of station. Agricultural abstractions are relatively minor.

name: Dean Water at Dean Bridge
description-summary: Velocity area station gauging a mainly rural catchment; some artificial influences.
description-general: Velocity area station 12m wide.
description-station-hydrometry: Cableway present.
description-flow-record: NA
description-catchment: Gently sloping catchment except for the S which drains N flank of Sidlaw Hills (350m). Bedrock ORS. Land use is mainly arable. Predominantly rural, but urbanised (Forfar) around the head of the main channel.
description-flow-regime: The town of Forfar discharges treated effluent into Forfar Loch in the upper catchment; this is an import from the Isla catchment.

name: Ordie Burn at Jackstone
description-summary: Velocity area station opened to monitor irrigation abstractions; closed in 1997.
description-general: Lowland Perthshire station built after 15028 and 15027 to address spray irrigation abstractions specifically within this sub-catchment. From 1997 station abandoned due to unstable control.
description-station-hydrometry: Control provided by unstable gravel island under road bridge immediately d/s. Low flows frequently gauged, providing good accuracy; this deteriorates at higher flows. High flows exceed channel capacity but are contained within the bridge.
description-flow-record: NA
description-catchment: Gentle topography underlain by ORS and some dykes. Land use mostly arable - cereals, potatoes, berries, with rough grazing at higher levels.
description-flow-regime: NA

name: Garry at Killiecrankie
description-summary: Velocity area station used for flood warning on the Tay.
description-general: Velocity-area station; 48m wide. Built as part of the Tay Flood Warning Scheme.
description-station-hydrometry: Cableway present.
description-flow-record: Flash flooding in the catchment can cause isolated peaks in the record, e.g. 2nd of July 2009. Flows in December 2010 and January 2011 should be treated with caution due to severe icing at the station.
description-catchment: Bedrock Moinian and Dalradian Metamorphics. Most of the catchment is steeply sloping, supporting rough grazing and forestry.
description-flow-regime: 66% of the area is severely affected by HEP, with water exported from the catchment.

name: Tummel at Kinloch Rannoch
description-summary: Velocity area station with highly artificial flow regime. Station closed in 2006.
description-general: Flood warning station installed after Feb 1990 flood. Deep channel with smooth flow and natural control. Station closed during 2006.
description-station-hydrometry: Cableway present.
description-flow-record: NA
description-catchment: A mountainous catchment with rough grazing and some forestry. Bedrock mostly metamorphic, granite in SW.
description-flow-regime: Flow from Loch Rannoch u/s is regulated for supply to Tummel Power Station, hydrograph therefore highly artificial. Most of catchment drains through regulated Lochs Ericht and Eigheach. Also receives diverted flow from Garry and right-bank Spey tributaries. Small diversion out of catchment to Loch Errochty.

name: Gaur at Bridge of Gaur
description-summary: Velocity area station in the Tummel headwaters; flow regime dominated by power station discharge.
description-general: Flood warning station in Tummel headwaters. Stable section on gentle right-hand bend, with large boulders protruding from gravel bed. Station closed during 2006.
description-station-hydrometry: Cableway present. Large floods contained.
description-flow-record: NA
description-catchment: Catchment covers Rannoch Moor and surrounding mountains (>1000m). Impermeable bedrock geology (mostly granitic); mostly overlain by superficial deposits. Small part of the catchment is afforested.
description-flow-regime: Flow is dominated by discharge from Gaur Power Station immediately u/s, however, no imports or exports so runoff volumes unaffected by HEP.

name: Tilt at Marble Lodge
description-summary: Velocity area station gauging a natural, upland catchment draining the Grampians.
description-general: Velocity area station in a straight reach 17m wide.
description-station-hydrometry: Cableway present. Separate low and high flow controls are shoals and rock steps, respectively. Steep rb extends up a hillside; lb contains gauge hut and access road. All flows contained.
description-flow-record: NA
description-catchment: Upland catchment. Bedrock Moinian and Dalradian Metamorphics partially overlain by peat and boulder clay. Land use: predominantly rough grazing.
description-flow-regime: Natural catchment. Rainfall may be underestimated.

name: Lyon at Camusvrachan
description-summary: Velocity area station gauging a steep wet mountainous catchment. Artificial flow regime.
description-general: Velocity area station on straight, deep reach with very smooth flow. Station closed during 2009.
description-station-hydrometry: Minor bypassing in very high floods. Stable natural control, though d/s bridge may take effect in extreme floods. Gauged by wading u/s and with cableway.
description-flow-record: NA
description-catchment: Steep, wet mountain catchment with only sparse settlement, mostly rough grazing with a little forestry. Mixed metamorphic geology.
description-flow-regime: Imports from Orchy, Lochay and Dochart catchments, and exports to Cashlie and Lochay Power Stations. Station therefore measures compensation flows and runoff from part of natural catchment below Loch an Daimh and Stronuich Reservoir.

name: Garry Burn at Loakmill
description-summary: Velocity area station opened as a replacement for 15027.
description-general: Station opened in 2010 as a replacement for 15027, 500m d/s.
description-station-hydrometry: An artificially straight channel, high concrete walls mean it is generally well contained. Possibly some bypassing during July 2015 high flows.
description-flow-record: NA
description-catchment: Moderately sloping catchment rising to 400m. Bedrock metamorphic and ORS; approx. 70% overlain by superficial deposits. Land use mixed farming, forest.
description-flow-regime: Small influence of effluent on flow regime.

name: Earn at Kinkell Bridge
description-summary: Velocity area station draining the southern Grampians. A third of the catchment is controlled for HEP.
description-general: Velocity area station, about 35m wide.
description-station-hydrometry: Cableway present, natural control. An allowance is made for any high flows which bypass gauged section on lb above about 2.2m. Weed growth can be a problem at low flows. Ratings derived from current meter gaugings up to 3.2m (about 1.2QMED), simple extrapolation beyond. Hydraulic reconstruction of largest event (1993) to check maximum extent of rating curves.
description-flow-record: Monthly naturalised flows available 1963-1987.
description-catchment: Drains the southern Grampians; mountainous, often snowy in winter. Steep slopes plus extensive flatter areas in lower parts. Metamorphic bedrock in west, sandstone elsewhere with superficial deposits in valley. Mixed agricultural use in east; forestry and rough grazing in west. Notable floodplains with some agricultural flood embankments. Hydro-electric power has developed within the catchment.
description-flow-regime: 189 sq km (32%) of the catchment has been controlled for hydroelectric power since 1958. Loch Earn direct (1958) catchment 122.51 sq km, reservoir diversion capacity 16.1 cumecs. Loch Lednock direct (1957) catchment 19.2 sq km, reservoir diversion capacity 10.5 cumecs. Loch Turret is used for public water supply. Import of water from Tay catchment into Lednock Reservoir.

name: Earn at Aberuchill
description-summary: Velocity area station closed in December 1977.
description-general: Velocity area station located one mile upstream of Ross Bridge, Comrie. Station closed in December 1977. Station re-opened in 1991 but as level only for flood warning so no flow data are held on the NRFA for this period.
description-station-hydrometry: NA
description-flow-record: NA
description-catchment: NA
description-flow-regime: Around 40% of the catchment is controlled for HEP.

name: Ruchill Water at Cultybraggan
description-summary: Velocity area station in a mountainous catchment.
description-general: Velocity area station, about 20m wide. Left bank = 2.5m high, Right bank = 3.5m high.
description-station-hydrometry: Cableway present. Natural control. All flows contained to date. Flashiness and remoteness hinder flood gauging. Multiple peak flow ratings across period of record up to ~2.5m, simple extrapolation beyond.
description-flow-record: Early peak flow data rejected due to uncertainty in rating. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2019 (WINFAP Files v8).
description-catchment: A mountainous catchment with steep slopes, often snowy in winter. Main channel follows a major geological fault, the geology consists of sandstone to its south, metamorphic to its north. More than half is overlain by Boulder Clay. Thick peat on the flatter hill tops. Land is used mainly for rough grazing and army ranges; some woodland. No significant catchment changes known.
description-flow-regime: Natural regime.

name: Earn at Forteviot Bridge
description-summary: Velocity area station, the most downstream on the Earn. Part of the catchment is controlled for HEP.
description-general: Velocity area station, 50m wide. Station moved 100m downstream 09/11/1989, and rebuilt with cableway.
description-station-hydrometry: Bridge forms control. Cableway too close to the bridge resulting in operational difficulties. Floods above 2.8m bypass station on right bank. Ratings derived from gaugings up to 2.73m (around QMED). Modelled upper segment beyond 2.8m, created 2017. Same upper segment used for full record starting 1972. Bridge piers were strengthened and widened in early 2007. Multiple peak flow ratings across period of record.
description-flow-record: Naturalised monthly flows available from 1975-1985. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in October 2018 (WINFAP Files v7) and in August 2026 (WINFAP Files v15).
description-catchment: Catchment draining southern Grampians, rising to >950m; mountainous headwaters, often snowy in winter. Steep slopes plus extensive flatter areas in lower catchment and some agricultural flood embankments. Metamorphic bedrock dominant in the west, sandstones in the east. Substantial superficial deposits, mainly boulder clay, along the valley. Mixed agricultural use in lowland east, rough grazing in west and some forest cover. Notable floodplains. No significant catchment changes known.
description-flow-regime: 189 sq km (24%) of the catchment is controlled for hydroelectric power. Loch Turret is used for public water supply. Import of water from Tay catchment into Lednock Reservoir. Loch Earn (1958) direct catchment 122.51 sq km, reservoir diversion capacity 16.1 cumecs. Loch Lednock (1957) direct catchment 19.2 sq km, reservoir diversion capacity 10.5 cumecs.

name: Ruthven Water at Aberuthven
description-summary: Velocity area station gauging a mainly low-lying catchment.
description-general: Velocity-area station 9m wide.
description-station-hydrometry: Cableway present. Large floods bypass the station.
description-flow-record: NA
description-catchment: Mostly low-lying catchment draining N side of the Ochil Hills. Bedrock Lower ORS, over 55% of which is overlain by superficial deposits. Land use mixed grazing and arable, some forest.
description-flow-regime: Water imported through STW at Gleneagles and Auchterarder.

name: Carron at Headswood
description-summary: Flat V weir with flows affected by the Carron Valley Reservoir.
description-general: Flat V weir installed in Oct 1988 in an artificial meander cutoff. Straight, uniform channel (concrete walls) lined with gabions; banks are steep to 2.0m. Previously velocity-area station: instability in rating caused by d/s deposition.
description-station-hydrometry: Prior to weir installation in October 1988, the high flow control was probably the bridge downstream, but deposition caused problems. After the weir installation: up to 1.4m stage the flow is modular. Non-modular flow sets in somewhere above this level though not precisely known, partly due to occasional dredging of downstream deposition. Multiple peak flow rating derived from gaugings up to 2.3m and then informed by hydraulic modelling.
description-flow-record: Flows pre-October 1988 are not fit for flood estimation and are therefore rejected. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2019 (WINFAP Files v8), August 2021 (WINFAP Files v10), and August 2025 (v14).
description-catchment: The upper part of the catchment drains part of the Campsie Fells. Bedrock composed of igneous rocks in headwaters and Carboniferous rocks in the valley; predominantly overlain by superficial deposits. Land use predominantly moorland and plantation forestry in headwaters, pasture in lower reaches. Minimal floodplains. No significant catchment changes known.
description-flow-regime: Flashy response. Catchment contains Carron Valley Reservoir, which pre-dates gauge. Export of water and operation of reservoir can significantly influence flow patterns. Influence of effluent return to Endrick Water on floods is negligible.

name: Leven at Leven
description-summary: Velocity area station in Scotland. Flows affected by lochs within the catchment.
description-general: Velocity area station on a straight reach with artificially heightened and steeped banks. Removed from peak flows dataset in September 2019 (WINFAP Files v8).
description-station-hydrometry: The control was formerly a gravel bar, in Sep 1977 stabilised with gabions to form an irregular broad-crested weir. Possible movement in control, evident at low flows. Weir is thought to be modular throughout range. All flows contained to date. Peak flow rating derived from current meter gaugings up to 1.6m (about QMED), simple extrapolation beyond.
description-flow-record: NA
description-catchment: Mostly low-lying catchment. Bedrock predominantly Carboniferous rocks; predominately overlain by superficial deposits. Land use lowland arable farming, and forest with significant urbanisation. Minimal floodplains. No significant catchment changes known.
description-flow-regime: Relatively un-flashy. There are a number of small storage reservoirs in the catchment plus Loch Leven whose outflow is controlled by sluice gates (these can produce seemingly anomalous flow hydrographs). Effluent return and industrial/agricultural abstractions probably don't significantly influence flood peaks.

name: Bonny Water at Bonnybridge
description-summary: Velocity area station gauging a lowland catchment.
description-general: Open river section. Station added to peak flows dataset in September 2023 (WINFAP Files v12).
description-station-hydrometry: Gravel bar low flow control. Archive notes state, congestion by aquatic weeds in summer necessitates correction to recorded stage. However, stage correction is no longer practiced at SEPA. High flows largely contained. One flood rating deemed suitable through the digital period (post 1992), informed by gaugings up to 1.989m (measured flow of 26.2 cumecs) and then upper segments based on hydraulic modelling to incorporate flow in the floodplain.
description-flow-record: Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in August 2026 (WINFAP Files v15).
description-catchment: Lowland catchment. Bedrock Carboniferous rocks with igneous intrusions; almost entirely covered by superficial deposits, mainly boulder clay. Land use: predominantly grassland, forest, and arable with urban development at Cumbernauld in the headwaters.
description-flow-regime: Low flows influenced by diurnal fluctuations caused by Dunswood WWTW discharge at Cumbernauld.

name: Ore at Balfour Mains
description-summary: Velocity area station gauging a lowland catchment with some urban land use.
description-general: Open river section. A railway embankment forms the rb, whilst the lb is steep to the floodplain at 1.6m. Station added to peak flows dataset in August 2021 (WINFAP Files v10).
description-station-hydrometry: Stable rock bar low flow control, has shown instability at right bank. Although an open channel, the gradual growth and capsizing of a tree just downstream of the station is a key factor in understanding the stage-discharge relationship. Its evolution is pretty well documented by pictures. Its size and extent to which it slumps in the channel increases through the station period of record until it collapses completely and falls into the channel in February 2020. The impact of the tree is evident in the ratings from 2012, where the second segment parameters are not typical of open channel hydraulics. Two peak flow ratings across period of record.
description-flow-record: May 1994 flows affected by work at the Loch Fitty outlet. Record frozen after 30/09/2019 due to tree fall onto station control. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2022 (WINFAP Files v11).
description-catchment: Lowland catchment in the coal mining area of W Fife. Bedrock Carboniferous rocks, >90% overlain by superficial deposits, mainly boulder clay. Land use predominantly grassland, forest, and arable with urban development.
description-flow-regime: Low flows moderately affected by pumping from collieries.

name: Avon at Polmonthill
description-summary: Velocity area station. Flows affected by some storage in reservoirs and industrial and agricultural abstractions.
description-general: Velocity area station; the river takes a sharp left turn u/s at a site of river capture.
description-station-hydrometry: Archive notes state the low flow control was an unstable gravel control 40m d/s; replaced by gabion weir in Aug 1989. It was subsequently capped with concrete and the upstream face lined with sheet piling; this was completed on the Sept 1995. High flow control was a small island in mid-channel immediately below station; now it is probably the channel bend d/s. Following a full review of ratings in 2021, it is suspected that the stage discharge relation is complex. The random scatter of available flood gaugings suggests the site is affected by variable tidal states, being so near to the Firth of Forth, assuming the weirs between the station and river mouth are drowned out. There is very poor confidence in the flood estimates from this site and especially during the early period before the gabion weir was built on 01/08/89 as tidal influence will likely have been more pronounced in this early period. Flows in the period between the gabion weir build up to the upgrade to the concrete design (01/08/89 to a date between 1995 and 1999) will likely be a period of relatively lower confidence considering the typical poor performance of gabion weirs. The exact date of the weir rebuild has yet to be confirmed as different dates exist in the records ranging from 01/10/1995 to 01/01/1999. The pre 1999 records have been rejected until the all the pre digital information is available to allow a thorough assessment of this early period. The banks have contained all recorded flows. It has tentatively been kept in Peak Flows as a QMED only site.
description-flow-record: Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2019 (WINFAP Files v8), and in September 2022 (WINFAP Files v11).
