description-catchment: NA
description-flow-regime: NA

name: Anker at Polesworth
description-summary: Crump profile weir with flanking floodbanks to contain out-of-channel flows draining a highly responsive catchment.
description-general: Crump profile weir with flanking floodbanks to contain out of bank flows - includes a downstream recorder. The flow bypasses on the left bank and rejoins downstream after the railway bridge.
description-station-hydrometry: Multiple ratings accross period of record. Variable drowning makes calculating upper limb difficult. Low modular limit (drowns at approximately 0.6 m [~8.0 m3/s]) and prone to weed growth, causing variable drowning and uncertainty with high flows. ADCP gaugings performed between weir wing walls during summer weed growth. High flow gaugings carried out using remote controlled ADCP in old cableway section. In-channel weed growth is managed during the summer months.
description-flow-record: Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in October 2018 (WINFAP Files v7).
description-catchment: Lower reaches drain Permian and Triassic Sandstones and the Coal Measures. Sherwood sandstone and Mercia Mudstone over the remainder of the catchment are widely blanketed with Boulder Clay. Predominantly agricultural catchment, although contains Nuneaton and Hinkley; with urban land use accounting a signifcant proportion of the catchment area.
description-flow-regime: Substantial modification owing to PWS imports to the catchment.

name: Erewash at Sandiacre
description-summary: Twin Laserflow Index Velocity gauges from 01/10/2022, replacing multipath ultrasonic time-of-flight gauge. River splits flows through two rectangular flood drainage channels.
description-general: Two rectangular concrete flood drainage channels, each 3.9m wide, 3.09m deep, separated by divide wall 1m high. Informal low flow controls installed 1981; closed 1984, reopened 1991 as multipath ultrasonic gauge, replaced with Laserflow index velocity gauge in 2022.
description-station-hydrometry: No ratings available. Unstable ratings in early record. Somewhat improved following installation of informal low flow controls in 1981. Closed 1984, reopened 1991 as a multipath ultrasonic operation. Stop boards can close one channel at low flows. All flows contained.
description-flow-record: Pre-1972 the data is from CEH data holdings. Between 1972 and 1992 the data is the sum of the flows from the left (4027) and right (4227) channels. Summary and daily mean flow data available for this period. Use with care (especially low flows) due to unstable ratings. Informal low flow controls improved data somewhat from 1981. Closed 1984. 15min data available from 1991 when the site reopened as a multipath ultrasonic operation, continues with data from Laserflow Index Velocity gauge from 2022. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in August 2025 (WINFAP Files v14).
description-catchment: Low to moderate relief catchment draining Carboniferous Coal Measures with Permian and Triassic rocks on east and south boundaries. Significant urban fraction, otherwise arable and grazing land use.
description-flow-regime: Substantial augmentation from mine drainage and mining towns' STW. Runoff influenced by groundwater abstraction/recharge. Runoff increased by effluent returns. Runoff reduced by industrial/agricultural abstraction. Substantial mining in catchment.

name: Soar at Wanlip
description-summary: Compound Crump weir on the Soar. Station closed in 1981.
description-general: Compound Crump weir, closed in 1981.
description-station-hydrometry: NA
description-flow-record: NA
description-catchment: Lower catchment dominated by Leicester; headwaters rural.
description-flow-regime: Responsive regime.

name: Kingston Brook at Kingston Hall
description-summary: Compound Crump weir on the Kingston Brook, gauging the upstream flat agricultural land.
description-general: Compound Crump profile weir with crest tapping. Experimental catchment.
description-station-hydrometry: Channel flanked by floodbanks. Weed growth problems, severe backing up from the Soar in high flows. Not bypassed but inundates u/s. Theoretical rating appears to underestimate flows.
description-flow-record: NA
description-catchment: Flat, agricultural catchment whose solid geology is Triassic Mudstones and Lower Lias. Diamicton overlays the upper reaches of the catchment, whilst the lower valley is overlain by alluvial deposits.
description-flow-regime: Moderate influence from WRW and spray irrigation.

name: Black Brook at Onebarrow
description-summary: Trapezoidal Flume on the Black Brook, covering the full range of flows.
description-general: Trapezoidal Flume. International Hydrological Decade Experimental Basin.
description-station-hydrometry: Well rated, full range station, not bypassed.
description-flow-record: NA
description-catchment: Small rural catchment of moderate relief; hills of impermeable Pre-Cambrian rocks, valleys infilled with Keuper Marl and Boulder clay. Responsive. Mostly pasture.
description-flow-regime: Some contribution from M1 runoff, but otherwise natural.

name: Manifold at Ilam
description-summary: Crump profile weir somewhat insensitive but good quality data throughout the range of flows but difficult to gauge at higher flows.
description-general: Crump profile weir, 12.5m wide in a straight reach - modular to bankfull. Rocky bed, somewhat insensitive but good quality data throughout the range. Gaugings possible with ADCP just upstream of weir at levels up to around 0.8m after which it becomes increasingly more difficult due to turbulent flow. Gaugings can also be performed in Ilam village however are not always reliable. Located downstream of Ilam town and 700m upstream of Manifold/Dove confluence. Fish baffles and eel pass installed on weir in July 2015. Modular style eel bristles added to right bank side of weir, on downstream face in July 2024.
description-station-hydrometry: One rating applies up to 0.465 m. Above this stage, top section rating limbs covering the pre 2015 period give higher discharges for a given stage, while post 2015 top sections (3 and 4) define a less steep relationship and therefore lower discharges at equivalent stages. This reflects the installation of fish baffles at the site in 2015, which increased resistance to flow. The revised high-flow rating is applied from 01/07/2015. Two peak flow ratings across period of record.
description-flow-record: Water Year 1971/1972 is rejected as the true AMAX occurs during missing period and likely to be substantially higher. Drop in flow August 2022 due to debris being cleared from the weir. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in August 2021 (WINFAP Files v10).
description-catchment: Headwaters of moderate relief and drain sandstone and mudstone of the Millstone Grit; middle reach has cut deep gorges through Carboniferous Limestone. Responsive catchment. Sheep grazing and moorland.
description-flow-regime: Minimal interference from PWS.

name: Meden at Church Warsop
description-summary: Non-standard pre 2015. Flat-V from 2015 onwards.
description-general: Flat-V weir installed in Jan 2015 to replace the trapezoidal flume built in 1964. 1972-2015 flume was unsatisfactory so site used as velocity area except 1984-1990 when station was inactive. Built to measure flows entering Sherwood Sandstone outcrop.
description-station-hydrometry: Theoretical Flat-V equation applies from 2015 onwards with tail water corrections above modular limit of structure. Two ratings applied to pre-2015 period of record, one post-2015. Mining subsidence in 1976 caused permanent drowning of flume until downstream channel was regraded in 1981.
description-flow-record: 15 minute derived data starts 1972, only summary and daily mean data prior to this. Station closed between 1984 and 1990. June 2007 and October 2023 high flows beyond limit of rating curve. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in August 2025 (WINFAP Files v14).
description-catchment: Ribbon-like, SW-NE catchment of moderate relief, rising on Magnesian Limestone, subordinate Permian Marl and Sherwood Sandstone. Mining was dominant industry; many spoil tips. Sutton in Ashfield in headwaters, also part of Mansfield Woodhouse.
description-flow-regime: Significant proportion of low flows are comprised of effluent.

name: Dove at Hollinsclough
description-summary: Compound Crump profile weir built to investigate the water balance of a Millstone Grit catchment typical of the area south of the High Peak.
description-general: Small compound Crump profile weir, crest lengths 1.2 and 3.02m in rocky channel. Originally an experimental catchment with associated comprehensive climate station. Station out of action Oct 1986-Oct 1996.
description-station-hydrometry: Fully modular, has never been overtopped. Some trouble with left bank. accretion, incised gauging section, and heavy undergrowth. One rating applied across period of record, based on rating tables not gaugings. Difficult to gauge higher flows the largest of which suggests rating underestimates flow. Rating revised in 2016. Salt dilution method has been used at the gauging station at low flows, with promising results so far. It may be considered for higher level gaugings where an ADCP cannot be easily deployed.
description-flow-record: Zero flow in Jan 1986 thought to be due to frozen catchment. Winter 21-22 has no flow to large debris jam in the flume. Unable to apply correction due to uncertainty in point of accumulation, flows were too high to keep in. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2019 (WINFAP Files v8).
description-catchment: Headwater gauge for the River Dove. Steep slopes and flashy regime. Namurian Grits and Shales with some Dinantian limestone (about 10%). Highland catchment, steep gradients. Mainly rural grazing land. Catchment heavily instrumented for rainfall and evaporation measurements.
description-flow-regime: Natural to within 10% at the 95 percentile flow with flashy regime.

name: Leen at Triumph Road Nottingham
description-summary: Station in central Nottingham gauging the baseflow dominated regime of the Leen. Twin concrete channels in urban area.
description-general: Two rectangular concrete channels, each 3.05m wide, 2.75m deep, separated by divide wall 1m high. All flows contained. Closed 1984, reopened in 1991 as multiple Ultrasonic operation. Laser flow gauge operational from 2023. Station added to peak flows dataset in August 2024 (WINFAP Files v13).
description-station-hydrometry: Use pre-ultrasonic record with care especially at low flows due to unstable rating. Informal low flow controls installed in 1981 produced some improvement.
description-flow-record: Peak Flows available from the Ultrasonic gauge only after WY1991/1992.
description-catchment: Moderate to low relief catchment draining south into Nottingham. Geology predominantly Magnesian Limestone in the west with Permian Mudstones and Sherwood Sandstones to the east. Significant urban fraction, approx 50%, in lower catchment otherwise arable and grazing land use.
description-flow-regime: An extremely urban, flashy catchment producing a very spiky data record. Minor net disturbance to baseflow dominated flow regime. There is also a high level of flood attenuation in the catchment, with a number of dams and storage reservoirs that can hold back flow and level.

name: Poulter at Twyford Bridge
description-summary: LaserFlow gauge gauge on the Poulter. Large amounts of missing data.
description-general: Station sites where Poulter leaves Sherwood Sandstone outcrop. Original 4.88m wide Crump profile weir submerged from late 1972 by mining subsidence; channel regraded in 1981, but no solution. Ultrasonic gauge installed in 1992 revived the station and was replaced by a LaserFlow gauge in October 2017.
description-station-hydrometry: Laserflow capable of measuring full range of flows. Extreme high flows suspect due to backing up from River Idle and inaccessibility for gauging.
description-flow-record: Periods of missing data from 2007 until 2009 due to difficulties with ultrasonic gauge. Early flow record for the ultrasonic gauge did not measure bypass flow. Further periods of suspect data and edited data from 2015-2019 due to measurement problems. The laser flow gauge post 2019 measures the full range of flows to a better standard.
description-catchment: Catchment rises on Magnesian Limestone with subordinant Permian Marl; mainly underlain by Sherwood Sandstone. Predominantly rural; part of Bolsover and Shirebrook in headwaters.
description-flow-regime: Minor augmentation from sewage; inline lakes in Clumber and Welbeck Parks ensure sluggish response.

name: Derwent at Mytham Bridge
description-summary: Gauging station on the Derwent, downstream of the Ladybower Reservoir.
description-general: Downstream of Ladybower Reservoir.
description-station-hydrometry: NA
description-flow-record: Data covers 1978-1984 and 1992-1996.
description-catchment: Steep moorland headwaters, with extensive hilltop peat. Shale and sandstone form the lower parts of the valleys, gritstone tops the hills (Middle Carboniferous).
description-flow-regime: Artificial flow regime, substantial reduction in runoff due to PWS exports.

name: Manifold at Hulme End
description-summary: Velocity area station closed in 1982.
description-general: Concrete weir with iron girder across crest (metal crest added 1968). Crest level 213.281mAOD, 8.5m wide. Removed from peak flows dataset in September 2023 (WINFAP Files v12).
description-station-hydrometry: Rating applied across period of record, not believed to be based on theoretical weir equations. No gaugings above 0.7m. Rating not validated above level of highest spot gauging (0.7m / ~11 cumecs).
description-flow-record: NA
description-catchment: Underlain entirely by Namurian shales and grits. Land use upland pasture with sheep grazing and moorland.
description-flow-regime: Responsive catchment. Runoff reduced by public water supply abstraction. Runoff increased by effluent returns.

name: Rea at Calthorpe Park
description-summary: Crump profile weir draining an almost totally urbanised catchment with data used for flood forecasting.
description-general: Crump profile weir, 3.66m wide, with flanking broad-crested weirs set in a formalised, roughly rectangular channel. Station data is used for flood forecasting.
description-station-hydrometry: High flows gauged from nearby footbridge, but hazardous owing to high velocities. Prone to upstream siltation. Drowns at high flows. At 0.7m the flows go over the broad-crested weir shoulders, but all flows are in bank. Possibly some backing up effects but of uncertain cause. Multiple peak flow ratings across period of record, derived from current meter gaugings.
description-flow-record: Summer 2007 peak flows under review. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2019 (WINFAP Files v8).
description-catchment: Almost totally urbanised catchment overlying clay except in the headwaters in the Lickey Hills.
description-flow-regime: Very responsive. Significant imports modify flow regime. Runoff increased by effluent returns.

name: Trent at Stoke-On-Trent
description-summary: Crump profile weir draining and urbanised and industrialised catchment with significant flow modification.
description-general: Crump profile weir, 4.12m wide, modular throughout range. Liable to collect rubbish and fish baffles added in 2012.
description-station-hydrometry: Four peak flow ratings applied across period of record. Current meter gaugings show a high degree of accuracy compared to rating. Low flow ADCP gaugings typically carried out between weir wing walls. High flow gaugings performed off or near upstream footbridge.
description-flow-record: Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2019 (WINFAP Files v8).
description-catchment: Moderate relief catchment, significantly urbanised at Biddulph and Stoke on Trent, draining the Coal Measures; approximately quarter of catchment is covered with Boulder Clay.
description-flow-regime: A responsive catchment affected by impounding reservoirs, discharges from three WRW's, plus mine drainage. Substantial flow modification in the early record, but reduced to significant through the 1980s. Flow affected by STW closure: effluent from Stoke diverted to other STW downstream of the gauge.

name: Hamps at Waterhouses
description-summary: Flat V weir with poor, rocky, approach.
description-general: Flat vee weir. Poor approach to weir - rocks and shoal. Station closed 1982-2000.
description-station-hydrometry: Mostly contained within bank except for Aug 1971 maximum. Two peaks flow ratings applied across period of record. ADCP gaugings carried out in village approx 300m upstream, off a farm bridge or by wading, due to the rocky nature of the channel immediately upstream and downstream of the weir. Gauging location needs to be confirmed due to variations in results, with salt dilution methods being considered. Salt dilution method has been used at the gauging station at low flows, with promising results so far. It may be considered for higher level gaugings where an ADCP cannot be easily deployed.
description-flow-record: Station closed 1982-2000. High flows in August 1971 missing from GDF record. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2019 (WINFAP Files v8).
description-catchment: NA
description-flow-regime: Runoff increased by effluent returns. Natural to within 10% at the 95 percentile flow.

name: Derwent at Chatsworth
description-summary: Velocity area station approx. 36m wide at bankfull.
description-general: Velocity area station approx. 36m wide at bankfull. Important flood forecasting station.
description-station-hydrometry: Downstream shoal acts as a control, but shoal and rating are not too stable. All but extreme flows contained. Complex rating history including multipe peak flow ratings applied over period of record.
description-flow-record: Peak flow record starts from 30 June 1976. Flow data before this date is less reliable due to inconsistencies over the way the datum change has been handled. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in August 2026 (WINFAP Files v15).
description-catchment: Upland catchment with peat covered moorlands in the headwaters. Geology: predominantly Millstone Grit, with some western tributaries draining Carboniferous Limestone. Predominantly pasture.
description-flow-regime: Quite responsive. Flows substantially affected by Derwent reservoirs.

name: Poulter at Cuckney
description-summary: Cross-correlation doppler on the Poulter, with a high baseflow component. Cross correlation gauge operational from 2025. Bed-mounted ADCP with IV rating from November 2016. 3.71m width crump profile weir provided flow measurement from start of record until 2016.
description-general: Designed to measure the flow as the Poulter entered the Bunter Sandstone outcrop.
description-station-hydrometry: Cross correlation and ADCP devices located upstream of crump profile weir which is still in place. The original construction had higher wing walls up to a height of 1.7 metres above the crest. Modifications were made to the vertical wing walls and embankments in the summer of 1990. The capacity of the structure was reduced to 0.49 metres.
description-flow-record: Flows ungauged for period 1984 to 1990 due to mothballing of station. Evidence of reduced performance of crump weir from 2006, and affected further by mining subsidence from 2011.
description-catchment: Catchment of moderate relief draining from the scarp of the Magnesian Limestone eastwards. Subordinate outcrops of Permian Marl. Some urban development and coal mining spoil heaps.
description-flow-regime: High baseflow component, subdued hydrographs. U/s water gardens further damp response. U/s farm abstraction. Minimal modifications to flow regime from WRW.

name: Meden/Maun at Bothamsall / Haughton
description-summary: Site data is a combination of DMFs from Bothamsall (4045) on the Meden and Haughton (4034) on the Maun - both trapezoidal flumes, rated by C/m - the river divides upstream of the two gauging points and then joins again downstream. Station closed in 1984.
description-general: The Meden and Maun join then split u/s of the gauging points. This is a combination record of DMFs from the Meden at Bothamshall and the Maun at Haughton. No combined peak flows available (those provided are for the Meden). Both stations originally velocity-area stations with trapezoidal flumes built in 1963/4 - closed in 1984.
description-station-hydrometry: Flows derived from addition of two subsidiary sites - no ratings. Poor ratings record.
description-flow-record: The levels given are at Bothamsall (the site with greater flows).
description-catchment: The lower two thirds of the catchment is Permian and Triassic Sandstones with Permain Magensian Limestone upstream. The catchment includes Mansfield and adjacent former coal mining area. It is almost entirely free of Drift deposits.
description-flow-regime: Runoff influenced by groundwater abstraction/recharge. Runoff increased by effluent returns.

name: Dove at Izaak Walton
description-summary: Crump profile Flat V weir modular to bankfull draining catchment with natural flow regime.
description-general: Crump profile flat vee weir, 7.59m wide, deep vertical sidewalls, modular to bankfull. Excellent station, narrower than the main channel.
description-station-hydrometry: Fish baffles installed on weir in August 2016. Bypassing may occur at high flows on the left bank. Multiple peak flow ratings applied across period of record. Gaugings generally performed with ADCP within or just upstream of the weir wing walls across the stage range.
description-flow-record: Water Year 1969/1970 rejected due to low confidence. Debris in summer 2022 leading to unusual peak in August. Unable to correct. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in August 2021 (WINFAP Files v10).
description-catchment: Long narrow catchment. Upper reaches on Millstone Grit mudstone and sandstone. Western watershed is formed by a steep Carboniferous Limestone ridge. The Dove's passage across the Carb. l'st is characterised by deep gorges (Wolfscote Dale, Dove Dale). Largely moorland.
description-flow-regime: Flashy response but natural catchment.

name: Oldcotes Dyke at Blyth
description-summary: Crump profile Flat V weir station draining baseflow dominated catchment with substantial augmentation of low flows from WRW.
description-general: Crump profile Flat V weir with reasonable approach d/s of a road bridge. Removed from peak flows dataset in September 2023 (WINFAP Files v12).
description-station-hydrometry: Low modular limit (~0.75m, 7-8 cumecs), rating does not take account of non-modular flow conditions. Three ratings applied across period of record. Ratings have generic upper limb and slightly different limbs for low flows. Wading gaugings taken u/s of bridge should site back-up (owing to weed growth).
description-flow-record: High flows unreliable, rating is extrapolated beyond 0.682m. Flows from October 1999 reprocessed in 2012 to account for negative shift in gaugings of unknown cause - resulting in lowering of low flow estimates. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in October 2018 (WINFAP Files v7).
description-catchment: Moderate relief catchment, sited where the river crosses the Triassic Sandstone outcrop, mostly draining Magnesian Limestone but includes Coal Measures, Permian Marl & sandstones. Rural catchment arable farming as dominant land use.
description-flow-regime: Base flow dominated with substantial augmentation of low flows from WRW.

name: Amber at Wingfield Park
description-summary: Crump profile Flat V weir draining catchment containing coal measures and moorland and PWS reservoir.
description-general: Crump profile Flat V weir in trapezoidal channel. Higher flows gauged from bridge upstream. Extreme flows bypass on right bank. Fairly low modular limit. Stream joins downstream, which causes drowning of gauging station weir. Pumped Eel pass installed 2015.
description-station-hydrometry: Two ratings applied across period of record which are identical above 0.5m. The top section of the curve (out of bank) is derived using channel cross sections. Higher flows gauged from bridge upstream. Extreme flows bypass on right bank.
description-flow-record: June 2007 peak flows estimated using flood curve. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2020 (WINFAP Files v9).
description-catchment: Upland catchment with moorland headwaters. Upper half of catchment drains Millstone Grit, partially blanketed with Boulder Clay. Bisects limestone and tuff inlier of Ashover. Lower half predominantly Coal Measures. Landuse predominantly moorland in the headwaters.
description-flow-regime: Contains Ogston PWS reservoir; substantial augmentation from mine pumping and sewage.

name: Ryton at Worksop
description-summary: Crump profile Flat V weir draining mixed farming, industry and forestry catchment.
description-general: Crump profile Flat V weir in trapezoidal channel. Downstream bridge provokes early non-modularity. Modified stage discharge curve produced for non-modularity at high flows.
description-station-hydrometry: Two ratings applied across period of record, the reason for change unknown. Ratings fit well to gaugings which are quite scattered, however all flows are contained. Downstream bridge provokes early non-modularity. Modified stage discharge curve produced for non-modularity at high flows.
description-flow-record: June 2007 flows should be treated with caution as levels exceeded bankfull. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in October 2018 (WINFAP Files v7).
description-catchment: Catchment of moderate relief on dip slope of Magnesian L'st outcrop with a narrow band of Permian Marl near the gauge. Extractive industries in the west otherwise mixed farming and forestry.
description-flow-regime: Significant flow augmentation via groundwater pumping and WRW, and abstractions for canal use. High baseflow component and subdued hydrographs.

name: Torne at Auckley
description-summary: Cross Correlation Doppler flow gauge on the River Torne.
description-general: Cross correlation doppler at bridge operational from 6th May 2021. Measurement was previously from side-looking doppler from 2016. From start of record until 2016 measurement from crump profile Flat V weir 50m upstream of bridge in trapezoidal channel, 8.9m wide at V-full. Weir removed November 2025.
description-station-hydrometry: Late spring/summer weed growth substantially raises water levels in low gradient catchment. Cross correlation gauge has provided good quality data since 2021. A number of measurement issues prior to this. Subsidence affected performance in 1990s, second well installed d/s. Bypassing unlikely but high range unreliable prior to 2021 due to backing up from artificial drainage and/or summer weed growth. Low local hydraulic gradients: tail water level measurements allowed correction for drowned flow. Submerged weir rating derived based on gaugings taken when the submergence ratio was zero.
description-flow-record: 1973 peak under review - triggered by 70mm storm but flow may be over-estimated. Significant weed growth has an impact on flow record.
description-catchment: R. Torne rises on dip slope of Magnesian L'st and Sherwood S'st but soon enters Trent/Humber ancient floodplain. Tidally drained. Contains mine workings and agriculture.
description-flow-regime: Generally, sluggish response. Substantial flow augmentation from WRW and mine drainage.

name: Soar at Narborough
description-summary: Crump profile Flat V weir on the Soar. Records for the Soar were previously held under one site, Soar at Littlethorpe (28082), covering the period August 1971 to present. Starting from 2026, the records have been separated due to a large difference in catchment area between the sites. Records for Soar at Narborough (28051) begin in August 1971 and end in May 1984. Records for Soar at Littlethorpe (28082) start in April 1983 and continue to the present day.
description-general: Crump profile Flat V weir as the invert to a road bridge. Station added to peak flows dataset in August 2026 (WINFAP Files v15).
description-station-hydrometry: Flow data for the Narborough between 1971-1984 are derived from the weir rating. Sidespilling began at 1 m due to backwater effects and floodplain inundation, although peak floods remained contained within and constrained by the road bridge opening. No bypassing of the station occurred. Weed growth problems in summer.
description-flow-record: Record reprocessed using single rating, with segment 1 a powerlaw fit to theoretical weir equation.
description-catchment: Predominantly agricultural catchment, gauged in southern outskirts of Leicester. Extensive Boulder Clay and glacial gravel cover; Keuper sediments exposed in some valley flanks. Significant river terraces and alluvium in lower reaches.
description-flow-regime: Substantial imports enter river from WRW.

name: Sow at Great Bridgeford
description-summary: Crump profile Flat V weir in trapezoidal channel, with floodbanks to contain out of channel flows.
description-general: Crump profile Flat V weir, 9.1m wide, in trapezoidal channel, with floodbanks to contain out of channel flows. Fish and eel pass constructed in 2014. Removed from peak flows dataset in September 2023 (WINFAP Files v12).
description-station-hydrometry: Downstream channel widened in 2015 to allow for modular conditions throughout the year. Large amount of scatter in gaugings making flow calculations unreliable, compounded by bypass flow during flood conditions which is difficult to measure accurately. Rating problems include summer weed growth that causes variable drowning, affecting flow quality at all levels. Sedimentation in the measurement section can also cause inaccuracies. ADCP gaugings carried out by wading and remote craft at low flows within measurement section. High flow gaugings carried out within measurement section using remote controlled ADCP, as cableway no longer in use. In-channel weed growth upstream and downstream of measurement section is managed during the summer months.
description-flow-record: Flows rejected during Jun to Sep 2016 due to weed growth. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2022 (WINFAP Files v11).
description-catchment: Low relief agricultural catchment, primarily on Mercia Mudstone, with some Sherwood Sandstone in headwaters. Glacial gravel in valleys maintain baseflows.
description-flow-regime: Minimal interference from sewage effluent and groundwater pumping for PWS.

name: Penk at Penkridge
description-summary: Originally a velocity area station the station was closed in 1983 and operated at level only until 1990 when a crump profile Flat V weir in trapezoidal channel was installed.
description-general: ADCP gaugings performed between weir wing walls or approximately 15m upstream of weir. High level/flood gaugings also carried out by remote controlled ADCP 5-10m downstream of road bridge. Periodic weed cutting carried out by contractors during growing season to prevent weir from drowning out prematurely.
description-station-hydrometry: Multiple peak flow ratings applied across period of record. Current rating fits corresponding gaugings very well to maximum gaugings (2.3m). Local bankfull conditions - channel width is 15m. Early drowning caused by weed growth.
description-flow-record: Station closed in 1983 with level only data until 1990 when data recommences after installation of crump profile weir. Missing data from 2017-05-14 to 2017-09-24 because the site was affected by downstream weed, so the weir was drowned (non-modular) during the summer months. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in October 2018 (WINFAP Files v7). Rating reviewed in 2022 and data reprocessed from 2015.
description-catchment: Low to moderate relief catchment, glacial gravels over Mercia Mudstone to the west with Boulder Clay over Sherwood S'st to the east. Western part of the catchment rural; part of Wolverhampton in the south and Cannock in the East. Elsewhere, mixed farming with some forestry.
description-flow-regime: Substantial augmentation of flows from WRW.

name: Ecclesbourne at Duffield
description-summary: Crump profile Flat V (1:10) weir set in sloping sidewalls - station closed 1983-1989.
description-general: Crump profile Flat V (1:10) weir set in sloping (1:1) 1.25m high sidewalls, 7.2m wide at V-full. Likely to be modular to structure full. Closed 1983-89. High flows gauged from d/s bridge - bridge downstream may restrict flood flows. Adjustable pre-barrage to improve fish passage installed on weir apron in Jan 2013. Remains modular to structure full. Pre-barrage to improve fish passage installed on weir apron in 2013. Remains modular to structure full.
description-station-hydrometry: Two ratings applied across period of record. Rating should not be applied beyond bankfull. Gauged at low flows only. High flows gauged from d/s bridge. Adjustable pre-barrage to improve fish passage installed on weir apron in Jan 2013. Bridge downstream may restrict flood flows.
description-flow-record: Good high flows site - station closed 1983-89. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2019 (WINFAP Files v8).
description-catchment: Moderate relief catchment, solid geology Coal Measures. Minor Boulder Clay cover in mid-catchment. Essentially rural; Wirksworth in headwaters.
description-flow-regime: PWS abstraction and WRW discharge balance to yield substantially natural regime.

name: Rothley Brook at Rothley
description-summary: Crump profile Flat V weir in a trapezoidal channel.
description-general: NA
description-station-hydrometry: Some flow uncertainty possibly caused by substantial sediment deposition in upstream section, upstream bend, and more recently deteriorating condition of weir surface. Three ratings applied across period of record, with most recent fit to a shift in lower flow gaugings from 2016. Modular section of the rating is theoretical prior to 2016. 1997 rating change updated the non-modular section. Weir drowns at high flows above 1.1m, starting at 0.5m. Rating limit is level of highest gauging and bankfull level 1.7m. Bypassing on right bank starts above this for which the rating is extrapolated and does not account for. Very high flow backs up from twin arch stone bridge immediately downstream with wrack marks indicating substantial drawdown at the bridge.
description-flow-record: Unusual flow pattern in Oct 1978 due to drawdown of Thornton Reservoir. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in October 2018 (WINFAP Files v7).
description-catchment: Geology predominantly Mercia Mudstone overlain by Boulder Clay with ancient Charnwood Forest rocks outcrop to the N. Predominantly rural, but drains a portion of NW Leicester and contains number of small towns.
description-flow-regime: Substantial imports enter the river from WRW.

name: Henmore Brook at Ashbourne
description-summary: Crump profile Flat V weir within vertical wing walls - station closed between 1984 and 1993.
description-general: Crump profile Flat V weir, 6.0m wide, within vertical wing walls. Right bank approach built up into low floodbank. Modular limit high, but no arrangements to deal with non-modular discharge. Contains Carsington pump storage reservoir - impounded from September 1991. Station closed between 1984 and 1993. Peak flow data are for record before Carsington Reservoir. Fish baffles added to the downstream weir face in March 2021.
description-station-hydrometry: Single rating applied across the period of record. This accounts for non-modular flow due to the high modular limit of the station. Station closed between 1984 and 1993. Remote controlled ADCP gaugings carried out within weir wing walls or a few metres upstream of the weir, across the flow range.
description-flow-record: Impounded from September 1991, and post-reservoir data marked as rejected. Rating reviewed in 2022 and data reprocessed from full period of record. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2019 (WINFAP Files v8).
description-catchment: Catchment of moderate relief in South Pennines, draining Drift free Millstone Grit and Carboniferous Limestone. Predominantly forest and pasture, some moorland. Pre-reservoir FARL2015 (for WINFAP 5.3 or later) or FARL (for earlier versions of WINFAP) should be used with these records because the peak flow data after the reservoir started impounding is rejected. Pre- and post-reservoir values for FARL2015 are 0.966 and 0.7447, respectively. Pre-reservoir value for FARL is 0.977, while post-reservoir cannot be calculated from the original FARL water layer.
description-flow-regime: Responsive catchment affected by Carsington pump storage reservoir.

name: Maun at Mansfield STW
description-summary: Velocity area station installed in 1964 and Closed in 1984 and replaced by 28115 (Mansfield The Dykes) in 1996.
description-general: Velocity area station opened in 1958. Trapezoidal critical depth flume installed in 1964. Flume has drowned in past due to summer weed growth and rubbish accumulation. Station situated immediately downstream of STW. Closed in 1984, replaced by 28115 (Mansfield The Dykes) in May 1992. All flows contained.
description-station-hydrometry: One rating applied across period of record. Structure designed to measure flows only up to modular limit (3m3/s) with poor fit to gaugings. Flume has drowned in past due to summer weed growth and rubbish accumulation. Station situated immediately downstream of STW. Flows augmented by runoff from urban area of Mansfield which effectively increases catchment area.
description-flow-record: NA
description-catchment: Underlying geology Magensian Limestone and Permian sandstone. Catchment almost entirely urbanised: Mansfield and Sutton in Ashfield.
description-flow-regime: Flows augmented by runoff from urban area of Mansfield which effectively increases catchment area. Runoff influenced by groundwater abstraction/recharge. Runoff increased by effluent returns.

name: Dover Beck at Lowdham
description-summary: Crump profile Flat V weir in a trapezoidal channel draining a baseflow dominated catchment affected by significant abstractions.
description-general: Crump profile flat V weir (1:10) in a trapezoidal (1:1) channel. Subject to weed growth; low modular limit. Shallow flow upstream and downstream of the weir.
description-station-hydrometry: Two ratings applied across period of record, the most recent adjusting the non-modular limb based on new high flow gaugings up to 2007, re-processed back to January-1990. Older high flow gaugings have better fit to the previous curve. The same theoretical flat-V weir equation for modular flows applies over whole period of record. High deviation at low flows may be accounted for by increased gauging error at low flows and silt accumulation. Subject to weed growth; low modular limit but rating has high flow component.
description-flow-record: Daily flow peak on 4th August 2018 caused by burst water main in the area which caused water to enter the river from the nearby areas. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2019 (WINFAP Files v8). and in August 2024 (WINFAP Files v13).
description-catchment: The river drains SE from a moderate to low relief catchment. The bulk of the catchment comprises outcrop Triassic sandstone. Flanking hills nearer the gauge are of Mercia Mudstone. Predominantly rural catchment with mixed farming.
description-flow-regime: Baseflow dominated. Affected by spray irrigation abstraction and minor WRW effluent.

name: Churnet at Basford Bridge
description-summary: Crump profile Flat V weir in trapezoidal channel draining catchment with significant modifications to flow regime - replaced 28042 in 1975.
description-general: Crump profile Flat V weir in trapezoidal channel. Drowns out above +0.55mASD, especially owing to weed growth. Prescribed flow point. Replaced 28042 in 1975. At levels above 2.2mASD bypassing occurs along adjacent canal. Cableway de-roped and no longer operational.
description-station-hydrometry: Four peak flow ratings applied across period of record. Gaugings up to bankfull, but some scatter in gaugings and bypassing beyond 2.2m which makes gauging difficult. Rating less reliable beyond this point but still fits gaugings well. High flow gaugings carried out using remote controlled ADCP as cableway no longer used. At lower levels, gaugings waded using ADCP upstream of section or using remote craft.
description-flow-record: Rejected data in 2011 and 2012 due to downstream weed grwoth and sedimentation issues, and in 2015 due to equipment issues. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2022 (WINFAP Files v11).
description-catchment: Catchment of moderate relief with mixed geology; primarily Sherwood Sandstone and shales and s'st of the Millstone Grit series. Some blanketing of Boulder Clay and glacial sand and gravel. Contains Leek and Tittesworth Reservoir but otherwise low grade agriculture or pasture.
description-flow-regime: Substantial modification to flow regime by exports from reservoirs and imports via WRW and industrial usage.

name: Cole at Coleshill
description-summary: Crump profile Flat V weir in trapezoidal channel draining a highly urbanised catchment.
description-general: Crump profile Flat V weir in trapezoidal channel, 10.9m at V-full, with floodbanks to contain out-of-channel flow. Eel tiles were put on weir in 2016. Site also referred to as Bacons End. Removed from peak flows dataset in September 2023 (WINFAP Files v12).
description-station-hydrometry: Gauged from bridge during high flows using a rope - formerly a cableway of span 48m, which extended across floodbanks. Highest flows inundate narrow floodplain. Low flow gaugings measured by waded ADCP or remote craft. There is wide scatter in gaugings below QMED that could lead to underestimation of QMED by up to 30%, although a single gauging above 1.5m which agrees well with the rating. Needs further high flow gaugings and a review of the rating above bankfull.
description-flow-record: Blockage of stilling well during 2012 resulted in under-recording - with re-processed flows for 2012 based on downstream site at Swan's Barn used although these are marked as unreprentative in the Peak Flow Dataset. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2022 (WINFAP Files v11).
description-catchment: Substantially urbanised catchment (S Birmingham suburbs). Underlying geology: Mercia Mudstone with extensive coverings of Boulder Clay and glacial sand and gravel.
description-flow-regime: Responsive catchment. Moderate modification to flows from effluent returns.

name: Derwent at Church Wilne
description-summary: Crump profile Flat V weir in trapezoidal channel with variable quality high flows data as weir drowns and can back up from Trent. Sidelooker ADCP velocity index gauge 1km downstream will replace weir in future, currently running in parallel during calibration period.
description-general: Crump profile flat V weir is 27m wide, in trapezoidal channel. Very broad floodplain - flows readily and extensively occur out of bank at approx 2.0mASD. 20km downstream of St Marys Bridge; substantial abstractions and returns in between.
description-station-hydrometry: High flows of variable quality as weir drowns; calculated by extrapolation from St Mary's Bridge and gaugings at Draycott. At high flows the gauging site becomes cut off due to floodplain flows and is impossible to gauge except through the use of a boat. Three peak flow ratings applied across period of record. Little evidence to support the top end of the rating.
description-flow-record: Flows for the period 01/01/2004 onwards re-processed using new ratings following rating review in 2014. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2022 (WINFAP Files v11).
description-catchment: Large catchment with moorland headwaters on Carboniferous Grit and Limestone. Lower reaches on Sherwood Sandstone and Mercia Mudstone. Valley broadens considerably below Derby with extensive sand and gravel terraces. Range of agricultural and industrial activity.
description-flow-regime: Can back up from Trent. Abstraction point nearby at Draycott can affect flows (e.g. summer 2018).

name: Lathkill at Pickering Wood
description-summary: Compound rectangular thin plate weir on the Lathkill, shortly upstream of the confluence of the Wye.
description-general: Compound rectangular thin plate weir, lower crest only active during lowest flows below stage 0.1 metres. Head measurement in a stilling well with shaft encoder. Site located 600 metres upstream with confluence of the River Wye giving potential for backing up in flood conditions. Originally built in 1964 with charts commencing in 1969. Station closed in 1982. Site reinstated 1997 as part of Environmental change network following significant works.
description-station-hydrometry: Rating review in 2013 returned measurement of thin plate weir to theoretical with high flow rating extension above capacity of the structure using gauging of 5.94 m3/s on 31st October 2000 with flows processed back to 2000. A minewater sough blockage increased baseflow between 2000-2020, resulting in the lower crest becoming less active.
description-flow-record: Flow data between 01/08/76 to 01/05/81 erroneous following reopening and review of data and removed from records. Digital records commence in 1998. Data quality deemed poor due to lack of maintenance of the thin plate weir resulting in siltation issues behind the crest. Rating curve pre-2000 is fit to gaugings to try and account for the inaccuracy of the thin plate weir equation. Weed growth upstream of the structure causes issues with the approach conditions.
description-catchment: SSSI & Habitat's Directive site, located in nature reserve in Derbyshire Peak district. Catchment composed of Dinantion limestone.
description-flow-regime: NA

name: Burbage Brook at Burbage
description-summary: Compound rectangular thin-plate weir draining a natural peat based catchment.
description-general: Compound rectangular thin plate weir (1.5 m wide section at right bank, 4.5 m section 0.15 m higher at left bank, separated by sheet steel divide plate between crests; overall width 6 m). Wing wall stage 1.09 m for small section, over 2m for large weir. No cableway, but footbridge; site unlikely to ever be gauged during events.
description-station-hydrometry: One theoretical (modular flow) rating applied across period of record. Lower weir crest around 0.8m above downstream bed, but the very highest events likely to have been drowned due to the narrow channel of gentle slope downstream No spot gaugings.
description-flow-record: NA
description-catchment: Natural peat based catchment on Millstone Grit. Lower parts of catchment steep while upper parts flatter.
description-flow-regime: Very responsive, natural regime. Natural to within 10% at the 95 percentile flow.

name: Greet at Southwell
description-summary: Crump profile Flat V weir on the Greet to monitor flows where the river crosses a geological boundary.
description-general: Crump profile Flat V (1:10) weir, 6m wide, in concrete 1:1 trapezoidal channel, straightened reach. Rough, inclined sides to about 2.5m. Installed to monitor flows where river crosses Sherwood/Mercia Sandstone to Mercia Mudstone boundary.
description-station-hydrometry: Drowned flow rating established by high flow gauging in June 2007, full period of record reprocessed.
description-flow-record: Short term rises and falls in flow due to upstream sluice gate operation.
description-catchment: Geology: predominantly Sherwood/Mercia Sandstone, with some Mercia Mudstone along southern border. Low relief, river channels lined with clay, sand and gravel alluvium, more extensive u/s. Rural, agricultural land use.
description-flow-regime: Natural regime with substantial groundwater component - but responsive to significant rainfall events.

name: Soar at Kegworth
description-summary: Ultrasonic gauge in a canalised reach of the River Soar, with substantially modified flow.
description-general: Ultrasonic multi-path gauge in a unidirectional arrangement. Rebuilt in 1991 (no data Jan and Feb 1991) to improve on accuracy of existing single-path gauge (1978-84). Replaced velocity-area site at Zouch. Cableway added in 2002. Upgraded during December 2006 and September 2020.
description-station-hydrometry: Reach at station is canalised part of Soar navigation, has low velocities and wide floodplain. Bypassing possible above bankfull (>1.17m). Two weirs and navigation lock 700m downstream are full range controls.
description-flow-record: The early record 1978 to 1984 is of doubtful quality due to the limitations and reliability of the single-path gauge. This ultrasonic gauge was removed in 1984 and no flows were produced.
description-catchment: Moderate to low relief. Geology: predominantly Mercia Mudstone with some sandstones in the west and Lias clays and l'sts in the east. Ancient hard rocks outcrop in Charnwood Forest. Majority of catchment overlain with Boulder Clay with sands and gravels within river valleys. Catchment contains Leicester and Loughborough. Agricultural land use.
description-flow-regime: Flows substantially modified by inputs from WRW along Soar valley.

name: Meece Brook at Shallowford
description-summary: A crump profile Flat V weir, which does suffer from some interference from groundwater pumping and sewage effluent.
description-general: Crump profile Flat V weir, 5m wide, 1:10 cross-slopes, with crest tapping. In 2016 the site has undergone silt clearance and eal pass and pre-barrage fish pass were installed.
description-station-hydrometry: Cableway is no longer in use - ADCP remote controlled gaugings carried out within measurement section and across adjacent floodplain on left bank during out of bank flows. In-channel weed growth is managed during the Summer months. Upstream railway bridge can cause skewed flow affecting gaugings across the flow range at times. Upstream right bank vegetation was cleared in 2024 to improve flow conditions.
description-flow-record: In 2016 during the conducted works, a gauge was installed at a nearby location, thus there are continuous measurements in the database.
description-catchment: Low relief, agricultural catchment, draining Sherwood S'st in the North-east headwaters, Mercia Mudstone elsewhere. Overlain by river terrace gravels and alluvium in valleys.
description-flow-regime: Backs up from d/s bridge. Interference from gw pumping and sewage effluent, net effect of reduction in runoff. Baseflow maintained by glacial valley gravel.

name: Tame at Lea Marston Lakes
description-summary: Unusual twin bay, chevron shaped Crump profile weirs discharging into an inline settlement lagoon - replaces Lea Marston (28004) in 1982.
description-general: Unusual twin bay, chevron shaped Crump profile weirs, 21.5m total width, discharging into an inline settlement lagoon. Replaced 28004 Lea Marston in 1982 (large scatter in gaugings at all levels), record combined. Weed booms were installed in 2001, 30m upstream of twin weirs but produced large head difference. Weed booms damaged/bent when hit by debris during medium/high flow and were replaced with automatic screens. These can produce pulses in flow when cleared and still have a slight head difference but not as bad as previous screens. Automatic screens removed in 2019.
description-station-hydrometry: The weirs are affected by drowning due to high levels in downstream lake, but this is only minor. Site is known to bypass at high levels, but this floodplain flow is taken into account in most recent rating. Two peak flow ratings applied across period of record, the most recent is valid from June-2001. Ratings fit gaugings well and account for bypassing.
description-flow-record: Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in October 2018 (WINFAP Files v7).
description-catchment: Substantially urbanised catchment containing Birmingham. Solid geology: Coal Measures group with sandstones in the west and Mercia Mudstone elsewhere. Catchment mostly overlain by extensive cover of Boulder Clay and glacial sand and gravel in equal proportion.
description-flow-regime: Substantial flow modification from large imports and urbanised areas.

name: Tame at Bescot
description-summary: An ultrasonic gauging station with trapezoidal flume.
description-general: Station opened 1989 to provide flow data for water resources, water quality monitoring and flood forecasting. Original flume never reached critical velocity since Tame dredging not carried out to anticipated depth. Ultrasonic installed in 2003 but appeared to be underestimating flows. Replaced with NivuFlow gauge in June 2020. Sensor racks located in same position as previous install, though with a slightly reduced transducer depth so as to minimise impacts of weed and debris accumulation.
description-station-hydrometry: Fully modular, has never been overtopped. Some trouble with left bank accretion, incised gauging section, and heavy undergrowth. Difficult to gauge higher flows the largest of which suggests rating underestimates flow. ADCP gaugings performed within ultrasonic section. In-channel weed growth immediately upstream of measurement section can cause the ultrasoinc to over-record.
description-flow-record: Low flow data possibly inaccurate, as at best only two paths are in the river. Routine maintenance helps combat silt and weed accumulation within the measurement section. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2023 (WINFAP Files v12). Flow data were corrected in 2026, with rating-derived values replaced by logged values. The current dataset therefore contains some differences compared to previously available records.
description-catchment: Almost entirely urbanised catchment just below confluence of upper Tame branches. Solid geology predominantly Coal Measures overlain by extensive Boulder Clay and sand and gravel.
description-flow-regime: Very responsive. Substantial imports from water reclamation work. Above 70 cumecs washland overspill upstream operates.

name: Soar at Littlethorpe
description-summary: Crump profile Flat V weir on the Soar. Records for the Soar were previously held under one site, Soar at Littlethorpe (28082), covering the period August 1971 to present. Starting from 2026, the records have been separated due to a large difference in catchment area between the sites. Records for Soar at Narborough (28051) begin in August 1971 and end in May 1984. Records for Soar at Littlethorpe (28082) start in April 1983 and continue to the present day.
description-general: Electromagnetic gauge record started in 1983, replaced with cross-correlation method from April 2018. Site is downstream of a flood relief channel, which joins on the right bank just upstream. Bypassed at high flows above 2.5mAOD. Banks raised just upstream of station in 1998 to keep flows in bank to a higher stage.
description-station-hydrometry: Channel prone to weed growth.
description-flow-record: Bypass flow added to discharge recorded by flow meter for full station history. Electromagnetic flow gauge data during low flows spikey especially during early 2000s due to ageing instrument. Missing data in early electromagnetic gauge record means first complete water year is 1986/87. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in August 2026 (WINFAP Files v15).
description-catchment: Predominantly agricultural catchment just south of Leicester. Geology predominantly Mercia Mudstones overlain by extensive Boulder Clay and glacial gravel cover. Significant river terraces and alluvium in lower reaches.
description-flow-regime: Substantial imports via WRW.

name: Trent at Darlaston
description-summary: Rated station gauging a relatively urban catchment near Stoke-on-Trent.
description-general: Time-of-flight ultrasonic installed at the site, however, peak flow data are from ratings.
description-station-hydrometry: Complex rating history owing to river re-grading (1965 and 1973). Multiple peak flow ratings, particularly since 2001. High flow precision limited by ungauged flow over the left bank. Much storage in valley gravels. A number of gaugings have been taken to assess out of bank flows; on 1/11/2000 gaugings taken at 3.216mASD showed floodplain flow to be 26% of the total flow of 252m3/s. Extreme high flow gaugings carried out across the floodplain and main river section in Burton-upon-Trent, from St. Peters Bridge using a remote controlled ADCP. In-channel weed growth at the station can affect low and medium flow gaugings. Rating under review due to deviation of gaugings and inconsistent POT distribution between 2021-2025.
description-flow-record: AMAX levels in water years 1985/86 and 1986/87 are suspect, but AMAX and daily mean flow magnitudes are consistent with analogue station 28040 upstream. Station undermined in 1987 flood, reconstructed 1990/1. In 2001-2002, gauge not performing v well. Transducers failing constantly, especially lower ones (due to silt). Problems in 2002-2003 with rubble in channel now creating skew flows and siltation. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in August 2025 (WINFAP Files v14). Flow data were corrected in 2026, with rating-derived values replaced by logged values. The current dataset therefore contains some differences compared to previously available records.
description-catchment: Moderate relief catchment, substantially urbanised with Stoke-on-Trent and Newcastle-under-Lyme. Geology mainly Coal Measures and Marls, Millstone Grit and subordinate Sherwood S'st, widely covered by Boulder Clay. Mining, industrial and mixed agricultural land use.
description-flow-regime: Quite responsive but flow regime dominated by Strongford WRW discharge (Stoke-on-Trent).

name: Derwent at St Mary's Bridge
description-summary: Ten-channel, interleaved cross path US gauge in the centre of Derby. Replaced Longbridge Weir (28010, 1935-1986) - combined record held at St Marys Bridge.
description-general: Ten-channel, interleaved cross path US gauge in the centre of Derby, 0.5km upstream of Longbridge Weir (28010) which it replaced. Opened in 1984, ultrasonic gauge reconfigured in March 1993. Record combined with 28010 (a long, curved broad-crested masonry weir with complex rating history, very insensitive).
description-station-hydrometry: Negligible bypassing. Two ratings shown are applied to Longbridge Weir record, the most recent valid from August 1970 when the weir was narrowed. Station is ultrasonic thereafter.
description-flow-record: Following statistical assessment of continuity, mean and peak flow record shown are a combination of 28010 (Longbridge Weir) to 1986, and St Marys Bridge thereafter; POT thresholds prior to merge were 105.667 and 69.256 cumecs respectively. Chart and UKCEH POT date ranges are for 28010. Some Longbridge AMAX events pre-1985 are of a smaller magnitude than daily mean flows as instantaneous data have been re-processed following rating review. Continuous 15-minute data are awaiting digitisation and re-processing. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2022 (WINFAP Files v11).
description-catchment: Large, predominantly upland catchment draining Millstone Grit and Carboniferous Limestone. Lower reaches drain Coal Measures on the Lb and Triassic sandstones and marls on the Rb. Peat moorland headwaters; forestry, pasture and some arable. Contains the towns of Matlock and Buxton.
description-flow-regime: Substantial flow modification owing to Derwent reservoirs, mill operations (particularly before 1970s), and PWS abstractions.

name: Sence at South Wigston
description-summary: LaserFlow Index Velocity gauge post-2017. Previously Electromagnetic gauge set in 1:1 formalised banks. Replaces Blaby (28054), daily flow records combined, but not peak flows.
description-general: LaserFlow ultrasonic gauge under Crow Mill bridge from 2017 onwards. Early record from electromagnetic flow gauge just downstream of bridge.
description-station-hydrometry: No bypassing - all flows contained. In 2002 the electromagnetic flows were out by 10% - a new coil/cable was installed in March 2002. Missing data July-December 2016 due to electromagnetic gauge failure. Gauge replaced with LaserFlow index velocity gauge in January 2017.
description-flow-record: Flow contained at high flows and fully measured. Early peak flow data are of poor quality, and are therefore rejected. Accuracy of electromagnetic gauge poor from 2006 until replacement in 2017. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in August 2025 (WINFAP Files v14).
description-catchment: Moderate to low relief catchment to East and South of Leicester. Mainly Lower Lias (mudstones and limestone) but wholly blanketed by Boulder Clay and alluvium except for headwaters. Urbanised downstream end, otherwise arable and grazing land use.
description-flow-regime: Moderately responsive. Substantially augmented by WRW discharges, particularly Wigston.

name: Tame at Perry Park
description-summary: Flume gauging station with a responsive flow regime.
description-general: Flume gauging station.
description-station-hydrometry: NA
description-flow-record: NA
description-catchment: Low-lying catchment with large urban component.
description-flow-regime: Responsive regime with significant artificial influences.

name: Ryton at Blyth
description-summary: Laserflow index velocity gauge post 2021. Previously electromagnetic station installed in March 1984. Replaced Serlby Park (28016).
description-general: Laserflow index velocity gauge operational from 29/03/2022, in a straight reach downstream of a gentle bend. Previously electromagnetic station installed in March 1984. Data transmitted to West Stockwith pumping station to control regime to the tidal Trent.
description-station-hydrometry: Extreme events overtop flood banks locally but no bypassing of gauge. New laser gauge provides reasonable quality data.
description-flow-record: Performance of the Laser flow gauge and the previous electromagnetic gauge is reasonable during full range. Heavy weed growth through the entire river causes backing up of levels during the summer. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in October 2018 (WINFAP Files v7).
description-catchment: Moderate and low relief catchment. Headwaters drain Magnesian Limestone; bulk underlain by Permian Marl and Sherwood Sandstone. Mainly Drift free. Apart from Worksop, wholly rural, mainly arable farming.
description-flow-regime: Deep, slow, baseflow dominated flow regime. Moderate net effect on flows by WRWs and abstraction.

name: Soar at Pillings Lock
description-summary: Multipath US gauge on the Soar Navigation Canal, subject to significant flow modification.
description-general: 12 cross path ultrasonic gauge set in Soar Navigation (merges with Grand Union Canal) 100m upstream of Pillings Lock. Low banks.
description-station-hydrometry: Raised water level for navigation is controlled by radial gate and flood relief channel 100 metres downstream of the gauge. Significant bypassing of the gauge on both banks at peak flows is included in the flow calculation through addition to ultrasonic gauge flow. Bypassing starts at 1.5m water level.
description-flow-record: Ultrasonic flow measurement since start of record in 1986.
description-catchment: Moderate to low relief catchment with Triassic Marls and S'st to the west and Lias clays and l'sts to the east, widely blanketed in Boulder Clay. Ancient hard rocks outcrop in Charnwood Forest. Lower catchment dominated by Leicester; headwaters rural.
description-flow-regime: Very substantial flow modification from WRW and reservoirs in Charnwood Forest.

name: Tame at Hopwas Bridge
description-summary: Velocity area station used primarily for water quality purposes - replaces 28005, Elford which was several km upstream. Very broad flood plain on both banks.
description-general: Velocity area station immediately downstream of Hopwas road bridge between training banks that contain the majority of high flows. Station used primarily for water quality purposes. Some bypassing, but accounted for in rating. Site replaces 28005, Elford which was several km upstream. Very broad flood plain on both banks.
description-station-hydrometry: Suffers from heavy weed growth which contributes to over-estimation of runoff requiring retrospective rating adjustments (not shown) - but all are based on the winter curve applied here as the majority of floods are in winter and flatten weeds. As a result of these weeds there is significant scatter in gaugings. Ratings revised in 2016. Three peak flow ratings across period of record. Gaugings carried out using remote controlled ADCP within the measurement section and adjacent floodplain area on the left bank.
description-flow-record: Magnitude of June and July 2007 flood events subject to considerable overestimation due to hydraulic conditions and increased channel and floodplain rugosity. Gaugings taken during events suggest peak flows of around 210 cumecs in June and 200 cumecs in July 2007. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in October 2018 (WINFAP Files v7) and in August 2024 (WINFAP Files v13). Pre-2000 data were added in the 24/25 annual update.
description-catchment: Catchment predominantly Mercia Mudstones with some shales and limestones. Overlain by Boulder Clay in the headwater with sands and gravels within the valleys. Mixed farming and urbanised catchment.
description-flow-regime: NA

name: Tame at Sheepwash
description-summary: Velocity area station used for flood warning purposes and a time of travel pollution assessment point. Key reservoir site.
description-general: Velocity area station commissioned in October 1985 to measure levels on the uppermost reaches of the River Tame in the Tipton and Oldbury area. River heads northwest from its source at Oldbury towards West Bromwich and the next flow station at Bescot. Gauge house replaced in July 2012 following vandalism in June 2010 (station closed between this period). Either side of the channel are two large balancing lakes which act as a flood storage area.
description-station-hydrometry: Channel is a uniform concrete flume with a trapezoidal cross-section. High level gaugings problematic due to rapid response times following heavy rainfall. The channel is generally silt free with no or very minimal weed growth.
description-flow-record: Station closed November 2020.
description-catchment: Heavy urbanised.
description-flow-regime: Flashy regime owing to the highly urbanised catchment and high levels of surface run-off.

name: Blythe at Whitacre
description-summary: Electromagnetic gauging station immediately upstream of confluence with the River Cole. Some data quality issues.
description-general: EM gauge immediately upstream of confluence with R. Cole. Owned by Severn-Trent plc, operated by NRA/EA until late 1996. Residual flow gauge for PWS abstraction for Shustoke Res. Channel approx 16m wide.
description-station-hydrometry: Widespread u/s inundation in flood, backs up from Tame and Cole.
description-flow-record: Data quality poor; numerous gaps in record.
description-catchment: Low relief catchment SE of Birmingham. Mercia Mudstone faulted against Coal Measures in extreme E. Predominantly cover of glacial sands and gravels and terrace gravels. Mainly rural with mixed farming but contains part of Solihull and Dorridge. All river u/s of gauge designated as SSSI.
description-flow-regime: Net effects of WRW and PWS modest but all the flow may be abstracted. Quite responsive.

name: Henmore Brook at Carsington Outflow
description-summary: Rectangular thin-plate weir measuring outflows from Carsington Water (used as storage in Derwent compensation scheme).
description-general: Rectangular thin-plate weir with a central notch and sides for large releases from Carsington Water.
description-station-hydrometry: NA
description-flow-record: NA
description-catchment: NA
description-flow-regime: NA

name: Sow at Walkmill
description-summary: V-notch weir opened in 2002. Some drops in flow due to upstream sluice gate. Station closed in July 2013.
description-general: V-notch weir. Site located 200m d/s of mill pool. Station closed in July 2013.
description-station-hydrometry: NA
description-flow-record: Drop in flow on 28/8/07 thought to be due to closure of sluice u/s of station. Analomous drop in flows during Sep and Oct 2011 due to sluice action.
description-catchment: Low relief, agricultural catchment. Predominately sandstone.
description-flow-regime: NA

name: Oldacre Brook at Brocton
description-summary: Two thin-plate V-notch weirs that measure Oldacre Brook, and one of it's small tributaries. Station closed in January 2013.
description-general: Two thin-plate V-notch weirs in one structure; the right measures Oldacre Brook, left a small tributary. Station closed in January 2013.
description-station-hydrometry: Structures suffer from heavy silting and debris, with both known to drown-out.
description-flow-record: NA
description-catchment: Small, rural, sandstone catchment. Drains western edge of Cannock Chase AONB and passes through Brocton Hall golf course.
description-flow-regime: NA

name: Churnet at Quixhill
description-summary: Triangular profile Flat Vee weir set within vertical wing walls, with brick gauge house and cableway opened in 1998.
description-general: Station was built in 1998 and is located on the late Joseph Cyril Bamford Estate (JCB) near the village of Rocester.
description-station-hydrometry: A Flat V triangular profile weir with vertical side walls provides a hydraulic control to measure discharge. Cableway no longer in use - remote controlled ADCP gaugings carried out. During out of bank flows in extreme flood events, alternative locations further upstream have to be used as the adjacent floodplain area is not measurable and the main river section unreachable.
description-flow-record: Complete period of record flow. Notable peak events in November 2000 and October 2019.
description-catchment: The River Churnet originates approximately 30km North of Quixhill gauging station on the Middle Hills (7km North East of Leek, Staffordshire). The river flows in a south-westerly direction where it flows into Tittesworth Reservoir. The River Churnet then continues in a southerly direction through Staffordshire.
description-flow-regime: The Churnet is generally baseflow dominated and can rise quite rapidly following heavy rainfall, owing to the upland nature of the catchment. It is a very silty river often with high sediment load except at the lowest of flows.

name: Erewash at Pinxton
description-summary: Informal weir rated section in the upper reaches of the Erewash.
description-general: Gauge in the upper reaches of the Erewash.
description-station-hydrometry: NA
description-flow-record: Some missing data between 2001 and 2002. Localised flooding prevents access for gaugings during recent extreme events, with extreme high flows beyond the limit of the rating curve. Treat with caution. Low flow section of rating improved in 2023 and historic flow data reprocessed.
description-catchment: Semi-urbanised catchment, draining agricultural land and coal mines.
description-flow-regime: NA

name: Maun at Mansfield the Dykes
description-summary: Crump profile Flat V weir that replaces (1996) 28059 Mansfield STW - closed in 1984.
description-general: Crump profile Flat V (1:10) weir, 4.8m wide, low vertical wingwalls set in wider channel. Lb at about 2m, Rb higher. Weir prone to u/s siltation - sand is mobile, especially under high flow conditions and is washed away in high events - results in variable levels and scatter in gaugings. Replaced 28059 Mansfield - old site was replaced due to drowning of the flume and accumulation of rubbish. Structure situated downstream of sewage works in Mansfield.
description-station-hydrometry: Flows are derived from the Flat-V Theoretical equation throughout the full flow range. Mobilisation of sand results in variable levels, scatter in gaugings. Difficult to gauge above 0.4mASD due to very flashy response; difficult to catch events. Structure becomes non-modular at high flows.
description-flow-record: Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2019 (WINFAP Files v8).
description-catchment: Moderate relief catchment near headwaters of Maun. Rises on Magnesian Limestone and crosses onto Sherwood S'st. Heavily urbanised with Mansfield and Sutton in Ashfield immediately u/s.
description-flow-regime: Urbanised catchment. Very responsive to rainfall, very rapid rise and fall in the hydrograph. Low flows dominated by sewage effluent and augmented by runoff from urban area that effectively increases catchment area. Very atypical water balance. Second rise in flood hydrograph often follows initial peak from urban runoff, as flows from the rural upper catchment move downstream.

name: Maun at Whitewater Bridge
description-summary: Time-of-flight ultrasonic flow gauge installed in Jan/Feb 2019 replacing measurement from Flat V Weir. Widespread subsidence in the area caused intermittent drowning of the weir between October 2015 and April 2019 for which a tailwater correction was applied to account for non-modularity.
description-general: Time of flight ultrasonic flow gauge post Jan 2019. Pre-2019 Flat V weir, 5.2m wide with 0.64m high wingwalls. Built to measure flows d/s of the Sherwood Sandstone aquifer and to complement gauge at Mansfield (28115) which measures flows u/s of aquifer. Weir drowned during June 2007 high flows, flows over wingwalls.
description-station-hydrometry: High flows during full period of record to be used with caution. No out of bank rating during period of weir or ultrasonic measurement. Out of bank flow occurs more frequently since 2015 due to widespread subsidence. Wingwalls raised for installation of the ultrasonic sensors with bypassing occuring below top transducer level.
description-flow-record: Record from 1997-present.
description-catchment: Geology predominantly Sherwood Sandstone with Limestone in the west and Mercia Mudstone to the east. Little Drift cover. Contains urban areas of Mansfield and Sutton in Ashfield. Mixed land use of arable and woodland.
description-flow-regime: The Maun is influent in the Sherwood Sandstone reaches; low flows can decline below those at 28115.

name: Derwent at Whatstandwell
description-summary: Large Flat V weir on the Derwent, built to provide flow information for the Ambergate/Carsington intake. Flows substantially affected by Derwent reservoirs. Fish pass added in 2014.
description-general: 25 metre wide Flat-V crump profile weir with bypass Larinier Fish Pass. Upstream of A6 road bridge. Level measurement from separate stilling wells on weir and fish pass. Theoretical flow calculation from fish pass channel added to weir flow calculation, increases channel capacity. Station built to provide accurate flow information upstream of Ambergate/Carsington intake point.
description-station-hydrometry: NA
description-flow-record: Period of record 1997-present.
description-catchment: Responsive upland catchment, peat covered moorlands in headwaters. Main Derwent drains the Millstone Grit; the largest tributary, the Wye, drains Carboniferous L'st. Land use mainly pasture and forestry.
description-flow-regime: Flows substantially affected by Derwent reservoirs.

name: Meden at Perlethorpe
description-summary: Cross-correlation gauge on the Meden to measure flows downstream of the Sherwood Sandstone.
description-general: Replacing d/s station (28045). Data from cross-correlation gauge commences in 2019. Prior measurement from Flat V weir with 1:10 cross slopes, Crump profile, 5.2m wide, wing walls at 0.64m.
description-station-hydrometry: NA
description-flow-record: No daily flow data available July 2013 - September 2016 due to subsidence of the weir. Flows from October 2016 onwards are calculated through a new rating and from February 2019 onwards from the cross-correlation gauge. June 2007 high flows were over the wingwalls of the structure.
description-catchment: Moderate to low relief catchment underlain by the Notts coalfield. The Maun rises on generally sandy facies of the Magnesian Lst, crosses onto Sherwood Sst, the gauge sited close to the junction with the Mercia Mudst. Upper catchment dominated by urban centres (Mansfield) and mining spoil; middle and lower reaches rural and forest.
description-flow-regime: Subdued response with WRW effluent augmenting low flows.

name: Waithe Beck at Brigsley
description-summary: Structure is able to contain all flows, gauging a rural, predominantly Chalk, catchment with significant artificial influences.
description-general: Broad trapezoidal flume (1.83m wide at base) with theoretical rating confirmed to 0.9 cumecs. All recorded flows have been contained within the structure.
description-station-hydrometry: One theoretical peak flow rating applied across period of record.
description-flow-record: Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in October 2018 (WINFAP Files v7) and in August 2026 (WINFAP Files v15).
description-catchment: Predominantly Chalk catchment with rural (mainly arable) land use.
description-flow-regime: Groundwater abstraction near Grimsby and irrigation abstractions have significant effect on low flows. Also abstractions for PWS and industry. Runoff increased by effluent returns.

name: Great Eau at Claythorpe Mill
description-summary: Compound structure gauging a rural, predominantly Chalk catchment with some artificial influences.
description-general: Simple low flow Crump profile weir 3.073m wide with flanking broad-crest sections. Total width 9.687m.
description-station-hydrometry: A cableway at Abby Bridge was used to gauge flows in the early 1970's. Both components are theoretically rated with rating valid to 6.976 cumecs, flows above this limit are missing. One rating applied across period of record.
description-flow-record: Flows to May 1973 suspect due to error in gauged head and rounding of crest during cleaning. Flows above the rating limit are missing e.g. 25/06/2007. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in October 2018 (WINFAP Files v7) and in August 2026 (WINFAP Files v15).
description-catchment: Predominantly Chalk catchment with around one third of catchment covered with superficial deposits (Boulder Clay, sands and gravels and alluvium - gravel beds of glacial origin are found at Aby, South Thoresby, Thetford, South Ormsby and Brinkhill. Deposits of beach gravels on the edge of Chalk cut through the Chalk and a line of springs are formed which contribute a high baseflow to the Eau. Land use is predominantly rural. Rural, predominantly arable land.
description-flow-regime: Runoff influenced by gw abstraction/recharge. Small amounts of abstraction for irrigation in summer.

name: Lud at Louth
description-summary: Station located in an urban area but gauging a predominantly rural, Chalk catchment with some artificial influences.
