description-general: Crump profile weir, 4.569m wide, at u/s end of long culvert (capacity limited to 20 cumecs - yet to be exceeded). Flows recorded 1966-1968 at sharp-crested weir at Bridge Street. Charted data started at Tathwell Nov 1968, and South Elkington Mar-Nov 1968.
description-station-hydrometry: Two ratings applied across period of record, the most recent is valid from January-1968 when theoretical rating applied. Theoretical rating supported by current metering, but gaugings needed to confirm at high flows.
description-flow-record: Flood of 1920 estimated at approx. 140 cumecs. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2019 (WINFAP Files v8).
description-catchment: Catchment is predominantly Chalk, with around one third covered with superficial deposits, mainly Boulder Clay. Largely rural catchment with mainly arable farming, although there is urban development (Louth) just upstream of station.
description-flow-regime: Groundwater abstraction has a modest impact on flows; mill regulation can also produce short-term artificial spikes. Work is underway to construct two retention ponds on the Lud.

name: Ancholme at Bishopbridge
description-summary: Compound structure, with major artificial influences.
description-general: Compound Crump profile weir, with central crest 2.448m wide and total width of 9.131m.
description-station-hydrometry: Structure drowns in high flows and is affected by weed growth in summer. Gauging at 0.73m (4.96 cumecs) is thought to be unreliable. Theoretical rating confirmed to 5.5 cumecs (0.6m). One rating applied across period of record.
description-flow-record: POTs at this site had to be adjusted to account for datum correction. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2019 (WINFAP Files v8).
description-catchment: Flat low-lying catchment. Geology: clay and Lincolnshire limestone, significant cover of superficial deposits - mainly Boulder Clay and confined to eastern half of catchment. Rural, predominantly arable land.
description-flow-regime: Regime influenced by gw abstraction/recharge. Flows are very heavily augmented in summer from Trent-Witham-Ancholme transfer scheme. Reservoir(s) in catchment affect runoff.

name: Rase at Bishopbridge
description-summary: Structure gauging upper, more natural, parts of catchment.
description-general: Crump profile weir (crest length 3.658m). Removed from peak flows dataset in September 2020 (WINFAP Files v9).
description-station-hydrometry: Station drowns above about 9 cumecs, and relationship between u/s and d/s levels depends on weed growth and the disposition of sluices and gates at Harlam Weir 3.5km d/s. Data removed from peak flow dataset due to significant scatter in gaugings and two flood-storage reservoirs impacting flows above QMED. Theoretical calibration. One rating applied across period of record.
description-flow-record: Missing daily flow for June 2019 event as stage exceeded rating.
description-catchment: Upper parts of the catchment elevated, highest point around 150mASL (Lincolnshire Wolds), but most of the catchment is flat and low lying. Predominantly clay, over half of the catchment is covered with superficial deposits of blown sand and Boulder Clay. Predominantly rural catchment, mixed arable and pasture.
description-flow-regime: Abstractions for PWS in the upper reaches has some effect on summer low flows. Some effluent returns. Missing data in recent years due to stage exceeding upper limit of the rating.

name: Ancholme at Toft Newton
description-summary: Flat V weir immediately u/s of entry point of flows from a reservoir.
description-general: Flat V weir (3.03m wide). The station is immediately u/s of entry point of flows from Toft Newton reservoir.
description-station-hydrometry: There is no drowning or bypassing. Theoretical calibration, confirmed by check gaugings. Rating expected to be modular up to bank full but gauging at 0.4m introduces some uncertainty. Theoretical rating applied across period of record.
description-flow-record: POT has been corrected to zero stage - was previously offset by 1m. Site inoperative due to vandalism 10/04/2002-05/01/2003. Low flows in May 2003 are suspect. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2019 (WINFAP Files v8).
description-catchment: Flat, low-lying catchment, with elevated upper part, developed on Lincolnshire limestone and clays, with some Boulder Clay cover in eastern half. Predominantly rural, mainly arable land.
description-flow-regime: No major abstractions or returns.

name: Witham at Claypole Mill
description-summary: Gauging a predominantly rural catchment with mixed geology and substantial artificial influences.
description-general: An old three level weir, total width of 24.99m converted to a standard broad-crested Lea design.
description-station-hydrometry: No bypassing or drowning. Fairly insensitive but range and gauge quality good. Rated by current meter. Scatter in gaugings evident. One rating applied across period of record.
description-flow-record: Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in October 2018 (WINFAP Files v7) and in August 2026 (WINFAP Files v15).
description-catchment: The catchment is about half clay and half limestone, mainly clay d/s of Grantham. Some superficial deposits of Boulder Clay in headwaters and gravel terrace deposits in valleys. Some drainage from the Lincolnshire Limestone in the form of springs. Other springs have been found to emanate from gravel beds perched on the Lias Clays. Largely rural, although Grantham is within the catchment.
description-flow-regime: Substantial modification of low flows by transfer to Rutland Water and PWS at Saltersford; >50% of low flows may be abstracted representing between 10 and 30% of average flow. Some effluent returns.

name: Barlings Eau at Langworth Bridge
description-summary: Several gauging structures have been used at this site, gauging a rural catchment with mixed geology and some artificial influences.
description-general: Ultrasonic gauge, commissioned 09/03/1999. Originally a natural section until Nov 1965, replaced by a low flow compound Crump profile weir, which ceased operating in Sept 1978 and was replaced by a flat V weir in June 1980.
description-station-hydrometry: Cableway in early 1970s used for gauging the station rating. The structure operating since June 1980 has the theoretical rating confirmed by check gaugings. Structure drowns at about 19 cumecs.
description-flow-record: NA
description-catchment: Flat catchment. Mixed geology, with significant superficial deposits, predominantly Boulder Clay. Predominantly rural but with some new urban development.
description-flow-regime: Runoff influenced by gw abstraction/recharge. Runoff reduced by industrial/agricultural abstraction. Irrigation abstractions reduce summer low flows.

name: Bain at Fulsby Lock
description-summary: Gauging a rural catchment with mixed geology located in the Lincolnshire Wolds, with modest artificial influences.
description-general: Broad-crested weir 4.6m wide situated in old lock; rated by model tests. Small bypass channel u/s feeds original river course and a disused model flume (wall ht=1.136m), gauged by sharp-crested weir.
description-station-hydrometry: Rating derived from model tests. One rating applied across period of record.
description-flow-record: Flows over bypass not processed since 1981 and subsequent low flows therefore underestimated however peak flows will not be significantly affected. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2019 (WINFAP Files v8).
description-catchment: Catchment is mainly Chalk and clay, with sandstone in the headwaters, largely overlain by superficial deposits (predominantly Boulder Clay, with alluvium and sands and gravels along valley bottom). Rural catchment, predominantly arable land.
description-flow-regime: Revesby Reservoir has a very minor influence, and abstractions for irrigation may be significant in summer months.

name: Lymn at Partney Mill
description-summary: Crump weir gauging a rural catchment with mixed geology located in Lincolnshire Wolds, with minor artificial influences.
description-general: Crump weir with 5m crest.
description-station-hydrometry: The weir is probably non-modular at very high flows due to backing up behind struts and a bridge, but is bypassed just before this point. Rated by model tests and confirmed by check gaugings to highest gauging of 0.6m. One rating applied across period of record.
description-flow-record: Station was bypassed in Oct 1993. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in October 2018 (WINFAP Files v7) and in August 2026 (WINFAP Files v15).
description-catchment: Catchment with mixed permeability bedrock geology and some superficial deposits. Wholly rural, predominantly arable land use.
description-flow-regime: Abstraction for irrigation in upper reaches and some abstraction for PWS may have effect on low flows in summer.

name: Witham at Saltersford Total
description-summary: Compound structure gauging a rural catchment u/s of Grantham, mixed geology and significant artificial influences.
description-general: Compound weir with round-crested low flow weir, 1.83m wide, and broad-crested high flow portion, 8.25m wide. The Measuring Authority recorded these structures separately until 1985.
description-station-hydrometry: Discharge computed from a single stage recorder to 1973, when it was discovered that a trout screen diverted flow over high flow weir. Second recorder installed, which was removed in Feb 1985 when trout screen was removed. One rating applied across period of record.
description-flow-record: Data prior to 1973 should not be used; data from 1973 to 1985 calculated from addition of high & low flow weir. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2020 (WINFAP Files v9).
description-catchment: Flat catchment, underlain by limestone and clay with about quarter of the area covered with Boulder Clay on east margin and in south. Predominantly rural.
description-flow-regime: Runoff influenced by groundwater abstraction/recharge. Major abstractions for PWS immediately u/s, with significant effect on low flows.

name: Slea at Leasingham Mill
description-summary: Rectangular thin plate weir gauging a predominantly rural catchment with gw-dominated regime and very low or zero summer/autumn flows. Significant artificial influences.
description-general: Rectangular thin-plate weir 1.372m wide set in old gate site, modified in 1984.
description-station-hydrometry: Weir does not drown - modular limit pre weir 3 cumecs and post weir 12 cumecs. Theoretical rating, with section above thin-plate treated as broad-crested weir. Gaugings taken at footbridge in Sleaford (below Carre Lane). Two peak flow ratings applied across period of record, pre- and post- modification of the weir, with post-1984 rating accounting for bypass flow.
description-flow-record: Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2022 (WINFAP Files v11).
description-catchment: Predominantly l'st with some superficial deposits including river terrace deposits (sand and gravel) in valley. Rural catchment, mixed agriculture, some urban development in lower catchment u/s of station.
description-flow-regime: Unresponsive, gw-dominated catchment with intermittent flow regime. Runoff influenced by groundwater abstraction/recharge, including abstraction for industry, and agriculture. Groundwater abstraction has potential for reducing summer low flows. Limestone spring flow rises and falls rapidly depending on groundwater level.

name: Bain at Goulceby Bridge
description-summary: Crump weir gauging a rural catchment with mixed geology, located in the Lincolnshire Wolds.
description-general: Free-fall drop under bridge calibrated by c/m until Dec 1969 and standard full-range Crump profile weir (crest length 4.877m) since Aug 1971 (no records between).
description-station-hydrometry: Three ratings applied across period of record, the first pre-weir, the second valid from 1971 when Crump installed, the third from 1979 following rating review.
description-flow-record: Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2023 (WINFAP Files v12).
description-catchment: Catchment on the scarp slope of the Lincolnshire Wolds. Underlain by Chalk and s'st with more than half of the catchment covered with superficial deposits, mainly Boulder Clay and some sands and gravels. Rural catchment, predominantly arable farming.
description-flow-regime: Regime influenced by gw abstraction/recharge. Abstraction for irrigation could have significant effect on low flows in dry summers. Reservoir(s) in catchment affect runoff.

name: Stainfield Beck at Cream Poke Farm
description-summary: Gauging a predominantly rural catchment with upper part located in the Lincolnshire Wolds, minimal artificial influences.
description-general: Before 1998, compound Crump profile weir with (non-processed) crest tapping which became non-modular above about 2 cumec (stage 0.42m) leading to uncertainty in high flows. Central weir 1.225m wide, total width 5.791m. Divide piers lowered in 1986 to stop debris entrapment. Replaced by 8m wide Flat V with crest tapping.
description-station-hydrometry: Use mainframe rating up to maximum rating limit, no out of bank rating available.
description-flow-record: Missing data from 12/1997-10/1998 due to construction of new weir during this period. Peak flow on 25/04/1981-26/04/1981 not available as station non-modular, stage peaked at 1.61m.
description-catchment: Upper part of the catchment located in Lincolnshire Wolds but lower part near the station is flat and low lying. Underlain by Kimmeridge Clay. Extensive superficial deposits, mainly Boulder Clay, blown sand and alluvium. Rural, mixed farming with minor urban development along river valley u/s of station.
description-flow-regime: No major abstractions or returns.

name: Heighington Beck at Heighington
description-summary: Crump weir gauging a slow responding limestone catchment with significant artificial influences during summer.
description-general: Crump profile weir 3.51m wide.
description-station-hydrometry: Theoretical calibration but drowning expected at high flows. One rating applied across period of record.
description-flow-record: Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2019 (WINFAP Files v8).
description-catchment: Permeable geology - almost entirely limestone, with minimal superficial deposits. Predominantly rural, mixed farming but with some urban development.
description-flow-regime: Very slow responding. Summer low flows may be heavily influenced by gw abstraction for irrigation.

name: Pointon Lode at Pointon
description-summary: Crump weir gauging a rural, limestone catchment with minor artificial influences.
description-general: British Standard Crump profile weir 2.445m wide, 2.667mAOD, at centre section. Raised walls at Crump weir sides, level 3.426mAOD, with flat concrete surface between each wall and channel bank 1.53m wide.
description-station-hydrometry: When upstream level higher than Crump walls, whole structure acts as non-standard compound weir. Known to drown at high flows. No high flow gaugings are available and so higher flows should be treated with caution. Post-2012 flows above 5.5 m3/s are missing due to rating set up at site. Theoretical calibration. One rating applied across period of record.
description-flow-record: GDF POR maximum listed as 5.69 cumecs in Jan 1998. Maximum peak flow of 12.9 cumecs registered in Jul 2001. This was undoubtedly a large event caused by >80mm rainfall, but considerable uncertainty surrounds the magnitude owing to extrapolation. Unusual pattern of flows in Apr 2007 thought to be due to accretion and weir cleaning. Some anomalous recessions in e.g. 1994, 1998, 1999, the reason for which is unknown. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2019 (WINFAP Files v8).
description-catchment: Drainage channel in low lying area draining highland limestone, largely covered with Boulder Clay. Rural catchment with mixed farming and, mainly in upper catchment, significant woodland. Catchment area is 11.05 sq km in 1972 ref, 11.9 sq km in NRFA.
description-flow-regime: Abstractions for irrigation have minor effect on summer low flows (e.g. August 2017).

name: Cringle Brook at Stoke Rochford
description-summary: Structure in a tunnel under A1 gauging a rural, near-natural catchment with mixed geology. Removed from Peak Flows Dataset in September 2022 (WINFAP Files v11).
description-general: Sharp-crested weir 2.74m wide in tunnel under A1.
description-station-hydrometry: Weir drowns above about 0.25 cumecs, but flows depend on position of weirs and sluices immediately d/s. Rating includes an allowance for drowning using assumed positions of d/s weirs and sluices. Two ratings accross period of record.
description-flow-record: Exceptionally low flows in Oct 1990 are suspect. No flow data were recorded from February 2024 to November 2024 due to a communications problem which could not be fixed, as access was restricted due to the bridge being condemned.
description-catchment: Catchment underlain by Oolitic L'st and Lias Clay. Rural, land use is mixed farming.
description-flow-regime: No artificial influences. Natural to within 10% at the Q95. Major supply abstraction point d/s of station. Major supply abstraction point d/s of station.

name: Witham at Colsterworth
description-summary: Gauging a rural catchment underlain by limestone, heavy artificial augmentation of flows until 1985.
description-general: Flat V weir 4.996m wide. Removed from peak flows dataset in September 2023 (WINFAP Files v12).
description-station-hydrometry: Theoretical calibration.
description-flow-record: Low flows in summer 1994 are suspect.
description-catchment: Rural catchment underlain by l'st and with some Boulder Clay cover.
description-flow-regime: Summer flows very heavily augmented by transfers from Rutland Water until Jun 1985, when direct Rutland/Saltersford pipeline opened.

name: Honington Beck at Honington
description-summary: Gauge on the Honington Beck, a tributary of the Witham. Suitable for low flows only.
description-general: NA
description-station-hydrometry: Station suffers from siltation.
description-flow-record: Data from 1984-present. Missing data June 1992-Dec 1995.
description-catchment: Small rural catchment draining into the River Witham.
description-flow-regime: NA

name: Brant at Brant Broughton
description-summary: Crump profile Flat V weir gauge on the Brant.
description-general: Crump profile Flat V (1:10) weir, 6m wide, set in vertical wingwalls 1.5m high. U/s and sidewall tappings for non-modular flow estimation (not used). Channel u/s formed by training banks circa 1m higher than walls.
description-station-hydrometry: NA
description-flow-record: 1991-present. Patchy record 1994-1995.
description-catchment: Low relief catchment to W of Lincoln Edge. Geology: Lower Lias clays and subordinant l'sts with some Middle Lias on eastern watershed. Over 20% cover by broad band of river terrace sands and gravels, which forms much of western catchment. Rural catchment, with predominantly arable land use.
description-flow-regime: NA

name: Eye Brook at Eye Brook Reservoir
description-summary: Crump weir gauge on the Eye Brook, d/s of reservoir supplying Corby Steelworks.
description-general: Crump weir with 10.89m crest replaced broad-crested weir with central rectangular notch in 1957. Small Crump weir for compensation flows. Originally operated by Corby and District Water Co. Immediately d/s of reservoir built to supply water to Corby Steelworks.
description-station-hydrometry: NA
description-flow-record: 1938-1999. Very patchy. Records also kept of reservoir levels.
description-catchment: Mostly clay with some sand and gravel. Catchment is largely rural. Surface area of reservoir constitutes about 3% of catchment.
description-flow-regime: Water from reservoir lost to catchment but licensed abstractions have been halved since 1980.

name: Glen at Kates Br & King St Br
description-summary: Compound structures gauging the total flow of the river Glen from a rural catchment with mixed geology and significant artificial influences.
description-general: Compound structure site. Kates Bridge was originally a broad-crested weir, replaced in Nov 1971 by Flat V weir, 9.7m wide, Ultrasonic gauge for high flows installed in 1999. Combined with standing-wave flume at King Street. Ultrasonic measurement closed in February 2013.
description-station-hydrometry: All recorded flows within modular limits. During flood periods, some flow is diverted from the Glen down the Greatford Cut, which is measured at King Street. The diversion is about 4 km upstream from Kates Bridge on the Glen.
description-flow-record: Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2020 (WINFAP Files v9).
description-catchment: Mixed geology of clay and limestone in headwaters. Significant superficial deposits, mainly Boulder Clay. Rural catchment, mixed agricultural land use with some woodland. Glen becomes a Fenland river below the gauging stations, and is a losing stream in its upper reaches. Digital catchment created from separate DTM-derived catchments for compound structure sites.
description-flow-regime: The Glen is influent in upper reaches. Low flows reduced by irrigation abstractions, influenced by pumping from gravel works and groundwater abstraction outside the catchment. Flows also affected by Gwash-Glen transfer scheme since 1989.

name: Welland at Tallington Total
description-summary: Compound site of three parts, gauging a predominantly rural catchment with mixed geology, with significant artificial influences including the Rutland water reservoir, record post 1994 are for indicative purposes only.
description-general: Compound site. Flows measured over broad-crested weir (total width 28.35m) on main River Welland/Maxey Cutand, two Crump profile weirs (both with 6.1m crest length) on West Deeping, plus flow into Tallington stream and Lolham Mill stream. Total flow is sum of three records - Lolham, West Deeping, and Tallington.
description-station-hydrometry: Weir at Lolham drowns in summer due to weeds, and true flows estimated. New improved theoretical rating developed to account for new Larinier fish pass channel (0.6m wide) installed in December 2014.
description-flow-record: Post-1994 flow record contains many gaps and anomalous sequences and should be used for indicative purposes only, particularly at low flows. 10 days missing in March-April 2018 due to new huts at Lolham and West Deeping. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in August 2024 (WINFAP Files v13).
description-catchment: Site is at a place where river becomes Fenland river. Largely clay, with some Boulder Clay cover. Rural catchment, mixed farming, some urban development u/s of station.
description-flow-regime: About 11% of the catchment area drains into Rutland Water construction on Gwash (drinking water reservoir) opened in 1976. Significant quantities of water also abstracted u/s for transmission to Rutland Water with significant effect on low flows. Abstraction in catchment also for PWS, industry and agriculture. Runoff increased by effluent returns.

name: Welland at Tixover
description-summary: Station measuring peak flows from a rural catchment with mixed geology and some artificial influences.
description-general: Rated VA station with cableway. A Crump weir at Barrowden upstream measures the low flow range up to 4.3 cumecs, with Tixover used above this.
description-station-hydrometry: Sluices at Doddington downstream affect flow below 11.33 cumecs, but are always open during high floods. Channel works as part of the Stamford to Market Harborough improvement scheme in 1971 affected the rating at Tixover - hence new rating from 01/10/1971. Two ratings applied across period of record, the most recent is valid from 01/10/1971 after channel works were conducted. Both ratings assume gates fully open at Doddington.
description-flow-record: Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in August 2024 (WINFAP Files v13).
description-catchment: Geology mixed, predominantly very low permeability, mostly covered with Boulder Clay. Land use mainly rural.
description-flow-regime: Abstraction upstream at Eye Brook Reservoir.

name: Gwash at Belmesthorpe
description-summary: Crump weir gauging a predominantly rural catchment with flow largely affected by the Rutland Water reservoir that began filling in 1975. Removed from Peak Flow Dataset in September 2022 (WINFAP Files v11).
description-general: Crump profile weir (crest length 8.5m).
description-station-hydrometry: No drowning problems, designed to be modular throughout range. Has been suggested that flow estimates are less reliable above 0.4m stage, but no gaugings to confirm either way. Theoretical Crump formula rating used for the whole POR.
description-flow-record: The presented POT data include only the pre-reservoir period.
description-catchment: Clay and limestone, Boulder Clay covers about a third of the catchment. Predominantly rural catchment with mixed farming, but dominated by reservoir.
description-flow-regime: Station is 13 km downstream of Rutland Water, which began filling in February 1975. Flows since 1975 are dominated by this reservoir. Flows also affected by Gwash-Glen transfer scheme, and PWS abstraction. Station is also downstream of Ryhall pumping station.

name: Welland at Barrowden
description-summary: Crump weir gauge on the Welland. High flows bypass weir.
description-general: Crump weir 3.04m wide measures flows to 4.2 cumecs. Flow record from 1996 subject to truncation when flows exceed this limit. High flows measured at Tixover (31005).
description-station-hydrometry: Higher flows bypass weir via syphon and are measured d/s at Tixover (31005). Tixover is a rated section about 18m wide with rating depending on position of d/s sluices: assumed open in floods. Very high Tixover flows possibly influenced by overbank spillage u/s.
description-flow-record: Period-of-record maximum flow of 107.8 cumecs recorded in March 1975, but the flood record is not homogeneous owing to changes post-1997. Missing data in 2017 due to fish pass construction.
description-catchment: Geology is mostly l'st overlain by 30% Boulder Clay and alluvium. Rural catchment with mixed farming.
description-flow-regime: Eye brook reservoir has little influence, but low flows reduced by abstractions.

name: East Glen at Manthorpe
description-summary: Flat V weir gauge on the East Glen. High and low flows are unreliable.
description-general: Flat V weir replaced simple Crump profile weir in Mar 1973. Low flows only.
description-station-hydrometry: Low flows often below lower limit of rating curve. Many high flows are truncated or missing, which means the mean runoff is unrepresentative.
description-flow-record: Large amounts of missing data. Missing daily flow for June 2019 event as stage exceeded rating. Flows are truncated at 3.783 m3/s, resulting in missing or censored data above this limit.
description-catchment: Predominantly agricultural catchment east of Grantham.
description-flow-regime: Missing data in recent years due to stage exceeding upper limit of the rating.

name: West Glen at Shillingthorpe
description-summary: Simple Crump profile weir and multipath US gauge on the West Glen. Issues with truncation of high flows.
description-general: Simple Crump profile weir, crest 1.83m broad. Rated up to 0.49m (3.0 cumecs - flows truncated, hence not a full range station). Multi-path, cross configuration ultrasonic gauge installed to measure high flows from 2000, although truncation problem persists in recent flow record.
description-station-hydrometry: Truncated and missing flows make for an unrepresentative annual runoff.
description-flow-record: Data from 1971-present. Missing data for 1992-1994.
description-catchment: Predominantly agricultural catchment draining area east of the A1 between Grantham and Stamford.
description-flow-regime: Flow regime affected by the Gwash-Glen transfer scheme. Missing data in recent years due to stage exceeding upper limit of the rating.

name: Chater at Fosters Bridge
description-summary: Compound Crump gauging a rural, near-natural catchment with minimal artificial influences and with mixed geology.
description-general: Compound Crump profile weir. Central weir 1.054m wide, total width 6.077m.
description-station-hydrometry: Not drowned but possibly bypassed in very extreme floods. Theoretical rating applied across period of record.
description-flow-record: Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2020 (WINFAP Files v9).
description-catchment: Geology mixed, predominantly clay but contains also limestone and sandstone. Some Boulder Clay cover. Rural catchment with mixed farming, some woodland in lower catchment.
description-flow-regime: No major abstractions or returns - natural to within 10% at Q95.

name: West Glen at Burton Coggles
description-summary: Flat V weir on the upper reaches of the West Glen.
description-general: Flat V weir replaced simple Crump profile weir in 1973.
description-station-hydrometry: NA
description-flow-record: Missing daily flow for June 2019 event as stage exceeded rating.
description-catchment: Upper reaches of the West Glen south of Grantham. Predominantly agricultural land.
description-flow-regime: NA

name: East Glen at Irnham
description-summary: Flat V weir gauge on the East Glen. Low flows only.
description-general: Flat V weir replaced simple Crump profile weir in Nov 1977.
description-station-hydrometry: Low flows only. Many high flows truncated or missing, which means that mean runoff is unrepresentative.
description-flow-record: Missing data in 1976 and 1977. Missing daily flow for June 2019 event as stage exceeded rating.
description-catchment: N-S trending catchment of subdued relief. Mixed geology: Upper Jurassic Oxford Clay in lower catchment overlying Cornbrash and Oolite Series of Mid Jurassic. Around 30% Boulder Clay cover. Rural, predominantly arable land use.
description-flow-regime: Missing data in recent years due to stage exceeding upper limit of the rating.

name: North Brook at Empingham
description-summary: Simple crump weir on the North Brook. Unsuitable for high flows.
description-general: Simple Crump profile weir, crest 2.36m broad. Rated up to 0.584m (2.503 cumecs) but unsuitable for high flows.
description-station-hydrometry: NA
description-flow-record: NA
description-catchment: Geology: Lincolnshire Limestone, Boulder Clay on highest ground. Rural catchment of mixed farming, with small wooded areas.
description-flow-regime: Catchment contains two artificial lakes.

name: Welland at Ashley
description-summary: Gauging a predominantly rural catchment with low permeability and with some artificial influences.
description-general: Crump profile weir in realigned channel beneath bridge. Weir has crest length of 6.97m. Original prebarrage and drop off weirs removed in 2013. Replaced by broad-crested weir 8.7m downstream of gauging weir, with rock prebarrage 3m further downstream. Removed from peak flows dataset in September 2020 (WINFAP Files v9).
description-station-hydrometry: Flows above 22 cumecs - including all floods - influenced by bridge soffit and are therefore unreliable - removed from peak flow dataset due to this truncation. Weir is theoretically calibrated to wing wall height with rated section above. Theoretical rating applied to wing wall height across period of record.
description-flow-record: NA
description-catchment: Catchment developed on low permeability bedrock geology with significant superficial deposits, mainly Boulder Clay. Rural catchment with mixed farming; Market Harborough is in upper catchment.
description-flow-regime: Abstractions for irrigation, and reservoir for maintenance of canal flow. Some effluent returns. Missing data in recent years due to stage exceeding upper limit of the rating.

name: Jordan at Market Harborough
description-summary: Simple Crump profile weir gauge on the Jordan. Low flows only.
description-general: Simple Crump profile weir, crest 1.47m broad. Rated up to 0.354m (0.673 cumecs).
description-station-hydrometry: Low flows only. Most high flows are truncated or missing, leading to unrepresentative mean runoff.
description-flow-record: Data available 1970-present. Missing data 05/1992-01/1995.
description-catchment: Low permeability bedrock geology, with 50% superficial deposits, mainly Boulder Clay. Rural catchment with mixed farming.
description-flow-regime: Missing data in recent years due to stage exceeding upper limit of the rating.

name: West Glen at Easton Wood
description-summary: Ephemeral site installed to gauge a small rural catchment as part of study into recharge of Lincolnshire Limestone.
description-general: Flat V weir with crest length of 8.05m. Installed as part of study into recharge of Lincolnshire L'st.
description-station-hydrometry: There is a 90 degree bend in the channel immediately d/s of the crest. Theoretically rated to 10.7 cumecs. No out of bank flow rating. One peak flow rating across period of record.
description-flow-record: Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in August 2024 (WINFAP Files v13).
description-catchment: Small catchment entirely on Boulder Clay: flows disappear into l'st d/s of gauging station. Rural catchment, mixed farming with significant woodland component.
description-flow-regime: Ephemeral regime. Natural to within 10% at Q95. No abstractions or returns.

name: Holywell Brook at Holywell
description-summary: Crump weir on the Holywell Brook.
description-general: Crump weir, 2.498m wide. Calibrated up to around 1.8 cumecs only.
description-station-hydrometry: NA
description-flow-record: Missing data 12/1990-01/1995. Missing daily flow for June 2019 event as stage exceeded rating.
description-catchment: A rural catchment (some woodland) developed mainly on Jurassic l'st - with some superficial deposits.
description-flow-regime: Baseflow dominated flow regime. Missing data in recent years due to stage exceeding upper limit of the rating.

name: Gwash South Arm at Manton
description-summary: Measuring inflows into Rutland Water reservoir from a rural catchment, station affected by bypassing, weed-growth and siltation.
description-general: Flat V weir (crest length 5m) measuring inflows to Rutland Water.
description-station-hydrometry: Weir bypassed at high flows. Some effect of weed and silt. HR Wallingford report suggests modular to around 15.3 cumecs in summer and 17 cumecs in winter. Theoretically calibrated, one rating applied across period of record.
description-flow-record: Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in October 2018 (WINFAP Files v7) and in August 2026 (WINFAP Files v15).
description-catchment: Rural catchment on Boulder Clay.
description-flow-regime: No abstractions, small returns.

name: Egleton Brook at Egleton
description-summary: Flat V weir measuring inflows to Rutland Water reservoir from a small, rural, natural catchment.
description-general: Flat V weir 2m wide measuring inflows to Rutland Water.
description-station-hydrometry: Theoretically rated, but could drown at high flows due to sharp bend d/s and weed growth. One rating applied across period of record.
description-flow-record: Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in August 2024 (WINFAP Files v13).
description-catchment: Small catchment on Boulder Clay and low permeability geology. Rural, mixed farming.
description-flow-regime: Natural to within 10% at Q95. No abstractions or returns.

name: Gwash at Church Bridge
description-summary: Compound crump profile weir immediately d/s of Rutland Water.
description-general: Compound Crump profile weir. Immediately d/s of Rutland Water. Site monitors compensation flows.
description-station-hydrometry: NA
description-flow-record: Data available from 1983-present. Missing data in 01/2005-12/2007.
description-catchment: Upper reaches of the Gwash starting in Knossington, draining Oakham. Catchment dominated by Rutland Water, but is otherwise predominantly grassland and agricultural land.
description-flow-regime: Heavily influenced by the outflow of Rutland Water.

name: Nene at Orton
description-summary: Series of sluices, weirs and lock on the Nene.
description-general: Series of sluices, weirs and lock. High flows measured at Wansford (32010) and corrected.
description-station-hydrometry: Ratings revised and historical data altered in 1975 and 1983. Ultrasonic gauge tested in 1976 but abandoned. Flows >17 cumecs measured at Wansford (32010) 12km u/s and corrected for smaller area. Wansford was a rated section (ratings and data revised in 1981) but now has a cross, multiple path ultrasonic gauge measuring the full-range. Provenance of 1947 peak data is uncertain and under review, but this was undoubtedly an exceptional event.
description-flow-record: NA
description-catchment: Lowest gauging point on Nene. Mostly clay (72%) and rural, but includes some towns and several small reservoirs.
description-flow-regime: Water abstracted at Wansford and sent to Rutland Water, with significant effect on low flows.

name: Willow Brook at Fotheringhay
description-summary: Flat V weir gauging a predominantly urban catchment with significant urban cover in the upper part. Artificial influences evident at low flows.
description-general: From 2000, Flat V weir (with wall height 16.42mAOD). Pre-2000, structure was a flume (1.676m wide throat, wall height 16.6mAOD).
description-station-hydrometry: Flat V weir is subject to bypassing and considered unreliable above 1.2m. Pre-2000 flume rating based on model tests, bypassing occurred at 6.5 cumecs and was not allowed for. The most recent rating is valid from 2000 when weir reconstructed. Two ratings applied across period of record. Pre-2000 rating considered unreliable above 1.38m; post-2000 rating considered unreliable above 1.2m. Flood plain flow is considerable above QMED.
description-flow-record: 1938-2000 record considered unreliable above 1.38m because of poor rating for that period. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in October 2018 (WINFAP Files v7) and in August 2026 (WINFAP Files v15).
description-catchment: Underlain by clay in headwaters and some l'st, around half Boulder Clay cover. Largely rural with mixed farming in lower catchment, but includes Corby in upper catchment. Diversion caused loss of 4.66 sq.km of catchment to Harpers Brook in 1963.
description-flow-regime: Three small reservoirs continue to have minor influence on low flows. Low flows significantly influenced by abstractions for Corby steelworks (including imports from Eye Brook) until 1980.

name: Harpers Brook at Old Mill Bridge
description-summary: Site with several gauging structures throughout POR, gauging a predominantly rural, natural catchment.
description-general: Rated section prior to 1965, then compound Crump profile weir (central crest 1.22m, total crest length 3.66m). Replaced in 1998 by flat V (4.04m wide between existing wing walls).
description-station-hydrometry: The compound Crump profile had calibration confirmed to 4.8 cumecs, but the weir drowned around 7 cumecs and was bypassed in extreme floods. Current flat V is modular to approx. 20 cumecs. Considerable floodplain inundation above about 1.5 QMED, therefore significant uncertainty attends highest flows. Two ratings applied across period of record, the most recent is valid from Oct 1998 when flat-V installed. No ratings have out of bank limbs; 1938-1964 considered unreliable above 1.99m, 1964-1998 unreliable above 1.67m, 1998-date unreliable above 1.7m.
description-flow-record: Highest peak flow of 22 cumecs in 1981 is extrapolated and should be treated with caution. The HIF of 15.6 cumecs on 10/04/1998 is likely to be an under-estimate; the flow was not captured but it may have been the highest on record. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2020 (WINFAP Files v9).
description-catchment: Natural catchment. Low-lying impervious catchment, clay largely covered with Boulder Clay. Predominantly agricultural with some forest. Some ironstone mines working until early 1980s. Catchment area increased by 8% (4.66sq.km) after diversion from Willow Brook in 1963. In April 1979, 3.64sq.km was diverted from Harpers Brook to Ise Brook - this is not accounted for in the catchment area.
description-flow-regime: Natural to within 10% at Q95.

name: Ise Brook at Harrowden
description-summary: Site with several different structures installed throughout POR, gauging a rural catchment with mixed geology and some artificial influences.
description-general: A weir existed already in 1936, so a rectangular notch was cut in in Oct 1936. In Jun-Dec 1943, the rectangular notch was replaced by a flume with low flow notch and the bypass channel was straightened. In 1964, this flume was replaced by a compound Crump weir (its construction. Finally, in 1976, a flat V weir with 5.15m crest was constructed.
description-station-hydrometry: Considerable flood plain flow above bankfull. Crump weir was modular to 15.6 cumecs (but bypassed at 14.2 cumecs). Flat V is also bypassed. Multiple ratings for various structures applied across period of record, the most recent is valid from April-1976 (flat V) and accounts for the bypassing. 1943-1965 rating considered unreliable above 1.6m, 1965-1976 rating unreliable above 1.39m.
description-flow-record: Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2022 (WINFAP Files v11).
description-catchment: Underlain by clay and sandstone, nearly half covered with superficial deposits, mainly in higher areas on catchment margins. Predominantly rural catchment of mixed farming, but includes Kettering in lower catchment.
description-flow-regime: Two small storage reservoirs with minor influence on low flows; receives Kettering effluent.

name: Nene/Kislingbury at Upton Total
description-summary: Compound site of main channel and bypass channel with long POR gauging a rural catchment on clay, with some artificial influences.
description-general: Compound site. Main channel flow measured in 3.2m wide standing wave flume under mill. Flow in bypass channel measured at Crump profile weir (crest 6.12m) since 1969 and flows summed to produce total.
description-station-hydrometry: Very high flows bypass both channels. Before 1969 flows through bypass controlled by broad-crested weir with no recorder, and total flows based on average relationship between levels in main channel and bypass; rating for this period considered unreliable above 1.2m. Since 1969, flows measured separately at mill and bypass; respective limits of reliability are 1.2m (mill) and 1.05m (bypass).
description-flow-record: NA
description-catchment: Mostly clay with some superficial deposits, mainly Boulder Clay. predominantly rural catchment with land use of mixed farming.
description-flow-regime: No major abstractions but several sewage work effluent returns.

name: Nene/Brampton at St Andrews Total
description-summary: Compound site located in Northampton, gauging a catchment with mixed geology and three reservoirs significantly affecting runoff.
description-general: Compound site. Main channel flow measured in 2.743m wide standing-wave flume in mill race. Flow in bypass channel measured at 9.11m wide broad crested weir and flows summed to produce total. St Andrews Mill Bypass has 2 ratings for the digital data, a station rating from digital SOR to 24/08/1998, and then there was a new one created applied from 24/08/1998 till present. The pre 1969 data before the gauge was installed at the bypass St Andrews total is estimated.
description-station-hydrometry: Bypassing of both structures commences at about 17 cumecs. No recorder on bypass before 1969, total flows were estimated using average relationship between levels in flume and bypass. 1940-1969 AMAX gives total flow at mill and bypass sites; considered unreliable above 1.39m. Post-1969 mill rating unreliable above 1.11m.
description-flow-record: NA
description-catchment: Mixed geology, mostly clay, about one third covered with Boulder Clay. Predominantly rural catchment of mixed farming. Urban development (Northampton) in lower catchment, u/s of station. Significant water reservoirs in the catchment.
description-flow-regime: Abstraction from reservoirs reduce low flows. Some effluent returns. Pitsford reservoir (filled between 1952 and 1956) is the largest of the three PWS reservoirs controlling flow from about one third of the catchment.

name: Nene/Kislingbury at Dodford
description-summary: Gauging a catchment with mixed geology, predominantly rural land use, and with some significant artificial influences.
description-general: Crump profile weir with 2.667m crest replaced broad-crested weir with low flow notch in 1967.
description-station-hydrometry: Weir theoretically calibrated, but bypassing begins at 7 cumecs (1.038m). Weir can drown at high flows, floodplain flow is considerable once the river is out of bank, so flows are significantly underestimated from about 1.1m stage. Two ratings applied across period of record, the most recent is valid from Dec 1966 when weir was replaced. No allowances for out of bank flow, thus ratings unreliable above 1.45m pre-1966 and 1.4m post-1966. Scatter in gaugings above 0.3m. High flows measured 2km upstream at Flore Hill.
description-flow-record: Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2020 (WINFAP Files v9). Uncertainty in high flows between 1945-1970 due to a different structure - this period has been marked as unrepresentative.
description-catchment: Mostly clay with nearly half of the catchment covered with superficial deposits (Boulder Clay, glacial sand and gravel in lower valley). Predominantly rural with mixed farming but some urban areas present, especially in W. Daventry and Drayton reservoirs in catchment (8.65 sq.km), built in 1804. Motorways (M1, M45) cross the catchment.
description-flow-regime: Reservoirs and abstractions affect regime, and low flows influenced by returns from STW. Abstraction for supply to Grand Union Canal.

name: Nene at Wansford
description-summary: Velocity-area station measuring peak flows only superseded by an ultrasonic station in 1996. Gauging a predominantly rural catchment with significant urban areas, with mixed geology, and with significant artificial influences.
description-general: Cross, multiple path (6 velocity and 1 depth) ultrasonic gauge installed 01/06/1996. Previously was a 97m wide VA station with cable way for current metering and sounding, for flows over 28.3 cumecs, used for high flow measurement on River Nene, with low and medium flows measured at Nene at Orton (32001).
description-station-hydrometry: Structure spills into a lake on the right bank. Bankfull was originally 9.4 mAOD, increasing to 10.3 mAOD after bank raising work in 1964. Datum used for majority of record is 7.9mAOD but discrepancies found over years (maximum 120mm), accepted level record accuracy +-50mm. Multiple peak flow ratings applied across period of record. Current rating unreliable above 1.9m with no out of bank limb post-1964 (2.34m).
description-flow-record: Dataset up to October 1970 has been reset to same datum (7.9 mAOD). Peak flows held (no daily means) during velocity area operation and rejected until 1964 because of rating uncertainty. Although ultrasonics were installed in 1996, data quality was poor until 2004 when the NRFA daily flow record begins. Missing data in May 2020 due to upgrade of ultrasonic gauge.
description-catchment: Mixed geology, moderate to very low permeability. Predominantly agricultural land use but several small towns in the catchment. Northampton is completely within this catchment on R. Nene.
description-flow-regime: Flows influenced by abstractions for public water supply. Water level below 8.36mAOD affected by mill operation at Water Newton. Navigation retention level is 8.0mAOD.

name: Wootton Brook at Lady Bridge
description-summary: Simple Crump profile weir on the Wooton Brook. Short low flows record, and short full flow record.
description-general: Simple Crump profile weir, crest 1.83m broad. Rated up to 0.25m (0.488 cumecs).
description-station-hydrometry: Low flows only until mid 1990s.
description-flow-record: Patchy data (high flows missing) 07/1969-09/1982. Data begins again 01/1997 and extends to 06/2000.
description-catchment: Underlain by 80% Boulder Clay. Small rural catchment, with 20% woodland.
description-flow-regime: Largely natural regime; one small discharge in headwaters. Sporadic flow record.

name: Willow Brook South at Corby South
description-summary: Simple Crump profile weir on the upper reaches of the Willow Brook. Low flows only.
description-general: Simple Crump profile weir, crest 1.83m broad. Rated up to 0.304m (0.651 cumecs).
description-station-hydrometry: Low flows only.
description-flow-record: Data available 02/1971-present.
description-catchment: Upper reaches of a largely urban catchment draining Corby.
description-flow-regime: NA

name: Slade Brook at Kettering
description-summary: Flat V weir gauge on the Slade Brook, recording full range post-1995. Most high flows truncated or missing pre-1995.
description-general: Full-range Flat V weir. Replaced low flow simple Crump profile weir (crest 2.42m broad, rated up to 0.3m: 0.848 cumecs) in early 1988, following river improvements.
description-station-hydrometry: NA
description-flow-record: Most high flows are truncated or missing in pre-1995 record; water balance more realistic over subsequent years. Due to subsisdence at the station, low flow data from 17th November 2023 onwards may be of reduced quality. Temporary equipment has been used since this date until the station can be rebuilt.
description-catchment: Catchment is 50% clay and 50% s'st, with over 20% cover of Boulder Clay. Rural headwaters, with urban development (Kettering) in lower catchment.
description-flow-regime: NA

name: Wittering Brook at Wansford
description-summary: Simple Crump profile weir at confluence with Nene. Low flows only.
description-general: Simple Crump profile weir, crest 2.44m broad. Rated up to 0.308m (0.896 cumecs).
description-station-hydrometry: Low flows only. Truncation of high flows results in unrepresentative mean runoff.
description-flow-record: Data available 03/1970-03/1984.
description-catchment: Tributary of the Nene.
description-flow-regime: NA

name: Flore at Experimental Catchment
description-summary: Trapezoidal critical depth flume gauging only low flows of a responsive catchment but producing a patchy record.
description-general: Trapezoidal critical depth flume. Low flows only. Built upstream of the culvert beneath the M1 motorway. Station removed from peak flows dataset in August 2024 (WINFAP Files v13).
description-station-hydrometry: Rated to 1.92m (8.49 cumecs). Rating based on theoretical equations for flume. No check gauging carried out at this site. One peak flow rating across period of record.
description-flow-record: Patchy record.
description-catchment: Entirely rural and consists mainly of Jurassic and drift clay. There are small pockets of limestone and gravel sand.
description-flow-regime: Responsive regime.

name: Wootton Brook at Wootton Park
description-summary: Triangular Flat V weir on the Wooton Brook. Drowns at high flows.
description-general: Triangular Flat V weir (crest length 8m); theoretical rating. Drowns at high flows due to limited capacity of culverts d/s.
description-station-hydrometry: Just d/s of Lady Bridge gauging station (32012), a low flow-only station running 1968 to 1985.
description-flow-record: Data available 09/1983-present. Missing data Jun-Nov 2000 and all months of 2006.
description-catchment: Mostly underlain by Boulder Clay with some exposed Upper Lias clays and small areas of plateau gravel and Oolitic L'st. Catchment predominantly rural, with expanding Northampton suburbs near gauging station.
description-flow-regime: No abstractions or returns.

name: Bedford Ouse at Brownshill Staunch
description-summary: Complex structure measuring discharge from Bedford Ouse, providing indication of runoff patterns between 1936 and 1962.
description-general: Station consisted of a navigation lock and three radial gates with a low flow notch.
description-station-hydrometry: Complicated hydrometric arrangement, with no unique stage-discharge relationship. Low flows based on gate openings. Rated section for high flows, using calibration by float measurement.
description-flow-record: Record likely to be of poor quality, but provides indication of runoff patterns from 1936-62.
description-catchment: Large, mixed catchment. Geology of Great Oolite and Oxford clays, with substantial Boulder Clay cover. Mixed rural land use, some urban development in lower valleys.
description-flow-regime: NA

name: Bedford Ouse at Bedford
description-summary: Compound broad-crested weir with the oldest record in HA 33. From 1972, more convincing flow series available from Roxton d/s (33039). Station closed 31/12/2015.
description-general: 3 broad-crested weirs, 30m, 20m and 12m wide + 3 vertical sluice gates (either fully open/closed). Duckmill Weir is a broad crested weir with 2 sluice gates; width 30.48m, wing wall 25.885mAOD. Boathouse Weir is a broad crested weir, width 19.5m. Newnham Weir is a weir with 1 sluice gate, width 11.8m. Removed from peak flows dataset in February 2018 (WINFAP Files v6).
description-station-hydrometry: Above bankfull, water spills over right bank to join d/s channel. Lock gates opened at high flows. One peak flow rating applied across period of record. Confirmed by current meter measurements, the rating assumes set gate openings. Recommended to be used to bankfull only.
description-flow-record: From 1972, more convincing flow series available from Roxton d/s (33039). The Apr 1998 peak flow is thought to be an overestimate. The period-of-record maximum is believed to have occurred in Mar 1947; no peak flow available but is unlikely to be significantly higher than the DMF (278 cumecs). Records before 1959 based on daily gauge-board levels and gate openings (limited accuracy, few HIFs & many replicated GDFs). Flow record may be inaccurate due to flow manipulation (kayaking) and 33039 should be used instead.
description-catchment: Predominantly clay. Mainly agricultural land use with substantial urban development over last 25 years.
description-flow-regime: Reservoir(s) in catchment affect runoff. Surface and groundwater abstractions in catchment for PWS and Milton Keynes' effluent significant.

name: Cam at Bottisham
description-summary: Complex structure gauging Chalk catchment of River Lee in its lower reach with some artificial influences.
description-general: Triangular profile weir, 7.7m wide, plus two vertical lift gates and a lock. Prior to Jun 1982 broad-crested weir incorporating a sharp-crested rectangular central notch, 2.4m wide.
description-station-hydrometry: The lock is opened at high flows. Weir drowns at approx. 0.3m head.
description-flow-record: Patchy peak-flow record available.
description-catchment: Chalk overlain by Boulder Clay in the S. Predominantly agricultural land use.
description-flow-regime: Two substantial gw abstractions for industry; 21 for PWS. All abstractions returned within the catchment.

name: Lark at Isleham
description-summary: Station gauging a navigation lock with Bury St Edmunds and large gw abstractions in the catchment dominated by Chalk geology and arable agriculture.
description-general: Navigation lock with vertical lift gate u/s plus a 16m broad high level weir in bypass channel for flood flows only. Small notch inserted in 1980. 1986 weir was lowered, altered to triangular profile and flows diverted to the bypass channel. The lock is now used during high flows only.
description-station-hydrometry: NA
description-flow-record: Since 1968 major peaks diverted through cutoff channel (10km u/s) - to the Relief Channel at Denver.
description-catchment: Chalk, predominantly arable.
description-flow-regime: Two large gw abstractions (Bury St Edmunds).

name: Bedford Ouse at Thornborough Mill
description-summary: Flow records generally affected by sluice movement and implementation of digital recording in 1979.
description-general: Flat V Crump profile weir 10.2m wide and two sluice gates 3.6m broad. Before 1976 weir was broad-crested with centre V notch.
description-station-hydrometry: A bypass channel exists, but operation of gates has ensured the highest flows have been recorded. Significant scatter in gaugings as a result of differing gate positions.
description-flow-record: Since 1979, peak flow recordings have been digital but recorded only upstream stage, not gate opening and downstream level. Peak flows since 1979 are therefore unreliable and rejected. Daily flows not calculated since Aug 1991. Inaccurate DMF measurement complicated by automatic sluice movement which was not integrated into flow calculation methods. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2023 (WINFAP Files v12).
description-catchment: The catchment is flat and lies mainly on the Great Oolite. One large tributary drains an area of Oxford Clay. There is a water supply reservoir and a number of ornamental lakes in the catchment.
description-flow-regime: Flows affected by reservoirs in catchment. Abstraction for public water supply, and industrial and agricultural uses reduces runoff. Runoff increased by effluent returns.

name: Wissey at Northwold Total
description-summary: Single site until 1983, since then a compound site with flows calculated as summation of the main flume and a side flume.
description-general: Flow record is summation of a rectangular critical depth flume (4.9m wide) and a flume on a separate side stream which takes approx. 30-40% of the runoff. Streams rejoin just d/s of gauges. Post-1983, the flow from the second weir (side stream) was recorded, and 33006 is the summation of both structures. Eel tiles are installed on the main stream. Removed from peak flows dataset in September 2019 (WINFAP Files v8).
description-station-hydrometry: Drowning common - flows adjusted. Flows are the summation of two weirs. In 1980, Northwold Brook was diverted into the Wissey and Little River equally. More recently, all flow has been diverted into the Little River.
description-flow-record: DMF in June-Dec 2007 were anomalously high and therefore adjusted by the Environment Agency; values appear plausible but should be treated with caution. Since 2012, non-modular flow has become more common and occurs at lower stages. This is currently under investigation.
description-catchment: Chalk largely overlain by Boulder Clay (permeable in parts). Low population density. Largely arable in upper (northern) catchment, extensive grassland, heathland, and some woodland in lower (southern) part of catchment.
description-flow-regime: Abstraction for public water supply, industry and agriculture. Effluent returns increase runoff. Limited net impact of abstractions and discharges but spray irrigation increasing (substantial proportion from groundwater).

name: Nar at Marham
description-summary: Critical depth flume measuring Chalk catchment with predominantly agricultural land use.
description-general: Round nosed horizontal crest weir (7.13m wide). Prior to April 1982, low flow flume in centre making structure 7.47m wide (now sealed off).
description-station-hydrometry: Weed growth can be a problem during summer if not cut regularly. Level measurements taken just upstream of weir. Two peak flow ratings applied across period of record. Modular limit is estimated at 6 cumecs and is accounted for in the current rating.
description-flow-record: Anomalous summer flows in June 2004 and August 2006, resulting from locals damming the weir. Peak flows derived from flume (pre-1982) are rejected as they do not form a historically consistent record with the weir data. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in October 2018 (WINFAP Files v7) and August 2025 (WINFAP v14).
description-catchment: Chalk catchment overlain by Boulder Clay in upper reaches. Agricultural land use, predominantly arable.
description-flow-regime: Surface water abstraction for PWS immediately u/s of station. Also surface/groundwater abstraction in catchment for industry/agriculture. Three small underground abstractions were abandoned in 1986. Effluent returns may increase runoff.

name: Bedford Ouse at Harrold Mill
description-summary: Compound broad-crested weir gauging a catchment with significant PWS abstractions.
description-general: Compound structure comprising a compound broad-crested weir plus two side spilling broad-crested weirs u/s. Not primarily constructed for flow measurement, essentially a level site. Harrold mill weir under the mill structure. Removed from peak flows dataset in September 2023 (WINFAP Files v12).
description-station-hydrometry: Ratings are theoretical and do not include out of bank flows.
description-flow-record: Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2023 (WINFAP Files v12).
description-catchment: Limestone overlain by Boulder Clay. Mainly agricultural land use with substantial urban development associated with Milton Keynes.
description-flow-regime: Major public water supply abstractions in catchment, for Milton Keynes and Foxcots. Also abstractions for industrial/agricultural purposes. Effluent returns may increase runoff. Reservoir(s) in catchment.

name: Little Ouse at County Bridge Euston
description-summary: Compound weir gauging a Chalk catchment with predominantly agricultural land use.
description-general: Compound weir with triangular profile centre section, 3.4m broad; broad-crested flanks in trapezoidal channel 9m broad.
description-station-hydrometry: One rating applied across period of record. Hydraulic model used to derive rating for peak flows, including out of bank and bypassing. Reasonable fit to gaugings. Part of the Thet-Little Ouse groundwater support scheme, which triggers at 95 l/s to maintain flow.
description-flow-record: Peak flows available from 1960. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in August 2021 (WINFAP Files v10).
description-catchment: Predominantly Chalk with significant Boulder Clay cover. Agricultural land use, predominantly arable.
description-flow-regime: Groundwater abstractions for PWS and spray irrigation. Some effluent returns.

name: Kym at Meagre Farm
description-summary: Compound weir gauging a predominantly clay catchment with near-natural flow regime.
description-general: Compound weir with triangular profile centre section 3m wide and broad-crested flanks in a trapezoidal channel, 8.5m wide. One of 3 stations used to calculate Offord flow to determine abstraction regime at Grafham Water. No major bridge/weir change from 1959 drawings to H Reed 1994 survey.
description-station-hydrometry: Downstream level used to flag non-modularity. Peak flow rating takes non-modularity into account but there is a high degree of scatter. One peak flow ratings applied across period of record. There is a stage offset of +1m in WISKI. This has been applied to all stage data, ratings, gaugings, bankfull and wingwall height.
description-flow-record: Peak flows rejected between 1963 and 1966 due to low confidence. Water year 2002/2003 rejected due to AMAX occurring during missing period in Jan-Mar 2003. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in August 2021 (WINFAP Files v10).
description-catchment: Predominantly clay catchment - very flashy by Anglian standards. Agricultural, predominantly arable.
description-flow-regime: Predominantly natural regime with modest abstractions for agriculture. Some effluent returns.

name: Sapiston at Rectory Bridge
description-summary: Gauging a catchment with minor artificial influences using a theoretical rating.
description-general: Rectangular thin-plate weir, 8.8m broad, suppressed end contractions.
description-station-hydrometry: Rating theoretical. Rating confirmed by gaugings to 0.6m, non-modular conditions unaccounted for. One rating applied across period of record.
description-flow-record: Flows in 2014 may be affected by periodic damming. Since 2012 the site suffers from sudden and localized changes in river flow which manifest as short term increase, decrease, and recovery in GDF and as HIF much higher than GDF. Occasional gate openings upstream cause short-term increases in flow which only last a few hours. During low flows these increases may be reflected in HIFs and AMAX but have a minor effect on GDFs. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in August 2021 (WINFAP Files v10).
description-catchment: Predominately Chalk with Boulder Clay cover. Agricultural land use, predominantly arable.
description-flow-regime: Minor groundwater abstractions for PWS and agriculture. Some effluent returns.

name: Lark at Temple
description-summary: Compound broad-crested weir gauging a Chalk catchment with significant artificial influences.
description-general: Compound broad-crested weir with rectangular cross-section, 5.8m broad, central notch 3m broad.
description-station-hydrometry: Not drowned at 1.8m stage. One rating applied across period of record, full range rating confirmed by current meter measurements.
description-flow-record: Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in October 2018 (WINFAP Files v7).
description-catchment: Predominantly Chalk overlain with Boulder Clay. Agricultural land use.
description-flow-regime: Flows affected by milling u/s of gauging station. Significant groundwater abstractions in catchment for PWS, industry and agriculture. Some effluent returns.

name: Ouzel at Willen
description-summary: Gauging a predominantly rural catchment with mixed bedrock, influenced by Leighton Buzzard and by Milton Keys in the lower part, high flows may be underestimated.
description-general: Flat V Crump profile weir (10m broad) and sluices. The present weir replaced a compound broad-crested weir (10m broad) with bypass channel in 1977 when the river was realigned.
description-station-hydrometry: Radial lifting gate immediately u/s of weir diverts very high flows to adjacent balancing reservoir which empties d/s of weir. This may result in high flows being appreciably less than those seen upstream at Bletchley (33058). Annual floods do not bypass. FSR Grade A1 in 1971. Two ratings applied across period of record, the most recent is valid from July 1977 when weir rebuilt.
description-flow-record: Monthly maxima (HIFs) may be offset from daily mean flows during periods of gate movement. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2020 (WINFAP Files v9).
description-catchment: Mixed bedrock geology, with Greensand and Oxford Clay and some Boulder Clay cover. Primarily a rural catchment of mixed agriculture, although Leighton Buzzard is in catchment, and southern suburbs of Milton Keynes are situated in lower valley just u/s of station.
description-flow-regime: Runoff influenced by industrial/agricultural abstraction and effluent returns.

name: Cam at Jesus Lock
description-summary: Complex structure located in Cambridge, gauging a Chalk catchment with some artificial influences.
description-general: Broad-crested weir V-shaped in plan, 21.3m long in parallel with two sluice gates and a navigation lock. Gauging station is in Cambridge.
description-station-hydrometry: Flows based on upstream and downstream levels and gate openings, subject to inaccuracies from gate opening data.
description-flow-record: GDF until Jun 1960 is likely incorrect.
description-catchment: Chalk catchment partly overlain by Boulder Clay.
description-flow-regime: Some abstractions in catchment.

name: Tove at Cappenham Bridge
description-summary: Compound broad-crested weir gauging a predominantly Chalk catchment. Station has record length over 50 years.
description-general: Compound broad-crested trapezoidal weir, 7.6m broad; central notch, 2.7m broad.
description-station-hydrometry: The weir is subject to drowning at high flows with some bypassing on the left bank; further gaugings required to confirm extent of this. Theoretical rating since Aug 1970. Previously, rating derived using a hydraulic model. Full EA rating developed in 2012 combining existing EA rating for first 3 segments, regression through check gaugings for segments 4 and 5, and an EA modelled high flow rating used for the top segment. New rating applied to length of record.
description-flow-record: Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in October 2018 (WINFAP Files v7).
description-catchment: Predominantly Chalk overlain with 50% Boulder Clay. Agricultural land use.
description-flow-regime: Runoff increased by effluent returns and reduced by industrial/agricultural abstraction.

name: Thet at Melford Bridge
description-summary: Triangular profile weir gauging rural, predominantly Chalk catchment, and with some artificial influences.
description-general: Triangular profile weir, 6.2m broad.
description-station-hydrometry: Infrequent drowning due to weed growth. Intense localised rainfall causes flashy response. Theoretical rating modified Apr 68. One peak flow rating applied across period of record. Out of bank and non-modular gaugings required to review rating.
description-flow-record: Significant high flow event in September 1968 missing from record. Flows in autumn 2003 raised by flow augmentation during drought conditions. 2007-2008 late summer peak flows suspect due to possible stilling well blockage causing underestimation of flows. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2020 (WINFAP Files v9).
description-catchment: Predominantly Chalk catchment largely overlain by Boulder Clay. Primarily arable land, with some grassland and forestry.
description-flow-regime: Flows are affected by groundwater abstraction for agriculture/industry, and by groundwater augmentation during drought conditions which can significantly raise flows. Sharp increases and decreases in flow due to surface water outfall just upstream of weir.Runoff increased by effluent returns.

name: Alconbury Brook at Brampton
description-summary: Flat V weir gauging a rural, impervious catchment with some artificial influences. Record includes data from earlier broad-crested weir.
description-general: Flat V weir in trapezoidal channel (used to have ultrasonic for use when head above crest >1m) replaced (from 03/06/1995) former broad-crested CP weir with central low flow notch (closed in Sep 1993). Removed from peak flows dataset in May 2016 (WINFAP Files v4).
description-station-hydrometry: Drowns at approx. 1m stage and spills at 2m on a nearby horse racecourse. High flows impeded by bridges u/s and d/s. Theoretical rating but hydraulic model calibration for flanks prior to Apr 1978. Pre 1993 rating modified by current meter measurement to correct for drowning.
description-flow-record: The highest flow on record is estimated by the EA to be 70 cumecs on 10/04/1998, although the gauge was subject to bypassing. Data post 1995 reprocessed following rating review. High flows from pre-1995 structure and post-1995 structure appear inconsistent.
description-catchment: Predominantly impervious catchment, Boulder Clay covers about half of the area. Agricultural land use, mainly arable.
description-flow-regime: Runoff affected by industrial/agricultural abstraction and effluent returns.

name: Rhee at Burnt Mill
description-summary: Trapezoidal weir gauging a predominantly Chalk catchment with primarily arable land and with significant artificial influences.
description-general: Trapezoidal cross-section weir with triangular profile crest, 6.1m broad. Also called Haslingfield (Burnt Mill). Consistent records available of groundwater pump operation. Pre barrage fish pass and eel tiles installed.
description-station-hydrometry: Weir drowns at high flows, starting from 0.48m stage and drowns completely at higher flows, worsened during summer due to weed growth downstream. Non-modular conditions are accounted for in the current rating. Rating modified by current meter measurements to correct for drowning and applied across period of record. Gauging station is used as part of the Rhee groundwater support scheme, which triggers at a combined flow of 301 l/s to maintain flow. One peak flow rating across period of record.
description-flow-record: Daily mean flow from 24/10/2013 to 04/03/2015 was updated after September 2014 to compensate for site maintenance. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in October 2018 (WINFAP Files v7) and August 2025 (WINFAP Files v14).
description-catchment: Predominantly Chalk catchment partly overlain with Boulder Clay in NW. Primarily arable land.
description-flow-regime: Substantial groundwater abstractions for public water supply, plus industrial and agricultural abstractions. Some effluent returns. Augmentation from ground water sources to regulate river flow - scheme aims to maintain minimum 0.3 cumecs flow at gauging station.

name: Ivel at Blunham
description-summary: Crump profile gauging a catchment with mixed bedrock and significant artificial influences.
description-general: Crump profile weir 7.31m wide. Drowning occurs at 0.91m (rating includes drowning correction). Significant bypassing of station upstream. Pre-1966 record of poorer quality. One of 3 stations used to calculate Offord flows to determine abstraction regime at Grafham Water.
description-station-hydrometry: Significant bypassing when stage exceeds 1.1m causing 'truncation' effect in annual maxima series. Hydrograph reflects u/s mill operation. One rating applied across period of record based on current meter gaugings. There is no correction for non modularity as spot flows suggest modular to at least 1m. No correction has been made for out of bank flow and spot flows are taken downstream of bypass.
description-flow-record: Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in August 2021 (WINFAP Files v10).
description-catchment: The Ivel rises near Hitchin and flows north across Greensand, Chalk and Gault Clays to meet the Great Ouse east of Bedford. Predominantly superficial deposits, mainly Boulder Clay with some glacial sands and gravels. Predominantly agricultural, with some urban development.
description-flow-regime: Effluent from STW has substantial effect on low flows. Many abstractions for spray irrigation, and groundwater abstractions for PWS.

name: Lea Brook at Beck Bridge
description-summary: Crump profile weir gauging a rural, Chalk catchment with some Boulder Clay and terrace deposits and with some artificial influences, all but the very highest flows are contained.
description-general: Crump profile weir 4m wide, situated approx. 20m u/s of new road bridge.
description-station-hydrometry: The POR maximum flow is believed to have been in Sept 1968, estimated as 15.1 cumecs by the EA but likely to have been extrapolated.
description-flow-record: Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2020 (WINFAP Files v9).
description-catchment: A rural Chalk catchment with Boulder Clay cover in upper (S) part of catchment. Some river terrace deposits in N. Mixed agricultural land use.
description-flow-regime: Some groundwater abstraction for PWS, also industrial/agricultural abstraction. Runoff increased by effluent returns.

name: Cam at Dernford
description-summary: Rectangular thin-plate weir gauging predominantly pervious Chalk catchment with arable land use and significant artificial influences.
description-general: Rectangular thin-plate weir, 5.8m broad. Removed from peak flows dataset in September 2023 (WINFAP Files v12).
description-station-hydrometry: Bridge pier may affect approach velocity at high flows. Weir subject to drowning, tailwater levels measured to assist rating. Rating does not consider out of bank flow.
description-flow-record: Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in October 2018 (WINFAP Files v7).
description-catchment: Predominantly pervious catchment underlain by Chalk. Some Boulder Clay cover, primarily in headwater areas. Land use mainly arable.
description-flow-regime: Five groundwater abstractions for PWS. Also abstractions for industry and agriculture. Flow regime is affected by industrial effluent returns derived from groundwater pumped within the catchment.

name: Babingly at West Newton Mill
description-summary: Station gauging a relatively small spring-fed stream with relatively short record of unrealistic runoff.
description-general: Sharp-crested weir inside converted mill building, with a bypass gate to a mill wheel.
description-station-hydrometry: NA
description-flow-record: Owners manipulated bypass gate, with no record kept of such openings, which limits accuracy of flows (particularly high flows, so unsuitable for flood purposes).
description-catchment: Small rural catchment, Chalk with some Boulder Clay.
description-flow-regime: Spring-fed stream, with unrealistic runoff because contributing area is greater than topographical catchment.

name: Bedford Ouse at Offord
description-summary: Complex structure with no formal gauging. Offord flow is calculated using stations Roxton: 33039, Meagre Farm: 33012 and Blunham: 33022.
description-general: Offord Flow = (33039 + 33012 + 33022) x 1.08 - abstraction. The contribution of the station components depends on catchment response, with Roxton: 33039 contributing ~70-90%, Meagre Farm: 33012 contributing ~0-5% and Blunham: 33022 contributing the rest.Historic gauging from complex of automatic radial tilting weir, 15.2m broad; triangular profile weir, 14.8m broad; compound broad-crested weir, 22.7m broad.
description-station-hydrometry: Navigation lock opened at flows above 40 cumecs.
description-flow-record: October 2016 - full period of record for net flows provided and loaded to NRFA, peak flow data were deleted as this is a complex site. Pollution monitoring can lead to the cessation of the abstraction pumps resulting in flow increases and subsequent drops, e.g., 03/09/2007 - 11/09/2007 and 20/02/2008 - 25/02/2008. No quality assurance at station as non H and T site, use data with caution.
description-catchment: Large catchment of mixed geology, with substantial superficial deposits (about half Boulder Clay). Mixed agricultural land use with some substantial urban areas (Milton Keynes, Bedford) although overall urban fraction is small.
description-flow-regime: Substantial surface water abstractions for PWS, industry and agriculture. Significant gw abstractions. Abstraction 2km u/s for Grafham Water Res. (approx. 2 cumecs).

name: Rhee at Wimpole
description-summary: Trapezoidal critical depth flume gauges predominantly Chalk catchment with predominantly agricultural land use and some artificial influences.
description-general: Trapezoidal critical depth flume, 6.6m broad, horizontal crest 3.8m. Eel tiles installed.
