description-station-hydrometry: Drowns at peak levels; correction incorporated into theoretical rating. Spills occasionally - high flows impeded by bridge abutments 20m d/s. One peak flow rating applied across period of record. Part of the Rhee groundwater support scheme.
description-flow-record: Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in August 2021 (WINFAP Files v10).
description-catchment: Predominantly Chalk catchment with some Boulder Clay cover in N and W. Land use predominantly agricultural, predominantly arable.
description-flow-regime: Some surface water and groundwater abstractions in catchment. Runoff increased by effluent returns.

name: Flit at Shefford
description-summary: Trapezoidal critical depth flume gauging predominantly greedsand catchment with mixed land use and some artificial influences including effluent from Luton.
description-general: Trapezoidal critical depth flume, 9.8m broad; 2.1m broad at horizontal crest. Structurefull 0.76m stage.
description-station-hydrometry: Subject to drowning at medium flows. Includes un-calibrated floodplain flow but, in practice, rating above 1.1m is not reliable. One peak flow rating applied across period of record.
description-flow-record: The highest peak flow on record is 33 cumecs on 03/01/2003, although uncertainty attends this value because of non-modularity and considerable ungauged floodplain flow. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2019 (WINFAP Files v8).
description-catchment: Predominantly Greensand with some Boulder Clay cover. Mixed agricultural land use with patches of woodland. Several small towns in catchment.
description-flow-regime: Flows affected by u/s mill operation. Surface water abstraction for spray irrigation. Abstraction for PWS closed in 1985. Flows augmented by effluent from Luton.

name: Stringside at Whitebridge
description-summary: Trapezoidal critical depth flume designed to operate in the non-modular range, gauging a small rural catchment on Chalk with some artificial influences.
description-general: Trapezoidal critical depth flume, calibrated by model and designed to operate in the non-modular range.
description-station-hydrometry: Drowns at very high flows (e.g. Easter Floods 1998) and can spill on rare occasions. Peak flow events are influenced by timing of peak on the Ivel. There is great uncertainty when levels go above 0.8m. One peak flow rating applied across period of record. Includes floodplain and non-modular flow.
description-flow-record: Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2019 (WINFAP Files v8).
description-catchment: A small rural catchment, mostly low-lying, developed mainly on chalk with some Boulder Clay cover (mainly in west). Mixed land use, predominantly arable land, with significant woodland in east and no urban areas.
description-flow-regime: Baseflow-dominated regime but can be responsive. Two groundwater abstractions for PWS. Also abstractions for industry/agriculture.

name: Clipstone Brook at Clipstone
description-summary: A triangular Flat V weir gauging a predominantly rural, Greensand catchment with some artificial influences. Multiple structures in operation during POR.
description-general: A triangular Flat V weir installed in 2002, 1km u/s of the previous structures: Crump weir (1966-1980) broad-crested weir (1957-1962).
description-station-hydrometry: Current daily flow rating considers drowning although there are limited gaugings to confirm rating. Two peak flow ratings applied across period of record, the most recent is valid from Oct 2002 when the new weir was constructed.
description-flow-record: Peak flow data are only presented for the current structure (01/10/2006 onwards). Gap in record when station not operational (1980-2002). Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2023 (WINFAP Files v12).
description-catchment: Greensand catchment, tributary to the river Ouzel. Predominantly rural, minor urban development (Leighton Buzzard).
description-flow-regime: Runoff influenced by groundwater abstraction/recharge. Runoff reduced by industrial/agricultural abstraction. Runoff augmented by effluent returns.

name: Broughton Brook at Broughton
description-summary: Station modified in 1977 gauging a flat catchment with greedsand bedrock, significant artificial influences due to public water supply abstraction.
description-general: Flat V Crump profile weir 7.0m wide installed in 1977 when river realigned. Prior to 23/6/77 trapezoidal critical depth flume 7.4m wide, horizontal crest 1m wide, located at SP892405.
description-station-hydrometry: Flume was subject to drowning but flows were corrected. Current rating includes floodplain flow and accounts for drowning. One peak flow rating applied across period of record.
description-flow-record: Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2023 (WINFAP Files v12).
description-catchment: Predominantly flat, the edge just impinging on the Chiltern escarpment. Clay and Greensand catchment, with some Boulder Clay cover. Mixed agricultural land use with some forestry in S, and significant urban development.
description-flow-regime: Runoff influenced by groundwater abstraction and recharge. One Greensand groundwater puclic water supply abstraction accounts for virtually all the abstraction in the catchment. Station located near Cotton Valley STW. Runoff increased by effluent return.

name: Heacham at Heacham
description-summary: Two crump weirs gauging a predominantly Chalk catchment with agricultural land use, topographical catchment area substantially exceeds the true contributing area.
description-general: Two Crump profile weirs in parallel, 3m broad in total.
description-station-hydrometry: Weirs never drown. Small bypass channel with weir upstream of station, rejoining downstream of weir, is factored in to the stage-discharge relationship. One rating applied across period of record.
description-flow-record: Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2020 (WINFAP Files v9).
description-catchment: Topographical catchment area substantially exceeds the true contributing area (by a factor of about two). Catchment area was determined in different ways. Area 55 sq. km is taken from the GA catchment area review of the Heacham/Wensum catchment boundary in 1996. This reduces the area from 59 sq. km, calculated in 1987, and from 89 sq. km adopted before 1987. The area of the NRFA catchment derived from IHDTM is 56 sq. km. Predominantly Chalk in parts overlain by Boulder Clay. Agricultural land use.
description-flow-regime: Groundwater abstraction for PWS and irrigation.

name: Hiz at Arlesey
description-summary: Crump profile gauging a predominantly Chalk catchment with arable farming and urban development, flows affected by weir drowning and artificial influences in the catchment.
description-general: Crump profile weir, 7m broad. Removed from peak flows dataset in September 2023 (WINFAP Files v12).
description-station-hydrometry: Highest recorded flow was contained by weir banks. Subject to drowning at peak flows, but flows are not corrected. Out of bank rare and floodplain limb not verified. Few gaugings to confirm rating which is uncertain. Station subject to drowning with no non-modular correction.
description-flow-record: Flows in August 2010 affected by drowning. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2019 (WINFAP Files v8).
description-catchment: Predominantly Chalk catchment, with significant superficial deposits (Boulder Clay, sands and gravels). Predominantly arable farming but with significant urban development (Hitchin).
description-flow-regime: Significant gw abstractions for PWS. Industrial/agricultural abstractions also occur. Augmentation by effluent affects diurnal flow pattern.

name: Little Ouse at Abbey Heath
description-summary: Rectangular section Crump profile weir gauging predominantly rural, Chalk catchment with some artificial influences.Eel tiles installed.
description-general: Rectangular section Crump profile weir with downstream recorder. Replaced 33008 (Thetford Staunch) in 1968.
description-station-hydrometry: Weir subject to drowning and spills on rare occasions, with a very small amount of bypassing on left bank at high flows, but potential for further erosion. Subject to weed growth, on crest and in channel. One peak flow rating applied across period of record, not thought to account for out of bank flows.
description-flow-record: Instrument hut vandalised in August 2000 and rebuilt in 2001/2002, peak flow data missing until August 2002. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2020 (WINFAP Files v9).
description-catchment: Chalk with largely overlain with superficial deposits, mainly Boulder Clay. Predominantly arable with significant areas of forest and heathland, particularly in centre and E. Urban development (Thetford) just u/s of station.
description-flow-regime: Affected by gw abstraction/recharge and, since the late 1980s, low flows augmented with groundwater in drought conditions. Abstraction mainly for industry and agriculture. Some effluent returns.

name: Ely Ouse at Denver Complex
description-summary: Complex structure gauging the whole of Ely Ouse catchment but with major gaps and inconsistencies in the flow record so the data should be used with great caution.
description-general: Three sluices: d/s sluice discharges flow to maintain level in Relief Channel; u/s sluice diverts surplus into Cut Off Channel; dividing sluice can raise level by 0.6m, reversing flow in the Cut Off Channel where it is abstracted at Blackdyke and diverted into the headwaters of Essex rivers (Ely Ouse/Essex Transfer Scheme). Larrinier fish pass installed.
description-station-hydrometry: NA
description-flow-record: Data should be used with great caution. In high floods gates are raised permitting channel to be used for original flood protection purpose. Complexity of the structure and its management is reflected in the homogeneity of the flow series - which has extensive periods with no data or zero flows.
description-catchment: Low lying catchment. Mixed geology with predominantly peat and alluvium on Fenland Plain and with Chalk overlain with Boulder Clay in higher regions to east and south. West is predominantly clay. High quality agricultural land.
description-flow-regime: Abstractions and diversion into the headwaters of Essex rivers (Ely Ouse/Essex Transfer Scheme).

name: Bedford Ouse at Newport Pagnell Total
description-summary: Compound site of main weir and mill weir gauging a catchment with mixed geology and mixed land use.
description-general: Compound site. Main weir is Compound Crump profile weir (29.3m broad), with central notch (3m broad) and downstream recorder. Separate, complementary Crump weir (3.7m broad) constructed in old mill throttle, 7m u/s of a double arch culvert. Flow record combines the main weir with a weir in the mill channel. Removed from peak flows dataset in September 2023 (WINFAP Files v12).
description-station-hydrometry: The mill weir is subject to drowning at high flows and therefore affects the total flows too. Combined rating for both main and mill weirs, based on stage at main weir. This rating is not used for generation of modern flow data. Rating fits poorly to available gaugings at extreme high flows, however this is likely to be due to flow bypassing/channels becoming undefined.
description-flow-record: Early peak flow data rejected due to uncertainty in stage data and rating. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2019 (WINFAP Files v8). No data from 7th September 2024 onwards due to telemetry and instrumentation failure during a flood event.
description-catchment: Mixed geology with significant component of permeable rocks, much of which is overlain by Boulder Clay. Mixed land use, arable land and grassland, some forest and some urban development in lower catchment.
description-flow-regime: Influenced by gw abstraction/recharge and some effluent returns. Abstractions for PWS approx. 25km u/s, and abstractions within catchment for industry/agriculture.

name: Bedford Ouse at Roxton
description-summary: Flat V Crump profile weir gauging a mixed land use catchment, mixed geology and with some artificial influences.
description-general: Flat V Crump profile weir (26m broad) with downstream recorder, situated immediately u/s of confluence with R. Ivel. Use in preference to Bedford (33002) if possible.
description-station-hydrometry: Drowns at very high flows (e.g. Easter Floods 1998), is influenced by timing of flood peak on R. Ivel, and can spill on rare occasions. Adjacent lock acts as an overspill in flood conditions. There is great uncertainty when levels go above 1.8m above crest. A single rating applied across period of record, however, there are multiple ratings that have been used in its history. Includes floodplain and non-modular flow. Assumes lock shut.
description-flow-record: The POR maximum flow in April 1998 was extrapolated and subject to bypassing but thought to be a reasonable estimate in a contemporary report by WS Atkins. POR reprocessed in 2018, changes mainly in 2010 to 2013. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2019 (WINFAP Files v8). Data quality issues from April 2025, use with caution.
description-catchment: Mixed geology, including significant Clay and Greensand fractions, with about half of the catchment covered with Boulder Clay. Predominantly agricultural with substantial urban development (Milton Keynes and Bedford).
description-flow-regime: Regime influenced by groundwater abstraction/recharge. Some effluent returns. Significant surface water and gw abstractions for PWS, industry and agriculture. One of 3 stations used to calculate Offord flows to determine abstraction regime at Grafham Water.

name: Rhee at Ashwell
description-summary: The station is located near the source of the River Rhee, where the groundwater contributing area is significantly larger than the topographic area.
description-general: Trapezoidal flume constructed from prefabricated glass-reinforced plastic, located 0.5 km downstream from the source of the River Rhee. Assessed as a candidate for the Peak Flow Dataset however determined not suitable due to frequent and consistent fluctuations owing to artificial influences, which introduces data quality issues over high flow range.
description-station-hydrometry: Flows influenced by substantial groundwater abstractions for public water supply. Station is part of the Rhee Groundwater Support Scheme, which is triggered when flows fall to 0.0295 cumecs to ensure minimum flow is sustained. If flow cannot be maintained, public water abstraction is stopped.
description-flow-record: Runoff data unrealistic.
description-catchment: The catchment area above the gauging station is 2km2. Predominantly Chalk catchment with agricultural land use. Groundwater contributing area exceeds topographic contributing area.
description-flow-regime: Flows influenced by large groundwater abstractions for public water supply. To support conservation, a minimum spring flow of 0.03mcube/s is maintained through artificial recharge.

name: Thet at Bridgham
description-summary: Crump weir gauging a Chalk rural catchment with some artificial influences, station reconstructed in 1979.
description-general: Crump profile weir, 6m broad. Prior to Oct 1979, broad-crested weir (crest: 7.4m), situated under double-arch bridge.
description-station-hydrometry: Two peak flow ratings applied across period of record, the most recent is valid from October-1979. Current rating only reliable to bankfull. Dredging increased modular limit. Theoretical rating for original weir confirmed by c/m measurements. Part of the Thet-Little Ouse groundwater support scheme, which triggers at 350 l/s to maintain flow. These trigger flows apply when the scheme is being used as a river support scheme for water users (not for Ely Ouse to Essex Transfer Scheme). The amount pumped in any one season is initially limited to 3 per cent of the annual licenced quantity of the Thet-Little Ouse scheme.
description-flow-record: Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2019 (WINFAP Files v8).
description-catchment: Chalk with large Boulder Clay cover. Rural catchment, arable with some forest and grassland, several small towns.
description-flow-regime: Regime influenced by groundwater abstraction/recharge. Abstractions for industry and agriculture. Some effluent returns.

name: Wittle at Quidenham
description-summary: Compound broad-crested weir gauging a Chalk catchment with large Boulder Clay overlay and predominantly arable land use. Flows are heavily affected by artificial influences.
description-general: Compound broad-crested weir (crest 3m), with central notch separated by splitter plates; situated under a road bridge.
description-station-hydrometry: No out of bank flow rating and weir known to drown during high flows which is not accounted for. Road embankment prevents bypassing. One rating applied across period of record. Theoretical rating modified by current meter measurements suitable to 0.64m.
description-flow-record: Weir drowned in 1968 floods. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in October 2018 (WINFAP Files v7).
description-catchment: Predominantly Chalk largely overlain with Boulder Clay. Predominantly arable land.
description-flow-regime: Flow regime altered by pumping of two boreholes into the river u/s of Quidenham to support Ely Ouse to Essex Transfer Scheme (abstraction point at Hockwold on the Little Ouse). This can lead to artifically raised flows during the summer. Other abstractions in the catchment.

name: Thet at Redbridge
description-summary: Crump profile gauging a Chalk catchment largely overlain with Boulder Clay and with predominantly agricultural land use, some artificial influences.
description-general: Crump profile weir, 4m broad. Ultrasonic flow gauge (sidelooker) installed in 2012 to measure non-modular flows more accurately.
description-station-hydrometry: Theoretical rating confirmed by current metering to structure full, thereafter rating allows for drowning and spilling, but there is significant scatter in gaugings beyond 0.3m. One rating applied across period of record. Since 2007 there has been an increase in the frequency of occurrence of non-modular flows, and since 2013 this station has been non-modular or drowned 90% of the time. This is thought to be caused by changes in land use downstream affecting downstream water levels. An ultrasonic flow gauge was installed in 2012. In modular flow conditions flows are calculated with the conventional rating, in non-modular conditions flows are calculated from the index-velocity rating based on the measurements of the ultrasonic flow gauge.
description-flow-record: Sept 1968 flooded entire area under water, maximum POR level recorded as 17.5cumecs, flow extrapolated as the river was out of bank. GDF and HIF POR updated in 2014. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in August 2021 (WINFAP Files v10).
description-catchment: Chalk largely overlain with Boulder Clay. Agricultural land use, predominantly arable.
description-flow-regime: Gw abstractions for PWS and industry; surface water abstractions for spray irrigation.

name: Larling Brook at Stonebridge
description-summary: Small concrete flume producing poor flow record because of permanent drowning. Station closed 2000.
description-general: A concrete flume of triangular cross-section with 1:1.5 side slopes, depth 0.8m. Station closed 2000.
description-station-hydrometry: Flume is permanently drowned: record very poor. Theoretical rating for in bank flows only applied across period of record.
description-flow-record: Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2023 (WINFAP Files v12).
description-catchment: Geology comprises Chalk overlain by glacial sand and gravel. Land use - rural, largely non arable.
description-flow-regime: Influenced by gw abstraction/recharge. Abstraction for agriculture/industry.

name: Stanford Water at Buckenham Tofts
description-summary: Discontinued station situated between two lakes used to measure discharge from pilot groundwater scheme in a Chalk catchment overlain by Boulder Clay, nearly natural flow at Q95.
description-general: Site used pre-existing broad-crested weir between two small lakes. Station was designed to measure discharge from pilot groundwater scheme area, although is largely natural. Lake outlet is at TL 834 953, joining Wissey 0.5 miles downstream of station. Punch tape recorder at upstream face introduced in Jan 1973. The recorder measured the level of the lake, and runoff of whole catchment drained to the lake, hence catchment area is calculated to the outlet. Watercourse is also referred to as Buckenham Tofts Stream.
description-station-hydrometry: Two peak flow ratings across period of record, the most recent is valid from October 1973.
description-flow-record: Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in August 2026 (WINFAP Files v15).
description-catchment: Chalk overlain by Boulder Clay with some gravel and alluvium in the valley. Predominantly impervious.
description-flow-regime: Natural to within 10% at Q95.

name: Snail at Fordham
description-summary: Flat V Crump (with a side weir in 1974-1985) gauging a predominantly rural and predominantly Chalk catchment with significant artificial influences.
description-general: Flat V Crump profile weir (Fordham No1 mill main station), 4m broad. From Oct 1974, a subsidiary Crump profile weir (Fordham No2 side stream station), 0.7m broad, measured bypass channel discharge. Flows were combined into single series. Side weir was removed in Dec 1984 and main weir rating adjusted to compensate (flows increased by 2%).
description-station-hydrometry: One rating applied across period of record, valid to modular limit. Flows prior to 1984 were calculated using tables and adding together flow at the main and side weir. Side weir was removed in Dec 1984 and main weir rating adjusted to compensate (flows increased by 2%). Part of the Lodes-Granta groundwater support scheme, operated according to site conditions.
description-flow-record: Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in August 2021 (WINFAP Files v10).
description-catchment: Predominantly Chalk covered by Boulder Clay in S part and containing some river terrace deposits. Land use largely rural with limited urbanised development (Newmarket).
description-flow-regime: Significant gw abstractions for PWS and surface water abstractions for spray irrigation.

name: Cam at Chesterford
description-summary: Compound broad-crested weir gauging a rural predominantly Chalk catchment largely overlain with Boulder Clay, significant artificial influences.
description-general: Compound broad-crested weir, 22.3m broad (in trapezoidal section) with central notch 3m broad, 0.23m deep. Previously called Chesterford Mill, and included millstream flow through old mill on the side of existing river channel.
description-station-hydrometry: Flow remains modular to 1.06m. One peak flow rating applied across period of record. Stage record before 14 May 1969 truncated at around 0.46m; peaks are therefore unknown over this period and the peak flow record present here starts on 14 May 1969. Prior to 1964, millstream flow was added to main weir rating using a rating table.
description-flow-record: Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in October 2018 (WINFAP Files v7) and August 2025 (WINFAP Files v14).
description-catchment: Predominantly Chalk largely overlain by Boulder Clay. Rural, predominantly arable land use.
description-flow-regime: Significant gw abstractions for PWS, with additional abstractions for industry/agriculture. Runoff increased by effluent returns.

name: Swaffham Lode at Swaffham Bulbeck
description-summary: Crump profile weir gauging a Chalk catchment with predominantly arable land use and significant artificial deposits.
description-general: Crump profile weir, 2.5m broad (wing wall height 1.6m), situated immediately upstream of road bridge. Prior to 1973 thin-plate weir, 1.45m broad. Also called Gutter Bridge.
description-station-hydrometry: Current theoretical rating fits well to gaugings. Two ratings applied across period of record, the most recent is valid from December-1973 when crump weir installed necessitating a change in rating. Part of the Lodes-Granta groundwater support scheme, operated according to site conditions.
description-flow-record: Data between 26-03-2017 to 09-04-2017 marked as suspect; tree branches were found to be blocking the weir. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in October 2018 (WINFAP Files v7) and August 2025 (WINFAP Files v14).
description-catchment: Chalk with no appreciable superficial deposits. Predominantly arable land use. Catchment boundary manually digitised due to issue with IHDTM incorrectly delineating the upper catchment.
description-flow-regime: Regime influenced by groundwater abstraction/recharge. Significant groundwater abstractions for public water supply. Runoff increased by effluent returns.

name: Granta at Stapleford
description-summary: Compound weir gauging a gw dominated Chalk catchment with predominantly arable land use.
description-general: Compound weir with Crump notch (1.5m broad) and broad-crested flanks (3m broad) superseded - in 1981 - original thin-plate weir.
description-station-hydrometry: NA
description-flow-record: Suspect flows in Sept 2005 may be due to artificial damming upstream. Some flows estimated, only monthly means are considered valid. Flows between 16/10/2013 and 20/10/2013 may be affected by debris accumulation.
description-catchment: Chalk catchment with significant Boulder Clay cover. Land use dominated by arable agriculture.
description-flow-regime: High baseflow component; area of groundwater catchment is less than topographical catchment.

name: Babingley at Castle Rising
description-summary: Crump weir gauging a river with high baseflow component. Catchment is predominantly Chalk bedrock and arable land.
description-general: Triangular profile Flat V Crump weir, 4.5m broad; level of wingwalls is 1.2m above crest.
description-station-hydrometry: Weir is subject to drowning. One rating applied from July 1976.
description-flow-record: Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in August 2021 (WINFAP Files v10).
description-catchment: Predominantly Chalk, patchy cover of Boulder Clay, sands, and gravels. Predominantly arable land use. Gw catchment area exceeds topographic divide.
description-flow-regime: High baseflow catchment. Significant gw abstraction for PWS and industry/agriculture. Runoff increased by effluent returns.

name: Granta at Babraham
description-summary: Structure gauging a Chalk catchment with some superficial deposits, predominantly arable land use, and significant artificial influences.
description-general: Triangular profile Flat V weir, 8.3m broad; constructed on an old brick weir. Height of wing walls above crest - 0.6m. Also called Babraham Hall.
description-station-hydrometry: The station is drowned and bypassed at high flows. Current rating accounts for out of bank flow. However, from 12.94cumecs (0.95m) floodplain flow is over a wide area with great uncertainty in flows, and no gaugings above 0.4m to verify rating. Two ratings applied across period of record, the most recent is valid from January 1979. Part of the Lodes-Granta groundwater support scheme, which triggers at 26 l/s to maintain flow.
description-flow-record: The POR maximum flow in Oct 2001 derived from peak flow measurements as 20.41 cumecs, but this is subject to considerable uncertainty - high proportion of overbank flows. Water year 1996/1997 rejected due to low confidence on whether AMAX occurred during a missing data period. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in August 2021 (WINFAP Files v10).
description-catchment: Chalk catchment with superficial deposits in headwater areas. Predominantly arable land use.
description-flow-regime: Regime influenced by gw abstraction/recharge. Significant gw abstractions for PWS and for industrial/agricultural uses. Runoff increased by effluent returns.

name: Quy Water at Lode
description-summary: Station gauging a rural, Chalk catchment with significant artificial influences.
description-general: Compound weir, 4.8m broad, with Crump profile centre section, 1m broad, 0.3m deep.
description-station-hydrometry: At flows greater than 0.32 cumecs flow occurs over broad-crested flanks between vertical side walls. Part of the Lodes-Granta groundwater support scheme, operated according to site conditions.
description-flow-record: Pre-1975 data imprecise.
description-catchment: Chalk catchment, with patchy superficial deposits of Boulder Clay and sands and gravels. Rural, predominantly arable.
description-flow-regime: In dry weather stream leaks through bed into the fen and can dry up. Three large abstractions in catchment for PWS.

name: Ouzel at Leighton Buzzard
description-summary: Structure gauging a predominantly rural catchment with Chalk bedrock and with some artificial influences. Some flow diverted immediately u/s of station.
description-general: Crump profile weir (6m broad) in trapezoidal section (7.5m broad). Eel tiles and baffles added to structure in 2016. Removed from peak flows dataset in September 2023 (WINFAP Files v12).
description-station-hydrometry: Weir subject to drowning at flows of approx. 4 cumecs. Some flow is diverted into a gravel pit through a weir (1m broad) located immediately u/s of station and infiltrates into Lower Greensand aquifer. Addition of low cost baffles and eel tiles in 2016 has minimal impact on rating. Rating does not fit well to gaugings during non-modular conditions.
description-flow-record: Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2019 (WINFAP Files v8). Data quality has been affected since approximately March 2022 due to lack of routine maintenance and vegetation growth at the weir, resulting in increased frequency of drowned and non-modular flow conditions. Flows during this period should be treated with caution.
description-catchment: Land in lower reaches is gently undulating. Predominantly Chalk. Rural catchment draining from the Chiltern escarpment.
description-flow-regime: Regime influenced by gw abstraction/recharge. Mainly industrial/agricultural abstraction. Some effluent returns.

name: Ouzel at Bletchley
description-summary: Constructed to measure flows just u/s of Milton Keys in a predominantly rural catchment with mixed geology, the station is located in a country park and is subject to vandalism.
description-general: Flat V weir, 10m broad. Constructed to measure flows just u/s of urban development (Milton Keynes). In a country park and subject to vandalism.
description-station-hydrometry: One rating applied across period of record. Floodplain flow accounted for, although not clear if accurate. Non modularity can occur as low as 0.8m, although rating only accounts for non-modularity at 1.3m.
description-flow-record: Peak flows rejected after 2012, when gaugings deviate from rating. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2020 (WINFAP Files v9).
description-catchment: Mixed geology - predominantly Upper and Lower Greensand, with some Chalk and Oxford Clay. Predominantly rural with mixed farming, Leighton Buzzard within catchment.
description-flow-regime: Flows augmented by effluent from Leighton Buzzard. Small gw abstractions.

name: Shep at Fowlmere One
description-summary: Station gauging a gw fed stream, opened as part of gw scheme.
description-general: Crump weir 1.1m wide installed in Mar 1983. Replaced a rectangular thin-plate weir operational from 1978. Station opened as part of gw scheme.
description-station-hydrometry: Weed growth d/s may affect flow. Bridge invert immediately d/s would cause drowning above 0.4cumecs. Part of the Rhee groundwater support scheme, which triggers at combined flow of 65 l/s at Fowlmere 1 and 2 to maintain flow.
description-flow-record: Levels from 1964. Mean annual runoff exceeds mean annual rainfall - this is under investigation (Jan 2008). Since 2014 occasional blockage on a grill covering a culvert just downstream of the site can result in unrealistically high flows which would be removed from the before loading to NRFA and infilled using linear infill where possible.
description-catchment: Very small, mainly gw fed, catchment draining from the Chalk. Rural, mainly arable with some grassland, marsh and woodland.
description-flow-regime: NA

name: Guilden Brook at Fowlmere Two
description-summary: Station opened as part of gw scheme to gauge a gw dominated stream.
description-general: Trapezoidal flume in trapezoidal, straight channel. Opened as part of gw scheme.
description-station-hydrometry: Part of the Rhee groundwater support scheme, which triggers at combined flow of 65 l/s at Fowlmere 1 and 2 to maintain flow.
description-flow-record: Access issues at station mean that field quality assurance checks cannot be performed. Use data with caution.
description-catchment: Very small, mainly gw fed, catchment draining the Chalk. Rural, mainly arable, some grassland, orchard and deciduous woodland. High baseflow contribution - groundwater catchment area exceeds topographical area, resulting in unrealistic runoff.
description-flow-regime: Abstraction u/s for spray irrigation.

name: Little Ouse at Knettishall
description-summary: Gauging a Chalk catchment with large Boulder Clay cover and predominantly arable land, flow record significantly affected by drowning and artificial influences.
description-general: Crump profile weir, 4.5m broad. Structure drowns above 3.35 cumecs. 3 wells constructed in 1987 to augment low flows. In 1979 replaced a broad crested weir called Knettishall Heath Weir located just u/s from current station. Removed from peak flows dataset in September 2020 (WINFAP Files v9).
description-station-hydrometry: Weir drowned regularly, particular in summer. Significant scatter in gaugings above 0.2m - removed from peak flow dataset for this reason. Rating is for the structure built in 1979 and has been applied to whole record.
description-flow-record: The 1960 flood level of 17.9mAOD (1.5m stage) was recorded on the Knettishall Heath Weir drawing.
description-catchment: Chalk catchment with large Boulder Clay cover. Predominantly arable.
description-flow-regime: Minor industrial/agricultural abstractions and returns. 3 wells constructed in 1987 to augment low flows. Flow in summer 2022 potentially affected by groundwater pumping scheme.

name: Whaddon Brook at Whaddon
description-summary: Station gauging a Chalk catchment with significant artificial influences.
description-general: Pre-cast fibreglass flume set in concrete; long-crested flume crest 0.1m broad.
description-station-hydrometry: Part of the Rhee groundwater support scheme, operated according to site conditions.
description-flow-record: Flow from 2014/11/20 to 2015/02/25 was likely non-modular. Flow from 2015/03/02 to 2015/06/15 may be affected by the Rhee Groundwater Support Scheme and flows during that period are higher than what could be expected based on nearby stations.
description-catchment: Chalk catchment used mainly for mixed farming but with significant built-up area (Royston).
description-flow-regime: Flows affected by effluent from Royston STW u/s of station.

name: Hiz at Hitchin
description-summary: Station gauging a small spring-fed stream with significant artificial influences.
description-general: Old concrete weir with crest reshaped by steel beam to form compound Crump profile, 6.2m wide; central notch 1m wide, 0.14m deep. Small spring fed stream flowing through Hitchin market place.
description-station-hydrometry: Part of the Thet-Little Ouse groundwater support scheme, which is triggered at Charlton Mill Pond.
description-flow-record: NA
description-catchment: Predominantly Chalk catchment with small amounts of sand, gravel and clay. Almost entirely arable land with only minor urban development.
description-flow-regime: Substantial abstractions for PWS. High baseflow - groundwater catchment area is less than the topographical area, resulting in notably low mean runoff. Local abstractions visible during March & April 2016.

name: Granta at Linton
description-summary: Station gauging a pump-supported stream draining from a rural catchment with some artificial influences.
description-general: Compound Crump Weir, 5.3m broad with 1.5m central crest.
description-station-hydrometry: Structure drowns when u/s water level exceeds about 0.46m. River is pump supported to maintain flow at approx. 0.03 cumecs; zero flows occur when pumps fail. Part of the Lodes-Granta groundwater support scheme.
description-flow-record: NA
description-catchment: Small Chalk catchment largely overlain with Boulder Clay. Land use is agricultural, predominantly arable land.
description-flow-regime: Some gw abstraction.

name: Cheney Water at Gatley End
description-summary: Crump weir gauging a spring fed pool in a very small catchment.
description-general: Crump weir, 0.3m broad. It dams a broad pool immediately u/s which is spring fed. The station was opened to monitor this spring as part of a gw scheme.
description-station-hydrometry: Only measures up to 0.073 cumecs (0.23 m), higher flows truncated. Part of the Rhee groundwater support scheme, which triggers at 0 l/s.
description-flow-record: The spring did not flow at all throughout 1997.
description-catchment: Superficial deposits free Chalk catchment. Rural, mainly arable farming.
description-flow-regime: Flows are affected by gw abstraction. Flows are now normally supported by gw pumping (pumps failed in 1998).

name: Lark at Fornham St Martin
description-summary: The station is situated on the River Lark at Fornham St. Martin, just downstream of Bury St Edmunds, and monitors a predominantly rural catchment. It features a Triangular Profile (Crump) weir with broad-crested flanking shoulders, as well as a flood bypass channel, which also includes a Triangular Profile (Crump) weir.
description-general: Site consists of three parts: Central crump profile low flow weir, 2.57 m wide, set between flanks which are treated as a broad-crested weir 0.796 m wide (rb width 0.66 m, lb width 0.136 m, length of crest 1.30 m), and a side-weir for flood relief purposes, which consists of a crump weir 5.17 m wide in a bypass channel.
description-station-hydrometry: One rating applied across period of record.
description-flow-record: Current rating does not appear to account for flow through the bypass channel. Analysis indicates that it tends to overestimate flows at the lower end and underestimate the higher gauged flows.
description-catchment: Predominantly rural catchment 110.2 km2 with Bury St Edmunds just upstream from the station.
description-flow-regime: NA

name: Yare at Colney
description-summary: Frequently bypassed structure gauging a rural, Chalk catchment with superficial deposits and with significant artificial influences.
description-general: A compound weir 11.9m wide reconstructed in Jan 1964 from single level broad-crested weir. The present structure has a Crump section 8.9m wide separated by a pier from a broad-crested weir at a lower level.
description-station-hydrometry: Mill sluices artificially regulate flow, but have little influence on flood flows. Frequent bypassing on the left bank. Road bridge built downstream in the late 1990s, after which all gaugings above 1m were taken which fit poorly to rating. One peak flow rating applied across period of record.
description-flow-record: Groundwater river support scheme extensively used in 1974, 1976 and 1990s to augment low flows. Not used in 2018, so flows are much lower. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2023 (WINFAP Files v12).
description-catchment: Topographical catchment exceeds contributing area (groundwater catchment), discrepancies along the south eastern boundary in the headwaters of the Blackwater and Tiffey. However the total estimated groundwater and surface water catchment areas are almost identical. No major changes during the period of record. Chalk catchment with superficial deposits, mainly Boulder Clay and alluvium - glacial till and some sand and gravel. Rural catchment, land use is predominantly arable.
description-flow-regime: Groundwater is abstracted for agricultural uses. Significant seasonal variations in abstractions due to the use of water for spray irrigation in the summer.

name: Tas at Shotesham
description-summary: Several times modified structure with poor rating in high flows and pre 1970 flows, gauging a rural, Chalk catchment overlain by till and with some artificial influences.
description-general: Originally a flume set between high rough walls bypassed at 14 cumecs. Reconstructed in 1970 as a Flat V Crump and a bypass channel with movable gates added in 1980 on the left bank, as part of Newton Flotman flood alleviation scheme.
description-station-hydrometry: Some high flows only partially gauged as water diverts around the station through the bypass channel. Bypass thought to cause more frequent drowning out. Bypass channel has not been successfully rated, due to inadequate records of gate position. Flood peaks derived assuming gate is fully open during flood conditions. No rating found applicable for the pre-1970 flume. Source of present rating unknown.
description-flow-record: Magnitude of flood peak in Sept 1968 is uncertain owing to bypassing, but was undoubtedly an exceptional event generated by 80-100mm rainfall. Peaks 25-28/04/1981 and 02-04/05/1981 suspect due to instrument fault. Period of 5 May- 25 August 1986 has been deleted due to anomalously low flows - probable stage shift. Data for Jan-Apr 1989 are missing due to instrument fault.
description-catchment: Groundwater catchment thought to be 24% smaller than the surface catchment (differences mainly in E). Predominantly Chalk, almost entirely overlain with drift, mainly Boulder Clay. Rural catchment, mainly arable. No major changes during the period of record.
description-flow-regime: Runoff reduced by groundwater abstractions for public water supply and agriculture. Runoff increased by effluent returns.

name: Bure at Ingworth
description-summary: Structure gauging a predominantly arable catchment with mixed geology and with some artificial influences and significant seasonal variation in flow.
description-general: Two ogee profile weirs beneath bridge arches. Wingwall height not known.
description-station-hydrometry: Arches bypassed (through low spots in the bank about 400m u/s) at 4.3 cumecs, but station maintains modularity. Occasionally drowns owing to weed and reed growth - some contention with coincident SSSI regime means that weed clearance is only done annually. One peak flow rating applied across period of record. Good fit to available gaugings.
description-flow-record: Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in October 2018 (WINFAP Files v7).
description-catchment: Mixed Clay and Chalk geology, overlain with superficial deposits of Boulder Clay and glacial sands and gravels. Agricultural land use, predominantly arable.
description-flow-regime: Important seasonal variation in flow. Runoff influenced by groundwater abstraction/recharge. Limited ground and surface water abstractions with some returns from public and agricultural uses.

name: Wensum at Costessey Mill
description-summary: Complex structure with crump weirs and gates gauging a rural, predominantly Chalk catchment overlain by deposits, with moderate artificial influences.
description-general: Complex structure comprising 30m Crump weir in main channel (crescent shape in plan view, but standard Crump profile slopes); the parallel mill channel has tilting gate and 1.5m wide Crump weir. Also artificial regulation by sluice action at Taversham. Removed from peak flows dataset in September 2019 (WINFAP Files v8).
description-station-hydrometry: The tilting gate is moved between three positions to maintain stable water level upstream and to maintain level through the mill race, and was fully automated in 1998. Each gate position has its own rating - when the gate moves, the station switches to the rating for that position. At 20-25 cumecs, which does not occur frequently, the station is bypassed further upstream on the left bank.
description-flow-record: Very low flows in July 2006 believed to be due to over-abstraction.
description-catchment: Predominantly Chalk catchment almost entirely overlain with superficial deposits, mainly Boulder Clay but with sands and gravels in valley bottoms. Rural, predominantly arable farming. No major changes during the period of record.
description-flow-regime: Moderate surface and gw abstractions, influential in low flow years. Runoff influenced by groundwater abstraction/recharge and surface water abstraction for Norwich. Mill sluices artificially regulate water levels, but have little influence on flood flows.

name: Tud at Costessey Park
description-summary: Structure gauging a Chalk catchment with gw catchment smaller than topographical catchment, some artificial influences.
description-general: Four trapezoidal standing-wave flumes under a road bridge.
description-station-hydrometry: Dam boards placed across the two outer arches to increase the sensitivity of low flow measurements. Dam boards are only used at very low flows, less than 1 cumec. Thought to be drowned above 10.5 cumecs (April 1981 flood). The rating is valid when all flumes are open. An alternative rating is used when dam boards are placed across the two outer arches for very low flows. Early part of the record affected by a mill structure u/s.
description-flow-record: Thought to be drowned above 10.5 cumecs during April 1981 flood. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2020 (WINFAP Files v9).
description-catchment: Gw catchment is smaller than the topographical catchment with consequent losses to adjacent catchments and low annual gauged runoff. Chalk catchment with superficial deposits, predominantly Boulder Clay, also sands and gravels and alluvium. Rural catchment with mixed farming, mostly arable.
description-flow-regime: Runoff influenced by groundwater abstraction/recharge, reduced by industrial/agricultural abstraction.

name: Waveney at Needham Mill
description-summary: Main weir and side weir gauging a rural catchment with clay and Chalk bedrock, weed growth and u/s sluice action apparent in flow record.
description-general: Compound Crump weir 8.5m wide in main channel with single crested Crump in mill bypass.
description-station-hydrometry: Suffers from weed growth problems. Sluice action at mill 2.4km u/s is infrequent but evident in flow records; sluice rarely open after 1985. Multiple ratings applied to period of record. Rating shapes comparable to bankfull/QMED before they diverge. Reasonable fit to gaugings. Rating takes account of both the main weir and the mill bypass. Flows between 16.8m3/s and 24.4m3/s are non-modular and flows over 25.5m3/s are non-modular with some bypassing of the weir accounted for by modelling.
description-flow-record: Record affected by the Waveney Groundwater Scheme between 1975 and 1979. Rating reviewed in 2022 and data reprocessed from 1980. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in August 2024 (WINFAP Files v13).
description-catchment: Clay and Chalk largely overlain with Boulder Clay. Rural, predominantly arable land.
description-flow-regime: Record affected by the Waveney Groundwater Scheme between 1975 and 1979 and during some summers e.g. Jun-Sep 2022. Rating reviewed in 2022 and data reprocessed from 1980.

name: Dove at Oakley Park
description-summary: Gauging a rural, Chalk and clay catchment with Boulder Clay cover, significant gw abstraction in 1975-1979 due to the Waveney Groundwater Scheme.
description-general: Compound Crump weir with low flow notch and crest tapping.
description-station-hydrometry: Non-modular at 13 cumecs and bypassed at 18 cumecs. Obstructions on the weir have occasionally led to erroneously high summer flows. Good fit to gaugings below 0.7m The SG value of 1.74m is believed theoretical and the FQ of 38.6 cumecs is an estimate (including the bypass), not a gauging. One rating applied across period of record. Station was reviewed in 2014 but rating was not changed because no method for estimating non-modular flows was found.
description-flow-record: No POT data are presented for this station as they have no non-modular flow correction applied. AMAX data have been corrected (pre-2007 only, affecting suitability for trend analysis), but in some cases can be below the daily flow as these are not corrected. Three suspect events in spring 2015 (2015/03/26, 2015/03/26, 2015/04/26, 2015/04/27, 2015/05/25, 2015/05/26) which also affect HIF for those months. Occasionally suffers from drops in level due to operation of upstream mill, identified by a large spike in GDF followed by a large drop. Examples of mill effects on 15/08/2016 and 15/09/2018. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2019 (WINFAP Files v8).
description-catchment: Chalk and clay catchment, largely overlain with Boulder Clay. Predominately arable land.
description-flow-regime: Records affected by the Waveney Groundwater Scheme between 1975 and 1979 and during some summers e.g. Jun-Sep 2022. Groundwater abstractions and effluent returns have a minor net effect on flows. Occasional effects from operation of upstream mill.

name: Ant at Honing Lock
description-summary: Structure utilising the fall of an old navigation lock, gauging a rural catchment with sand, gravel, and loam, some flow bypasses the station through a marsh u/s of station.
description-general: Crump type weir utilising the fall of an old navigation lock. No chart back up: limited space within kiosk.
description-station-hydrometry: One rating applied across period of record.
description-flow-record: Logger failure Jan 1998 so no DMFs. Suspect data in summer 1996. Pre-digital data peak flow data are rejected as stage cannot be reprocessed following a datum change pre-1992. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2019 (WINFAP Files v8). No data between 17 May 2019 to 3 July 2019 due to due to weir works to restore upstream levels.
description-catchment: Predominantly rural catchment of approximately half sand and gravel and half loam. Immediately u/s is a large marshy area with dense weed growth from which some flow bypasses the station.
description-flow-regime: Groundwater abstractions for public water supply moderately reduce the natural runoff.

name: Waveney at Billingford Bridge
description-summary: Compound site where bypassing and drowning can affect flows, gauging a Chalk catchment with Boulder Clay overlay, effects of Waveney Groundwater Scheme significant in 1975-1979.
description-general: Compound site of two structures located u/s of two bridge arches: a compound Crump with low flow notch and a simple Crump with lifting gate to retain higher summer levels. Removed from peak flows dataset in May 2016 (WINFAP Files v4).
description-station-hydrometry: Flows above 1.66 cumecs are only available when the structure gate is open, otherwise they cannot be calculated. Bypassing occurs at 6.4 cumecs, drowning can result from sluice action at Hoxne Mill (manual correction applied). The compound weir is insensitive and suffers occasional drowning due to d/s weed growth. Summer flows (e.g. July 2008) on the simple crump weir can be affected by partial gate movements. Partial gate movements due to maintenance are not logged and are unrated, resulting in erroneous data in the flow record.
description-flow-record: Affected by Waveney Groundwater Scheme between 1975 and 1979. Crest tapping blocked 25/11/2008-05/12/2008, estimation of hydrograph peak not possible. July 2008 flows on the simple crump weir affected by partial gate movements. Drop out in flows between 30th October 2016 and 6th November 2016 suspect, likely result of partial gate operation for maintenance.
description-catchment: Chalk catchment largely overlain with Boulder Clay, supporting mixed agriculture, predominantly arable land.
description-flow-regime: Runoff reduced by industrial/agricultural gw abstraction and by effluent returns.

name: Wensum at Fakenham
description-summary: Station gauging a Chalk catchment with mainly permeable soil types that contribute to muted flood response, minimal gw extractions.
description-general: Compound Crump with low flow notch, immediately u/s of Fakenham Mill. Removed from peak flows dataset in September 2019 (WINFAP Files v8).
description-station-hydrometry: An automated lifting gate for retaining summer levels acts as a sharp-crested weir. Gate is raised in winter to pass high flows. Unlikely to be bypassed apart from in exceptional events, not known to go non modular within operating range, theoretically rated. There are two ratings at the site, one for gate open and one for gate closed. When gate is up (open) there appears to be a small underestimation of flow by the rating, probably due to small amount of bypass at structure.
description-flow-record: No data for 17/01/2020 to 02/03/2020 due to manual gate movements. Unable to calculate flow when gate is manually operated.
description-catchment: Low-lying Chalk catchment largely overlain with Boulder Clay and some sands and gravels. Mainly permeable soil types. Predominantly arable.
description-flow-regime: Permeable soils contribute to muted flood response. Groundwater abstractions have a minimal impact on runoff.

name: Burn at Burnham Overy
description-summary: Crump weir gauging a gw influenced, rural catchment with Chalk bedrock overlain with superficial deposits and with only minor artificial influences, station is bypassed at high flows.
description-general: Compound Crump weir with three sections - central low flow crest 0.6m, flanked by two crests 1.2m wide each.
description-station-hydrometry: Bypasses at 2.3 cumecs. Can be affected by mill operations c 50m u/s. One rating applied across period of record.
description-flow-record: Low flows in summer 2005 and 2008 affected by u/s mill operation. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2020 (WINFAP Files v9).
description-catchment: Predominantly Boulder Clay with some sand and gravel, underlying Chalk exposed in the valleys. Rural, predominantly arable.
description-flow-regime: Gw-influenced regime, annual hydrographs reflect high baseflow component from the Chalk aquifer. Industrial/agricultural abstraction reduces natural runoff but impacts are minimal. Effluent returns increase runoff and may produce a minor net import from outside the catchment.

name: Wensum at Swanton Morley Total
description-summary: Total flow of a compound site gauging a rural catchment, predominantly Chalk overlain with drift, and with moderate artificial influences.
description-general: Two structures 150m apart operate in parallel. There is a two-arch bridge with two crump weirs and a three-arch bridge with three crump weirs in the arches.
description-station-hydrometry: Beneath the two-arch bridge are two Crump weirs which sometimes display non-modular flow as a result of summer weed growth d/s.
description-flow-record: NA
description-catchment: Chalk overlain by drift (predominantly Boulder Clay with sands and gravels). Rural, predominantly arable land.
description-flow-regime: Gw abstractions cause a moderate reduction in the natural runoff.

name: Stiffkey at Warham
description-summary: Gauging a rural, Chalk catchment, largely covered with Boulder Clay, with gw-influenced regime and significant artificial influences.
description-general: Flat V weir with crest tapping, 4m wide. ADCP installed in 2012 and used when the structure becomes non-modular.
description-station-hydrometry: Drowns above 0.8 cumecs. Riffle constructed d/s. One rating applied across period of record. Prior to 1978 (when dredging took place) d/s weed growth during summer months could cause complete drowning of gauging structure at lower flows.
description-flow-record: No POT data are presented for this station as they have no non-modular flow correction applied. AMAX data have been corrected, but in some cases can be below the daily flow as these are not corrected. HIF in July 2015 is not aligned with the highest GDF for that month.
description-catchment: Chalk catchment largely covered with Boulder Clay. Rural, predominantly arable.
description-flow-regime: Groundwater-influenced regime. Large gw abstractions for PWS, in addition to industrial/agricultural abstractions, cause a significant reduction in the natural runoff.

name: Bure at Horstead Mill
description-summary: Station gauging a rural catchment, flow record significantly affected by flow control operations.
description-general: Compound Crump weir consisting of 5 Crumps: 4 at fixed levels, the narrowest of which incorporates a fish pass. A vertical lift gate converts the largest to a sharp edge weir, this gate is used, during summer months, to retain u/s water levels.
description-station-hydrometry: NA
description-flow-record: Hydrograph closely reflects mill gate operation. Data for 1997 - 2000 was reprocessed and loaded in 2003, previous data was suspect owing to error in rating.
description-catchment: Low lying rural catchment of sand and gravel.
description-flow-regime: Limited ground and surface water abstractions u/s.

name: Gipping at Constantine Weir
description-summary: Structure located in Ipswich, within a tidal range, gauging a rural, predominantly Chalk catchment. Only measures flow at low tide, retained for estimation of peak flows.
description-general: A 152 ft long, broad-crested weir with a sluice gate, located within the tidal range (thus strictly on the Orwell, not Gipping). Station is retained primarily for estimation of high flows.
description-station-hydrometry: Only measures flow at low tide. U/s and d/s bends are measured to correct for drowning. Weir calibrated by model tests, no checks made.
description-flow-record: Large gaps in periods of unreliable data.
description-catchment: Boulder Clay overlying Chalk. Predominantly rural catchment, the only major town is Ipswich where the station is located.
description-flow-regime: Gw-influenced regime. Major artificial influences but net import is minor. Runoff reduced by industrial/agricultural abstraction. High flows affected since late 1980s by the Ipswich Flood Defence Scheme.

name: Deben at Naunton Hall
description-summary: Compound crump weir gauging a rural catchment, affected by bypassing, weed growth, and artificial influences.
description-general: A compound Crump (with crest tapping) and low flow notch.
description-station-hydrometry: Bypassing occurs at 12 cumecs and seasonal weed growth causes drowning.
description-flow-record: NA
description-catchment: Mainly clay and Chalk, overlain primarily by Boulder Clay and also some sands and gravels. Rural catchment, predominantly arable land.
description-flow-regime: Some gw is transferred to beyond the catchment boundary and some is abstracted from within the catchment. The overall impact is to significantly reduce the natural runoff.

name: Alde at Farnham
description-summary: Broad-crested weir gauging a rural, groundwater-influenced, clay and Chalk catchment.
description-general: Broad-crested weir of ogee section with low flow notch and steel plate divide walls.
description-station-hydrometry: Rating is non-modular at high flows (above 0.838m stage) and flows go out of bank; rating confirmed by gaugings. Rating accounts for drowning but significant scatter in gaugings between 0.6m and 1.1m. Outside of this range rating fits well to gaugings. One rating applied across period of record.
description-flow-record: No POT data are presented for this station as they have no non-modular flow correction applied. AMAX data have been corrected, but in some cases can be below the daily flow as these are not corrected. AMAX data are calculated through the extrapolated range of the modular rating for non-modular flows and all flows over 15.5 cumecs (0.838m) are overstimated. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in October 2018 (WINFAP Files v7).
description-catchment: The gw contours show only token relationship to the surface topography. Predominantly clay and Chalk, overlain mainly by Boulder Clay and some sands and gravels. Rural, predominantly arable land.
description-flow-regime: Gw-influenced regime. Significant gw abstractions for industry/agriculture, some water exported from the catchment.

name: Ore at Beversham
description-summary: Compound crump weir gauging a rural catchment with clay and Chalk bedrock. Flows affected by some artificial influences.
description-general: A compound Crump weir with low flow notch and crest tapping.
description-station-hydrometry: Drowning starts below QMED and has significant impact on flows, occasionally drowns as a result of d/s weed growth and siltation. One rating applied across period of record.
description-flow-record: No POT data are presented for this station as they have no non-modular flow correction applied. AMAX data have been corrected, but in some cases can be below the daily flow as these are not corrected. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2019 (WINFAP Files v8).
description-catchment: Gw-influenced regime, gw catchment exceeds topographic catchment. Predominantly clay and Chalk bedrock overlain with Boulder Clay and sand and gravel. Rural, predominantly arable land.
description-flow-regime: Industrial/agricultural abstraction or gw causes a moderate reduction in natural runoff.

name: Gipping at Stowmarket
description-summary: Structure able to contain all flows, gauging a flashy rural catchment with some artificial influences.
description-general: Compound Crump weir rebuilt in 1966 from a compound broad-crested weir, with spillway in tail.
description-station-hydrometry: All flows contained with one rating applied across period of record. Modular throughout range of flows. Eel pass installed in summer 2017, pumped but with negligible flow.
description-flow-record: Missing data in June and July 2017 due to equipment removed from site for renovation. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in October 2018 (WINFAP Files v7).
description-catchment: Minimal natural storage within the catchment, flashy response. Predominantly clay and Chalk largely overlain with Boulder Clay with valley sand and gravel. Rural, mainly arable land, some urban development just u/s of station.
description-flow-regime: Industrial/agricultural abstractions broadly balance with effluent returns. High flows have been significantly affected by flood relief scheme since the late 1980s.

name: Gipping at Bramford
description-summary: Compound Crump weir gauging a rural, gw-influenced, clay and Chalk catchment with significant artificial influences.
description-general: Compound Crump weir with 2m, 5m & 12m sections. The largest section is in the middle and uses flood gate (automated during summer 2001) to convert to a sharp-edge weir. The 5m weir, on the left, is heavily truncated on the down slope - historically used for narrow boat transition. The weir on the right side is the lowest, or "fish-pass" weir.
description-station-hydrometry: Bypassing occurs at 12 cumecs and sluice operation on the weir is evident in the daily flow record. Separate ratings for open and closed gates apply to period of record.
description-flow-record: Missing data 03-04-2017 as gates removed while eel pass constructed, resulting in erroneous data. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2020 (WINFAP Files v9). WY2018/2019 marked as rejected because the AMAX is on a data spike due to gate movement. GDF have been infilled. Gate opening and closing can cause issues with AMAX data, use with caution.
description-catchment: Predominantly clay and Chalk, overlain by superficial deposits - mainly Boulder Clay and some crag deposits. Rural, predominantly arable land, some urban development in the valley.
description-flow-regime: Groundwater-influenced regime. Groundwater abstractions have a significant impact on the natural runoff.

name: Blyth at Holton
description-summary: Station gauging a rural catchment very responsive to rainfall and with significant artificial influences.
description-general: An asymmetric compound Crump weir with low flow notch.
description-station-hydrometry: NA
description-flow-record: NA
description-catchment: Surface geology dominated by Boulder Clay, with sands, gravels and crag deposits. The land use is predominantly rural.
description-flow-regime: Gw abstractions have a significant effect on the natural runoff and stage, resulting in reduced flow. The river responds very rapidly to rainfall.

name: Mill River at Newbourne
description-summary: Structure know to suffer from bypassing even at moderate flood flows, gauging a small rural catchment.
description-general: Trapezoidal sharp-edged weir in an old mill stream.
description-station-hydrometry: Site known to suffer from bypassing. Watercourse is an old mill stream on a steep valley side so flows tend not to return to the channel once overflowing occurs. Weir bypassed by moderate flood flows on many occasions.
description-flow-record: NA
description-catchment: Small rural catchment formed on Crag geology, outer suburbs of Ipswich at the upstream end.
description-flow-regime: Runoff reduced by industrial/agricultural abstraction.

name: Stour at Stratford St Mary
description-summary: Complex, theoretically rated station gauging a predominantly rural, predominantly Chalk catchment with a long period of record.
description-general: Three separate weirs and five sluice gates operated by Essex and Suffolk Water plc at Stratford St Mary WTW.
description-station-hydrometry: Extreme floods bypass on rb. Theoretically rated. Since Apr 1978 upper limit of reliable gauging 16 cumecs.
description-flow-record: Daily naturalised flows from 1932 to 1976.
description-catchment: Chalk overlain by Boulder Clay in upper catchment and London Clay in lower part. Predominantly agricultural land use, mainly arable, but some towns present in the catchment.
description-flow-regime: Gw-influenced regime. WTW (including PWS abstractions) and, to lesser extent Ely/Ouse Transfer Scheme (since 1971), highly influence flow. Runoff increased by effluent returns.

name: Glem at Glemsford
description-summary: Trapezoidal flume gauging a gw-influenced, rural catchment, bypassing at high flows and with problematic rating.
description-general: Trapezoidal flume.
description-station-hydrometry: Bypassing at high flows, occasional problems with weed growth. Modest modular limit, but downstream level recorder can allow for drowning. Flow appears to go non-modular around 0.75m, but drowning may be variable, caused at least in part by the Stour downstream. Gaugings above 1m are float runs and do not account for bypassing. Highest floods unreliably gauged. From Oct 1969, the rating applied allows for average drowning conditions. Two peak flow ratings applied across period of record, derived from a combination of theory and hydraulic modelling. Affected by Cranmore Green borehole pumping, e.g. elevated flows 05-07-18 to 30-07-18.
description-flow-record: No POT data are presented for this station as they have no non-modular flow correction applied. AMAX data have been corrected, but in some cases can be below the daily flow as these are not corrected. Naturalised flows from 1960 to Sep 1976. Exceptional minimum in Oct 1997 follows cessation of augmentation (via Cranmore Green outfall) in Sept 1997. Flow during summer 2017, 2018, 2019 and 2022 affected by Cranmore Green augementation borehole, hence abrupt high values. GDF POR reprocessed in 2014. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2019 (WINFAP Files v8).
description-catchment: Rural catchment of the Upper Stour. Upper Chalk (exposed in river valley sides) is overlain by glacial sand and gravel and semi-pervious Boulder Clay. Rural, predominantly arable land.
description-flow-regime: Gw-influenced regime. Runoff reduced by industrial/agricultural abstraction.

name: Box at Polstead
description-summary: Gauging a rural, predominantly London Clay and Chalk catchment with superficial deposits and with only minor artificial influences. Station is occasionally affected by weed growth.
description-general: Trapezoidal flume with high flow rated spillway. Throat tapping.
description-station-hydrometry: Subject to reed/weed growth problems. One rating applied across period of record. Non-modular flows recorded since 1997 using secondary instrument.
description-flow-record: No POT data are presented for this station as they have no non-modular flow correction applied. AMAX data have been corrected, but in some cases can be below the daily flow as these are not corrected. Naturalised flows from 1961 to 1976. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2020 (WINFAP Files v9).
description-catchment: Predominantly London Clay; Chalk in N, all overlain by Boulder Clay and some sands and gravels. Rural, predominantly arable land.
description-flow-regime: Gw-influenced regime. Minimal ground and surface water abstractions for agricultural/industrial purposes. Runoff increased by effluent returns.

name: Chad Brook at Long Melford
description-summary: An 'Essex' profile with side weir which can be affected by drowning in summer, gauging a rural, Chalk catchment completely covered with Boulder Clay.
description-general: 'Essex' profile (modified Flat V Crump) weir with low flow side weir.
description-station-hydrometry: Low flow side weir drowns in summer due to weed growth. Poorly maintained channel also influences modular limit. High flow spillway accurate to 1.1m. Theoretically rated. Full range with convincing water-balance but low flow data should be treated as indicative only. One rating applied across period of record.
description-flow-record: Naturalised flows from 1965 to 1976. Missing data in 2010 and 2011 is as a result of water level management practices which caused the structure to become non-modular. Magnitude of POR maximum flow in Sept 1968 is supported by EA, but may be an underestimate as flow known to have been extrapolated. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2019 (WINFAP Files v8).
description-catchment: Chalk with complete cover of Boulder Clay. Rural catchment, predominantly arable farming.
description-flow-regime: Gw-influenced regime. Runoff reduced by industrial/agricultural abstraction.

name: Brett at Hadleigh
description-summary: 'Essex' profile gauging a rural, Upper Chalk semi-pervious catchment with some artificial influences.
description-general: 'Essex' profile (modified Flat V Crump) weir with low flow side weir and high flow rated spillway. D/s water level recorder to allow for drowning. Station removed from peak flows dataset in August 2024 (WINFAP Files v13).
description-station-hydrometry: Drowning compensated for using d/s water level recorder. Rating potentially overestimates flows below 0.6m but this is slight. One rating applied across period of record.
description-flow-record: No peak flow data are presented for this station as uncertainty related to non-modularity mean there is limited confidence in high flows. Naturalised flows from 1962 to 1976. Since 1976, adjustments for gw abstractions no longer made to the DMFs.
description-catchment: Upper Chalk largely covered mainly with semi-pervious Boulder Clay and some sands and gravels. Predominantly rural catchment, mainly arable land.
description-flow-regime: Gw-influenced regime. Since 1976, adjustments for gw abstractions for PWS and industrial abstraction from surface water are no longer made to the gauged daily mean flows. Minor effluent returns may affect flow.

name: Stour at Langham
description-summary: Station provides high quality record from a rural catchment with minor urban areas, although some bypassing and artificial influences are significant.
description-general: Twin-trapezoidal flume with throat tapping. Spillway channel with broad-crested weir constructed in 12/1985 takes some flow above 1.45m. Excellent site.
description-station-hydrometry: Bypassing occurs over opposite bank above 1.85m. More bypassing possible from 0.5km u/s during extreme events. One rating applied across period of record. Throat tapping installed during flume construction. Around 2003 the data from this point moved from chart to logger. No adjustments are made to flows, or thought necessary, for non-modularity. Above a stage of 1.435m, spillway flow should be added to rated flow.
description-flow-record: No POT data are presented for this station as they have no spillway correction applied. AMAX data have been corrected, but in some cases can be below the daily flow as these are not corrected. June and July 2008 affected by PWS abstractions. Naturalised flows to September 1976. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2020 (WINFAP Files v9).
description-catchment: Chalk outcrops in N, London Clay in S, overlain by superficial deposits, mainly semi-pervious Boulder Clay. Mainly rural catchment, predominantly arable land, with minor urban development in valley bottom.
description-flow-regime: Gw-influenced. Runoff reduced by surface water and ground water abstraction for PWS, industry and agriculture. Decreased flow since ~2014 due to increased intake for PWS. Occasional augmentation from Stour Augmentation Groundwater Scheme (SAGS) borehole pumping, and intermittent pumping from Ely/Ouse Transfer Scheme. Occasional peaks due to mill operation. Pumping periodically carried out on the Stour, resulting in noisy stage value and observed as a step up in stage from September 2019 to October 2019.

name: Belchamp Brook at Bardfield Bridge
description-summary: Station provides good quality, close to natural, record from a rural catchment with mixed geology.
description-general: Trapezoidal flume with throat tapping.
description-station-hydrometry: Full range station in winter, occasionally drowns in summer due to weed growth. One rating applied across period of record. Confirmed by gaugings to 1.6m.
description-flow-record: No POT data are presented for this station as they have no non-modular flow correction applied. AMAX data have been corrected, but in some cases can be below the daily flow as these are not corrected. Naturalised flows from 1965 to 1976, only minimal adjustments needed to flows since then. Daily flow POR reprocessed in 2014. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2019 (WINFAP Files v8).
description-catchment: Chalk in N, clays in S, all overlain mainly by Boulder Clay and some sands and gravels. Rural, predominantly arable land.
description-flow-regime: Gw-influenced regime. Runoff reduced by industrial/agricultural abstraction. Natural flow to within 10% at Q95.

name: Stour at Westmill
description-summary: Record of low accuracy from a rural, Upper Chalk catchment with major artificial influences. The site theoretically has a modular limit of around 1.7m.
description-general: Compound trapezoidal critical depth flume with d/s level recorder.
description-station-hydrometry: Affected by weed growth but rarely drowns out. Above 1.15m some flow passes over a broad-crested weir 100m u/s into a spillway. The gaugings for this station are float runs and are less accurate than standard methods and result in some scatter around the rating. One rating applied across period of record. Affected by non-modular flow.
description-flow-record: No POT data are presented for this station as they have no non-modular flow correction applied. AMAX data have been corrected, but in some cases can be below the daily flow as these are not corrected. Archived daily flows adjusted for the effects of Ely/Ouse Transfer Scheme until 1976. Peak flow in December 2014 not available (non-modular). Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2022 (WINFAP Files v11).
description-catchment: Upper Chalk overlain by superficial deposits, mainly semi-pervious Boulder Clay and some sand and gravel. Rural, predominantly arable land.
description-flow-regime: Gw-influenced regime. Since 22/3/1971, flow augmented by intermittent pumping from the Ely/Ouse Transfer Scheme. Runoff also influenced by industrial/agricultural abstraction from surface and groundwater, and effluent returns.

name: Brett at Cockfield
description-summary: 'Essex' profile gauging a small, rural, close to natural, catchment with Upper Chalk covered with Boulder Clay.
description-general: 'Essex' profile (modified Flat V Crump weir). No spillway.
description-station-hydrometry: Modular limit of 0.66m theoretically derived; secondary instrument to record non-modular flows installed in 2003. Lack of gaugings at high flows. One rating applied across period of record.
description-flow-record: No POT data are presented for this station as they have no non-modular flow correction applied. AMAX data have been corrected, but in some cases can be below the daily flow as these are not corrected. Naturalised flows from 1969 to 1976, only minimal adjustments needed since. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2020 (WINFAP Files v9).
description-catchment: Upper Chalk completely covered with Boulder Clay. Rural, predominantly arable land.
description-flow-regime: Natural to within 10% at Q95.

name: Bumpstead Brook at Broad Green
description-summary: 'Essex' profile gauging a small, rural, virtually natural catchment.
description-general: 'Essex' profile (modified Flat V Crump) weir with crest tapping and high flow spillway.
description-station-hydrometry: Modular limit approx. 6.0 cumecs. Approx. limit of gauging is 12.5 cumecs. Bypassing estimated to start at 1.2m. Rating accounts for non-modular flow above 6 cumecs. One rating applied across period of record.
description-flow-record: No POT data are presented for this station as they have no non-modular flow correction applied. AMAX data have been corrected, but in some cases can be below the daily flow as these are not corrected. Highest gauging taken in 1968 and is an estimate. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2020 (WINFAP Files v9).
description-catchment: Chalk and glacial gravel in the catchment completely overlain with Boulder Clay. Rural, predominantly arable land.
description-flow-regime: Some industrial/agricultural abstraction, but natural to within 10% at Q95. Only minor adjustments needed, virtually natural catchment.

name: Stour Brook at Sturmer
description-summary: 'Essex' profile weir gauging a small, groundwater-influenced catchment with significant artificial influences.
description-general: 'Essex' profile (modified Flat V Crump) weir with crest tapping, insensitive.
