description-station-hydrometry: Modular limit approx. 5.0 cumecs. Rating accounts for non-modular flow. One rating applied across period of record.
description-flow-record: No POT data are presented for this station as they have no non-modular flow correction applied. AMAX data have been corrected, but in some cases can be below the daily flow as these are not corrected. Flood in Sept 1968 inundated the station and has been separately estimated. Adjustments were made for industrial and sewage effluent and gw abstractions from 1968 to 1976. AMAX events in Nov 2000, Feb 2009 and Nov 2014 rejected as suspect crest tapping data affected non-modular adjustment. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2022 (WINFAP Files v11).
description-catchment: Chalk with superficial deposits, mainly Boulder Clay. Upper catchment is mainly rural (arable farming), considerable urban development (Haverhill) in lower catchment.
description-flow-regime: Gw-influenced regime. Runoff reduced by industrial/agricultural abstraction. Station is immediately d/s of Haverhill - urban runoff and STW discharges cause short, sharp peaks.

name: Stour at Kedington
description-summary: Insensitive 'Essex' profile gauging a small, rural, Chalk catchment.
description-general: 'Essex' profile (modified Flat V Crump) weir with crest tapping. No spillway.
description-station-hydrometry: Insensitive. High downstream levels make estimate of flow peak uncertain. Ponding u/s above 11.5 cumecs. Rating above bank full tends to overestimate flows. Crest tapping prone to siltation which made modular limit uncertain until 1970, when channel improved for Ely/Ouse Transfer Scheme, making station full range. Structure built on peat, some percolation beneath. Adjustments have been to flows to account for non-modularity. One rating applied across period of record.
description-flow-record: Station was completely overwhelmed in Sept 1968 floods, which is the highest event on record. Post 1976 adjustments made for Ely/Ouse Transfer Scheme. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2022 (WINFAP Files v11).
description-catchment: Boulder Clay overlying Chalk, some outcropping. Rural, predominantly arable land.
description-flow-regime: Gw-influenced regime. Effect of Transfer Scheme results in unrealistic water balance. Abstraction from surface water and gw for industrial/agricultural purposes. Runoff increased by effluent returns.

name: Brett at Higham
description-summary: Station gauging the whole catchment of R Brett, heavily affected by drowning.
description-general: 'Essex' profile (modified Flat V Crump) weir with crest tapping. Located approx. 450m u/s from confluence with R. Stour.
description-station-hydrometry: Flows not calculated when drowning. Very low modular limit due to backing up from Essex and Suffolk Water plc waterworks on Stour at Stratford St Mary.
description-flow-record: Record is incomplete due to drowning, gaps present especially before 2003.
description-catchment: Upper Chalk covered with semi-pervious Boulder Clay N of Hadleigh, lower reaches mainly London Clay overlain by superficial deposits. Predominantly rural catchment (except for Hadleigh).
description-flow-regime: NA

name: Stour at Lamarsh
description-summary: Station using float runs for gauging a predominantly rural catchment with mixed geology and with major artificial influences.
description-general: Flat V weir with low flow sharp-crested rectangular notch.
description-station-hydrometry: No spillway. Flood banks contain approx. 35 cumecs. Reasonable fit to gaugings up to bank full. Breaching u/s may cause bypassing. Gaugings for this station are float runs, and less accurate than standard methods. One rating applied across period of record.
description-flow-record: No POT data are presented for this station as they have no non-modular flow correction applied. AMAX data have been corrected, but in some cases can be below the daily flow as these are not corrected. Naturalised flows 1972-1976, since then adjustments needed for abstractions, discharges and PWS predominantly for Haverhill. First year of record rejected due to partial data. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2022 (WINFAP Files v11).
description-catchment: Mainly Upper Chalk with some London Clay in S, overlain by superficial deposits (predominantly Boulder Clay). Mainly rural, predominantly arable land, some built-up areas.
description-flow-regime: Ely/Ouse Transfer Scheme adjustments already made. Runoff reduced by public water supply (predominantly for Haverhill), industrial and agricultural abstraction from surface water and gw. Runoff increased by effluent returns. Flow affected by Ely/Ouse Transfer Scheme.

name: Roding at Redbridge
description-summary: A non-standard Essex profile Flat V weir based in the Roding catchment with rural headwaters but influenced by urban development in the lower reaches. The flow regime has artificial influences.
description-general: Originally a broad crested weir but was replaced due to insensitivity at low flows. Replaced by the current Essex profile weir (modified Flat V weir) in 1962. Used for both flood warning/forecasting and water resource purposes.
description-station-hydrometry: One peak flow rating applied across period of record. Rating may not estimate flow accurately above 1m. Calibration above 35 cumecs is based upon model tests.
description-flow-record: Significant floods in Nov 1974 and Oct 2000. Questions whether gauge drowned during these events. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2022 (WINFAP Files v11).
description-catchment: Low lying, mainly impervious (London Clay and superficial deposits) catchment. Land use is rural with significant urban development close to the G/s.
description-flow-regime: Pattern of low flows influenced by abstractions and effluent returns. Flows augmented by moderate net import of water from Thames Water Utilities but this was eliminated to produce naturalised flows between 1951-1975. The diversion of Luxborough Lane STW effluent, completed in 1987, reduced DMFs in Redbridge.

name: Chelmer at Rushes Lock
description-summary: Station with complex hydrometric history with rural catchment on London Clay with significant urban development.
description-general: Sharp-crested, shallow V profile weir (insensitive), replaced broad-crested timber weir in 1972.
description-station-hydrometry: Complex hydrometric history. Weir provides head for lock (navigable river), discharge through lock not measured. Lock thought to influence flow pattern at low flows during busy periods, e.g. in summer of 2006. Weir repaired in 1982 because of serious leakage. No accurate measure of low or high flow, upper limit is 0.7m (19.99 cumecs). Bypassing begins at 0.57m.
description-flow-record: GDF in 2006 may be affected by lock. Weir was being repaired in 1982 to fix serious leakage.
description-catchment: Mainly London Clay with extensive superficial deposits (predominantly Boulder Clay). Overall rural (arable farming), but significant urban development (especially Chelmsford u/s of station) and with dense road network.
description-flow-regime: NA

name: Ter at Crabbs Bridge
description-summary: Long period of record from a rural catchment, includes daily flow record of a former, less accurate station Hatfield Peverel.
description-general: Trapezoidal flume with throat tapping and low flow control, replaced less accurate station - Hatfield Peverel, 900m d/s, in 1964. Hatfield Peverel record held with this station (1932-1964).
description-station-hydrometry: Theoretically rated. Modular limit ~0.2m, depending on downstream weed, no level yet recorded above 1.6m (structurefull). Scatter in gaugings beyond QMED caused by drowning. One peak flow rating applied across period of record.
description-flow-record: No POT data are presented for this station as they have no non-modular flow correction applied. AMAX data have been corrected. Records in 1932-1964 are from a former, less accurate Hatfield Peverel station. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2020 (WINFAP Files v9).
description-catchment: London Clay, overlain with superficial deposits, mainly Boulder Clay and some sands and gravels. Rural, predominantly arable land.
description-flow-regime: Minor surface water abstractions for spray irrigation, small discharges from STW but net export through PWS.

name: Blackwater at Langford
description-summary: Complex of weirs and sluices gauging a predominantly rural catchment of R. Blackwater and monitoring intake of what was the Southend Water Company.
description-general: Complex of weirs and sluices near the intake of what was the Southend Water Company. Measurement included the amounts abstracted from the R. Blackwater before it joins with R. Chelmer.
description-station-hydrometry: NA
description-flow-record: Quality of data is unknown.
description-catchment: Practically the whole catchment is covered with Boulder Clay, overlying glacial gravels. In the SE, London clay underlies the drift but is rarely exposed.
description-flow-regime: NA

name: Colne at Lexden
description-summary: Large trapezoidal flume, station provides flood warning for Colchester.
description-general: Large trapezoidal flume with d/s level recorder. Provides flood warning for Colchester.
description-station-hydrometry: Bypassed on the left bank at very high flows, at 1.75 m stage. Suffers badly from weed growth issues, which is cleared monthly. Out of bank flows may be underestimated due to bypassing. One peak flow rating applied across period of record. Reasonable fit to gaugings although rated flows are adjusted for non-modular conditions.
description-flow-record: No POT data are presented for this station as they have no non-modular flow correction applied. AMAX data have been corrected. Naturalised flows for period 1959 to 1976. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in August 2024 (WINFAP Files v13).
description-catchment: Mainly London Clay and some Upper Chalk, with superficial deposits of semi-pervious Boulder Clay and some sands and gravels. Rural, predominantly arable land.
description-flow-regime: Runoff reduced by surface water/groundwater abstraction for public water supply, industry and agriculture.

name: Can at Beach's Mill
description-summary: Compound flume within a mill race gauging a predominantly rural catchment with London Clay covered by Boulder Clay, and with significant artificial influences.
description-general: Triple throated compound flume (built within mill race). Trapezoidal centre section for low flows.
description-station-hydrometry: Limit of station is 35 cumecs. Spillway flow starts at around 2m - very significant part of flow, allowance for this not made in record. Two peak flow rating applied across period of record.
description-flow-record: Naturalised flows from 1962 to 1976. Period-of-record maximum flow in Oct 2000 may have been higher due to spillway flows. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in August 2024 (WINFAP Files v13).
description-catchment: London Clay overlain with Boulder Clay in N. Rural, predominantly arable land with some grassland and some built-up areas in the S of the catchment.
description-flow-regime: Industrial and sewage effluent discharges, adjustments needed for effluent discharges.

name: Wid at Writtle
description-summary: 'Essex' profile gauging a rural catchment on London Clay, flows significantly increased by STW effluent especially in summer.
description-general: 'Essex' profile (modified Flat V Crump) weir.
description-station-hydrometry: Rated spillway starts at 1.25m. Full range, modular station. Weir began to subside in 1991. Flow during summer months consists predominantly of STW discharge, of which approximately 0.08 cumecs is derived from outside the catchment, adjustments needed for this. One rating applied across period of record.
description-flow-record: Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2019 (WINFAP Files v8).
description-catchment: Low-lying catchment on London Clay with scattered areas of Boulder Clay cover. Mainly rural, mixed arable and grassland, with significant urban component.
description-flow-regime: Responsive catchment. Runoff increased by STW effluent returns with net import, which significantly affects flows especially in summer. Runoff reduced by industrial/agricultural abstraction.

name: Chelmer at Springfield
description-summary: 'Essex' profile located in Chelmsford gauging a predominantly rural catchment with mixed geology and some artificial influences.
description-general: 'Essex' profile (modified Flat V Crump) weir.
description-station-hydrometry: Full range station, no drowning. Gaugings from float-runs are thought to have overestimated flows. One rating applied across period of record.
description-flow-record: Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2019 (WINFAP Files v8).
description-catchment: Mainly Upper Chalk and London Clay largely covered with Boulder Clay. Predominantly rural (mainly arable farming) but with urban development (N Chelmsford) just u/s of station.
description-flow-regime: Surface water abstraction, mainly for spray irrigation, some industrial purposes. Gw abstractions from confined Chalk aquifer for PWS and industrial activities.

name: Brain at Guithavon Valley
description-summary: 'Essex' profile gauging an elongated, predominantly rural, catchment on London Clay overlain with superficial deposits, with some artificial influences.
description-general: 'Essex' profile (modified Flat V Crump) weir with throat tapping. Secondary instrument installed in 2003 to record non-modular flows.
description-station-hydrometry: Drowning occurs at very high levels but with limited non-modular flow. Station has throat tapping. Station prone to vandalism. One peak flow rating applied across period of record.
description-flow-record: No POT data are presented for this station as they have no non-modular flow correction applied. AMAX data have been corrected. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2019 (WINFAP Files v8).
description-catchment: London Clay with superficial deposits, mainly Boulder Clay and some sands and gravels. Predominantly rural, but some built-up areas (Braintree in mid-catchment and parts of Witham just u/s of station).
description-flow-regime: Runoff increased by effluent returns and reduced by industrial/agricultural abstraction.

name: Blackwater at Appleford Bridge
description-summary: Station gauging a groundwater-influenced rural catchment with major artificial influences.
description-general: Double throated trapezoidal flume with throat tappings and a high flow rated spillway.
description-station-hydrometry: Spilling onto spillway stats at 1.80m, drowning starts at 1.2m (13.0 cumecs). Degree of drowning variable. Rating accounts for non-modular flow. One peak flow rating applied across period of record.
description-flow-record: No POT data are presented for this station as they have no non-modular flow correction applied. AMAX data have been corrected, but in some cases can be below the daily flow as these are not corrected. Irregular record from 01/10/1962. POT independence criteria applied to early (chart) record appears to require separation of 7 days. Exceptionally high flow recorded in Oct 2001, magnitude suspect as likely to have been affected by drowning. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2023 (WINFAP Files v12).
description-catchment: London Clay with Chalk in the headwaters, overlain with Boulder Clay and some sands and gravels. Rural, predominantly arable land.
description-flow-regime: Gw-influenced regime. Intermittently affected, since 1971, by Ely/Ouse Transfer Scheme pumping, significantly affected in the late 1980s and in the 1990s. Abstractions from both Chalk and gravel aquifers for PWS.

name: Chelmer at Churchend
description-summary: Good record of a responsive, rural catchment with mixed geology and with minor artificial influences.
description-general: Trapezoidal flume (with central division wall which commences above the lowest contraction) with throat recorder and spillway for flows over 1.42m. Secondary instrument to record non-modular flows installed in 2003.
description-station-hydrometry: Measures up to the 1 in 10 year flood (approx. 1.69m) above which bypassing occurs. Drowning is minimal but more gaugings required at higher flows to confirm rating. Two rating applied across period of record confirmed by gaugings to 1.58m.
description-flow-record: The sudden drop in flow on 20/07/2015 may be due to works on Elmbridge Mill gates located downstream of Churchend at Little Easton. The periods of high flows from 2015/05/12 to 2015/05/16 and from 2015/06/05 to 2015/06/10 were probably cased by vandalism (dams on the weir) which often occurs in summer months. Missing data in September 2017 due to lightning strike which damaged telemetry and data logger. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2023 (WINFAP Files v12).
description-catchment: Upland (for East Anglia) catchment at head of R. Chelmer. Upper quarter of catchment is Chalk, remainder is London Clay, both largely overlain with Boulder Clay. Rural, predominantly arable farming.
description-flow-regime: Responsive catchment. Some industrial/agricultural abstraction but minimal adjustments needed.

name: Colne at Poolstreet
description-summary: Located in upper part of the Colne, with very low to no flows in summer.
description-general: Trapezoidal flume with throat tapping. High flow spillway.
description-station-hydrometry: Flume is rarely non-modular. High flows spill onto a spillway (above 1.34m) and flows above wingwall height (1.6m) are estimated because of major bypassing. One peak flow rating applied across period of record.
description-flow-record: No POT data are presented for this station as they have no non-modular flow correction applied. AMAX data have been corrected, but in some cases can be below the daily flow as these are not corrected. Missing data in 2020 due to levels below the lower limit of the rating. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2023 (WINFAP Files v12).
description-catchment: Upland (for East Anglia) catchment. Upper Chalk with London Clay present in southern half, all overlain with Boulder Clay and minor patches of sands and gravels. Rural, predominantly arable land.
description-flow-regime: Great Yeldham PWS borehole may influence flows, but unquantifiable. Period of Ely/Ouse Transfer Scheme pumping in 1982. Some industrial/agricultural abstraction.

name: Sandon Brook at Sandon Bridge
description-summary: Insensitive 'Essex' profile weir gauging a rural catchment with reservoirs affecting the regime.
description-general: 'Essex' profile (modified Flat V Crump) weir with crest tapping.
description-station-hydrometry: Insensitive. One peak flow rating applied across period of record. Modular limit around 0.6m. All but highest flows contained. The flow is derived through the rating curve and then under non-modular conditions, a macro is applied within WISKI which applies a reduction factor. Therefore, under high flows, the stage and flow won't match through the modular rating. Subject to weed growth and siltation, particularly downstream.
description-flow-record: No POT data are presented for this station as they have no non-modular flow correction applied. AMAX data have been corrected. Some float-run gaugings are thought to be unreliable. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in August 2021 (WINFAP Files v10).
description-catchment: Catchment area includes 13.7 sq km draining to Hanningfield Reservoir 10km upstream. London Clay with sand and gravel over high ground in northeast, Boulder Clay in south. Rural, mainly arable land with some grassland.
description-flow-regime: Reservoir(s) in catchment affect runoff. Naturalised flows (1963-1976) account for reservoir compensation water (0.011 cumecs) and storm overflows. Minor additions from industrial effluent.

name: Roding at High Ongar
description-summary: Highest flow gauging station on the River Roding. Essex modified Flat V weir that was superceded by Ultrasonic time of flight due to repeated drowning.
description-general: Ultrasonic time of flight in an 11m section. Ultrasonic replaced Essex weir rating in November 2012. Essex weir used to maintain head for measuring cross section. Used for both water resource and flood warning/forecasting purposes.
description-station-hydrometry: Originally Essex weir superseded by Ultrasonic time of flight with the weir used to retain depth. Bypassing can also occur on both banks and can occur surprisingly quickly. Structure subject to drowning during high flows due to backwater effects from two d/s bridges. Heavy in-channel vegetation and surcharging of bridge soffit also influence drowning. Evidence that the modular limit has reduced over time due to the reduction in channel clearance and maintenance. Evidence of weir settlement discovered in 1991. Flows were corrected from 1987-91 to take account of this.
description-flow-record: Levels can exceed bankfull and gauge is bypassed. Naturalised flows available between 1964 and 1976. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in August 2021 (WINFAP Files v10).
description-catchment: Generally low lying, largely impermeable (London Clay/glacial deposits), agricultural catchment with some industrial land use.
description-flow-regime: Responsive flow regime. Minimal net import into the catchment but flows are influenced by groundwater abstraction/recharge. Abstraction for industrial/agricultural purposes, particularly spray irrigation, can substantially deplete low flows.

name: Cripsey Brook at Chipping Ongar
description-summary: Flat V weir located on Crispey Brook, a North London sub-catchment of the River Roding.
description-general: Flat V weir (5.6m broad) installed in 1981. It superseded a compound thin-plate weir of limited capacity.
description-station-hydrometry: Modular calibration - therefore over-estimation of flows during periods of drowned flow (e.g. autumn 2000 - exceptionally high flow on the 29th Oct.). The Flat-V weir drowns at mid-flows, and at higher flows the railway arch downstream becomes the control. Bypassing during high flows.
description-flow-record: Most early flows truncated at around 2.5 cumecs. Flows missing (probably including POR minima) for much of 1976.
description-catchment: Predominantly impermeable catchment (London Clay but with extensive areas of glacial deposits). A rural catchment where agriculture is the primary land use.
description-flow-regime: Responsive flow regime. Sewage effluent is an important component of low flows. Impact of abstraction also evident on the hydrograph.

name: Pant at Copford Hall
description-summary: 'Essex' profile 5km d/s of the Great Sampford Outfall which is part of Ely/Ouse Transfer Scheme and has major impact on flows.
description-general: 'Essex' profile (modified Flat V Crump) weir (insensitive) with crest tapping.
description-station-hydrometry: Measures up to 12.0 cumecs, flows above this are estimated because they spill on a spillway. One peak flow rating applied across period of record.
description-flow-record: No POT data are presented for this station as they have no non-modular flow correction applied. AMAX data have been corrected, but in some cases can be below the daily flow as these are not corrected. First year of record rejected due to AMAX occurring during missing period. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in August 2021 (WINFAP Files v10). Missing data in June 2022 due to repairs being carried out at the station.
description-catchment: Predominantly Upper Chalk largely overlain by Boulder Clay. Glacial gravels exposed along the whole river valley. Rural, predominantly arable land.
description-flow-regime: Intermittent pumping of Ely/Ouse Transfer Scheme has major effect on station, which is only 5km d/s of the Great Sampford Outfall. Some industrial/agricultural abstraction.

name: Blackwater at Stisted
description-summary: 'Essex' profile gauging a predominantly Chalk catchment affected by artificial influences including urban runoff and Ely Ouse/Essex scheme.
description-general: 'Essex' profile (modified Flat V Crump) weir with crest tapping. No spillway.
description-station-hydrometry: Modest modular limit (around 0.62m) affected by weed growth. No spillway. VA rating for high flows. One peak flow rating applied across period of record. Some of the gaugings were based on float-runs and may not be reliable. Post-1979, flow is derived through the rating curve and then under non-modular conditions, a macro is applied within WISKI which applies a reduction factor. Therefore, under high flows, the stage and flow will not match through the modular rating. In the earlier record, however, adjustment for non-modularity appears to have been made by correcting the artifical elevation of stage, and these events therefore agree through the rating.
description-flow-record: No POT data are presented for this station as they have no non-modular flow correction applied. AMAX data have been corrected, but in some cases can be below the daily flow as these are not corrected. Flows can be artificially increased by Ely Ouse transfer scheme (e.g. June 2015). Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in August 2021 (WINFAP Files v10).
description-catchment: Upper two-thirds of catchment are Chalk, remainder London Clay (exposed in valleys), all overlain with Boulder Clay and some glacial gravel. Mainly rural (arable predominates) but with Braintree urban area in lower valley, just u/s of station.
description-flow-regime: Urban runoff from Braintree. Minor adjustments needed for ground and surface water abstractions, sewage and industrial effluent and Ely Ouse/Essex discharges. Net effect - minor export of water.

name: Ingrebourne at Gaynes Park
description-summary: Essex profile modified Flat V Crump weir situated in a rural headwater with artificial influences from urban land uses.
description-general: Essex profile (modified Flat V Crump) weir in 9.5m wide section, operated as a rated section. Used for both Water Resource and Flood Incident management. Only gauging station on the Ingrebourne river, approximately 7km upstream of confluence with the Thames.
description-station-hydrometry: All but exceptional floods contained. Operated as a rated section but rating based on modelled equation for Essex weirs. Model-based calibration assumes modularity; however, non-modular flow can occur as low as 0.4mASD depending on downstream conditions. Rating estimates of modular flow thought to be reasonable but tendancy to overestimate below Q70. No gaugings beyond QMED. One peak flow rating applied across period of record.
description-flow-record: Naturalised flow available for period 1970-75. Bypassing thought to have occurred during the three highest peaks in AMAX series. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in August 2025 (WINFAP Files v14).
description-catchment: Largely impermeable catchment (London Clay/glacial deposits). Rural headwaters but substantial urban development around lower reaches.
description-flow-regime: Runoff increased by effluent returns but reduced by industrial/agricultural abstraction. Minor net augmentation of runoff through transfer from River Beam. Reservoir(s) in the catchment affect runoff.

name: Beam at Bretons Farm
description-summary: An Essex modified Flat V Crump weir situated in a mainly rural headwaters with significant urban influences in lower reaches.
description-general: Essex (modified Flat V Crump) weir in 10.4m wide section. The weir is non-standard. Used for both water resource and flood risk management.
description-station-hydrometry: Model-based calibration assumes modularity and drowning is uncommon. Rating estimates of flow thought to be reasonable, gauged approaching QMED. One peak flow rating has been applied across the period of record. Levels are affected by Washlands gate and flap valve controlling flow into the Thames.
description-flow-record: Naturalised flows available 1966-7, there is a very small net diminution in runoff. The site is prone to vandalism and data has been lost between 01/07/00 - 28/01/01 and 18/04/2020 - 01/06/2020. Peak flows rejected during WY2000/2001 due to the AMAX being recording at a neighbour station during this period. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in August 2024 (WINFAP Files v13).
description-catchment: A predominantly impermeable catchment. (London Clay exposed over much of the northern catchment with Claygate Beds, Bagshot Beds, Pebble Gravel and Boulder Clay capping the higher ground. Terrace gravels cover the London Clay in the southern half with narrow bands of London Clay and Alluvium bordering the river. Mainly rural headwaters with substantial expanding urban development in the lower reaches.
description-flow-regime: Runoff increased by effluent returns but reduced by industrial/agricultural abstraction. Flood storage lagoons built on the River Rom, from the late 1980s onwards, influence flows patterns.

name: Chelmer at Felsted
description-summary: 'Essex' profile gauging a rural, predominantly London Clay catchment with minor artificial influences.
description-general: 'Essex' profile (modified Flat V Crump) weir with crest tapping.
description-station-hydrometry: Drowning commences at 0.6m, and varies in severity. Limit of reliable gauging is at 1.21m, higher flows estimated. Flood plain storage starts at 1.1m. No spillway. Hydraulic model used to derive rating for high flows. Reasonable fit to gaugings. One peak flow rating applied across period of record.
description-flow-record: Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in August 2021 (WINFAP Files v10).
description-catchment: Chalk in N, London Clay elsewhere, largely overlain with Boulder Clay and some glacial gravel. Rural, agricultural land use, predominantly arable land.
description-flow-regime: Minimal abstractions, adjustments needed for STW and industrial effluent discharges.

name: Roman River at Bounstead Bridge
description-summary: 'Essex' profile that replaced a temporary weir in 1969, structure suffers from severe drowning.
description-general: 'Essex' profile (modified Flat V Crump) weir with crest tapping from 11/03/1970, replaced originally a temporary broad-crested weir 03/1965-09/1969 with low flow V notch (data suspect).
description-station-hydrometry: Low modular limit (0.4m), problems with drowning. Weir is known to drown but rating fits well to gaugings up to 1.2m. Affected by weed growth and siltation Limited overspill starts at 0.35m (3.0 cumecs). One rating applied across period of record.
description-flow-record: Data since 31/08/1991 not stored on NRFA due to continuing problems with drowning. Structure drowned from winter 1990/1991 to May 1992 and problems continue.
description-catchment: London Clay covered with glacial gravel and Boulder Clay in the upper third. Rural catchment in conservation area.
description-flow-regime: Gw-influenced regime. Runoff increased by effluent returns. Runoff reduced by industrial/agricultural abstraction.

name: Holland Brook at Thorpe le Soken
description-summary: Station heavily influenced by tide and with significant abstractions at low flows.
description-general: 'Essex' profile (modified Flat V Crump) weir (very insensitive) with crest tapping.
description-station-hydrometry: Tidal influence very important, gauging limits variable due to d/s tidal conditions, with drowning starting at very low levels. Very gentle river gradient makes siltation a major problem, accompanied by weed growth.
description-flow-record: NA
description-catchment: London Clay with some Boulder Clay cover in NW. Rural, predominantly arable with some grassland.
description-flow-regime: Abstractions are significant at low flows.

name: Roding at Loughton
description-summary: Ultrasonic gauging station located in the mid reaches of the River Roding catchment.
description-general: Prior to 1983, Essex weir, subject to drowning. In 1989, this was replaced by a single crest Crump weir. An ultrasonic gauge has been operating at the site since the 05/02/2012.
description-station-hydrometry: The Crump weir had a modular limit of approx. 0.6m (no tail or downstream levels recorded). Current meter calibration of the weir, updated following gaugings taken during 2000 and 2002 floods. The ultrasonic gauge consists of 12 paths, in a cross configuration, installed in a trapezoidal concrete section just upstream of the Crump weir. The installation was commissioned for two reasons: to combat the regular occurrence of non-modular flow conditions that readily formed during high flows and secondly due to the extensive weed growth in this reach of the river that hampered measurement during low flows. Out of bank flow observed in 2024 around QMED. Not clear if station by-passed or just ponding on left bank. Full channel maintenance has not occurred since at least 2012. Channel is noticeabley more choked with reeds leading to more frequent occurrence of out of bank flow.
description-flow-record: No flow data from 1982-88. High flow rating under review; treat flows with caution.
description-catchment: Predominantly impermeable catchment (London clay and glacial deposits). The main land use is agriculture but the catchment contains significant urban areas.
description-flow-regime: NA

name: Colne at Earls Colne
description-summary: Station gauging a predominantly rural catchment with mixed geology and significant artificial influences, prone to siltation.
description-general: 'Essex' profile (modified Flat V Crump) weir with crest tapping.
description-station-hydrometry: Prone to siltation. Flows are estimated when siltation severely affects response of station. Low modular limit - approx. 0.5m. No spillway.
description-flow-record: NA
description-catchment: Upper Chalk in N, London Clay in S, largely overlain with superficial deposits of Boulder Clay and Sands and gravels in the valley. Predominantly rural, dominated by arable land, but with some urban development in valley u/s of station.
description-flow-regime: Adjustments now needed for additions and abstractions.

name: Bourne Brook at Perces Bridge
description-summary: Station gauging a rural, responsive tributary of R. Colne but with flows truncated at rating limit.
description-general: Compound V-notch thin-plate weir.
description-station-hydrometry: Rating limit of 0.6m (approx. 0.1 cumec) so high flows are truncated and water balance unrealistic.
description-flow-record: Several large gaps in the flow record.
description-catchment: Rural tributary to the R. Colne.
description-flow-regime: Responsive regime.

name: Tenpenny Brook at Tenpenny Bridge
description-summary: Station gauging a rural catchment.
description-general: Thin-plate weir. Installed to monitor irrigation abstractions.
description-station-hydrometry: NA
description-flow-record: Several large gaps in the flow record.
description-catchment: Rural catchment on London Clay.
description-flow-regime: NA

name: Sixpenny Brook at Ship House Bridge
description-summary: Station gauging a rural catchment and monitoring abstractions for irrigation.
description-general: Thin-plate weir. Installed to monitor irrigation abstractions.
description-station-hydrometry: NA
description-flow-record: Until 1967 stages were recorded with Bristol instruments (circular charts). Discrepancies were reported between gauge board readings and Bristol readings.
description-catchment: Rural catchment on London Clay.
description-flow-regime: Significant gw abstraction for irrigation.

name: Bentley Brook at Saltwater Bridge
description-summary: Station gauging a rural catchment and monitoring abstractions for irrigation.
description-general: Thin-plate weir. Installed to monitor irrigation abstractions.
description-station-hydrometry: NA
description-flow-record: Until 1967 stages were recorded with Bristol instruments (circular charts). Discrepancies were reported between gauge board readings and Bristol readings.
description-catchment: Rural catchment on London Clay.
description-flow-regime: Monitors gw abstraction for irrigation.

name: St Osyth Brook at Main Road Bridge
description-summary: Station gauging a rural catchment and monitoring abstractions for irrigation.
description-general: Thin-plate weir. Installed to monitor irrigation abstractions.
description-station-hydrometry: NA
description-flow-record: Until 1967 stages were recorded with Bristol instruments (circular charts). Discrepancies were reported between gauge board readings and Bristol readings.
description-catchment: Rural catchment on London Clay.
description-flow-regime: Monitors gw abstraction for irrigation.

name: Crouch at Wickford
description-summary: Crump weir gauging a low-lying catchment.
description-general: Crump weir and a rated channel for high flows. Station is approaching tidal limit.
description-station-hydrometry: Crump weir has very small fall because approaching tidal limit. Rated channel for high flows calibrated by current meter and float measurements (2.85m high). Low modular limit. Rating confirmed by gaugings to 1.2m. One rating applied across period of record.
description-flow-record: Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2019 (WINFAP Files v8).
description-catchment: Low lying, undulating terrain. London Clay, negligible superficial deposits. Urban areas (Basildon, Billericay) make up about third of catchment, particularly developed in S. Remaining area in N of catchment is mixed farming.
description-flow-regime: Responsive regime. Significant urban runoff from Billericay and Basildon. Low flows heavily influenced by STW discharge.

name: Eastwood Brook at Eastwood
description-summary: Gauging full range of a very responsive, totally urbanized catchment on an industrial estate on the outskirts of Southend.
description-general: Non-standard weir, insensitive at low flows, however, a good stepped fall, so no drowning. In 1996, replaced original weir decommissioned in April 1995 (hence missing data). New weir is a replica of previous structure, non-standard flat V weir. Telemetry was installed at the beginning of 1997.
description-station-hydrometry: Full range station, all events within bank. Rapid response means peak levels can be missed by the 15 min telemetry readings. One rating applied across period of record. Weir not expected to drown with rating form confirmed by hydraulic modelling.
description-flow-record: High flows on 12 and 13/09/2003 (not seen at surrounding sites) are the result of a burst water main within the catchment. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2019 (WINFAP Files v8).
description-catchment: Small, low-lying. Underlying geology is London Clay, some superficial deposits. Totally urbanised catchment on an industrial estate on the outskirts of Southend.
description-flow-regime: Very flashy, composed almost entirely of urban runoff. Runoff increased by effluent returns.

name: Mar Dyke at Stifford
description-summary: Station gauging a tributary of The Thames with catchment partly below the sea level, affected by weed growth and low modular limit. Station closed as of 01/10/2021. The site has suffered from bad non-modularity for some time now and the decision was made to stop recording flow. Various reasons for the non-modular flows include reduced maintenance downstream and the tidal influence downstream. This is now a level recording only site for flood warning purposes only.
description-general: 'Essex' profile (modified Flat V Crump) weir with d/s tapping.
description-station-hydrometry: Low modular limit, degree of drowning variable: backs up from tidal gates 3km d/s. Reverse flow possible. Mar Dyke flood alleviation measures have widened channel and increased height of the banks; only overtopped in extreme events. Suffers from summer weed growth.
description-flow-record: Some large gaps in the record around 1990 to 2004.
description-catchment: G: Runoff influenced by groundwater abstraction and/or recharge. E: Runoff increased by effluent returns. I: Runoff reduced by industrial and/or agricultural abstraction.
description-flow-regime: NA

name: Wid at Margaretting
description-summary: Station gauging a mainly rural catchment developed on London Clay with some significant artificial influences.
description-general: Sharp-edged trapezoidal weir with central rectangular notch. Closed and replaced by Writtle (37007) about 6km d/s.
description-station-hydrometry: Weir becomes non-modular at relatively low flow (2.8 cumecs). Up to 9.6 cumecs acts as rated section with approximate rating determined by current meter readings. Some bypassing known to occur well before this flow.
description-flow-record: Several large gaps and truncated flows in the record, especially before 1964.
description-catchment: London Clay catchment, mainly rural although with urbanized parts (Brentwood at top of catchment).
description-flow-regime: Flows influenced by abstractions and effluent returns.

name: Lee at Feildes Weir
description-summary: Located in the middle reaches of the River Lee, this station is marked by a complex history of changes to channel controls and bypassing.
description-general: Historically the station was a 29m wide thin-plate weir (found to be insensitive) and 3 vertical-lift sluices controlling a parallel flood relief channel. The weir is immediately downstream of the confluence of the rivers Lee and Stort. Building started in 1976 and it completed in 1978 to improve hydrometric range and precision. Pre-1976 there was a barrage of gates/sluices (operation evident on hydrographs, pre-1930 especially) to control flows. From 1/1/97, flows normally the sum of stations 38027 (Stort at Glen Faba) and 38031 (Lee at Rye Bridge). In 2004 flow calculation changed to using a combination of weir and gate levels rather than summation. An ultrasonic station was built d/s and opened on the 01/01/2008.
description-station-hydrometry: All flows (bar lockages) now contained but Ryemeads STW effluent bypasses the station. Flood flows on the Lee can cause reverse flows on Stort. Flows up to about 4.7 cumecs discharge over the weir; higher flows enter a flood channel. One rating applied across period of record. Weir rated using a physical model, with flood channel flows computed separately.
description-flow-record: Occasional erratic performance of the two upstream stations (summed for total flow) can impact on the precision of Feildes Weir flows. Early peak flow data from the 1850s are estimates. Naturalised flows (New River abstraction only) from 1883. Gauging instigated by Beardmore during the 1850s (flood of October 1857 estimated as >250 cumecs, greatly exceeding any subsequent event). Annual calendar year gauged daily flows thereafter. This flow was particularly uncertain. Until 1931, gauged daily flows were calculated as the mean of three daily readings recorded by lock keeper. Chart record from March 1932. Low flows probably under-estimated during this period (especially pre-1930). Measured peak flows post 1965. Station was out of commission in 1976, naturalised flows have been modelled between March 1976 to April 1978 by Envirionment Agency. The quality of the record improved after these dates. Mill operation could produce particularly low flows in the early record (e.g. on Sundays). Flows at Rye Bridge can be affected by lock and boat movements.
description-catchment: A mainly pervious (Chalk) catchment with extensive Drift cover. Predominantly rural headwaters with significant urban growth in lower valley.
description-flow-regime: Runoff reduced by abstraction for industry, agriculture and pws. Significant gw abstraction, with net export from catchment. Runoff increased by effluent returns. Effluent from Rymeads STW bypasses measuring structure, as does lockage from the Lee Navigation.

name: Ash at Mardock
description-summary: Flat V weir that is located in the lower Ash catchment.
description-general: Flat V weir (1:10 cross-slope) 3.9m wide, constructed in 1979. The current station replaced the original hump flume weir that was built in 1939. The old station was not good due to the obstruction caused by the old gate at the mill bypass channel. It was insensitive, subject to bypassing and was inaccurate at low flows. Hence discharges was assessed at the d/s station at Easneye (38005).
description-station-hydrometry: No rating available for original hump flume weir. Remains modular and is virtually full range. Rating is valid from 1981 - theoretical standard Flat V calculation, extended in January 2012, using modelled flow to account for stages 0.9mASD to 3mASD. Peak flow rating is reasonably accurate. Some bypassing is known to occur at extreme flows. One peak flow rating across period of record which takes account of bypassing.
description-flow-record: Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in August 2024 (WINFAP Files v13).
description-catchment: Solid geology of Upper Chalk extensively overlain by boulder clay, glacial sands & gravel and alluvium in the valleys. Rural catchment in character.
description-flow-regime: Baseflow dominated regime but significant runoff generated from the clays in the headwaters. U/s lake storage, sluice activity and gw abstractions for industry/agriculture have a minor effect on flows.

name: Mimram at Panshanger Park
description-summary: Station located in the lower catchment of the River Mimram.
description-general: Critical-depth flume; 5m wide. All flows are contained.
description-station-hydrometry: One rating applied across period of record. Rating is reasonably accurate, though overestimates flow. Theoretical calibration confirmed by gaugings but computed flows may be slightly overestimated by as much as 10%. The gauge was reviewed in 2014.
description-flow-record: Frequent discharges caused by fish farm are eliminated to produce naturalised flows. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2019 (WINFAP Files v8).
description-catchment: A predominantly permeable catchment (Upper Chalk overlain by glacial deposits near headwaters). Mainly rural but substantial urban growth in the lower valley - the Mimram drains Welwyn Garden City.
description-flow-regime: Appreciable net export of water. Considerable gw abstraction for industry & agriculture occurs in the headwaters. Very high baseflow component but peak flows increasing due to urbanisation. AMAX is commonly recorded during the summer half-year.

name: Rib at Wadesmill
description-summary: Compound structured gauging station located in the lower Rib catchment.
description-general: Non conforming Trapezoidal flume operated as a rated section with a Crump weir on the overflow channel.
description-station-hydrometry: One rating applied across the POR. Reasonable fit to gaugings although evidence suggests rating underestimates flow slightly. Modular calibration has applied during rare periods of drowned flow.
description-flow-record: All except highest floods contained. GDF data available (1957-83) for d/s limited range station (Rib at Herts Training School - 38006). Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2022 (WINFAP Files v11).
description-catchment: Solid geology Upper Chalk, extensively overlain by boulder clay; glacial sands and gravel in the valleys. Predominantly a rural catchment. Significant runoff generated from the towns of Buntingford and Thundridge as well as clays high up the catchment.
description-flow-regime: A flashy regime. Flows influenced by significant groundwater abstractions for industrial and agricultural purposes (net export).

name: Ash at Easneye
description-summary: A compound thin-plate weir that was superseded by the Ash at Mardock (38002).
description-general: Compound thin-plate weir that was reconstructed in 1976 to increase flow range. It was decommissioned in 1981 and was superseded by the Ash at Mardock (38002).
description-station-hydrometry: NA
description-flow-record: It was subject to bypassing and was inaccurate at low flows.
description-catchment: Solid geology of Upper Chalk extensively overlain by boulder clay, glacial sands & gravel and alluvium in the valleys. Rural catchment in character.
description-flow-regime: NA

name: Rib at Herts Training School
description-summary: Compound rectangular thin-plate weir that was superseded by the Rib at Wadesmill (38004).
description-general: Compound rectangular thin-plate weir (c. 3 metres wide). The structure was used for measuring low flows while high flows were measured u/s by the Rib at Wadesmill (38004). The station was decommissioned in the early 1980s (when 38004 became the primary station).
description-station-hydrometry: NA
description-flow-record: NA
description-catchment: Solid geology Upper Chalk, extensively overlain by boulder clay; glacial sands and gravel in the valleys. Predominantly a rural catchment. Significant runoff generated from the towns of Buntingford and Thundridge as well as clays high up the catchment.
description-flow-regime: Flows influenced by significant gw abstractions for industrial and agricultural purposes (net export).

name: Canons Brook at Elizabeth Way
description-summary: Station located in the lower region of Canons Brook before it joins the Stort. It is an important (>50 yr) urban time series.
description-general: Full range critical-depth flume in rectangular section. Between the years 1965 to 1980, low flows were monitored at a (less sensitive) Crump weir that was in series with the flume.
description-station-hydrometry: 3 limb power law rating based on the theory of flumes applied since flume became only form of measurement in 1979. Single rating across the period of record. Rating extends to 11 cumecs but majority of gaugings taken at low flows. Performance at low flows is poor, with flows being overestimated. However at medium to high flows gaugings suggest flow is underestimated. Further gaugings are required in the medium to high flow range.
description-flow-record: Low flow record since 1979 thought to be inaccurate due to insensitive control. Uncertainty in the medium to high flow record due to lack of calibration gaugings. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2019 (WINFAP Files v8).
description-catchment: The catchment geology is impervious dominated by London Clay. Rural headwaters but heavily urbanised d/s.
description-flow-regime: Balancing resevoirs in Harlow (and the New Town development itself) influence the flow pattern but there are no significant abstractions or discharges. Natural to within 10% at Q95.

name: Mimram at Fulling Mill
description-summary: Crump profile weir located on the mid reaches of the River Mimram.
description-general: Crump profile weir, 2.75m wide, built in the mid 1970s. Originally the station was comprised of two complementary thin-plate weirs. Prior to 1993, gauging was a sum of flows through the mill weir and a leaky wooden weir. The station was not used as a full gauging station from 07/1984. It was used solely for low flows for licence purposes from 09/1984 to 05/1990. The data was processed but not archived during this period. However, due to demand, the site came back online in 1990 and the data was stored.
description-station-hydrometry: Standard crump weir rating that extends to 2.5 cumecs. The station was not designed for peak flow measurement and is insensitive at low flows.
description-flow-record: Accurate at modular flow, but large discrepancies at non-modular flow (> 0.18m). Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2022 (WINFAP Files v11).
description-catchment: Chalk catchment (with overlying glacial deposits in some areas). Predominantly rural.
description-flow-regime: Flows substantially diminished by gw abstractions (Three Valleys Water plc) with a considerable net export of water. The weir drowns easily possibly due to seasonal weed growth (cut prior to 1993). It has not been possible to remove weeds due to a Brown Trout (Salmo trutta) conservation project that was initiated in 1993.

name: Stevenage Brook at Bragbury Park
description-summary: Flat V weir located on the Stevenage Brook, a tributary of the River Beane and sub-catchment of the River Lee in North London.
description-general: Flat V weir - 2.75m wide. It was constructed in 1974 to supersede the original broad-crested weir operated by Stevenage Development Corporation. Station added to peak flows dataset in August 2026 (WINFAP Files v15).
description-station-hydrometry: Operated using the theoretical equation for a Flat V weir. Full range station with a high modular limit. No by-passing occurs, in extreme high flows the river has been observed to breach its banks on the approach where the water will pond. Gauged to within 13% of QMED.
description-flow-record: Overall general good agreement with check gaugings. AMAX 5 observed to have breached bank but not by-passing gauge.
description-catchment: A chalk catchment now largely urbanised.
description-flow-regime: Gw abstractions significantly reduce runoff and the release of water from flood storage lagoons can influence the flashy flow regime.

name: Upper Lee at Luton Hoo
description-summary: Gauging station that is located in the Upper Lee catchment.
description-general: The station has been replaced by a d/s site; the Upper Lee at Luton East Hyde (38033). The station was closed on the 12/05/2013. Rectangular thin-plate weir (0.92m wide) plus and insensitive broad-crested overfall weir (10m wide) for flows > 0.33 cumecs. The side weir has a removable board(s) that have at times been removed with knowledge of measuring authority. The small side weir was re-built in January 1989. The large weir then operated at a stage of 0.223m not at the original 0.304m level.
description-station-hydrometry: One rating applied across period of record. Derived theoretically and matched to a very few check gaugings.
description-flow-record: Only very high floods, such as September 1968, exceed the capacity of the overfall weir. The time series is to be used with caution, pre-1966 data particularly. A stoplog may be used to regulate lake levels and this can result in spurious zero flows.
description-catchment: A Chalk catchment (with Drift) now substantially urbanised.
description-flow-regime: There is storage capacity in Luton Hoo lakes and the station is d/s of the outfall from an ornamental lake. Flows are substantially reduced as a result of gw abstractions (significant export). Considerable interludes of zero flow, occasionally interrupted by small sluice releases (above the thin-plate weir). Some surface water drainage from Luton bypasses the gauge via the East Hyde STW.

name: Salmon Brook at Edmonton
description-summary: The gauging station is located on Salmon Brook, a tributary that enters the lower River Lee system in North London.
description-general: Flat V weir (1:10 cross-slope), 5m wide (insensitive at low flows) in a slightly trapezoidal section. It superseded a less effective (particularly at very low flows) compound broad-crested structure in 1980.
description-station-hydrometry: Backing-up behind the d/s culvert can (rarely) result in drowning during flood conditions.
description-flow-record: NA
description-catchment: Impervious (London Clay) catchment. Salmon Brook rises on Enfield Chase and in the lower reaches the catchment is heavily urbanised.
description-flow-regime: No significant abstractions or discharges are associated with Salmon Brook. Very similar minimum flows occurred during the 1964 and 1959 droughts.

name: Intercepting Drain at Enfield
description-summary: A gauging station located in the Salmon Brook catchment of the River Lee system, North London.
description-general: Trapezoidal flume installed as part of the Lower Lee Monitoring Programme.
description-station-hydrometry: NA
description-flow-record: NA
description-catchment: The catchment is located in a highly urbanised area.
description-flow-regime: Very responsive regime, with clear urban runoff signal. Runoff is surface drainage from the heavily built-up areas of Edmonton and Enfield. Parts of the high flows from the Sadlers Mill Stream, are diverted to the Intercepting Drain. This additional flow substantially enhancing the runoff.

name: Stansted Springs at Mountfitchet
description-summary: A largely rural based gauging station within the north eastern part of the Thames Basin.
description-general: Two complementary thin-plate weirs (rectangular and 90 degree V notch) measuring spring flow discharging to the River Stort. The V notch weir was rebuilt in 1989 and new rating table used.
description-station-hydrometry: NA
description-flow-record: Very stable discharge, which can be very low and is usually dominated by baseflow, but station can be overwhelmed in exceptional floods. 21/10/2001 peak triggered by >90mm storm.
description-catchment: The contributing area to the chalk springs is mainly rural. The hydrological catchment cannot be readily determined hence runoff is not representative.
description-flow-regime: Significant local gw abstraction producing substantial net export of water.

name: Mimram at Whitwell
description-summary: Located in the upper Mimram Catchment, a standard crump weir operating since 1970.
description-general: Built in 1970, a 2m wide Crump weir operated as a full range gauging station using the theoretical rating equation. Station added to peak flows dataset in August 2026 (WINFAP Files v15).
description-station-hydrometry: Theoretical rating equation used for duration of record. High modular limit, no tail recorder but thought to be always modular when within structure. Maximum reliable limit of 0.25m, some extreme flows will be beyond this level.
description-flow-record: Dry for short periods in 1992, 1997 and 2019. Gap in the high resolution data (15 min) between October 1982 and February 1987. AMAX 1-5 beyond structure limit with flows underestimated by approximately 10%.
description-catchment: A predominantly pervious (Chalk), rural catchment. Hydrological catchment divide is uncertain.
description-flow-regime: Generally stable flow regime, sustained from Chalk springs. Low flows are occasionally augmented by pumping from local tube wells but overall runoff is significantly reduced by gw abstraction. U/s cress-beds can influence low flow pattern.

name: Upper Lee at Water Hall
description-summary: Station located in the Upper Lee catchment above the confluences of tributary rivers.
description-general: Crump weir approximately 6m wide. Present station built in October 1971 to replace two temporary stations at Waterhall Farm and Roxford Farm. River course altered for gravel works and current station was built within this new artificial section.
description-station-hydrometry: Modular throughout the flow range. Standard Crump weir calculation. Theoretical rating has a reasonable level of accuracy. Approach channel can become heavily choked with vegetation and has to be regularly managed.
description-flow-record: All flows contained. Some early data (of limited quality) from two nearby gauging stations. There was a station on the River Lee at Roxford (38801) which, started in November 1952. In order to produce a single record, some correlations were undertaken between these stations. They had an overlapping record from September 1971 to August 1972. These were compared and a formula was used to derive Water Hall values. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2019 (WINFAP Files v8).
description-catchment: Catchment is mainly pervious (Chalk) but with glacial Drift in the headwaters. The land uses are principally agricultural with some important (expanding) urban centres.
description-flow-regime: There is storage capacity in Luton Hoo lakes and the station is downstream of the outfall from an ornamental lake. Flows are substantially reduced as a result of groundwater abstraction (significant export). Considerable interludes of zero flow, occasionally interrupted by small sluice releases (above the thin-plate weir). Some surface water drainage from Luton bypasses the gauge via the East Hyde sewage treatment works. Rununculus growth in upstream section is rampant in the growing season. Cutting does occur on a regular basis but can lead to minor drift adjustment of water level.

name: Salmon Brook at Montague Road
description-summary: The station was located on the Salmon Brook and has been decommissioned since 1981.
description-general: Trapezoidal flume. The station was decommissioned in 1981.
description-station-hydrometry: NA
description-flow-record: The structure drowned regularly. The flow record is short and the data is of poor quality.
description-catchment: The catchment is located in a highly urbanised area.
description-flow-regime: NA

name: Cobbins Brook at Sewardstone Road
description-summary: This station, opened in June 1971, is on a small tributary of the River Lee within a suburban area. The station has a relatively large capacity gauging structure and has a flow record in excess of forty years.
description-general: Trapezoidal critical-depth flume with an overall width of 10m.
description-station-hydrometry: Drowning and damage to the exit transition (repaired in 1992) influences the performance of the station. Two ratings have been applied across the POR. The most recent is valid from October 1982. This post M25 construction rating was derived by hydraulic modelling (Halcrow). It includes backwater effects from the M25 culvert (350m d/s of the station) and a double pipe crossing (500m d/s). Two existing ratings are very similar up to 1m.
description-flow-record: A gap in the record from June 1982 to May 1983 inclusive was due to the building of the M25 motorway; flows could not be estimated as the river was diverted through two pipes which were too small for the purpose. In January 1992 repairs were carried out to the exit transit which was damaged and affecting performance - datum unaffected. There was also a gap of 2 months - August to September 1994 - for repairs to the weir. Recorded flows may be overestimates and the structure is insensitive at low flows. Data suspect during summer months 2014-2022 due to stilling well blockage (notably 08/03/2014 - 09/07/2014, 08/03/2015 - 02/08/2015, 15/02/2016 - 27/06/2016, 12/05/2018 - 01/06/2018, 22/05/2020 - 23/07/2020, 11/03/2022 - 23/09/2022). Station records very low flows, but zero flows in 2020 and 2022 thought to result from siltation of the inlet pipe. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in August 2025 (WINFAP Files v14).
description-catchment: Cobbins Brook drains an impervious (London Clay) catchment which includes part of Epping Forest. Substantial urban development occurs in the vicinity of the gauging station but this constitutes a small percentage of the overall catchment landuse.
description-flow-regime: The net impact of PWS abstractions and discharges on the natural responsive flow pattern is minimal. M25 motorway runoff can, however, be significant. In 2010 a large flood storage area was built near Cobbins Brook to protect Waltham Abbey and so will reduce flood peaks at Sewardstone Road.

name: Turkey Brook at Albany Park
description-summary: Station located on a small tributary of the River Lee that has flow record of over fifty years. It is located within an suburban area with relatively low rainfall.
description-general: Flat V weir, 6m wide, situated within but at the end of a concrete-lined channel, the river then flows into a restored naturalised reach through an urban park.
description-station-hydrometry: Structure operates in accordance with theory of Flat V weirs. Tailwater recorder proves a high modular limit, however since the river restoration works in March 2021 this has reduced. Very few gaugings to prove theoretical rating.
description-flow-record: The structure remains unaltered from its original design other than occasional repairs for damage sustained to the weir crest resulting from vandalism. Level data and rating available for 1972 to 1979 data. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in August 2024 (WINFAP Files v13).
description-catchment: A largely impervious catchment (Tertiary clays and glacial deposits). The headwaters drain Enfield Chase but there is significant urban development near the gauging station. Mix of land use is typical of much of the English Lowlands.
description-flow-regime: Very responsive flow regime. Minor net export due to gw abstractions. Abstractions for pws. Large ornamental lake in headwaters. Levels occasionally affected by the new river overspill at Maidens Bridge.

name: Pymmes Brook at Edmonton Silver Street
description-summary: Station located on the Pymmes Brook with a catchment dominated by urban land use.
description-general: Crump weir (crest width 6.16m) in a concrete trapezoidal channel. Installed in 1972 a few metres upstream of the original station (Alcazaar 38025). The original station was commissioned in 1954 and operated as a rated section.
description-station-hydrometry: Theoretical crump weir formula used to calculate flows since the weir was built. Crest tapping and tail levels suggest the weir remains modular throughout the flow range. Station performs well at low flows but too few gaugings at mid to high flows to confirm levels of uncertainty.
description-flow-record: Original rating superseded in 1963 by a new discharge table and the old records were corrected. This was replaced in 1981 by one which took into account the trapezoidal nature of the channel. Data from November 1972 to 1981 was recalculated and the new rating was adopted since 1982. Flows corrected for weir drowning since 1982. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2019 (WINFAP Files v8).
description-catchment: Impervious (London Clay) catchment. Pymmes Brook rises on Enfield Chase but the catchment is now dominated by urban land use.
description-flow-regime: Pre-1965 runoff substantially enhanced by sewage effluent (now treated outside the catchment). Currently no significant abstractions or discharges. Natural to within 10% at Q95.

name: Lee flood relief at Low Hall
description-summary: Gauging station located in a flood relief channel in the lower Lee Valley.
description-general: Crump weir 17.1m broad (insensitive) located within a concrete flood relief channel.
description-station-hydrometry: NA
description-flow-record: Combination of flows with the Lee at Lea Bridge (38032) provides total outflow of the Lee into the tidal Thames.
description-catchment: A mainly pervious (Chalk) catchment with extensive Drift cover. Predominantly rural headwaters; significant urban growth in lower valley.
description-flow-regime: The distribution of flows in the R. Lee and the flood channel is controlled by sluices at Chalk Bridge. Discharge is a factor in the operational control of the tidal barrier at Bow Creek. As Low Hall is a managed channel with main purpose to convey flood flows, there are periods when the water level drops below the level of the weir crest and the gauging station records zero flow.

name: Small River Lee at Ordnance Road
description-summary: Station located in the lower reaches of the River Lee catchment.
description-general: Flat V weir (1:10 cross-slope), 8m wide. Crest tapping does not operate effectively.
description-station-hydrometry: NA
description-flow-record: Subject to drowning.
description-catchment: A predominantly impervious (clay), catchment with substantial superficial cover. Suburban in the valley, rural headwaters with considerable woodland.
description-flow-regime: Responsive regime. Minor impact of artificial influences on flows, low discharges affected by gravel workings and pumped drainage from the M25 can be important.

name: Pymmes Brook at Alcazar
description-summary: Station located on the Pymmes Brook, a tributary of the River Lee, that has been decommissioned since 1974.
description-general: Formalised rectangular section rated by c/m.
description-station-hydrometry: NA
description-flow-record: Limited accuracy. Minimum flows during the dry autumn of 1969. Notable 1965 peak is unconfirmed but was triggered by a storm of >50mm.
description-catchment: NA
description-flow-regime: NA

name: Pincey Brook at Sheering Hall
description-summary: Station located on a tributary of the River Stort. Flow regime affected by abstractions and irrigation.
description-general: Flat V weir (1:10.9 cross-slope) 4.02m wide. Removed from peak flows dataset in September 2023 (WINFAP Files v12).
description-station-hydrometry: Bypassing occurs at high flows (e.g. Oct 2001 flood). Flows > 17 cumecs exceed the capacity of the structure. At tail recorder was added in February 2011, to account for issues with non-modular flow. Non-modularity may have been increasing during the period of record. Flows derived from standard Flat V calculation. Rating is accurate, though more gauging is required to validate high flow range (no current meter readings above 0.6m). All flow is within bank, but by-passing does occur during floods.
description-flow-record: Data for period of record re-processed to correct for non-modularity. In the peak flow data, this correction has only been applied for 1982 onwards. For the daily flow data relevant modern levels of non-modularity were utilised to derive reprocessed flows.
description-catchment: Pervious (Chalk) headwaters, mainly London Clay in lowest reaches. Land use mainly agricultural but the Pincey Brook drains Stansted Airport and Hatfield Forest.
description-flow-regime: Flows reduced by public water supply abstraction. Spray irrigation can be significant (especially in the upper part of the catchment). Balancing ponds at Stansted Airport provide some headwater regulation.

name: Stort at Glen Faba
description-summary: The ultrasonic gauging station is located in the lower River Stort, a tributary in the upper River Lee catchment. Flows summed with Rye Bridge to generate Feildes Weir flows.
description-general: Multipath ultrasonic (cross-path superseded single-path device). River maintained by Canal and River Trust.
description-station-hydrometry: All but exceptional floods contained. Very low velocities (canalised river) hampered calibration and make low flow gauging difficult. Located immediately upstream of the confluence with the Lee at Feildes Weir with backing up when flows are high. Level measured by pressure transducer and radar in the stilling well.
description-flow-record: Some early gauged daily flows estimated due to instrument malfunction. Flows affected by canal operation at high flows.
description-catchment: Chalk headwaters, London Clay dominates lower catchment (considerable Drift cover). Rural upper catchment, substantial urban development (including Harlow & Bishops Stortford) in the valley.
description-flow-regime: Limited net impact of artificial influences but substantial gw abstraction in headwaters (a proportion is exported).

name: Stansted Brook at Gypsy Lane
description-summary: The gauging station is located on Stansted Brook in a largely rural catchment that contains Stansted Airport.
description-general: Thin plate weir from 1964 until 1977. Replaced in 1977 by the current Flat V weir (3.5m wide and 1:10 cross slope). Operated as a full range gauging station using the theoretical rating equation. Silt accumulation behind the weir can be significant. Station added to peak flows dataset in August 2026 (WINFAP Files v15).
description-station-hydrometry: Weir remains modular throughout the range and all flows are contained. Low flows are difficult to verify with good check gaugings. Gauged once beyond QMED (6% deviation).
description-flow-record: Flows pre-1977 are derived from thin plate data and show a clear discontinuity with post-1977 flows based on flat-V data. The pre-1977 period is considered unrepresentative. No check gaugings available for early thin plate weir.
description-catchment: Mixed geology with clear west-east contrast. Chalk dipping occur below Eocene clays and there is extensive Drift cover. Largely rural but with substantial urban development above the catchment outlet.
description-flow-regime: Stable discharge at very low flows, due to spring outflows, but is subject to artificial disturbance. Very few abstractions in the catchment but flows are influenced by motorway runoff and an u/s storage lagoon at Stansted Airport. Lagoon sluice closures can result in occasional zero flows.

name: Quin at Griggs Bridge
description-summary: A gauging station located in the lower River Quin catchment that is located within the River Lee system.
description-general: A 4.5m wide Flat V weir opened in 1978, after a period of operating as a level only site for flood warning purposes. A full range gauging station using the theoretical equation to derive flows since opening. Station added to peak flows dataset in August 2026 (WINFAP Files v15).
description-station-hydrometry: Modular rating used throughout flow range, no tail reduction for non-modular flow. Anecdotal evidence of non-modular conditions in extreme high flows. Gauged above QMED, within 10% deviation away from rated flow.
description-flow-record: Gap in high resolution data (15min) from October 1982 to October 1984. Extreme high flows thought to be over-estimated due to evidence of non- modular conditions.
description-catchment: A mainly impervious catchment with extensive glacial deposits overlying Chalk. Agricultural land use predominates but there is some urban development close to the gauging station.
description-flow-regime: Net export of water has increasing from the mid-1980s. Gw abstractions can be especially significant during droughts e.g. late-1990. Stable baseflow but responsive to storm events; sewage effluent discharge pattern also sometimes detectable.

name: Beane at Hartham
description-summary: The station is located in the lower River Beane within the River Lee catchment.
description-general: Flat V weir, 8m wide.
description-station-hydrometry: All flows are contained. Modular throughout the flow range; theoretical calibration adopted.
description-flow-record: NA
description-catchment: Solid geology: Chalk substantially overlain by boulder clay, glacial sands and gravel. Mainly rural but contains Stevenage, also moderate urban development close to the catchment outfall.
description-flow-regime: Substantial baseflow but the Drift cover (and urban areas) provide a rapid runoff response to storms. Significant gw abstractions (particularly in the headwaters); moderate net export of water.

name: Lee at Rye Bridge
description-summary: The ultrasonic gauging station is located in the upper River Lee catchment.
description-general: Multi-path, cross-configuration US. It is located 0.4km u/s of Feildes Weir and it provides a check on a major component of the Lee at Feildes Weir (38001) flows.
description-station-hydrometry: NA
description-flow-record: Sensibly continuous record.
description-catchment: A mainly pervious Chalk catchment. Predominantly rural headwaters. Significant urban growth in the lower valley.
description-flow-regime: Flows occasionally exceed bankfull but gate operation at Feildes Weir greatly restricts overbank flow.

name: Lee at Lea Bridge
description-summary: The ultrasonic gauging station is located in the lower River Lee catchment, close to the confluence of the River Thames.
description-general: Multi-path, cross-configuration US. Combined with input of the Lee flood relief channel (at Low Hall - 038023), represents total inflow into the River Thames from the River Lee.
description-station-hydrometry: NA
description-flow-record: Occasional anomalous behaviour at very low flows.
description-catchment: A mainly pervious (Chalk) catchment with extensive Drift cover. Predominantly rural headwaters. Substantial urban growth in lower valley.
description-flow-regime: Runoff reduced by New River abstraction (see the Lee at Feildes Weir - 38001).

name: Upper Lee at Luton East Hyde
description-summary: The station is a replacement of the former upstream gauging station, the Upper Lee at Luton Hoo (38013).
description-general: The station is a replacement of the d/s gauging station, the Upper Lee at Luton Hoo (38013). It is a rated section located 400m d/s of the old structure.
description-station-hydrometry: Rated section (using a control section) within an existing channel.
description-flow-record: Insensitive at very low flows. Significant periods of near zero flow.
description-catchment: A Chalk catchment (with Drift) that is heavily urbanised.
description-flow-regime: The station is located downstream of the outfall from an ornamental lake (with storage capacity) at Luton Hoo Park. It is also located above a significant discharge from a sewage treatment works. Flows are substantially reduced as a result of groundwater abstractions. The catchment has substantial amounts of urbanisation resulting in rapid run-off and a flashy response. Flow occassionally affected by operation of upstream penstock which is used by the Luton Hoo estate when carrying out maintenance on their ornanmental weir.

name: Thames at Kingston
description-summary: The Thames at Kingston, replacing the d/s Teddington weir measurement structures, has one of the longest flow records associated with any UK flow gauging station. Dating from 1883, it is of major historical and modern day significance. Naturalised flows are available for the period of record. In May 2023, Kingston was recognised by the World Meteorological Organization for having more than 100 years of hydrological observations.
description-general: Until 1974 the GDFs were derived from Teddington Weir (a 150m long complex of gates, sluices, weirs and locks that span 70m across the river), where a tailwater rating was used with twice-daily levels (at low tide) to compute flows >85 cumecs. In 1974 a single path US was commissioned 2km upstream to replace the weir as the primary method for flow derivation. This was upgraded to a multi-path configuration (6 paths) US in 1986, and a second US was installed in 1991 to confirm the performance of the primary gauge. Work undertaken in 2018 to further upgrade the ultrasonics to make the station resilient to a 1-in-1000 year flood event.
description-station-hydrometry: Kingston: US (6 paths) with back-up to confirm the performance of the primary gauge. During warm weather the gauge can malfunction as the ultrasonic beam is bent by temperature gradients in the river, however this is unlikely to affect high flows but can effect gauge performance at low flows. No issues from temperature gradients have been seen in the past 20 years. Increased channel capacity means that bank-full is now very rarely exceeded and the ultrasonic gauge is capable of measuring all within bank flows. Generally, accuracy is good at peak flows, although less so for flows below 5 cumecs. Teddington Weir: Only DMFs are estimated. High hydrometric accuracy is made difficult by leakage, lockages and the general complexity of the site.
