description-station-hydrometry: Probably drowns, rated section at high flows; well rated to 30 cumecs but considerable uncertainty in extreme flow range. Significant scatter in gaugings surrounding the current rating (post 2003), therefore station closed at the transition to the new rating. Period between 1961 - 2003 remains suitable for QMED. One rating applied across period of record.
description-flow-record: Data removed after 24/07/2003 due to uncertainties with the rating, and the station closed. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in August 2025 (WINFAP Files v14).
description-catchment: Catchment is mainly impermeable (chiefly Weald Clay) with mixed land use and growing urban component - includes Crawley, Gatwick Airport; considerable woodland also.
description-flow-regime: Runoff reduced by public water supply abstraction. Sewage effluent contribution is increasing (much of it from outside the catchment); moderate overall increase in runoff.

name: Mole at Gatwick Airport
description-summary: Ultrasonic station gauging an impervious catchment with some urban land use.
description-general: Since 2005, an ultrasonic station 200m downstream of original station - rectangular flume (2.74m broad) in culvert below airport runway plus Crump weir in overflow channel (built in 1984, and appears to influence the homogeneity of the flow record). Station added to peak flows dataset in September 2022 (WINFAP Files v11).
description-station-hydrometry: Six-path ultrasonic gauge, replacing four-path gauge in September 2019.
description-flow-record: Ran dry for the first time in summer of 1995. Four-path gauge failed in 2016, no data available until re-opening in September 2019. Multiple years rejected in the Peak Flow Dataset due to missing data.
description-catchment: Impervious (Weald Clay) catchment; mostly rural but heavy urban development in the eastern third.
description-flow-regime: Very limited disturbance to the responsive, natural flow regime (Gatwick Airport is not in the catchment); small net export of water.

name: Yeading Brook West at North Hillingdon
description-summary: Gauging station located on Yeading Brook West, a small tributary of the River Crane. The station was closed in 1995.
description-general: Flat V weir (width: 5.02m, 1:20 cross-slope) u/s of culvert below the Western Avenue. Station demolished 1995.
description-station-hydrometry: Limited depth of approach - structure drowns readily at low discharges (0.28 cumecs) but there is a satisfactory gauged rating. Control passes to the culvert d/s of the station. Since 1983 some bypassing has occurred via a feeder ditch. One rating applied across period of record. Capable of providing good quality data but persistant problems with the correct zero setting of the stage recorders in the 1970s.
description-flow-record: Daily mean flows are historically inconsistent, causing high uncertainty in the peak flow record therefore flows are rejected between 1979 and 1986. Flow data recorded during 1995 was very unreliable and as such the record ends of July 1994. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in August 2025 (WINFAP Files v14).
description-catchment: Impervious, suburban catchment in NW London, including some of the runoff from Northolt Airport. Some agricultural land immediately u/s of the station.
description-flow-regime: Additional floodplain storage (provided as part of 1983 river improvement scheme) increased lag times.

name: Ravensbourne at Catford Hill
description-summary: Trapezoidal flume; regime heavily affected by urbanisation.
description-general: Trapezoidal flume; breadth at the critical section: 4.267m; insensitive. Full range.
description-station-hydrometry: One rating applied across period of record. Rating adjusted from theoretical to better fit spot flow measurements. Due to flashy nature of channel, EA have been unable to capture flows in third limb of rating and so it remains unproven. Because of this, Limb 3 remains theoretical with no adjustment for spot flow measurements in lower limbs.
description-flow-record: Full record reprocessed Feb 2019 when new rating was developed. Peak flows marked as rejected between 1986 and 1987 as ascending oscillations are present and appear suspicious. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2020 (WINFAP Files v9).
description-catchment: The Ravensbourne rises as Tertiary sandstone springs in Keston Park (dry chalk valleys extend into the North Downs). The lower catchment is mainly impervious Eocene deposits. Below the headwaters the catchment is largely within London.
description-flow-regime: Artificial influences evident at low flows. Regime heavily affected by urbanisation. Artificial influences (including sewage outflow and urban runoff) very evident at low flows - see June 2009.

name: Crane at Cranford Park
description-summary: Flume located on the mid reaches of the River Crane. The regime is affected by complex water utilisation.
description-general: Non-standard critical depth flume improvised from the invert of a footbridge. Straight reach, banks stabilised by timber revetments. Removed from peak flows dataset in September 2023 (WINFAP Files v12).
description-station-hydrometry: Bypassing occurs on left bank above a stage of about 1.3m. Structure drowns at 1.2 m. Two ratings applied across period of record, the most recent is valid from April, 1978. Rating derived partly from hydraulic theory that does not accurately estimate flows. Flume is non-modular before QMED, which is not accounted for in the current rating.
description-flow-record: Pre-1984 flows generally less reliable.
description-catchment: A flat, generally impervious (mostly London Clay) catchment of urban / suburban character. It includes Northolt Airport.
description-flow-regime: Complex water utilisation. Small natural import of water from the Colne catchment along the Duke of Northumberland's River. A relatively responsive regime.

name: Pool River at Winsford Road
description-summary: Trapezoidal flume, runoff is reduced by groundwater abstractions.
description-general: Trapezoidal, critical depth flume constructed in 1974 located approximately 0.5km upstream of confluence with the Ravensbourne. The site replaces a previous station (Selworthy Road, 39827) that was located approximately 300m upstream of the current site and which was operational 1961-71. Removed from peak flows dataset in February 2018 (WINFAP Files v6).
description-station-hydrometry: Algal growth causes apparent higher flow than d/s site at Catford Hill (39056). Rating is derived theoretically for the structure and assumes no drowning or by-passing. Spot gaugings support the lower end of the rating but the maximum gauged flow is substantially below QMED. A 2009 modelling study confirmed the theoretical rating and found that the station doesn't drown and that all flow is contained within the structure to flows beyond QMED, so the rating curve is considered valid to above QMED. The rating history of the site is complex and has required flows to be reprocessed in the past. This has resulted from changes in measurement units and errors in rating derivation, rather than changes to the station control, however, and the current rating (FQ/migrated.V1) is considered definitive for the whole period of record in the absence of spot flow gaugings at higher stages.
description-flow-record: Daily flows reprocessed from Jan 1985. Some earlier daily flow data (1961-71) exist for an u/s site - Selworthy Road (39827).
description-catchment: The Pool River rises as Chalk springs (below Addington Hill) but flows mostly over impervious Eocene deposits. Land use: primarily a suburban/urban catchment in south London.
description-flow-regime: Runoff is reduced by groundwater abstractions and artificial influences evident at low flows.

name: Letcombe Brook at Letcombe Bassett
description-summary: The gauging station is located in the upper section of Letcombe Brook, just downstream of Letcombe Brook at Arabellas Lake (39112).
description-general: Flat V weir (3.0m wide) superseded original rectangular notch (1.0 m wide) in 1981.
description-station-hydrometry: NA
description-flow-record: Gw augmentation noticeable (eg. 2004).
description-catchment: Rural catchment on scarp slope of the Lambourn Downs (Chalk - Drift free except for peat on the highest hills in the south). Catchment area derived from a Digital Terrain Model.
description-flow-regime: Baseflow-dominated regime. Runoff suggests that the topographic catchment is considerably smaller than the actual contributing area. Flows substantially reduced by pumping from the Childrey Warren boreholes (groundwater pumping). This can impact substantially on low flow patterns. The alleviation of low flows scheme was implemented in 1992.

name: Ewelme Brook at Ewelme
description-summary: Headwater gauging station, based in a chalk catchment, that flows into the middle sections of the River Thames.
description-general: Flat V weir (width: 2m) installed in 1980 superseding (after 4-yr break) and built on top of a thin-plate weir (width: 1.524m). Significant pre-1950 artificial channel re-alignment in Ewelme.
description-station-hydrometry: Water level measured by radar sensor with pressure sensor for backup. Originally, a shaft encoder was used. Very long weir tail does not cause drowning as critical flow is achieved. Limited head - algal growth on crest can be a problem - flow is assumed (but not confirmed) to remain modular. Tail level is not measured. Gravel from river bed can build up on apron. Weeds (water crowfoot) can build up on apron when they are cut and not removed from the upstream channel.
description-flow-record: Missing data from June 1976 to April 1980 due to weir replacement works. 2000/01 daily flows outstanding.
description-catchment: A rural/agricultural catchment developed on the scarp-slope of the Chilterns (Chalk with some Drift cover). Ewelme village is the largest settlement. Groundwater catchment is smaller than the topographical catchment.
description-flow-regime: Natural, stable flow regime (but local surface runoff can produce sub-daily events). Occasional bypassing via informal sluice upstream. Pristine chalk stream, gravel bed (but largely impermeable in some reaches). Cress beds downstream can impact flows through action of sluices (e.g. summer 2018). Upstream in-channel weed growth and clearance can impact flows.

name: Mole at Dorking
description-summary: Crump weir (15.0m broad) superseded original mill weir (velocity-area rated) in 1978.
description-general: Crump weir with side channel for old mill, which rejoins the main river downstream.
description-station-hydrometry: Crump weir is modular to structurefull. All but very high flows contained. British standard weir calculation with tail correction.
description-flow-record: No flow data 03/76-01/78.
description-catchment: Impervious (mostly Weald Clay) catchment. Mixed land use with considerable urban/suburban development.
description-flow-regime: Significant net import of water (sewage effluent).

name: Mole at Kinnersley Manor
description-summary: Rectangular flume, levels respond quickly to rainfall.
description-general: Rectangular flume, 7.1m wide at throat, and 1.48m wide rectangular side sluice. Removed from peak flows dataset in February 2018 (WINFAP Files v6).
description-station-hydrometry: Flow bypasses the weir above 2.4m head (30 m3/s). Considerable flow in the road at levels approaching 3 m. Calibration based on current meter gaugings which extend beyond bankfull. Bypassing occurs at flows >30m3s-1; flows therefore uncertain in the highest range. One rating applied across period of record. Calibration based on current meter gaugings which extend beyond bankfull; rating overestimates flow beyond bankfull and is increasingly uncertain above 2.4m stage.
description-flow-record: Patchy record in the 1970's.
description-catchment: A largely impervious catchment (mostly Weald Clay)but more permeable headwaters. Very mixed land use of rural tracts and urban centres; Crawley and Gatwick Airport are in the catchment.
description-flow-regime: Responsive regime (reflecting growing urban contribution) and substantial effluent component (STWs at Crawley, Horley and Burstow) with a significant net import which has increasing over time (runoff therefore unrepresentative); otherwise moderate impact of artificial influences. Urban extent almost doubled between 1960 and 2002. Levels respond quickly to rainfall.

name: Thames at Ewen
description-summary: Flat-V weir. It is the nearest gauging station to the source of the Thames.
description-general: Upgraded to full-width Flat V in 2002, full range capability. Previously, a Flat V weir (4.0 metres broad, 1:10 cross-slope) with thin-plate overfalls. It is not considered a primary station.
description-station-hydrometry: Pre-2002 weir was very prone to drowning. Current weir is slightly prone to drowning.
description-flow-record: Pre-2002 data removed from NRFA as it was very prone to drowning, resulting in incomplete high flow record.
description-catchment: A small rural Cotswolds catchment developed on permeable Middle Jurassic formations (mostly Upper Oolite).
description-flow-regime: Zero discharge during extended droughts. Gw abstractions in catchment result in a small net export of water. Flows can be affected by weed growth. Flows can go slightly out-of-bank.

name: Thames at Royal Windsor Park
description-summary: Multi-path ultrasonic gauging station based in the lower River Thames catchment.
description-general: Multi-path US superseded, in 1988, original single-path configuration (installed 1978).
description-station-hydrometry: Post-1992 gaps filled by using equi-percentile flows with Reading (39130) as a surrogate, earlier gaps filled using Kingston (39001) naturalised flows as a surrogate. Calibration confirmed by gaugings.
description-flow-record: All but exceptional floods contained. 01/2003 peak: c405 cumecs.
description-catchment: Scarp and vale topography developed on diverse geology. Predominantly rural headwaters contrast with considerable suburban growth in the lower valley. Representative of large lowland catchments in England.
description-flow-regime: Baseflow from the Chalk and Oolitic L'st, quicker response from the Oxford Clay and Lower London Tertiaries. Station is u/s of the major PWS off-takes for London.

name: Churn at Cirencester
description-summary: The gauging station is located in the middle section of the River Churn just above Cirencester, in the western Thames Basin.
description-general: Flat V weir (1:10 cross-slope, 4.5m broad). Auxiliary d/s water level recorder.
description-station-hydrometry: NA
description-flow-record: All flows contained but bypassing can occur at very high flows (as in late 2000); hydrographs appear truncated. Zero flows occur during notable droughts.
description-catchment: Pervious (Oolitic L'st) catchment on the dip-slope of the Cotswolds. Primarily rural with small, scattered settlements.
description-flow-regime: Baseflow-dominated regime. Significant diminution of runoff due to groundwater and surface water abstractions.

name: Ampney Brook at Sheepen Bridge
description-summary: The station is located in the upper River Thames catchment on Ampney Brook.
description-general: Flat V weir (1:10 cross-slope, 4.5m broad). Often drowned.
description-station-hydrometry: Calibration under review - gaugings indicate that the drowned flow reduction factor (based on tailwater levels) over-compensates for non-modularity. Limited head at low flows, therefore insensitive.
description-flow-record: NA
description-catchment: The Ampney Brook rises in the pervious Great Oolite series but the lower catchment is principally Oxford Clay. A rural catchment.
description-flow-regime: Some bypassing at highest flows. Small diminution of flow due to abstraction, otherwise a naturally responding catchment.

name: Marston Meysey Brook at Whetstone Bridge
description-summary: The station is located on Marston Meysey Brook, in the upper River Thames catchment.
description-general: Flat V weir (1:10 cross-slope, 3.0m broad).
description-station-hydrometry: NA
description-flow-record: Some high flows are estimated or omitted.
description-catchment: The Marston Meysey Brook rises in the Great Oolite Series (pervious) but is predominantly impervious (Oxford Clay). Rural.
description-flow-regime: Intermittent flow. Runoff reduced by gw abstractions, also occasional direct augmentation from gw (e.g. during pumping tests throughout Aug 1983).

name: Windrush at Worsham
description-summary: The ultrasonic gauging station is located in the middle reaches of the River Windrush.
description-general: Multi-path ultrasonic commissioned in December, 1995. Previously two adjustable radial gate (sharp-crested) weirs.
description-station-hydrometry: It is principally a low flow station. Flood flows are commonly not calculated.
description-flow-record: Some early flow data (from 1942) held by the measuring authority for the original rhymer weir. There is also a very patchy record pre-1977. Drowning is very rare but high flows are unreliable.
description-catchment: A pervious (Oolitic L'st) catchment (with some low-permeability tracts) on the dip-slope of the Cotswolds. Predominantly rural - Witney is the largest settlement.
description-flow-regime: Large baseflow component but responsive to storm events. Negligible disturbance to the natural flow regime.

name: Og at Marlborough Poulton Fm
description-summary: The station is located on the River Og, a headwater tributary of the River Kennet.
description-general: Flat V weir (width: 3.0m) with auxiliary d/s recorder.
description-station-hydrometry: Seasonal weed growth causes drowning.
description-flow-record: NA
description-catchment: The Og drains from the Chalk of the Marlborough Downs; very limited Drift cover. A rural catchment.
description-flow-regime: Gw abstraction in the headwaters otherwise flow regime is natural and dominated by baseflow.

name: Wey (North) at Farnham
description-summary: The gauging station is located on the River Wey near Farnham.
description-general: Modified Crump weir (width: 9.14m) with thin-plate along the crest line.
description-station-hydrometry: Calibration is theoretically and is based on a few confirmatory gaugings. Non-modular at high flows - also possible bypassing via culvert immediately u/s.
description-flow-record: August 1997 dmfs estimated.
description-catchment: A mainly Chalk catchment with Gault Clay in the lower reaches. Predominantly rural, some urban development on the watershed and close to the station.
description-flow-regime: High baseflow component but very responsive to rainfall. Runoff considerably diminished by gw abstractions in the headwaters.

name: Wey at Weybridge
description-summary: The ultrasonic gauging station monitors the complete River Wey system.
description-general: A multi-path cross-configuration ultrasonic replaced a single-path US (Harwell design) in 2003.
description-station-hydrometry: Gaugings were used to develop adjustment factors. Weed-growth, low velocities and velocity distribution caused problems.
description-flow-record: No data between January 2019 and July 2020 due to gauge failure.
description-catchment: Diverse geology and land use. Largely permeable upper catchment (Chalk and Upper Greensand of the North Downs); impermeable Tertiary formations dominate the lower catchment. Land use: rural tracts with mixed woodland; considerable suburban development below the headwaters.
description-flow-regime: U/s storage produces some flood attenuation. Responsive regime. The confluence with canal is just u/s.

name: Ock at Abingdon
description-summary: It is the main flow measuring structure on the River Ock, just upstream of another peak flow station within Abingdon (39018) that it superseded.
description-general: Crump weir, 7.79m wide, with auxiliary d/s tapping. Superseded original compound structure in 1979 (with associated gaps in the record). Due for fish passage baffles FY 2019-20.
description-station-hydrometry: Substantial channel improvements but drowning became more frequent again. Standard Crump weir calculation using tail levels. Part of the weir is subject to non-modular flow conditions (0.5m), as the channel splits into a high and low level channel on the d/s side of the weir. Inaccurate at low flows, but otherwise reasonably accurate. Slight overestimation could result in anomalies at higher flows. A flood forecasting rating is available which estimates total flows including those on the flood plain. Sandford Brook flows into the side channel just downstream of the structure (piped from left bank under the channel).
description-flow-record: Although hydrometrically much improved it is still imprecise at low flows. Substantial channel improvements were completed but the weir drowns during floods and overspill can occur into Sandford Brook. This was more common pre-1979. There are doubts about the homogeneity of peak flows. No flow adjustment made. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2020 (WINFAP Files v9) and in August 2024 (WINFAP Files v13).
description-catchment: Flat, rural valley in Vale of The White Horse. Largely flat, rural valley in Vale of The White Horse. Mixed geology that is largely pervious. Chalk downland forms southern watershed while the remainder mostly Tertiary clays. Geology includes Corallian Beds, Greensand, Chalk, Kimmeridge Clay, Gault & Alluvium. Contributing area exceeds topographical catchment.
description-flow-regime: Runoff influenced by a significant number gw abstraction/recharge. Runoff augmented by sewage effluent (derived from outside catchment).

name: Brent at Brent Cross
description-summary: The station is located in the upper Brent Catchment, North London.
description-general: Rectangular thin-plate weir with rectangular notch.
description-station-hydrometry: Limited number of check gaugings, highest at 4.1 cumecs; they suggest that calibration modestly overestimates high flows. Regular occurence of debris on weir crest; camera installed and monitored daily so accumulation never gets too large, small amounts have neglible effect on stage.
description-flow-record: Very responsive regime.
description-catchment: Urban/suburban catchment in north-west London.
description-flow-regime: Debris in channel can be a problem. Very responsive regime.

name: Wandle at Wandle Park
description-summary: Flume.
description-general: NA
description-station-hydrometry: Hydrometric performance not documented.
description-flow-record: Patchy flow record but useful late 1930s data. 1956 peak should be considered as indicative only. Contemporary flows in the lower Wandle available for station 39003.
description-catchment: NA
description-flow-regime: NA

name: Gatwick Stream at Gatwick Link
description-summary: Crump weir gauging a mainly impervious catchment which responds quickly to rainfall.
description-general: Crump weir (4.6m broad) with crest-tapping (almost permanently blocked but weir remains modular except during exceptional floods); located at the end of a culvert. Superseded earlier u/s velocity-area station, 1952-1977.
description-station-hydrometry: Modular apart from exceptional discharges. One rating applied across period of record. Rating uses a modelled rating that accounts for drowning over the full period of record.
description-flow-record: Weir records begin in 1975. Rating adjusted in 1990 to include drowned flow, and back-dated over record. Records also exist from 1952-1977 for a rated section at a site 2 km u/s (station 39024); accuracy at this site was poor. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2023 (WINFAP Files v12).
description-catchment: Mixed geology but mainly impervious (Weald Clay). Mixed land use with significant urban and forested areas. Catchment does not include Gatwick Airport.
description-flow-regime: Very responsive to rainfall and flow pattern affected by sewage effluent and urban runoff; large net import to the catchment. Urban extent more than doubled between 1960-2002.

name: Ray at Water Eaton
description-summary: A ultrasonic gauging station located on the River Ray, in the upper Thames catchment.
description-general: Multi-path US superseded (in 1989) a Crump weir (width: 5.195m) with crest and d/s recorders.
description-station-hydrometry: NA
description-flow-record: Thames backwater caused frequent drowning and high submergence ratios thus flood data are of limited precision.
description-catchment: The Ray rises in the Marlborough Downs and drains a relatively flat, mainly impervious, catchment. Largely agricultural land use but very substantial and growing urban component (Swindon).
description-flow-regime: Responsive regime. Flows heavily influenced by Swindon runoff (sewage effluent, balancing ponds etc.). A net import of water results.

name: Chess at Rickmansworth
description-summary: The station is located in the lower catchment of the River Chess.
description-general: A crump weir (6.0m broad) with downstream recorder for non-modularity adjustment. Used for both water resource and flood warning/forecasting purposes. The Chess is a chalk stream with intemittence in the upper catchment.
description-station-hydrometry: Full range station but non-modular at high flows (tail levels monitored). Weir equation used since construction. Gravel accumulates above the weir. Protected flows derived from standard Crump weir equation using tail levels. A very small channel that is fed from a spring approximately 150m upstream, bypasses the weir and enters the river just downstream. The modular limit of the weir is head:tail ratio of 0.75 (~0.23m), extremely non-modular limit is head:tail ratio 0.92. All flows are adjusted for non-modularity, however, extremely non-modular flows are reduced too low, with deviations from the spot flow measurement of between 12 and 35% and resulting uncertainty in AMAX and POT series that is being investigated to improve flows.
description-flow-record: Generally a very reliable record in all but extremely non-modular flows. Periods of extremely non-modular flows in Feb 2001 and winter 2022/2023. Tail level adjustments used but surrounding data suggests the reduction factor has underestimated the true flow (see Hydrometric description). Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in August 2021 (WINFAP Files v10).
description-catchment: The Chess is a Chalk stream draining the dip-slope of the Chilterns (significant Drift cover). Headwaters are rural with significant urban growth in the lower valley. Chesham is the largest town.
description-flow-regime: Baseflow-dominated flow regime but artificial influences (primarily STW effluent) evident on the hydrograph. Abstractions are of a mainly low consumptive type with some groundwater abstractions for public water supply. There is a small net export from the catchment.

name: Gade at Bury Mill
description-summary: A non-standard flume structure located in the upper catchment of the River Gade, a tributary of the River Colne.
description-general: A non-standard rectangular flume with side contractions installed by Hemel Hempstead Development Corporation in the mid 1960s. The station was operated by the local authority until the mid 1970s when its operation passed to Thames Water and subsequently the Environment Agency. Used for both Water Resource and Flood Incident management. The station was closed 13/04/25, due to renaturalisation of the channel. The river was diverted to the new channel from 14/04/25. The station has been replaced by Gadebridge Park.
description-station-hydrometry: The original instrumentation was a Lea Integrating recorder and early records were of poor quality. Lea Recorder replaced in Jan 1978 by the more accurate Munro Recorder. One rating applied across period of record. Rating has tendency to overestimate low flows, peak flows show good agreement with calibration gaugings. Stage at Q95 lower than recommended for a flume structure. A large fall at the end of the structure ensures modular conditions throughout. Before Jan 1978, peaks were attenuated by use of upstream automatic sluice gate which passed flow into storage pond.
description-flow-record: Upstream channel through park is perched, through periods of high groundwater levels and high rainfall events the river will overtop into the park. Upstream trash screen prone to blockage and can also cause out of bank flow. Some gaps in data caused by vandalism of recording hut. Springflow is culverted through the park and enters the river downstream of the gauging station. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in August 2025 (WINFAP Files v14).
description-catchment: Dip-slope stream draining the Chilterns. The solid geology is Chalk with some tertiary and extensive boulder clay cover. A mainly rural catchment draining to Hemel Hempstead (part of which is u/s of the station).
description-flow-regime: Baseflow-dominated regime with significant artificial disturbance. The urban response runoff has a significant effect on flood peaks. Balancing ponds u/s within built-up area.

name: Cole at Inglesham
description-summary: The station, located in the lower River Cole catchment, forms part of the structure that splits the channel into two distributaries that flow into the River Thames.
description-general: Compound Crump Weir (high central crest).
description-station-hydrometry: The channel divides immediately below the weir, so levels in the left channel are higher than in the right channel. Part of the structure (left-hand side) is subject to non-modular conditions due to the differing levels in the weirs and this can cause significant data processing problems. Drowning, due to weed growth in summer, is likely. Standard Crump weir equation (summation of 3 crests) using tail levels. Tail reduction is employed in the left hand weir. Seems to estimate flows well.
description-flow-record: Peak flows, calculated before the current methods of calculation (pre-1992), may be too low as the whole weir was assumed to be drowned. D/s correction only applied to part of the structure, so some overestimation at extreme flows. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in August 2024 (WINFAP Files v13).
description-catchment: Chalk scarp headwaters but catchment is largely low-lying and impervious (clay). A mainly rural catchment with urban growth below the headwaters. The rapid development of eastern Swindon has been a recent major change. Storage ponds are also a catchment feature near Swindon.
description-flow-regime: Responsive regime with some baseflow from the Chalk. Runoff is influenced by gw abstraction/recharge.

name: Misbourne at Quarrendon Mill
description-summary: The station is located in the upper reaches of the River Misbourne.
description-general: Informal broad-crested control - secondary station, superseded in 1984 by the new Denham Lodge station d/s.
description-station-hydrometry: NA
description-flow-record: NA
description-catchment: The Misbourne is a dip-slope stream draining from the Chilterns - Chalk with a little Drift cover. Significant residential development in the valley but a largely rural (Green Belt) catchment given over to agriculture with scattered tracts of coniferous and mixed woodland.
description-flow-regime: Complex baseflow dominated regime (the Misbourne has a number of influent reaches). Substantial gw abstraction (especially for Aylesbury and Amersham) - historical decline in Misbourne flows.

name: Dollis Brook at Hendon Lane Bridge
description-summary: Station is located on Dollis Brook, within the upper catchment of the River Brent. The station was closed on the 13/05/2014 due to major siltation issues affecting flow measurements.
description-general: Flat V weir has replaced a compound broad-crested weir with rectangular thin-plate inset. Removed from peak flows dataset in May 2016 (WINFAP Files v4).
description-station-hydrometry: It suffers from a lack of confirmatory gaugings and severe siltation (both u/s and of the stilling well) though this is occasionally moderated by flushing via a sluice below weir. This can seriously affect hydrometric performance e.g. summer 2007. Unlikely to drown as there is a 2m drop over weir. Accumulation point for urban debris (trolleys, tyres, etc), especially in the u/s channel. Protected flows derived from standard flat V weir equation. Modular throughout the flow range. Poor fit to gaugings which precede rebuild in 1994. Lack of gaugings since the station was rebuilt in 1994. In April 2010, major de-silting works took place which restored operation for a time, however the scale and cost of ongoing maintenance was prohibitive to keeping the station operable.
description-flow-record: Some anomalous low flows (e.g. March 1997). Time series should be used with caution.
description-catchment: Catchment in north-west of London that contain the suburbs of Barnet and Hendon. There are significant rural tracts in the western headwaters. the geology is entirely London Clay of Eocene age. It is largely Drift free.
description-flow-regime: Very responsive regime.

name: Brent at Monks Park
description-summary: The station is located in North-West London on the River Brent, below Wealdstone Brook confluence and the Brent Reservoir.
description-general: Critical depth flume (rectangular) in a concrete channel, d/s of Brent Reservoir (informally called the Welsh Harp Reservoir).
description-station-hydrometry: One rating applied across period of record. The weir is insensitive at low flows. There are discrepancies between the rating and low flow gaugings. However at stages higher than 0.25m the rating is much more reliable. Downstream debris screen (approx. 700m) can cause a backwater effect at the weir resulting in non-modular conditions and overestimation of flow. The extent of the effect is not fully known but has been witnessed during larger events. Screen is maintained by Environment Agency field team but not on a regular basis.
description-flow-record: Peak flow data before water-year 1978/1979 has not been re-calculated using rating New1 as there is no stage data available. These events are calculated through the old rating. New rating gave minimal change to flow magnitude across the flow range so flows pre-1978 are still usable. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in August 2024 (WINFAP Files v13).
description-catchment: A largely urban/suburban catchment in North-West London.
description-flow-regime: Responsive regime with very artificial low flow pattern. Welsh Harp reservoir is upstream. The Canal and River Trust can take a maximum of 1.7 Ml/d from the Welsh Harp reservoir to feed the Grand Union Canal. Run-off from the North Circular road enters the river approximately 1.5km upstream of the station.

name: Crane at Marsh Farm
description-summary: The station is located in the lower catchment of the River Crane, just above the confluence with the River Thames in London. The Crane splits upstream of the gauging station at Mereway Flood Defence Gate. A feed is taken into the Duke of Northumberlands river and flows through Mogden sewage treatment works, whilst the main channel of the Crane continues down through Marsh Farm gauging station.
description-general: Rectangular critical depth flume (insensitive) in a straight concrete channel. Capacity approx. 30 cumecs; yet to be exceeded.
description-station-hydrometry: Theoretical rating; modular limit to be determined. Fish and eel passage were installed at Marsh Farm on 8/9th June 2021.
description-flow-record: NA
description-catchment: Very flat catchment. The drainage network is difficult to delineate. Mainly urban; catchment contains Heathrow Airport and several pumped storage reservoirs (abstracting from Thames).
description-flow-regime: Substantial artificial influence on flow pattern, evident at low flows: sewage effluent, automatic weir upstream at Mereway Flood Defence Gate that diverts flow into the Dukes River (may result in negligible flows), and considerable area of gravel workings. Mereway Flood Defence Gate was refurbished between February and March 2020. Problems with the refurbishment have meant the gate was subsequently manually altered to maintain a suitable operational level, causing irregular flow patterns at Marsh Farm. Some natural runoff gain from the River Colne catchment (but unlikely to compensate for the upstream diversion).

name: Quaggy at Manor House Gardens
description-summary: A critical depth flume. Very responsive regime.
description-general: A critical depth flume (width: 4m, wing wall height: 2m) in a concrete channel. Removed from peak flows dataset in February 2018 (WINFAP Files v6). Station closed.
description-station-hydrometry: The flume was constructed in 1961 and calibrated theoretically - the low flow rating has since been revised on the basis of c/m gauging results; more gauging required to confirm the high flow rating). Modular range uncertain. One peak flow rating applied across period of record. Current rating derived by hydraulic modelling. Good fit to gaugings although none at high flows. More current meter readings needed from 0.4m to bankfull at 2m.
description-flow-record: The structure was overwhelmed by the 1968 flood but sensibly full range otherwise. The September 1968 flood estimated at about 15 cumecs - bypassed the station, and exceeded the range of the recorder. Until June 1978, flows read from chart (rather than stage) - stages derived from rating applied, or GLC data where available.
description-catchment: The catchment is a mixture of urban and suburban development.
description-flow-regime: Very responsive regime.

name: Wealdstone Brook at Wembley
description-summary: North-West London station located in the urbanised middle reaches of the River Brent.
description-general: Flat V profile weir in a culvert (below Olympic Way Wembley). Following modifications to the structure in 1978, it was refurbished but the crest is sub-standard.
description-station-hydrometry: Not originally designed as a measurement structure but as a method of hydraulically reducing the head to allow free conveyance under the culverts supporting beams. The station was reviewed in 2010. A discharge point, that entered the channel immediately d/s of the weir, compromised gaugings. Approach conditions not ideal in high flow. One rating applied across period of record. The structure is non-standard and a few gaugings suggest that the theoretical rating may not be applicable especially in peak flow range.
description-flow-record: Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in August 2024 (WINFAP Files v13).
description-catchment: A largely impervious urban/suburban catchment in West London.
description-flow-regime: Responsive regime.

name: Thames at Buscot
description-summary: Gauging station located on the main River Thames channel in the upper catchment that was closed in 1998.
description-general: Complex weir - radial gates and overfall weirs - embracing two channels. Two u/s and two d/s head recorders.
description-station-hydrometry: All but highest flows contained. Calibrated using c/m measurements.
description-flow-record: NA
description-catchment: Mixed geology; runoff from the Cotswolds (Oolitic L'st) provides a significant baseflow but the Oxford Clay valley is much more responsive. Land use: rural/agricultural with settlements concentrated in the valley where gravel extraction is significant.
description-flow-regime: Small net export of water (due to gw abstraction).

name: Pinn at Uxbridge
description-summary: West London flood warning level-only gauging station located on the River Pinn at Uxbridge.
description-general: Initially an electromagentic station (overhead coil) in a formalised trapezoidal section. Flow derivation ceased due to the failure of the electromagnetic equipment in 2004 and station since has measured water level only, with data used for management of canal navigation. The station is being investigated (in 2025) for suitability for a bed mounted ADVP with a view to reopening the station for flow measurement.
description-station-hydrometry: Full-range capability but limited number of higher flow gaugings suggest substantial overestimation in this range.
description-flow-record: Multiple 0.01 cumecs entries are an instrumental artifact.
description-catchment: An impermeable (largely London Clay) surburban catchment west of London. Headwaters rise in the countryside but substantial urban development throughout the catchment - including Pinner, Ruislip and Ickenham.
description-flow-regime: Very flashy regime. Very limited impact of artificial influences on the flow pattern, particularly given its suburban character.

name: Ampney Brook at Ampney St Peter
description-summary: The station is located within the upper Thames catchment in the headwaters of Ampney Brook.
description-general: Flat V weir, 1:10 cross-slope.
description-station-hydrometry: Theoretical calibration confirmed by gaugings. Drowning unlikely (but d/s stilling well installed). Full range.
description-flow-record: Realistic late-2000 flow pattern (rare amongst Cotswold stations).
description-catchment: The Ampney Brook is a dip-slope stream draining the pervious Great Oolite of the Cotswolds. A rural catchment with small, scattered settlements. The contributing area is greater than the topographical catchment.
description-flow-regime: Primarily natural baseflow-dominated regime but gw abstraction lower down the Churn catchment is likely to have an impact. Station is located just d/s of a fish farm (now closed).

name: Swill Brook at Oaksey
description-summary: The gauging station is located on Swill Brook, in the headwaters of the River Thames.
description-general: Flat V weir installed in 2002 (with US installed more recently to improve measurement when FV drowned). Superseded unreliable EM. Not a primary gauging station.
description-station-hydrometry: Some bypassing at high flows over 2.2 cumecs.
description-flow-record: Early flow record is patchy. Large range of velocities. Zero flow during most summers and monitoring of the lowest flow rates is suspect.
description-catchment: Relatively flat, rural catchment given over to agriculture. Primarily impervious (Oxford Clay).
description-flow-regime: Essentially natural, responsive, flow regime but runoff may be influenced by gw pumping from the confined Oolite aquifer.

name: Aldbourne at Ramsbury
description-summary: The gauging station is located on the Aldbourne River, a tributary of the River Kennet, on the site of an old matchstick plantation. Site declared unsafe due to over mature trees rooted in shallow soil blowing over. Station closed in 2015 and decommissioned in 2017-18, removing barriers to fish movement along an important tributary of the Kennet SSSi.
description-general: Two Flat V weirs - 1:10 cross-slopes (one is located on a bypass stream).
description-station-hydrometry: Theoretical calibration. All flows contained.
description-flow-record: Flows 3/8/2000-28/10/2000 modelled by EA. Stilling well froze in Nov/Dec 2010; late-winter and spring flows under review. Some flows in Nov and Dec 2011 were estimated due to equipment failure.
description-catchment: The Aldbourne drains a Chalk downland catchment (very modest Drift cover). Land use: predominantly agricultural - Aldbourne is the only significant settlement.
description-flow-regime: Sensibly natural baseflow-dominated flow regime.

name: Misbourne at Denham Lodge
description-summary: The station is located in the lower reaches of the River Misbourne, close to the confluence of the River Colne. Flow is a summation of Denham Lodge Main and Denham Lodge Side.
description-general: Built in 1984 and operated as a full range gauging station it comprises of two gauging weirs, a 3.5m wide Crump weir on the main channel and a 2m wide Flat V weir on a small distributary that flows through the golf course and enters the Colne upstream of the Denham Colne gauging station (39010). The main channel enters the Colne downstream of the Denham Colne gauging station and downstream of the River Frays split. Station added to peak flows dataset in August 2026 (WINFAP Files v15).
description-station-hydrometry: Two stable weirs both using the BS theoretical equation to derive flow. Both have tail recorders to adjust flows for non-modularity. The main weir has a high modular limit, occasionally going non modular but never fully drowning. The side weir suffers from variable backwater and will drown on occasions. The theoretical equations have been used for the entire flow record.
description-flow-record: Flow through the side channel controlled by a penstock within the grounds of the Mill House. It is operated frequently and this is evident in the rapid rise and fall in flow. Peak flow values pre-1986 should be treated with caution, due to poor validation against daily flow data and absence of supporting sub-daily data prior to November 1986. Additional uncertainty applies to the 86/87 AMAX, as the source of the annual maximum cannot be determined with confidence.
description-catchment: Elongated dip-slope catchment in the Chilterns (Chalk with appreciable Drift cover). Significant urban growth in valley but catchment is largely Green Belt - agriculture with scattered tracts of woodland. Topographical catchment area confirmed as 94.8 sq.km (groundwater catchment estimated at 81 sq.km.).
description-flow-regime: Baseflow dominated Chalk stream, influent in some reaches (e.g. near the Chalfonts). Runoff substantially diminished by PWS abstractions; partially counteracted by alleviation of low flow scheme from 1992.

name: Kennet at Newbury
description-summary: Cross-correlation gauge located in Newbury, in the middle reaches of the River Kennet.
description-general: From December 2019 onwards, a cross-correlation gauge. From November 2016 onwards a side-looking ADCP gauge. Pre-November 2016, an ultrasonic with six pairs of transducers in cross-path configuration.
description-station-hydrometry: Full range, but relatively high velocities.
description-flow-record: No data held for period of side looker installation (November 2016 - December 2019).
description-catchment: Principally a Chalk catchment but small tracts of low permeability above the station. Mainly rural (arable and mixed farming) with some urban growth concentrated along the valley.
description-flow-regime: Sensibly natural baseflow dominated flow regime but possible small impact of WBGS during drought conditions.

name: Mole at Esher
description-summary: Ultrasonic gauging station situation on Mole Flood Aleviation Scheme. Gates upstream and downstream of the section.
description-general: New ultrasonic, full range capability and improved reliability. Replaced earlier US just u/s (in a reach created as part of the Mole Flood alleviation Scheme); debris and siltation (blocking transducers) and high temperature gradients caused substantial malfunction particularly at low flows. New gauge is prone to weed in channel, which can cause issues at low flows. Station added to peak flows dataset in September 2022 (WINFAP Files v11).
description-station-hydrometry: Flow and levels are affected by downstream Island Barn Weir and upstream Viaduct Sluice. Both are operated as part of the Lower Mole Flood Aleviation Scheme in high flows.
description-flow-record: Several drop outs in record including December 2016 due to level being dropped downstream to perform channel maintenance work. WY1998/1999 rejected because it is a partial first year of the record, and WY2009/2010 rejected as AMAX likely occured during period of fault with the gauge - GDF infilled.
description-catchment: A largely impervious catchment divided by the W-E trending ridge of the North Downs (Chalk and Upper Greensand). Diverse land use - rural tracts and considerable suburban development.
description-flow-regime: Responsive regime. Some sewage effluent derives from outside the catchment.

name: Thame at Wheatley
description-summary: Located on the River Thame at Wheatley the ultrasonic gauging station superseded the upstream station at Shabbington (39038).
description-general: Multi-path US (cross- configuration).
description-station-hydrometry: Full range, railway embankment ensures no bypassing. Skewed flow, weed-growth and summer temperature gradients can limit accuracy particularly at low flows (e.g. early autumn 2009).
description-flow-record: Approximately 80 cumecs gauged in 01/2003. Flows in August 2017 affected by weed growth. Missing data in December 2019 due to station upgrade works.
description-catchment: The Thame drains a typical clay (principally Oxford Clay, some Greensand also) vale NW of the Chiltern escarpment. Land use is largely agricultural (considerable grassland) while the urban areas within the catchment include the town is Aylesbury.
description-flow-regime: Some spring flow contribution but responsive regime. Net import of water; sewage effluent is a significant component of low flows.

name: Mole at Leatherhead
description-summary: Ultrasonic station gauging a mixed land use catchment.
description-general: Currently ultrasonic, replacing an electromagnetic gauge in 2009.
description-station-hydrometry: NA
description-flow-record: Gap and some flow truncation in the time series between 1996 and 2009.
description-catchment: A predominantly impervious (Weald Clay) catchment which drains through the Box Hill gap in the North Downs (Chalk and Upper Greensand). Diverse land use.
description-flow-regime: Some sewage effluent derives from outside the catchment; Gw abstraction from the Chalk headwaters also.

name: Hogsmill at Ewell
description-summary: Rectangular flume; stage-discharge relation confirmed by c/m gaugings.
description-general: Rectangular flume; Modular. Overfall u/s. Frequently vandalised. Station downgraded in 2010 to level only.
description-station-hydrometry: Grounding of float (stilling well floor corresponds to throat level of flume) can affect low flow accuracy. Debris on u/s grill can influence levels.
description-flow-record: Patchy flow record.
description-catchment: A largely suburban catchment developed mostly on Chalk (dip-slope of North Downs). Mean runoff suggests that topographical catchment greatly exceeds the contributing area.
description-flow-regime: NA

name: Churn at Perrott's Brook
description-summary: Flat V weir located in the upper River Churn, at the western edge of the Thames catchment.
description-general: Flat V weir, 6 metres wide, 1:10 cross-slope.
description-station-hydrometry: Full range - tailwater levels measured to facilitate flow computation in the non-modular range (but further gaugings are required to check the reduction factor).
description-flow-record: Zero flow in severe drought conditions. Extreme flow in July 2007. Data missing for Nov/Dec 2000 (when previous maximum would have been exceeded).
description-catchment: Permeable (Oolitic L'st) catchment on the dip-slope of the Cotswolds. Land use: mostly agricultural, some woodland and scattered settlements.
description-flow-regime: Baseflow dominant regime.

name: Coln at Fossebridge
description-summary: Gauging station, located in the upper River Coln, situated above structures at Bibury (39020) and Fairford (39110).
description-general: Crump-profile crest, 7.8m wide (constructed on original overfall).
description-station-hydrometry: Modular until high flows but submerged in floods as flow is restricted by a d/s culvert and construction under a d/s bridge. Some bypassing also occurs. Intermittent flow in small bypass channel not measured.
description-flow-record: NA
description-catchment: A rural, dip-slope, catchment developed on the Oolitic L'st of the Cotswolds.
description-flow-regime: Baseflow-dominated regime.

name: Coln at Fairford
description-summary: Gauging station located on the lower River Coln.
description-general: Opened as an electromagnetic gauging station (buried coil). Ultrasonic since 2011.
description-station-hydrometry: Current meter calibration to be completed. Station performance is generally good to bankfull (flows unreliable during exceptional floods (e.g. during the extreme July 2007 event). Reasonable velocities are maintained at low flows (0.5 cumecs is a typical drought minimum), but flows may be overestimated by around 10%. Weed growth impacted site between April and July 2025.
description-flow-record: NA
description-catchment: Linear catchment on the dip-slope of the Cotswolds (Oolitic Limestone). Rural with scattered settlements.
description-flow-regime: Baseflow-dominated regime. Levels affected by STW.

name: Thames at Staines
description-summary: Ultrasonic gauging station located on the main channel of the River Thames, within the lower reaches of the catchment.
description-general: US multi-path (6) in cross configuration. Transducers are located in piles set in the channel.
description-station-hydrometry: Excellent agreement between multi-meter check gaugings and US calibration. Levels affected by gate and lock movements. In hot weather temperature gradients can deflect beams.
description-flow-record: Gap in data August 2018 - June 2019 due to site works.
description-catchment: Scarp and vale topography. Diverse geology. Predominantly rural headwaters contrast with substantial urban and suburban development in the lower reaches.
description-flow-regime: Major PWS abstractions u/s very evident at low flows.

name: Letcombe Brook at Arabellas Lake
description-summary: Gauging station located in the headwaters of Letcombe Brook, a tributary of the River Ock.
description-general: Flat V weir at outfall of the lake.
description-station-hydrometry: NA
description-flow-record: Zero flow during notable droughts.
description-catchment: Catchment area derived from the Digital Terrain Model. The Letcombe Brook is fed from springs issuing from the scarp slope of the Lambourn Downs (Chalk, Drift free); contributing area is very rural.
description-flow-regime: Baseflow-dominated regime of the Letcombe Brook is heavily influenced by gw abstraction; flow augmentation scheme in operation.

name: Manor Farm Brook at Letcombe Regis
description-summary: Gauging station located in a headwater tributary of Letcombe Brook.
description-general: Flat V weir.
description-station-hydrometry: NA
description-flow-record: Interludes of zero flow in most years.
description-catchment: The Manor Farm Brook is fed by spring flow issuing from the scarp slope of the Lambourn Downs (Chalk). A very rural catchment.
description-flow-regime: Spring outflow. Flow augmented to counteract impact of gw abstractions (external to the topographical catchment).

name: Pang at Frilsham
description-summary: Gauging station located in the ephemeral stretch of the River Pang.
description-general: Flat V weir.
description-station-hydrometry: Floods exceed bankfull and weed growth causes occasional drowning (flows adjusted but high submergence ratios limit accuracy). Station was used to monitor progress under alleviation of low flows programme (reduction of headwater abstractions).
description-flow-record: NA
description-catchment: A largely permeable (Chalk with modest Drift cover) rural catchment; mostly arable and pasture with significant woodland on the Tertiary outcrops (in the south).
description-flow-regime: Baseflow dominated regime; effluent can form a significant component of low flows.

name: Pang at Bucklebury
description-summary: Gauging station located in the mid reaches of the River Pang.
description-general: Flat V weir.
description-station-hydrometry: All flows contained but weed growth causes drowning. Station monitored progress under alleviation of low flows programme (headwater abstractions impacted runoff but abstractions greatly reduced since 1992).
description-flow-record: Flows adjusted (due to weed growth) but high submergence ratios limit accuracy (e.g. May/June 1995 when flows unreliable).
description-catchment: A very rural and largely permeable (Chalk with modest Drift cover)) catchment with significant areas of woodland on the Tertiary outcrops.
description-flow-regime: Flows affected by STW effluent and, rarely, by West Berkshire Groundwater Scheme.

name: Sulham Brook at Sulham
description-summary: Gauging station located on Sulham Brook, a small tributary of the main River Thames.
description-general: Flat V weir. U/s and d/s levels monitored.
description-station-hydrometry: Modest d/s gradient and limited channel capacity/siltation cause the structure to drown for substantial periods. Silt build-up regularly caused by cows wading upstream of the weir. Both factors affect flow calculation.
description-flow-record: NA
description-catchment: A very rural catchment developed mostly on Chalk (with substantial Drift cover); some woodland on the Tertiary outcrops.
description-flow-regime: Relatively responsive regime. Topographical catchment is substantially less than the true contributing area; runoff (which is reduced by gw abstraction) is therefore unrepresentative - in wet years runoff can greatly exceed rainfall. Levels/flows affected by STW until the mid-1990s (when effluent diverted).

name: Colne Brook at Hythe End
description-summary: Gauging station located on a distributory of the River Colne.
description-general: Electromagnetic gauging station (buried coil).
description-station-hydrometry: NA
description-flow-record: NA
description-catchment: Mixed land use catchment.
description-flow-regime: NA

name: Wey at Alton
description-summary: Gauging station located in the headwaters of the River Wey.
description-general: Flat V weir (1:10) cross-slope. U/s and d/s levels monitored.
description-station-hydrometry: Weir lowered in 2002; drowning now occurs more frequently.
description-flow-record: NA
description-catchment: Mostly Chalk (with significant Drift cover); Upper Greensand outcrops in the east. Alton is the only large settlement; land use is largely pasture/arable. Topographic catchment differs from groundwater contributing area.
description-flow-regime: Baseflow dominated regime. The upper Wey is ephemeral. Significant abstractions in the catchment.

name: Wey at Kings Pond (Alton)
description-summary: Gauging station located in the headwaters of the River Wey, just downstream of the Wey at Alton (39118).
description-general: Rectangular thin-plate weir at outfall from lake.
description-station-hydrometry: Theoretical rating. Debris obstructing u/s grill can cause minor fluctuations in level.
description-flow-record: Flow data for Apr-Jul 1995 unreliable due to weed growth. Zero flow during notable droughts.
description-catchment: Mostly Chalk (with significant Drift cover) and Upper Greensand. Rural (apart from Alton).
description-flow-regime: Baseflow-dominated regime but some local urban runoff. Topographic catchment differs from groundwater contributing area.

name: Caker Stream at Alton
description-summary: Guaging station located in the headwaters of the River Wey system.
description-general: Flat V weir. U/s and d/s levels monitored.
description-station-hydrometry: Weed growth controlled by regular maintenance.
description-flow-record: NA
description-catchment: Mixed geology (largely Chalk with substantial Drift cover). A rural catchment. Contributing area substantially less than the topographical catchment: unrepresentative mean annual runoff.
description-flow-regime: Ephemeral stream but relatively responsive. Groundwater-dominated regime.

name: Thames at Walton
description-summary: Ultrasonic gauging station located on the main channel of the River Thames.
description-general: Multi-path, cross configuration US.
description-station-hydrometry: Gaugings confirm calibration. In hot weather the gauge can malfunction (due to temperature gradients in the measuring section).
description-flow-record: No routine naturalisation - therefore d/s Kingston (39001) series is more hydrologically representative).
description-catchment: Scarp and vale topography developed on diverse geology. Predominately rural headwaters contrast with considerable suburban growth in the lower valley.
description-flow-regime: NA

name: Cranleigh Waters at Bramley
description-summary: Gauging station located on Cranleigh Waters, a tributary that flows into the River Wey, south of the town of Guilford.
description-general: Multi-path cross-configuration ultrasonic gauging station beneath road bridge.
description-station-hydrometry: Enlarged bridge opening creates large capacity but, correspondingly, low velocities; these can impact on low flow precision. Full range station.
description-flow-record: Notable Nov. 2000 peak under review.
description-catchment: Predominantly impervious Weald Clay with some Lower Greensand in lower reaches. A largely rural catchment (south of Guildford) centred on Cranleigh.
description-flow-regime: Flashy response with lengthy periods of very low flow. Low flows influenced by effluent returns. Station is used for flood monitoring purposes.

name: Blackwater at Farnborough
description-summary: Side-look Acoustic Doppler Current Profiler (ADCP) gauge located on the River Blackwater at Farnborough.
description-general: Currently side-look ADCP. Side-look US installed in February 2009. This replaced the decommissioned EM. The EM had been installed as part of a R&D project into flow within two stage channels.
description-station-hydrometry: Calibration to be completed. Gaugings indicate that EM flows are overestimated in the low and medium range.
description-flow-record: September 1997 and 1998 flows particularly suspect but all flows should be treated with caution.
description-catchment: Tertiary geology - mainly Bagshot Beds with London Clay in the headwaters and alluvium in the valley. Substantial and expanding urban development including Farnborough and Aldershot but large rural tracts remain; significant areas of heathland and woodland.
description-flow-regime: Flows managed by STW, supplemented in summer. Siltation occurs.

name: Ver at Redbourn
description-summary: Gauging station located on the upper River Ver that was initially constructed to monitor low flows.
description-general: Flat-V weir (4.0m wide).
description-station-hydrometry: U/s and d/s level measurements are routinely made. Drowns but d/s reach regularly maintained by dredging to improve modularity.
description-flow-record: Groundwater-fed intermittent stream, with zero flows recorded during dry years. Runoff reduced by groundwater abstraction - which has greatly diminished since May 1993 (the Ver is included in the EA Alleviation of Low Flows Programme).
description-catchment: A predominantly rural catchment on the dip-slope of the Chilterns (Chalk with significant Drift cover); land-use mainly arable and pasture. Part of Redbourn is immediately above the station.
description-flow-regime: Groundwater-fed ephemeral stream. Runoff reduced by gw abstraction - which has greatly diminished since May 1993 (the Ver is included in the EA's Alleviation of Low Flows Programme).

name: Red at Redbourn
description-summary: Gauging station located on the upper River Ver that was initially constructed to monitor low flows.
description-general: Flat-V weir (4.0m wide) which frequently drowns.
description-station-hydrometry: Upstream and downstream measurements are routinely made. Downstream reach regularly maintained by dredging which improves modularity. Built in an over wide channel which has naturally narrowed over the years. Silt berms have built up on left bank up to the weir. Downstream channel also has narrowed, during high flow events the level backs up and drowns the weir.
description-flow-record: Flow data for Feb 1995 unreliable due to weed growth.
description-catchment: A predominantly rural catchment on the dip-slope of the Chilterns (Chalk); land-use is mainly arable/pasture; some urban development.
description-flow-regime: Groundwater-fed intermittent stream (but can be responsive).

name: Misbourne at Little Missenden
description-summary: Gauging station located in the headwaters of the River Misbourne.
description-general: Rectangular thin-plate weir with flanking Crump crests.
description-station-hydrometry: Theoretical rating supported by gaugings (more scheduled to confirm calibration). Fish screen on the structure regularly gets blocked with blanket weed causing upstream level to increase and overtop the banks. Water bypasses the weir. The screen is regularly cleaned but when doing so it causes a spike in the level as the built up head flushes through.
description-flow-record: Very rare, and minor, bypassing during extreme flood conditions (e.g. Feb. 2001). Instrumentation difficulties over the 12/2006 - 5/2007 period, data under review.
description-catchment: A mostly rural catchment on the dip-slope of the Chilterns (Chalk); some development in the lower catchment.
description-flow-regime: The Misbourne is a Chalk stream; ephemeral, and influent in some reaches. Heavy (but declining) gw pumping in the headwaters has reduced base flows (the Misbourne is included in the EA Low Flow Alleviation Programme).

name: Bourne (South) at Addlestone
description-summary: Ultrasonic station with patchy early record.
description-general: Cross-path time-of-flight ultrasonic station installed in 2012/13. After becoming ultrasonic, a bund was added to promote head level at low flows. Prior to ultrasonic, this was a velocity area station - low level sharp-crested weir (rather insensitive with poor approach conditions).
description-station-hydrometry: Control passes to road bridge at medium/high flows. Some confirmatory gaugings up to approx. 10 cumecs. Possible bypassing into R. Wey system (via canal) at very high flows. Rating change in Oct 1993 (earlier data may need reprocessing).
description-flow-record: Patchy early record (when no back-up recorder).
description-catchment: The geology is largely impermeable Bagshot Beds. Very mixed land use with woodland and heath plus significant urban development.
description-flow-regime: Responsive regime.

name: Thames at Farmoor
description-summary: Ultrasonic gauging station located on the main River Thames, downstream of the intake for Farmoor Reservoir.
description-general: Multi-path cross-configuration US.
description-station-hydrometry: Substantial left-bank by-passing (not via the Thames itself) under flood conditions.
description-flow-record: Drought flow accuracy uncertain (at very low velocities) and gaugings suggest that flows may be overestimated by around 5%. Naturalised flows not routinely calculated.
description-catchment: Catchment is predominantly rural u/s of the station. The geology is mixed - pervious headwaters (Oolitic l'st), Oxford Clay in the lower reaches.
description-flow-regime: Levels affected by d/s gate movements, abstractions and lockages.

name: Thames at Reading
description-summary: Ultrasonic gauging station located on the main river channel under Reading Bridge.
description-general: Multi-path cross-configuration US sited beneath Reading Bridge (incorporates adjustment for flows outside the transducer piers).
description-station-hydrometry: Very minor bypassing via Gosbrook stream. Good c/m confirmation of calibration throughout the range.
description-flow-record: Doppler gauging on 4/1/2003 at 300-310 cumecs.
description-catchment: Mixed geology with Cotswold headwaters (Oolitic L'st) and Oxford Clay. The land use is predominantly rural but with important, and growing, urban development in the valley (i.e. Oxford and Reading).
description-flow-regime: River levels affected by d/s weir and lock.

name: Brent at Costons Lane Greenford
description-summary: A flat V weir, the lowest flow gauging station on the River Brent.
description-general: An 11.25m flat V weir with vertical wing walls. Built in 1988, primarily for water resource purposes but used as a full range station used for flood warning and forecasting. Station does not record the Greenford Brook tributary that joins immediately downstream.
description-station-hydrometry: Flow is calculated using the ISO calculation for flat V-weir. Summer low flows and weed growth make it difficult to carry out calibration gaugings. There is no tail recorder to define a modular limit, but there is no evidence to suggest that the weir drowns. Gauge is not bypassed in high flows. Gauged within 22% of QMED.
description-flow-record: Complete 15-min flow record available from 1988.
description-catchment: The Brent catchment covers approximately 170km2 and flows from Totteridge and Stanmore to the River Thames at Brentford, Hounslow. The catchment is largely urban (>50%) and suburban in the North West of London which has developed over London Clay.
description-flow-regime: Flow does not incorporate the d/s Greenford brook tributary. The Welsh Harp reservoir has significant impact on the flow regime.

name: Wandle at Carshalton Ponds
description-summary: Rectangular sharp-edged weir constructed to monitor compensation inflows by Sutton and District Water Company.
description-general: Rectangular sharp-edged weir, not a primary gauging station.
description-station-hydrometry: Occasional problems with clinging nappe.
description-flow-record: Drop out in flow in December 2017 due to pump failure not providing water to the ponds.
description-catchment: The Wandle is spring-fed (Chalk), but catchment is predominantly London Clay. Mainly urban/suburban land use.
description-flow-regime: During dry conditions, flow is almost entirely augmented by pumping from downstream into Carshalton Ponds.

name: Ravensbourne at Bromley South
description-summary: Flat V weir (1:10 cross slope) with vertical wing walls. Very responsive flow regime.
description-general: Flat V weir (1:10 cross slope) with vertical wing walls. Straight approach with no significant modification to flow regime. Original structure built in 1962 as a critical depth flume. The structure was rebuilt in 1992.
description-station-hydrometry: Full range station, which has been theoretically rated (standard Flat V weir calculation). Higher gaugings show the structure appears to over-estimate higher flows. More gaugings are needed, but due to responsive regime it is difficult to capture high flow gaugings.
description-flow-record: Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2019 (WINFAP Files v8).
description-catchment: The Ravensbourne rises from springs fed by Tertiary Sandstones (in Holwood Park). The majority of the lower catchment is mainly impervious, due to Eocene clay deposits and high levels of urban development (South London).
description-flow-regime: Very responsive flow regime.

name: Quaggy at Chinbrook Meadows
description-summary: Intermittent river that regularly dries during the summer. Flat V weir installed 2002.
description-general: Flat V weir installed 2002 (large fall d/s implies full modular range); replaced (with marginal increase in catchment area) rectangular critical depth flume (flood walls added May 1982) 220m u/s.
description-station-hydrometry: NA
description-flow-record: Sensibly continuous flow record. Original station subject to considerable gravel accretion.
description-catchment: Geology: London Clay, also Reading/Woolwich Beds. A linear urban/suburban catchment in south London.
description-flow-regime: Responsive regime. No significant artificial influences.

name: Yeading West at Gutteridge Wood
description-summary: The station is located on the Yeading Brook, West London.
description-general: Rectangular flume.
description-station-hydrometry: NA
description-flow-record: Flow data in January 2003 under review - minimum appears unrealistically low.
description-catchment: Largely impervious suburban catchment in NW London.
description-flow-regime: NA

name: Loddon at Twyford
description-summary: Gauging station, employing ADCP devices, located in the lower stages of the River Loddon just above the confluence with the River Thames.
description-general: Two side-looking ADCP devices, installed since 2010, located within two rectangular road bridge culverts. Previously, data was supplied by a multi-path US (cross configuration) located 200m d/s on a gently curving reach spanning the total length of the lower stages of the river.
description-station-hydrometry: Full range. MAF easily contained. Significant weed growth in summer. Large step in middle of channel leads to two levels of water.
description-flow-record: Ultrasonics affected by power supply and instrumentation problems (e.g. siltation caused difficulties with the lowest of the six flight paths) causing some record gaps. No flows recorded 2006-2010 due to removal of ultrasonic equipment, installation of ADCPs and development of index velocity rating. Site level only since Jan 2023.
description-catchment: Mixed geology and land use. Chalk headwaters, mainly London Clay below. Large rural tracts but substantial urban development, in the eastern catchment particularly.
description-flow-regime: U/s spillage (floodplain storage rather than bypassing) begins around 60 cumecs.

name: Ray at Islip
description-summary: Ultrasonic gauging station located in the lower reaches of the River Ray just above the confluence of the River Cherwell.
description-general: Multi-path cross-configuration US (in two-channel section).
description-station-hydrometry: Good hydrometric performance but very low velocities in low flow conditions.
description-flow-record: NA
description-catchment: Relatively flat impermeable (Oxford Clay) catchment given over largely to agriculture (but includes Bicester). The station is just below Otmoor.
description-flow-regime: Only minor disturbances to the natural (and responsive) flow regime.

name: Wey at Guildford
description-summary: Ultrasonic gauging station installed below a road bridge in the centre of Guilford where the river and navigation channels are coincident.
description-general: Multi-path US (cross configuration) that was upgraded in 2003.
description-station-hydrometry: All but extremely rare flows contained.
description-flow-record: NA
description-catchment: Mixed geology and land use.
description-flow-regime: Responsive regime.

name: Windrush at Bourton on the Water
description-summary: Gauging station located in the upper reaches of the River Windrush.
description-general: Crump weir. U/s and d/s levels monitored.
description-station-hydrometry: The structure rarely drowns but submerged during exceptional floods.
description-flow-record: NA
description-catchment: The station is sited close to the edge of the Oolitic L'st outcrop. A largely permeable catchment, very rural in character.
description-flow-regime: Baseflow-dominated regime with significant groundwater abstraction.

name: Dikler at Bourton on the Water
description-summary: The gauging station is located on the River Dikler, a tributary of the upper River Windrush.
description-general: Crump Weir.
description-station-hydrometry: All flows contained, no bypassing but weir submerged during floods.
description-flow-record: NA
description-catchment: Mixed geology: Oolites and Lias. Rural catchment with very limited urban development (but the station is just below the town of Bourton-on-the-Water).
description-flow-regime: Substantial baseflow but responsive to rainfall. Significant gw abstraction.

name: Sor at Bodicote
description-summary: Located on Sor Brook, the crump weir replaced the Adderbury gauging station (39051) that closed in April 1988.
description-general: Crump Weir with u/s and d/s levels monitored.
description-station-hydrometry: NA
description-flow-record: Peak of the April 1998 flood was estimated at around 17 cumecs. Period between June and July 2024 removed due to erroneous data - infill requested.
description-catchment: Primarily an impermeable (Middle Lias) catchment. The catchment is rural in character.
description-flow-regime: Appreciable baseflow but also very responsive to rainfall. Significant abstraction u/s - but only operates when flows > 0.16 cumecs.

name: Yeading Brook East at Western Avenue A40
description-summary: Gauging station located on Yeading Brook East, West London.
description-general: Flat V weir that was rebuilt in 1993. Initially established from 1974 it was removed in 1981 and subsequently replaced in October 1985.
description-station-hydrometry: NA
description-flow-record: The NRFA holds records from 1995 onwards. The EA hold flow records from the 1988 water year.
description-catchment: A heavily urbanised catchment developed in London Clay.
description-flow-regime: Very responsive regime.

name: Mill Brook at Blewbury
description-summary: Gauging station located downstream of the Oxfordshire village of Blewbury at the foot of the Berkshire Downs.
description-general: Flat V weir.
description-station-hydrometry: NA
description-flow-record: Groundwater catchment substantially exceeds the topographical catchment; runoff totals are unrealistic.
description-catchment: Rural catchment developed on the Chalk (but Blewbury village is immediately u/s).
description-flow-regime: Stable regime - the Mill Brook is spring-fed. Thames Water abstraction occurs u/s. Flow constraint of 40 megalitres/day.

name: Wendover Springs at Wendover
description-summary: Earliest extant gauging station in the UK. It provides a unique insight into spring flow variability in the 19th century.
description-general: Thin-plate weir (0.91m wide) monitoring outflow from the Wendover Springs (into the Wendover Arm of the Grand Union Canal).
description-station-hydrometry: The station was commissioned in the 1962, processed flows from 1989 (microfilmed level charts for pre-1989 period). Complemented by historical monthly series 1841-1897; method of flow measurement uncertain but runoff patterns consistent with rainfall. Algal/weed growth on and u/s of the crest can affect levels - overestimating runoff.
description-flow-record: Some gaps in record, moreso in recent years. Large gap in data between from May 2024 to April 2025.
description-catchment: The Wendover Springs issue from the scarp slope of the Chilterns - Chalk (with a limited amount of Drift cover). Land use is mostly woodland and pasture but significant urban growth occurs near the gauging station.
description-flow-regime: NA

name: Thames at Maidenhead
description-summary: Ultrasonic gauging station (US) located on the lower reaches of the main River Thames.
description-general: NA
description-station-hydrometry: Multi-path ultrasonic gauge.
description-flow-record: Flows need to be added to the station at Taplow (39866) to get a representation of flow within the Thames.
description-catchment: Large catchment; scarp and vale topography developed on diverse geology. Predominately rural headwaters contrast with considerable suburban growth in the lower valley.
description-flow-regime: NA

name: Jubilee River at Taplow
description-summary: Ultrasonic gauging station located in a 12 km bypass channel of the River Thames.
description-general: Bypass channel commissioned in 2002 to alleviate flooding in Maidenhead, Bray and Windsor. Channel designed to carry 215 cumecs.
description-station-hydrometry: Multipath ultrasonic gauge.
description-flow-record: Flows need to be added to the station at Maidenhead (39148) to get a representation of flow within the Thames.
description-catchment: NA
description-flow-regime: NA

name: Medway at Weir Wood Reservoir
