Bounded to the north by the Ordovician inliers of Shucknall Hill and Bertestree. To the south bounded by the Silurian strata of the Woolhope Dome. Subdued relief, relatively low rainfall. Entirely rural, predominantly arable farming in lower areas with livestock on higher ground.
description-flow-regime: Mainly natural flow regime; runoff increased by effluent returns.

name: Pinsley Brook at Cholstrey Mill
description-summary: A Flat V weir located on the Pinsley brook, 3km upstream from the confluence with the River Lugg.
description-general: Flat V weir width with 1:5 downstream, 1:2 upstream and 1:5 cross stream slopes. The structure is 10m long and 2m wide with 1m high side walls. The station is located on the left bank of the Pinsley Brook, some 3km u/s from the confluence with the River Lugg.
description-station-hydrometry: Estimated bank full discharge is 3 cumecs. Gauged from adjacent footbridge.
description-flow-record: The catchment is of subdued relief as a result of the underlying marl-dominated strata of the Lower Old Red Sandstone and subsequent deposition of superficial deposits.
description-catchment: NA
description-flow-regime: NA

name: Lugg at Butts Bridge
description-summary: Velocity area station with low flows blockstone weir control.
description-general: Velocity area station with rough stone control (at low flows) providing flood warning station. Station rebuilt in 1984. Width at bankfull is 21m. Stanchion span is 24m.
description-station-hydrometry: Multiple ratings applied across period of record. Recent rating gauged to bankfull.
description-flow-record: July - Sept 1996 flows under review. Early peak flow data rejected due to uncertainty in pre-digital rating. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2019 (WINFAP Files v8). Ratings reviewed in 2022 and data reprocessed from 1988.
description-catchment: Headwaters drain Radnor Forest (developed on Silurian formations). Subdued relief in the lower valley (mostly Old Red Sandstone). Impervious catchment but extensive valley gravels provide some baseflow. Land use: mainly grassland in upper catchment, rough grazing with some forestry. Mixed farming with higher proportion of arable in the lower catchment.
description-flow-regime: Runoff reduced by public water supply abstraction.

name: Trothy at Mitchel Troy
description-summary: Velocity area station with Flat V weir. Level only station since 1982 for flood warning purposes.
description-general: Velocity area station, informal Flat V weir installed 1975 as a low flow control. Bankfull width approx 10 m. Level only station since 1982 for flood warning purposes.
description-station-hydrometry: Potential for station to be affected by backwater from arched bridge 40m downstream at high flows. Right bank is steep; left bank is lower and is where bypass starts above bankfull.
description-flow-record: NA
description-catchment: Area to south and west of Monmouth. Low rolling relief of catchment is underlain by strata of predominantly Upper and Lower Old Red Sandstone. Land use is rural, mainly agricultural with small areas of forestry.
description-flow-regime: NA

name: Wye at Redbrook
description-summary: Velocity area station, channel control. Modification of flows by reservoir regulation, public water supply abstraction and effluent returns.
description-general: Channel control velocity-area station replacing Cadora (55001, 1937-71; 4040 sq.km. which was tidally affected; flows incorporated in the Redbrook series). Width at bankfull stage approx 69m.
description-station-hydrometry: All but extreme floods contained. Severe summer weed growth problems causes gaugings to be increasingly undertaken by ADCP just u/s of Bigsweir Bridge, 7km d/s where channel is clearer. Gaugings at Redbrook are done by cableway. Flow regime moderately modified by exports and regulation. Two peak flow ratings applied across period of record.
description-flow-record: Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2020 (WINFAP Files v9).
description-catchment: Very large catchment; wet in upland areas to the west, drier in lower-lying areas in east and south. Mixed Palaeozoic geology, impermeable rocks of Ordovician to Carboniferous age. Catchment is mainly grassland, with moorland, forestry and grazing on higher ground; mixed farming with greater proportion of arable land in lower reaches. Little industrial development.
description-flow-regime: Modification of flows by exports and reservoir regulation, public water supply abstraction and effluent returns.

name: Llynfi at Three Cocks
description-summary: Velocity area station; informal broad-crested. Asymmetrical Flat V weir enhancing the natural rock bar control. Natural flow regime.
description-general: Velocity area station; informal broad-crested. Asymmetrical Flat V weir enhancing the natural rock bar control. Approx. width at bankfull stage is 16m.
description-station-hydrometry: Cableway was present, removed in 2010. Two peak flow ratings applied across period of record.
description-flow-record: Maximum peak flow occurred in Dec 1979 - this was undoubtedly exceptional although uncertainty surrounds the magnitude (198.4 cumecs on Peak flow database) as flow was extrapolated. Gap in record in 2001 the result of telemetry fault which could not be resolved due to Foot and Mouth restrictions. Data estimated for Aug - Nov 2003. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2020 (WINFAP Files v9).
description-catchment: Impermeable geology: headwaters drain the Old Red Sandstone of the Black Mountains; lower reaches expose Old Red Sandstone marls which have lower relief. Contains Llangorse Lake. Predominantly grassland with patches of woodland and some arable in lower reaches.
description-flow-regime: Natural to within 10% at Q95.

name: Wye at Ddol Farm
description-summary: Velocity area station with rock bar as control. Informal Flat V installed 1972. Natural flow regime.
description-general: Velocity area station with rock bar as control. Informal Flat V installed 1972. Station replaced 55005 Rhayader Groe (1937-69). Bankfull width 30m. No wingwalls/structure.
description-station-hydrometry: Cableway span 54m. All but exceptional floods contained. Issues with stilling well intake pipe from 2006, notably affecting low flows, lead to long-term reliance on back-up recorder and culminated in eventual station rebuild in 2012/13. Following rebuild in July 2013, all ratings reviewed. Two peak flow ratings across period of record.
description-flow-record: Flow series up to 1969 from 55005 Rhayader Groe; data generally thought to be of poorer quality. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2019 (WINFAP Files v8).
description-catchment: Wet, upland catchment draining impermeable, metamorphosed Silurian sediments. High relief, headwaters reach over 600m, and feature steep sided valleys and high gradient streams. Dominant land use is grassland with moorland and extensive areas of forest in headwaters.
description-flow-regime: Only gauging station on the main River Wye that is unaffected by large water supply reservoir (flows from Elan Valley Reservoir complex enter the Wye just d/s).

name: Rudhall Brook at Sandford Bridge
description-summary: Flat V Crump profile weir, with most data after 1991.
description-general: Flat V Crump profile weir.
description-station-hydrometry: NA
description-flow-record: Station reinstated in October 1991 (very little data for 1978-90 period). Data processing suspended in 1998 due to severe problems with the approach channel.
description-catchment: Small catchment on northern edge of the Forest of Dean. Mixed agriculture underlain by Old Red Sandstone.
description-flow-regime: NA

name: Frome at Bishops Frome
description-summary: A Flat V Crump weir which replaced a previous station in 1975.
description-general: Flat V Crump profile weir 5m wide, replaced velocity-area station in 1975. Cableway span 10m.
description-station-hydrometry: Steep banks do not contain flood flows; some throttling by d/s road bridge whose soffit is below bankfull.
description-flow-record: Rating review planned for the near future at this station, treat data with caution until this has been completed.
description-catchment: Natural catchment. Impermeable bedrock geology, headwaters cutting into ORS of Bromyard plateau. In NE area of Wye catchment, which is drier than other areas to W. Superficial deposits confined to valleys. Mixed arable and pasture farming.
description-flow-regime: NA

name: Monnow at Grosmont
description-summary: Velocity area station with an informal Flat V weir. Natural flow regime.
description-general: Velocity area station with an informal Flat V weir enhancing the natural rock step control 200m d/s. Approx. 30m wide at bankfull.
description-station-hydrometry: Cableway spans 42m. Wide floodplain (>150m) inundated at high flows. Banks reinforced with block stone on both sides. Three peak flow ratings applied across period of record. Out of bank flows not confirmed with check gaugings.
description-flow-record: Flows prior to Apr 1972 derived from 55009 Kentchurch (450m downstream). Missing flows in early 1963 likely to have been amongst the lowest winter flows on record. In August 2012, flows reprocessed from 01/01/1987 reflecting rating changes particularly affecting low flows. Lowest flows on record in 2003 corroborated by gaugings on 26th Aug and 13th Oct. Flows from 25 Mar 2009 from 55047 Grosmont Rhosllwyn, a replacement station 200m d/s of old station. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in April 2017 (WINFAP Files v5) and in August 2026 (WINFAP Files v15).
description-catchment: Impermeable catchment. Five parallel tributaries drain SE down the deeply dissected Old Red Sandstone plateau of the Black Mountains, the northern-most exposing the Old Red Sandstone marls. Moorland headwaters, mixed farming (with extensive arable) in lower reaches to east.
description-flow-regime: Natural to within 10% at Q95.

name: Claerwen at Dol-y-mynach
description-summary: Two sharp edged weirs constructed to monitor runoff from the partially completed Dol-y-Mynach dam. Regarded as natural runoff until the construction of Claerwen reservoir. Station discontinued in 1950.
description-general: Two sharp edged weirs, approx 22m each, constructed to monitor runoff from the partially completed Dol-y-Mynach dam. Total width approx 120m. Construction of the dam was abandoned, but it resulted in a storage of around 0.1 sq km. NRW have no records for this station. No HIF series. Station discontinued in 1950.
description-station-hydrometry: Station may drown, so high flows likely to be suspect (and over-estimated). Peaks exceeding capacity of weir have been truncated by recorder. Levels taken from flood marks and wall of meter chamber. Discharges above the weir capacity derived by straight-line extrapolation; this ignores the increased cross section length above weir flank walls, an additional 73m. Only Barnes formula rating found: Q= 3.324H^1.49 L^1.11 (L+2H)^-0.11.
description-flow-record: NA
description-catchment: Upland catchment on impermeable Lower Silurian slates, grits and conglomerates. Steep terrain with little soil cover and extensive areas of peat bogs.
description-flow-regime: The discharge was regarded as natural runoff until the construction of Claerwen reservoir in 1948.

name: Yazor Brook at Three Elms
description-summary: A Flat V weir, however record is known to be unreliable in parts, and can experience zero flows during summer.
description-general: Flat V weir, theoretically rated, replaced, in 1999, non-standard Flat V Crump (1:5 cross-slopes, 2.5m wide).
description-station-hydrometry: NA
description-flow-record: Flow record unreliable. Gravel accretion causes rating variability, checked by c/m. Floods contained.
description-catchment: Low relief catchment containing urban development of western Hereford. Some light industry but land use is mostly arable agriculture developed on Old Red Sandstone marls; extensively covered with glacial sands and gravel, which maintain baseflow in the Yazor Brk.
description-flow-regime: Zero flows experienced during summer months. Affected by industrial abstractions from groundwater, which can dominate flow pattern at low flows.

name: Elan at Caban Dam
description-summary: Flat V Crump profile weir, 350m d/s of Caban dam. Entirely regulated apart from overspill. Used as a flood warning station.
description-general: Flat V Crump profile weir; 23m wide, 350m d/s of Caban dam. Used as a flood warning station. Caban gauging station is located on the left hand bank of the river Elan with 40m span cableway.
description-station-hydrometry: Several changes in gauging patterns over period of record; therefore one peak flow rating only cannot be applied. Rating D provides best fit post March 2002, Rating A provided the best fit to high flow gaugings pre 2002.
description-flow-record: Flows from 3 Jun 1981 reprocessed in Aug 2012 as a result of rating changes slightly affecting low flows. Monthly naturalised flows available for certain periods from older Caban Coch station (55006). Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2020 (WINFAP Files v9).
description-catchment: Very wet, high elevation catchment draining impermeable geology, predominantly Silurian shales and slates. Upland pasture and moorland, patches of forest.
description-flow-regime: Station located immediately downstream of series of 5 reservoirs used for PWS (~4 cumecs exported to Midlands). Flow regime is entirely regulated apart from releases for compensation. Current compensation release is seasonally variable (0.79 cumecs during summer, 1.1 cumecs during winter) and was historically up to 1.5 cumecs. Releases also made from Caban Coch reservoir to support downstream abstraction during low flow periods. Release regime modified in 2015 to make more frequent regulation releases.

name: Wye at Gwy flume
description-summary: Rectangular, side contracted critical depth flume. Long term IH/UKCEH research catchment. Natural flow regime.
description-general: Rectangular, side contracted critical depth flume designed by Hydraulics Research Ltd, suitable for streams with steep gradients, heavy sediment loads and high flood/drought flow ratios. Catchment nested within Cefn Brwyn (55008). Primary 15 minute dataset available.
description-station-hydrometry: Shoal formation common, requiring prompt removal to avoid drowning. Check gauged by c/m, and volumetrically for lowest flows.
description-flow-record: Daily mean flows replaced from 01/10/1973 to 31/12/2010, and AMAX flows from 01/10/1973 to 01/10/2010 following detailed QC (August 2025, WINFAP Files v14).
description-catchment: Very wet catchment; drains highest area of Plynlimon upland massif. Composed of Ordovician massive grits (unconfined aquifer maintaining baseflow), slates and Silurian mudstones. Heath on peaty plateau; grassland on free draining slopes (supporting sheep grazing) and mires in valley bottoms.
description-flow-regime: Responsive regime. Natural to within 10% at Q95.

name: Cyff at Cyff flume
description-summary: Rectangular, side contracted critical depth flume. Long term IH/UKCEH research catchment. Natural flow regime.
description-general: Rectangular, side contracted critical depth flume designed by Hydraulics Research Ltd, suitable for streams with steep gradients, heavy sediment loads and high flood/drought flow ratios. Catchment nested within Cefn Brwyn (55008). Primary 15 minute dataset available.
description-station-hydrometry: Shoal formation common, requiring prompt removal to avoid drowning. Check gauged by c/m, and volumetrically at lowest flows.
description-flow-record: Daily mean flows replaced from 01/10/1973 to 31/12/2010, and AMAX flows from 01/10/1973 to 01/10/2010 following detailed QC (August 2025, WINFAP Files v14).
description-catchment: Very wet catchment; drains Plynlimon massif. Composed of Ordovician grits, shales and slates and Silurian mudstones, mostly covered by peaty soils. Mainly natural or partly reseeded grassland, supporting sheep grazing.
description-flow-regime: Responsive flow regime. Natural to within 10% at Q95.

name: Iago at Iago flume
description-summary: Rectangular, side contracted critical depth flume in IH/UKCEH research catchment. Natural flow regime. Discontinued in June 1999.
description-general: Rectangular, side contracted critical depth flume designed by Hydraulics Research Ltd, suitable for streams with steep gradients, heavy sediment loads and high flood/drought flow ratios. Catchment nested within Cefn Brwyn (55008). Primary 15 minute dataset available.
description-station-hydrometry: Shoal formation common, requiring prompt removal to avoid drowning. Gauged by c/m, and volumetrically at lowest flows.
description-flow-record: Daily mean flows replaced from 01/10/1973 to 03/02/1999, and AMAXs flow from 01/10/1973 to 03/02/1999 following detailed QC (August 2025, WINFAP Files v14).
description-catchment: Very wet catchment; drains Plynlimon massif. Composed of Ordovician grits, shales and slates and Silurian mudstones. Heath on peaty plateau; grassland on free draining slopes (supporting sheep grazing) and mires in valley bottoms.
description-flow-regime: Responsive flow regime. Natural to within 10% at Q95.

name: Garren at Marstow Mill
description-summary: A Velocity-Area station until 21/12/1997, ultrasonic time of flight (ToF) flow measurement until 14/08/2012 and then Acoustic Doppler flow measurement. New ultrasonic ToF flow meter installed and operational from 12/07/2022 until present. Periods of record replaced with rated flow during times when flow meter is unreliable.
description-general: A Velocity-Area station until 21/12/1997, ultrasonic time of flight (ToF) flow measurement until 14/08/2012 and then Acoustic Doppler flow measurement. New ultrasonic ToF flow meter installed and operational from 12/07/2022 until present. Periods of record replaced with rated flow during times when flow meter is unreliable. Immediately upstream of former mill in concrete-sided mill leat and just downstream of a side weir which operates during high flow conditions. Primarily for low flow measurement.
description-station-hydrometry: Located d/s of side overflow weir which operates during high flow conditions. Approx. 0.7km u/s of confluence with R. Wye.
description-flow-record: US gaugings became unreliable in 2011 and flows calculated from rating.
description-catchment: Geology: Lower ORS overlain with brown earth soils of Erdiston Association. Mixed agriculture.
description-flow-regime: NA

name: Usk at Chainbridge
description-summary: Velocity area station; straight and uniform cross section. Partial impact on flows resulting from three large existing PWS reservoirs in upper catchment.
description-general: Velocity area station; 45m wide, straight and uniform cross section.
description-station-hydrometry: All flows contained by bridge but some overspilling occurs during extreme events d/s on left bank. Permanent cableway. Two peak flow ratings applied across period of record, while daily mean flows based on four ratings. Rating extended to 7.815 m based on hydraulic modelling. No gaugings prior to 1975.
description-flow-record: Influence on flows from three large PWS reservoirs in the upper catchment. Abstraction for Monmouthshire and Brecon Canal at Brecon affects low flows. Large trees became lodged d/s of station in Dec 1979 flood, removed March 1981. Flows reprocessed from 2006 in 2024, resulting in some changes to high flows but minimal change to low flows.
description-catchment: Impermeable catchment, mainly Old Red Sandstone, some Boulder Clay and alluvium in valleys. Principal land use is grassland, hill farming in upper areas, with dairy or livestock farming below; heathland in highest elevations, some forested areas. Peaty soils in uplands, seasonally wet.
description-flow-regime: Influence on flows from three large PWS reservoirs in the upper catchment. Abstraction for Monmouthshire and Brecon Canal at Brecon affects low flows.

name: Ebbw at Rhiwderin
description-summary: Velocity area station, low flow Flat V weir. Flows influenced by PWS and GW abstraction/recharge.
description-general: Originally natural section, low flow Flat V weir installed in 1976, refurbished in 1996. Location may also be referred to as Rhiwderyn.
description-station-hydrometry: Weir width: 14.5m, cross-slope 1:20, 1:2 upstream, 1:5 downstream. Discharges up to MAF level contained. Two peak flow ratings applied across period of record.
description-flow-record: No GDF for 01/06/1975 to 31/01/1977 and 01/03/1977 to 31/10/1977. Weir refurbishment in 1996 did not alter the weir level or geometry, station completely rebuilt so no GDF 19/07/1996 to 05/01/1997. Flows from 1 January 1977 reprocessed due to rating changes (including a new modelled high flow rating) in January 2013, resulting in a significant reduction in the largest peak flows and minor reduction in daily mean and monthly maximum flows, particularly for period 1997-2000.
description-catchment: Moderate permeability, mainly Coal Measures. Mixed land use: mostly grassland, upland heath at highest elevations in north; some forest, mainly in lower valley to south. Significant urban development in valleys.
description-flow-regime: Small water supply reservoirs in uplands; public water supply abstraction. Runoff influenced by groundwater abstraction/recharge in valley. Drainage water from old coalmines can also influence flows.

name: Honddu at The Forge Brecon
description-summary: Three-bay compound crump weir. Station discontinued 1984.
description-general: Three-bay compound crump weir built in 1963 replacing problematic river section that was affected by bed scour and siltation of intake pipe and closed in 1960. Station discontinued 1984.
description-station-hydrometry: Weir centre crest width is 2.438m, flanking crests are 4.877m. Steep high banks on each flank. Good fall in river bed d/s ensures modularity at all stages. Current meter gaugings were taken to confirm theoretical rating.
description-flow-record: Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2020 (WINFAP Files v9).
description-catchment: Upland catchment, predominantly impermeable geology of Old Red Sandstone with an inlier of the Ludlow Series. Mainly rough grassland and moorland.
description-flow-regime: NA

name: Usk at Llandetty
description-summary: Velocity area station, natural river section. Cray and Usk Reservoirs in catchment affect runoff.
description-general: Velocity area station, natural river section. Downgraded to a flood warning level-only station in October 1985. Relocated 50m d/s and upgraded in Oct 1999.
description-station-hydrometry: Natural bankfull stage is 3.7m. There is a raised cableway stanchion on the lb. Banks in the measurement section are reinforced with boulders. Floods are contained (5.49m) and guided by longitudinal spur dyke on left bank and transverse bank on right, where recorder and cable are located. Inlet pipes are prone to blockage. Ratings are likely to under-estimate flow for events that go out of bank. Three peak flow ratings are applied over the period of record.
description-flow-record: NRFA record for original station ends Dec 1981 (now including 1980-81 data added in Aug 2014). The flow record for the reopened station available from Jan 2000. Peak flow data throughout missing period. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in April 2017 (WINFAP Files v5).
description-catchment: Geology predominantly impermeable Old Red Sandstone. Land use is mainly grazing and some forestry.
description-flow-regime: Cray and Usk Reservoirs in catchment affect runoff.

name: Lwyd at Ponthir
description-summary: Compound Crump weir, three crests. Flow affected by reservoirs and GW abstraction. Station closed in 2010.
description-general: Compound Crump weir (three crests, each 6.096m wide). Level-only station since July 1998, closed in 2010. Replaced by Ponthir Star Industrial Estate 200m d/s. Removed from peak flows dataset in September 2019 (WINFAP Files v8).
description-station-hydrometry: Flows <176 cumecs contained. Central crest subject to occasional blockage by debris in high flows, middle walls of structure removed Sept 1994 because of this. Channel enclosed by relatively steep river banks, walls, bridge abutments etc, and overbank flow does not occur till stage of approx 3m. Lb has been raised by flood defence embankment. Progressive drowning from 1.4m. No cableway. Calibration assumes modularity. Shoal development problem at existing site; feasibility study completed for replacement station 300 m d/s. New weir and work on approach channel needed. One peak flow rating applied across period of record. No confidence in rating for high flows as no gaugings above 0.81m and rating is poor fit even at this level. Shoal d/s affects performance of weir. Recommended upper limit 0.5 m.
description-flow-record: Now level only with no flow data processed after 10/07/98.
description-catchment: Predominantly Old Red Sandstone, overlain by Carboniferous Limestone, Millstone Grit and Upper Coal Series. Generally livestock farming with urban development in lower areas. Some Forest. Peaty soils in uplands, seasonally wet.
description-flow-regime: Small reservoirs for industrial and PWS in upper reaches. Some GW abstraction in valley where there is augmentation by drainage water from old mines.

name: Usk at Trallong
description-summary: Velocity area station. Catchment includes the Cray and Usk Reservoirs, used for PWS. De-rated to level only in 1984; now used as a flood warning facility.
description-general: Velocity area station in a straight reach. Situated in a valley with narrow floodplain bounded by moderately sloping hillsides. Gravel bed control associated with a rock exposure. Approx channel width is 31m. The approach is through buttresses of road bridge and an abandoned railway bridge. De-rated to level only in 1984 due to instability at high flows; now used as a flood warning facility.
description-station-hydrometry: All but very exceptional flows contained within banks. On rb water flows into flat fields at approx 3.3m. One peak flow rating applied across period of record. Rating fits gaugings very well. Upper limit set at highest current meter measurement (2.5m).
description-flow-record: Computation of daily flows ceased in 1984. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2020 (WINFAP Files v9).
description-catchment: Impervious catchment - mainly Old Red Sandstone - draining from the Brecon Beacons. Land use is mainly grazing, some forestry.
description-flow-regime: Responsive flow regime. Catchment includes the Cray and Usk Reservoirs, used for PWS. River Usk is regulated and abstraction allowed downstream.

name: Senni at Pont-Hen-Hafod
description-summary: Flat V Crump weir from Dec 1997; previously standard Crump weir. Natural flow regime.
description-general: Flat V Crump weir (width 7.01m) from Dec 1997; previously standard Crump weir. Concrete side walls form a contained approach to the weir, starting from road bridge approx 10 m u/s. Removed from peak flows dataset in September 2019 (WINFAP Files v8).
description-station-hydrometry: Bridge abutments funnel flow to station and prevent bypassing. Flows contained up to wingwalls of about 2.27 m. Beyond end of the walls, approx 10 m d/s, river banks significantly lower allowing flow area to expand rapidly again. Fish baffles on weir face may cause slight backing up at low flows. Crump weir was full range, modular, theoretically calibrated and confirmed by gaugings. Modification to flat V in 1997 necessitated change in peak flow rating. Three peak flow ratings apply over the period of record. Check gaugings confirm rating only to medium flows. Original fish pass removed in 1973.
description-flow-record: Gap in record in 2001 due to Foot and Mouth restrictions.
description-catchment: Natural catchment draining from high rainfall, upland area within Brecon Beacons national park. Impermeable bedrock geology (Old Red Sandstone). Dominant land use is grassland, supporting livestock farming, with mainly peaty soils. Small patches of heathland and forest.
description-flow-regime: Natural to within 10% at Q95.

name: Sirhowy at Wattsville
description-summary: Crump profile Flat V weir. Reservoirs in catchment affect runoff. Station closed in 1983.
description-general: Crump profile Flat V weir. Station closed in 1983.
description-station-hydrometry: Weir crest width approx 12m and cross slope of 1:10. Rb rises steeply up valley side after narrow berms. Severe accretion problems. Rating fits gaugings very well up to highest at 1.2m. Upper limit raised to slightly below wingwall height (2.0m). High confidence in theoretical rating. Reservoirs in catchment affect runoff.
description-flow-record: Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2020 (WINFAP Files v9).
description-catchment: Narrow, linear catchment trending approx N-S. Predominantly upland, mixed geology of moderate permeability - Pennant and Upper Coal series overlying Lower Coal series. Some Boulder Clay and gravels on valley floor. Predominantly grazing, moorland in N, with some urban development in lower valley.
description-flow-regime: NA

name: Grwyne at Millbrook
description-summary: Crump weir of reinforced concrete and local stone with phosphor bronze crest. Reservoirs in catchment affect runoff.
description-general: Crump weir of reinforced concrete and local stone with phosphor bronze crest, 10.67m wide.
description-station-hydrometry: Limited u/s shoaling and weed growth on weir may affect low flows. Fish counter on d/s side of weir not thought to affect performance. Flows contained up to 2.27m. No bypassing on either bank at high flows - channel contained by road wall on lb. Three peak flow ratings applied across period of record. NRW confirm no high flow gaugings; highest gauging at 7.6 cumecs. Reservoirs in catchment affect runoff.
description-flow-record: Gap in data between 1985 and 1988. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2020 (WINFAP Files v9).
description-catchment: Impermeable, predominantly Old Red Sandstone conglomerates, sandstone and marl. Predominantly grassland for livestock farming, significant heathland and some afforestation.
description-flow-regime: NA

name: Yscir at Pont-Ar-Yscir
description-summary: Crump weir with aluminium-bronze crest. Natural flow regime.
description-general: Crump weir with aluminium-bronze crest, width 9m.
description-station-hydrometry: Wingwalls up to 2.45m, then old railway abutments to 3.28m so station not bypassed. Banks either side of old railway crossing approx 2.3m. No cableway. Calibration confirmed by gaugings. Full range, rarely non-modular. Two peak flow ratings applied across period of record.
description-flow-record: Flows since 01/09/1999 reprocessed in 2011 due to new rating, leading to small changes in GDFs and HIFs. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2020 (WINFAP Files v9).
description-catchment: Old Red Sandstone, low permeability. Natural catchment draining from upland areas of Cambrian Hills. Permeable strata in lower catchment, seldom wet. Land use is mainly grassland, mostly hill farming. Upland heath in upper catchment with seasonally wet peaty soils. Isolated patches of forest.
description-flow-regime: Natural to within 10% at the Q95.

name: Usk at Usk Reservoir
description-summary: Outflows from Usk Reservoir. Highly artificial regime, and water balance substantially affected by PWS.
description-general: NA
description-station-hydrometry: NA
description-flow-record: NA
description-catchment: NA
description-flow-regime: NA

name: Olway Brook at Olway Inn
description-summary: Crump weir. Natural flow regime.
description-general: Crump weir, 4.0m wide. Removed from peak flows dataset in September 2019 (WINFAP Files v8).
description-station-hydrometry: Bypassing occurs above 1.8m into surrounding fields. Problems of backing up at high flows. GDFs and HIFs since 1982 reprocessed in 2014 following rating review, with effect of increasing flows >10 cumecs. Two peak flow ratings applied across period of record. Agrees with gaugings up to 1.0m when rating starts to overestimate flows. Rating does not have over bank limb so recommended rating upper limit 1.0m.
description-flow-record: NA
description-catchment: Lower Old Red Sandstone, Boulder Clay cover in NW and alluvium in valley bottom. Mainly grassland, with some arable agriculture and patchy woodland.
description-flow-regime: Natural to within 10% at Q95.

name: Ebbw at Aberbeeg
description-summary: Non-standard weir with notch for fish passage. Open channel immediately upstream of a vertical-drop weir.
description-general: Non-standard weir. Station rebuilt in 2014/15, located closer to bank than previous station. Station removed from peak flows dataset in August 2024 (WINFAP Files v13).
description-station-hydrometry: Channel sides reinforced with concrete in a trapezoidal construction for 30m upstream of weir. Rocky ramp fish passage built during August to October 2012 downstream of weir, plus a 1m wide x 0.3m deep notch cut into the centre of the weir for fish passage. Cableway added in 2015 for high flow gauging.
description-flow-record: NA
description-catchment: Mixed geology of varying permeability, predominantly Pennant and Upper Coal Series overlying Lower Coal Series. Upland catchment with moorland and rough grazing, but with significant urban development in the valley.
description-flow-regime: NA

name: Taf Fechan at Taf Fechan Reservoir
description-summary: Station measuring reservoir outflows. Artificially affected regime, and water balance substantially affected by exports for PWS.
description-general: Station measuring reservoir outflows.
description-station-hydrometry: Post 1979 weir constructed in order to monitor the outflow of Pontsticill Reservoir. It was originally constructed as a 12.5m wide Flat Vee weir, with 1:2 upslope, 1:5 downslope and 1:10 cross slope. In 2015, flood alleviation works reduced right bank by roughly 1m to allow installation of a bypass channel.
description-flow-record: From 2016 onwards, flood alleviation works mean site only measures lowest flows.
description-catchment: NA
description-flow-regime: Prior to 1973, station believed to be record of flows in compensation flume and flood channel. Post 1979, station believed to be record only of flows in compensation flume. Station should be regarded as a low flow station.

name: Taf Fawr at Llwynon Reservoir
description-summary: Reservoir outflows. Artificial regime, and water balance substantially affected by exports for PWS.
description-general: Reservoir outflows.
description-station-hydrometry: NA
description-flow-record: Prior to 1987, station believed to be record of flows in compensation flume (now NRW gauge 57817) and flood channel (now NRW gauge 57816). Post 1987, station believed to be record only of flows in compensation flume, which surcharges when flows exceed about 1m3/s, that is flood channel flow no longer measured. Hence, station should be regarded as a low flow station.
description-catchment: Old Red Sandstone, mainly peaty soils. Predominantly grassland and heath, used for rough grazing.
description-flow-regime: Artificial regime, and water balance substantially affected by exports for PWS.

name: Taff at Tongwynlais
description-summary: Natural river section with bed control. Reservoirs in upper catchment affect runoff. Abstraction and effluent returns in valley. Station used for flood warning.
description-general: Natural river section with bed control. Channel width approx 40m. Station closed 1972. Telemetry installed in 1999 and site opened as a flood warning station. Removed from peak flows dataset in September 2019 (WINFAP Files v8). Main station at 57005 Pontypridd.
description-station-hydrometry: Station located on left bank. Rated by current meter. Well-defined rating to bankfull, estimated thereafter but based on model for Treforest flood protection scheme. Most recent rating is valid from January 1965.
description-flow-record: NRFA hold no flow data past the stations closure in 1972.
description-catchment: Mainly Coal Measures in the south, with Millstone Grit. Carboniferous Limestone and Old Red Sandstone in the north. Some peat on hills, Boulder Clay and Alluvium in valleys. Taff valley, u/s of station, is narrow and steep. Land use is pasture, some forestry and moorland in headwaters, some urban development in lower valley.
description-flow-regime: Direct water supply reservoirs in upper catchment affect runoff. Abstraction and effluent returns in valley for mining, industry and agriculture.

name: Cynon at Abercynon
description-summary: Flat V weir. Station located 900m upstream of confluence with Taff. Flow influenced by reservoirs for PWS and effluent returns from industrial areas in valley.
description-general: Flat V weir from June 1966 - channel control at high flows. Located 900m upstream of confluence with Taff. Station opened Sept 1957 as rated section.
description-station-hydrometry: Weir width: 14.24m; cross-slope 1:20, u/s 1:2, d/s 1:5. Over-topped by extreme floods - e.g 1979; no gaugings above bankfull. One peak flow rating applied across period of record. Provides good fit to available gaugings.
description-flow-record: Data prior to 1962 of poorer quality than those since, although Sept / Oct 1959 minima realistic. Flow minima during period of missing data in 1960 likely to have been 0.30-0.35 cumecs. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in October 2018 (WINFAP Files v7).
description-catchment: Coal Measures with Millstone Grit on northern boundary. Carboniferous Limestone occurs in Penderyn area. Boulder Clay cover and alluvium in valley. Lower part of Cynon Valley is steep sided but in the north it is less steep. Livestock farming and heathland in upland area of peaty soils, seasonally wet. Extensive forest, mainly in S half. Extensive urban and industrial development in valley, which is generally steep-sided. Open cast coal abstraction in upper areas.
description-flow-regime: Small impounding reservoirs for PWS, effluent returns from industrial areas in valley.

name: Taff at Pontypridd
description-summary: Non-standard flat V weir. Flow regime influenced by reservoirs.
description-general: Non-standard flat V weir.
description-station-hydrometry: Weir width: 32m; cross-slope 1:20 upstream and downstream. Top of right bank is playing field, left bank much higher and is former railway bank. Full range and flows contained within the section. High flow gaugings taken using ADVP to around 3m.
description-flow-record: Weir refurbished Sep-Nov 1996, and weir was recapped Sep-Oct 1997; data during both periods have been infilled using data from Fiddler's Elbow (57007) upstream. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in Oct 2018 (WINFAP Files v7).
description-catchment: Coal Measures, some Boulder Clay cover and alluvial deposits in valleys. Mainly upland area with peaty soils on hills, seasonally wet. Catchment is largely grassland with livestock farming on hills, heathland at highest elevations and some forest cover. Extensive urban and industrial development in valleys.
description-flow-regime: Series of six public water supply impounding reservoirs in the upper catchment (Taf Fawr and Taf Fechan) affects runoff. Runoff at low flows influenced by groundwater abstraction/recharge and abstraction for industry/agriculture. The last operational coal mines in this area closed in 1985. Minewater recovery is understood to have occurred by the late 1980s. Mine dewatering increased low flows and mines may have provided some attenuation in flood events.

name: Rhondda at Trehafod
description-summary: Velocity area station. The station is now a concrete trapezoidal channel with armoured concrete side slopes and bed. Flows affected by reservoir and mine water discharge.
description-general: The station was constructed in 1967/68 and is a velocity area station with a bed width of 18m and a bankfull width of approximately 28m.
description-station-hydrometry: The station has no formal control, however the cross section is stable with the exception of some moving bed. In December 1980, the bed of the station was dropped by approximately 1m, the channel was widened, and the bed and banks were armoured with concrete. Recent ratings provide acceptable fit to gaugings. Two peak flow ratings across period of record.
description-flow-record: Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in October 2018 (WINFAP Files v7) and in August 2026 (WINFAP Files v15). 02/11/1980 to 07/10/1981 rejected due to weir construction. Data 2020-2021 has high uncertainty due to well blockage.
description-catchment: Coal Measures with alluvial deposits and Boulder Clay in valleys, peat in upper catchment. Upland area with livestock farming and heathland on hills, around a quarter forest cover (mainly on high ground to NW). Extensive urban and industrial development in valleys.
description-flow-regime: Flows affected by Trehafod Flood Alleviation Scheme after construction completed in 1981 and also small impounding reservoir for public water supply in upper catchment. The last operational coal mines in this area closed in 1985. Minewater recovery is understood to have occurred by the late 1980s. Mine dewatering increased low flows and mines may have provided some attenuation in flood events.

name: Taff at Fiddlers Elbow
description-summary: Flat V weir. Flows affected by impounding reservoirs.
description-general: Flat V weir with concrete side walls.
description-station-hydrometry: Weir width 23m; cross-slope 1:20, 1:5 downstream, 1:2 upstream. Station and cableway were moved during October 1982. Valid date for current rating (28 March 1985) is the date of the first gauging following the move.
description-flow-record: Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in April 2017 (WINFAP Files v5).
description-catchment: Coal Measures with Millstone Grit and Carboniferous Limestone in northern area. Boulder Clay and Alluvial deposits in valleys. Mainly upland area with peaty soils, seasonally wet. Land use is largely grassland, heathland at highest elevations and some forest. Considerable urban development in valley bottom. Half of catchment within Brecon Beacons National Park.
description-flow-regime: Series of six public water supply impounding reservoirs in the upper catchment (Taf Fawr and Taf Fechan), which all pre-date station records, affect runoff. Runoff at low flows influenced by groundwater abstraction/recharge and abstraction for industry/agriculture. Increased by effluent returns. The last operational coal mines in this area closed in 1985. Minewater recovery is understood to have occurred by the late 1980s. Mine dewatering increased low flows and mines may have provided some attenuation in flood events.

name: Rhymney at Llanedeyrn
description-summary: Flat V weir with vertical side walls, velocity area station for high flows. Impounding reservoirs for PWS, groundwater abstraction/recharge and effluent returns all affect flow.
description-general: Flat V weir with vertical side walls, velocity area station for high flows.
description-station-hydrometry: Weir width: 15m, cross-slope 1:20, 1:5 u/s, 1:2 d/s. Full range. Extensive floodplains on both banks. Cardiff Eastern Avenue bypass (200m d/s) keeps flow on floodplain. Station is bypassed at high flows but high flow gaugings are taken from the bridge upstream where flows are contained. Flood rating limbs produced by hydraulic modelling. One peak flow rating across period of record which is a good fit to high flow gaugings.
description-flow-record: Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in October 2018 (WINFAP Files v7). Ratings reviewed in 2025 and reprocessed flow from 1972.
description-catchment: Mainly Coal Measures (moderate permeability). Peaty soils on hills, seasonally wet. Majority grassland with upland heath at highest elevations in N, some forest (in lower valley to S). Livestock farming on uplands; dairy and livestock farming in lower catchment. Significant urban and industrial development in the valleys.
description-flow-regime: Impounding reservoirs for PWS in upper catchment affect flow. Flows also influenced by groundwater abstraction/recharge and effluent returns.

name: Ely at St Fagans
description-summary: Flat V weir, velocity area station for high flows. Flows affected by sewage works discharges and some industrial/agricultural abstractions.
description-general: Flat V weir with concrete side walls, velocity area station for high flows.
description-station-hydrometry: Weir width: 10.6m; cross-slope 1:20, 1:2 u/s, 1:5, d/s. Full range with flow gauged up to 96 cumecs. A proportion of flow (thought to be around 10%) bypasses the gauging station at higher levels, hence, above 55 cumecs, the rating is based on a hydraulic model in addition to gaugings, to account for the bypass flow. Two peak flow ratings applied across period of record.
description-flow-record: Some early (poorer quality) data available (station 57805; 1957-60). Flows from 7/3/2010 to 10/5/2010 suspect due to temporary damming of river at site. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2019 (WINFAP Files v8).
description-catchment: Mainly Coal Measures with some Millstone Grit in northern area; mixture of Trias, Lias, limestone and Old Red Sandstone to the S. Extensive superficial deposits, Boulder Clay in N and sands and gravels in S. Soils have permeable substrate. Mainly pasture, with patches of forest. Dairy farming in lowland area with some built-up areas.
description-flow-regime: Flows affected by sewage works discharges u/s. Some industrial and agricultural abstractions.

name: Ely at Lanelay
description-summary: Velocity area station with standard Flat V weir. Flows affected by effluent returns and industrial/agricultural abstractions.
description-general: Velocity area station with standard Flat V weir.
description-station-hydrometry: Non-standard Flat V weir installed in May 1974 to stabilise bed. New flat V weir installed 1999 resulting in new rating being applied. Fish baffles installed on downstream side of weir in 2000. Multiple peak flow ratings applied across period of record. Most recent rating validated by gaugings up to 1.8m.
description-flow-record: Flows from 16/10/2010 to 3/11/2010 suspect due to blocking of the inlet pipe. Peak flows from 01/10/1973 to 30/09/1999 rejected because of uncertainty in rating curves due to lack of gaugings in the upper limb. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2019 (WINFAP Files v8). Ratings reviewed in 2022 and data reprocessed for full period of record.
description-catchment: Coal Measures. Ely valley generally steep sided. Some forest. Soils have permeable substrate. Lowland catchment. Dairy and livestock farming with urban and industrial development in the valley.
description-flow-regime: Flows affected by effluent returns and industrial/agricultural abstractions.

name: Rhymney at Bargoed
description-summary: Flat V weir constructed 30m u/s of original site. Previously named 'Gilfach Bargoed'. Flood warning station.
description-general: Bargoed gauging station (previously called Gilfach Bargoed) opened in 1967, measuring stage in a natural river section; a weir was constructed in 1975 and a cableway added in 1977. The rating was unstable due to silting and, from 1986, the station operated as a flood warning station only. A new gauging station with a flat V weir was constructed in 2001, 30m u/s of the original site. Still used as flood warning station.
description-station-hydrometry: Bed at gauging site is rocky and underlain by concrete weir approach channel. Fish baffles installed on downstream side of weir in 2001. Two peak flow ratings apply to period of record. Ratings based on gaugings and extended using a modelled rating.
description-flow-record: Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in October 2018 (WINFAP Files v7).
description-catchment: Mainly Coal Measures. Peaty soils on hills with livestock farming and heathland. Significant urban and industrial development, with some forestry in valley bottoms.
description-flow-regime: Small impounding reservoirs for PWS in the upper catchment; some effluent returns.

name: Taff at Merthyr Tydfil
description-summary: Velocity area station for high flows. Site can be affected by upstream activities from DC/WW sites Llwynon and Pontsticill reservoirs.
description-general: Flood warning station for the River Taff. The weir was resurfaced in 2013 and construction work commenced to refurbish station. Building replaced with brick type and sloping roof made up of anti-vandal tiles.
description-station-hydrometry: Contol provided by Flat V weir. During 2013 rebuilding of the weir and station building, an eel pass was installed. High flows during Storm Dennis in 2020 damaged the weir structure, fish baffles and eel tiles. In May 2024 the weir was refurbished. Fish baffles and eel tiles that were damaged during Storm Dennis were also installed in May 2024. Two peak flow ratings across period of record.
description-flow-record: Data missing from Digital Archive from 01/12/79 to 29/02/80 and 01/04/80 to 31/05/80, PoTs and AMAX for these periods are from UKCEH POTs. Flow records from 1978 updated in Aug 2014 due to rating change. Dec 1979 flood (which destroyed the weir) may have been higher but considerable uncertainty surrounds magnitude. WY 1998/1999 AMAX should be treated with caution as extrapolated, may have been overestimated. Flows for the period 03/06/13 to 15/08/13 are backfilled from Troedyrhiw FWS (57032) due to weir refurbishment. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in April 2017 (WINFAP Files v5) and in August 2026 (WINFAP Files v15).
description-catchment: Upland catchment in Brecon Beacons National Park. Millstone Grit and Carboniferous Limestone. Old Red Sandstone in upper areas; some Boulder Clay in valleys. The two tributaries cross a Carboniferous Limestone outcrop. Mainly peaty soils, seasonally wet. Mainly grassland supporting livestock farming, significant upland heath and some forest. Minor urban development just u/s of station.
description-flow-regime: Series of six PWS impounding reservoirs in the upper catchment (Taf Fawr and Taf Fechan) affects runoff.

name: Rhondda Fawr at Tynewydd
description-summary: Flat V weir with fish baffles on d/s slope. Flood warning station. Natural flow regime.
description-general: Flat V weir in good condition with fish baffles on d/s slope. Channel is 7.35m wide. Flood warning station.
description-station-hydrometry: 1.667m high concrete wing walls either side of weir. Full range; no bypassing. Fish baffles installed on downstream side of weir in 2001. Gauging section is concrete channel with good bed stability, though prone to shoaling which has an adverse effect on the modular limit of the weir. The shoaling cannot be moved because there is a main gas line directly underneath and the operations delivery team cannot get into the channel to remove it. Low to medium flows are wade-gauged and high flows are gauged by cableway. Flows for levels above 1.1m are based on a hydraulic model. Peak flow Rating A combines the original rating with the modelled out of bank Hyder rating. Site has been gauged since 2001 but has only recently been rated (2011). Rating A fits the gaugings very well.
description-flow-record: Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in October 2018 (WINFAP Files v7).
description-catchment: Coal Measures with alluvial deposits and Boulder Clay in valleys, peat in upper catchment. Livestock farming and heathland on hills; forest cover on high ground to NW. Extensive urban and industrial development in valleys.
description-flow-regime: Natural flow regime.

name: Ogmore at Bridgend
description-summary: Velocity area station with Flat V weir (installed in July 1975).
description-general: Velocity area station with Flat V weir (installed in July 1975). Channel width: 20m.
description-station-hydrometry: Weir 1:20 cross-slope. Flat V weir installed in August 1975. Wingwalls raised from 1.8m to 3.75m in early/mid 1980s, bankfull prior to mid 1980s was 2.65m. Most events have been in-bank at the station, the exceptions being Dec 1960 (0.37m above bankfull) and Nov 1970 (0.08m above bankfull). Two peak flow ratings across period of record.
description-flow-record: Flows estimated for March-April 1986. Early rating (1960-1975) thought to underestimate flows above 1.8m. Current Rating A currently active over the full stage range, within channel banks, from 01/08/1975 onwards. The current rating is an improvement for flows derived from stages in excess of 1.8m. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in August 2026 (WINFAP Files v15).
description-catchment: Mainly Coal Measures, some Boulder Clay and alluvium in valleys. Peaty soils on hills, seasonally wet. Soils in lowland areas have permeable substrate. Land use is mainly grassland supporting livestock farming in uplands to N, dairy farming in S, with some forest cover throughout. Heavy urban and industrial development in valleys, including significant development just u/s of station.
description-flow-regime: Industrial/agricultural abstractions may reduce flows, but runoff also increased by effluent returns. Bridgend Flood defences built in early 1980s are likely to increase peak flows after that date. The last operational coal mines in this area closed in 1985 and minewater recovery is understood to have occurred by the late 1980s. Mine dewatering increased low flows and may have provided some attenuation in flood events. M4 was built approx 4km upstream of this station in 1980 and may hold back flow in higher events.

name: Neath at Resolven
description-summary: Flat V weir. Flows slightly affected by reservoir in upper catchment, industrial abstractions and effluent returns.
description-general: Flat V weir (installed in 1978); channel width: 28m.
description-station-hydrometry: Flat V Weir 1:20 cross slope, 1:2 downstream, 1:5 upstream, 0.7m V full, installed in July 1978. Some upstream right-bank spillage during floods; water stored on floodplain and does not bypass. Lb steep. At very high floods, e.g. 1979, river breaks out of banks at left hand bend 0.75km upstream onto floodplain. Diversion into a canal upstream but not significant at high flows. Early open channel section very unstable except for period with a blockstone weir (July 1971 to Sept 1977), but peak flow rating suspect above 0.6m throughout period before weir. Temporary site installed during weir refurbishment works in 2017 and 2018.
description-flow-record: Some record available from 1961 to 1978, but channel considered unstable and only low flow gaugings available. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in April 2017 (WINFAP Files v5). Data from temporary site in 2017-18 used to replace main site data during weir refurbishment. Coal mines in the general area until mid 1980s but uncertain if there was any influence on flows in the Neath catchment.
description-catchment: A mainly upland catchment with mixed geology, from S to N: Coal Measures; Millstone Grit; Carboniferous Limestone and Old Red Sandstone. Extensive Boulder Clay cover in mid-catchment. Livestock farming predominates; some areas of upland heath; some forest cover; minor urban development in valley.
description-flow-regime: PWS reservoir in upper catchment. Industrial abstractions and effluent returns.

name: Ewenny at Ewenny Priory
description-summary: Velocity area station. Runoff influenced by mine water returns. Station closed in 1965.
description-general: Velocity area station. Closed in 1965. Superseded in 1971 by Flat V weir d/s at 58009 Keeper's Lodge.
description-station-hydrometry: At high flows water overspills onto Ewenny Moor u/s and returns to river d/s of station. Monthly max rating does not fit all gaugings. Underestimates flow in early period of station.
description-flow-record: Water level records from Jul 1960. Discharge records (Oct 1962-1965) take account of mine water.
description-catchment: Coal Measures in N, mixture of Millstone Grit, Carboniferous Limestone, Trias, Lias and alluvial deposits in S. Soils have permeable substrate. Lowland area with urban/industrial development and dairy/livestock farming.
description-flow-regime: Runoff influenced by mine water returns.

name: Afan at Cwmafan
description-summary: Velocity area station with an informal control (sewage pipe crossing). Runoff influenced by PWS abstraction and minewater discharges.
description-general: Velocity area station with an informal control (sewage pipe crossing). Fully functional station. NRFA station name changed in 2013 from Cwmavon to Cwmafan for consistency with NRW spelling. Station closed in 1970s but reopened in 1989 at the site of the original auxiliary gauge as a level-only station - around 1.5km u/s of the main gauge location at Cwmafan (1961-1977).
description-station-hydrometry: Stilling well at site. Gravel bed is loose and variable, shoaling occurs. Station is d/s of road bridge that concentrates all flows. Rb is steep up to 3m. Floodplain is on lb at 1.7m. More stable station d/s at 58012 Marcroft Weir. Open channel rating. Sewer pipe catches debris, thus affecting the rating. Low flows are beyond rating lower limit. One peak flow rating applied across period of record. No gaugings found, and none available digitally.
description-flow-record: Data from 1989 to 1997 of low quality and not currently held on the NRFA. Flow data available for Jan 1998 onwards. 29 May - 9 June 2020: estimated flows, beyond lower limit of rating. Stage values verified during sites visits. Data from 2023 to 2024 of low quality as it was affected by stilling well blockages and instrumentation changes.
description-catchment: Coal Measures, mainly superficial deposits with peat in uplands and Boulder Clay in valleys. Steep valley sides. Large areas of forest, remainder rough grazing. Some urban development, including just u/s of station. Past mining activity evident.
description-flow-regime: Runoff reduced by PWS abstraction. Minewater discharges in upper catchment affect flows.

name: Ogmore at Brynmenyn
description-summary: Velocity area station on the River Ogmore.
description-general: Velocity area station for high flows. Channel width is 14.3m. Stage recording began at this site in 1970 with gaugings starting around this time, digital data is available since January 1982. 58001 Ogmore at Bridgend station is downstream and 58007 Llynfi at Coytrahen station is adjacent.
description-station-hydrometry: Flat V Weir 1:20 cross slope, 1:2 u/s slope, 1:5 d/s. All flows contained. Multiple peak flow ratings applied across period of record. No known common issues. An eel pass was installed on the left bank wing wall in 2013.
description-flow-record: Weir refurbishment carried out Sep 2012 - Apr 2013, with data recorded at a temporary sensor; downstream 58001 Ogmore at Bridgend used to infill missing data and correct erroneous data. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in April 2017 (WINFAP Files v5). Ratings reviewed in 2022 and data reprocessed for full period of record. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released again in August 2026 (WINFAP Files v15).
description-catchment: Mainly Coal Measures. Predominantly grassland with livestock farming, some heathland in upland area. Forested areas throughout. Peaty soils in upper areas, seasonally wet. Urban development in the valleys.
description-flow-regime: Runoff increased by effluent discharge upstream. Flow reduced by industrial and agricultural abstraction. The last operational coal mines in this area closed in 1985. Minewater recovery is understood to have occurred by the late 1980s. Mine dewatering increased low flows and mines may have provided some attenuation in flood events.

name: Mellte at Pontneddfechan
description-summary: Flat V weir and velocity area station. PWS reservoir in catchment has partial effect on flows.
description-general: Flat V weir and velocity area station; channel width 15m.
description-station-hydrometry: Weir 1:20 cross slope, 1:2 slope u/s, 1:5 slope d/s. Steep section with heavy bed load. Station in steep valley and flows well contained. Flashy river so high flow gaugings are problematic. Two peak flow ratings applied across period of record. Weir refurbishment in May-June 2009 is not believed to have impacted the flood rating. Gauged up to top of wing walls.
description-flow-record: During weir refurbishment over May-July 2009 an upstream sensor used in place of stage measurement instrument within stilling well; data may display minimal amount of variation to period of record data. Data estimated for Nov - Dec 1980, Sept - Oct 1991, and May - July 2005. Level records prior to opening not processed as original crest plates were stolen. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2020 (WINFAP Files v9). Ratings reviewed in 2022 and data reprocessed from 1982.
description-catchment: Rural upland catchment. Geology from S to N - Millstone Grit; Carboniferous Limestone and Old Red Sandstone, with majority Boulder Clay cover in S half of catchment. Predominantly grassland/pasture with significant areas of upland heath and some forestry.
description-flow-regime: PWS reservoir in catchment has partial effect on flows.

name: Llynfi at Coytrahen
description-summary: Velocity area station on the River Llynfi.
description-general: Velocity area station for high flows. Channel width 9.1m.Gaugings began at this site in 1966, digital data available from 1982. 58005 Ogmore at Brynmenyn station is adjacent.
description-station-hydrometry: Flat V Weir 1:20 cross slopes; u/s 1:2; d/s 1:5. Full range. Station in steep valley where flows fairly well contained. Flashy response so obtaining high flow gaugings problematic. Road bridge upstream. Two peak flow ratings applied across period of record. Upper limit at bank full with all flows contained and no major changes in cross section. Eel pass added on 13/08/2012.
description-flow-record: Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in October 2018 (WINFAP Files v7) and in August 2026 (WINFAP Files v15). Ratings reviewed in 2022 and data reprocessed from 1982.
description-catchment: Coal Measures, some Boulder Clay and alluvium in valley. Mainly peaty soils, seasonally wet. Upland area with livestock farming, significant forest cover and urban development in valleys.
description-flow-regime: Flow influenced by industrial/agricultural abstraction, some effluent returns. The last operational coal mines in this area closed in 1985. Minewater recovery is understood to have occurred by the late 1980s. Mine dewatering increased low flows and mines may have provided some attenuation in flood events.

name: Dulais at Cilfrew
description-summary: Compound Crump weir and Flat V weir.
description-general: Compound Crump weir and Flat V weir. Weir like-for-like refurbished in 2017. Sewage discharges and hydro-electric power scheme affect runoff.
description-station-hydrometry: One peak flow rating applied across period of record. Good fit to gauging. River regulated - Llyn Brianne Reservoir in upper catchment. Reservoir is used to augment low flows for public water supply abstractions downstream, also for hydro-electric power generation in winter.
description-flow-record: Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in April 2017 (WINFAP Files v5).
description-catchment: Coal Measures with some Boulder Clay Cover. Mainly peaty soils, seasonally wet. Lower part of catchment joins steep sided Neath Valley. Upland area with livestock farming, some heathland and extensive forest cover. Some urban development in valley, and open cast coal mining.
description-flow-regime: Sewage discharges affect runoff. Hydro-electric power abstraction less than 2 cumecs.

name: Ewenny at Keepers Lodge
description-summary: Flat V weir gauging a mainly lowland catchment.
description-general: Flat V weir. Channel width 12.25m.
description-station-hydrometry: Weir 1:15 cross-slope terminating in a 1:2 sloping revetment. All flows contained. Velocity area calibration for high flows. Station drowning caused by not being able to regularly clear d/s channel since early 1990s. Two peak flow ratings applied across period of record, the most recent is valid from June 1995. Ratings fit respective gaugings well.
description-flow-record: Poorer quality data (1962-1965) available for d/s station 58003 Ewenny Priory. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2019 (WINFAP Files v8).
description-catchment: Coal Measures in N. Mixture of Millstone Grit, Carboniferous Limestone, Triassic and Lias sediments in S. Significant superficial deposits with Boulder Clay and alluvium. Mainly lowland area with dairy and livestock farming, some forest and urban development (including just u/s of station). On-going industrial and residential expansion in the catchment. Ford and Sony factories built in 1980s as well as housing estates.
description-flow-regime: Some groundwater and surface water abstractions within catchment (less than 10% of Q95).

name: Hepste at Esgair Carnau
description-summary: Velocity area station with Flat V weir. Natural flow regime.
description-general: Velocity area station with Flat V weir. Channel width 7m.
description-station-hydrometry: Weir 1:10 cross slope; 1:2 u/s; 1:5 d/s. Modular up to wingwall height, QMED at approx. bankfull, but lack of high flow gaugings. Current rating has an upper limit of 0.451m, and flows above this level are derived by extrapolation and should be treated as uncertain. Low flow data believed to be of very good quality. The NRW ratings fitted gaugings well apart from on limb for non-modular flow (>0.8m). NRFA rating applied with lower limit at 0.8m, to provide rating for non-modular flow. Recommended upper limit at bankfull (1m).
description-flow-record: Record maximum flow in Oct 2000 was extrapolated and may be an overestimate. Data between 9th Jan and 16th May 2012 estimated due to logger problem. Flows from 1 Dec 1993 to 2012 reprocessed in 2012 following rating update, with minimal change to data.
description-catchment: Upland catchment within the Brecon Beacons National Park. Mostly impermeable Old Red Sandstone with carboniferous outcrops at southern limits, some Boulder Clay cover in SW. Peaty soils; seasonally wet. Land use mainly upland pasture.
description-flow-regime: Natural to within 10% at Q95.

name: Thaw at Gigman Bridge
description-summary: Flat V weir and Ultrasonic gauging station. Flows affected by effluent discharges and GW abstractions.
description-general: Originally designed as a temporary station; Flat V Weir structure replaced non-standard bed control weir in April 1999; velocity-area calibration was based on gaugings from bridge u/s.Removed from peak flows dataset in September 2019 (WINFAP Files v8).
description-station-hydrometry: Flat V weir for low and medium flows, US for high flows (>0.72m). Eel pass installed on downstream side of weir left bank in 2013. Out-of-bank flow can occur on rb. Two peak flow ratings applied across period of record. Upper limit at 1m as rating diverges from gaugings above this.
description-flow-record: Flows from April 1999 reprocessed in August 2014 due to rating change, with effect of lowering high flows. Experienced problems with leakage under bed control in early record. Station was taken off-line in September 1998 for complete rebuild with 7-month gap in data. Reason for further 3-month gap in 2004 not known.
description-catchment: Lowland catchment in the Vale of Glamorgan. Mixed geology: Lias; Trias; Carboniferous Limestone and Old Red Sandstone. Significant areas of low permeability substrate. Large Drift cover, mainly glacial sands and gravels. Grass pasture with dairy and livestock farming, some patches of arable and forest; minor urban development.
description-flow-regime: Flows affected by effluent discharges and GW abstractions.

name: Afan at Marcroft Weir
description-summary: Non-standard compound Crump profile weir.
description-general: Non-standard compound Crump profile weir. Channel width: 17.2m.
description-station-hydrometry: No divide walls between centre and side weirs. Stilling pipes not submerged at low flows and shoaling around pipes. High velocities due to steep gradients. One peak flow rating applied across period of record. Provides good fit to available gaugings. Extrapolation of rating is supported by gaugings at Cwmafan Station up to 100 cumecs. Weir remains modular to at least 2.5m (AMAX 1, as of June 2019).
description-flow-record: Weir refurbishment 3 Sep 2012 - 1 Jul 2013, period has been infilled using data from upstream gauging station Cwmafon. Refurbishment expected to have had no significant impact on rating, and gaugings since re-opening have confirmed this. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2020 (WINFAP Files v9).
description-catchment: Coal Measures, mainly superficial deposits with peat in uplands and Boulder Clay in valleys. High proportion of forest, remainder rough grazing. Some urban development, including just u/s of station. Past mining activity evident, restoration schemes employed.
description-flow-regime: The last operational coal mines in this area closed in 1985. Minewater recovery is understood to have occurred by the late 1980s. Mine dewatering increased low flows and mines may have provided some attenuation in flood events.

name: Tawe at Ynystanglws
description-summary: Velocity area station. Industrial and agricultural groundwater abstractions. Some effluent returns.
description-general: Velocity area station.
description-station-hydrometry: Gravel bed provides unstable control. Pressure transducer installed in 2005 with logger attached. Early record has bypassing above 2.75m not accounted for in rating. Several changes to bank levels have been made over the years: embankments and (lower) concrete side weir (right bank) to control flow to flood plain storage was built in 1973; the side weir was raised by ~1m to match embankment height in April 1998. During low flows (level below 0.448m), well intake pipe often out of water due to significant bed erosion. It is unclear when problem started, but results in limited low flow sensitivity; levels adjusted as necessary to be realistic though flow repetitions may occur (e.g. Aug 2006). Since Aug 2010 secondary sensor installed u/s of existing intake pipe to facilitate measurement at low water levels. Multiple peak flow ratings across period of record.
description-flow-record: Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2019 (WINFAP Files v8).
description-catchment: Principally Coal Measures. Mostly mixed permeability, with impermeable strata in headwaters. Some Boulder Clay cover. Mainly upland area with livestock farming. Forest and some Urban and industrial development at lower levels. 1/3 of catchment lies in Brecon Beacons National Park.
description-flow-regime: Limestone outcrop at north of catchment has partial effect on baseflow. A number of artificial influences within the catchment but overall impact on flows is expected to be less than 10% of Q95.

name: Loughor at Tir-y-dail
description-summary: Velocity area station with bed control (crude oblique Crump weir) built over sewer crossing. Flow affected by PWS abstraction and effluent returns.
description-general: Velocity area station with bed control (crude oblique Crump weir) built over sewer crossing.
description-station-hydrometry: Rb overtopped on rare occasions. One peak flow rating applied across period of record. Bankfull is thought to be somewhere between 2.0 and 2.2m. For now the upper limit is 2.2m but this will be revised by site survey.
description-flow-record: Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2020 (WINFAP Files v9). Uncertainty in high flows from 01-Jan-2025 onwards due to large changes at site.
description-catchment: Southern half of catchment is mainly Coal Measures; Millstone Grit, Carboniferous Limestone and Old Red Sandstone in northern half. Extensive Boulder Clay cover at lower elevations. Mainly dairy farming and some patches of forest.
description-flow-regime: PWS abstraction from main spring source. GW and industrial abstractions and effluent returns.

name: Twrch at Gurnos
description-summary: Velocity area station gauging a rural catchment with upland headwaters.
description-general: An open-channel velocity area station opened in 1995, located on the upstream face of the road bridge in Ystalyfera. Station added to peak flows dataset in September 2020 (WINFAP Files v9). Station re-numbered from 60017 to 59003 in February 2023 (WINFAP Files v11.1) to correct the Hydrometric Area, and to 59004 in August 2024 (WINFAP Files v13).
description-station-hydrometry: The site is 60m upstream of the old canal aqueduct and a large weir (~9m drop), which provides the hydraulic control. Flow is contained by the road embankments meaning there is no bypassing/out of bank flow. Low flow rating is calculated from spot gaugings, however the site is not maintained as a low flow station. One peak flow rating across the period of record calculated by hydraulic modelling. Sensitivity analysis shows the modelled rating is generally insensitive to parameter change, suggesting reasonably high confidence in the rating despite the absence of high flow gaugings.
description-flow-record: Scatter in the gauging history means that it is not considered suitable for daily mean flow measurement.
description-catchment: The majority of the catchment is upland/grassland with a large part of the catchment falling within the Brecon Beacons National Park. Lower parts of the catchment are agricultural with some woodlands and commercial forestry.
description-flow-regime: The flow regime is considered natural, with only minor abstractions and discharges in the catchment.

name: Tywi at Ty Castell
description-summary: Velocity area high flow station - Peak flows data only on NRFA.
description-general: Velocity area high flow station - only peak flows data is on NRFA. Low flows measured d/s at 60010 (Capel Dewi). Channel width: 42m. Natural open-channel section within a straight reach of river.
description-station-hydrometry: Levels are monitored using a telemetered in-river PTX. Left bank contains high flows, right bank allows only extreme high flows to spill and bypass station - accounted for in ratings. Ty Castell effective above 50 cumecs. Two peak flow ratings across period of record to account for datum change in summer 1990. Rating review in 2017, corrected data for historic gauge board level slippage and reviewed ratings from 1978, review in 2018 added upper limb for out of bank flow to current rating. Bank full stage is currently 5.3m, 5.76m with earlier datum.
description-flow-record: Only two events (October 1987 and October 2018) were significantly out of bank; the event of December 1979 was only just above bankfull. The historic flood in 1931 was of a similar magnitude to the 1987 event. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in October 2018 (WINFAP Files v7). Current rating was updated following the October 2018 flood with the addition of an upper limb which includes out of bank flow.
description-catchment: Predominantly impermeable, Ordovician and Silurian with Old Red Sandstone on southern boundary. Peaty soils in headwaters, seasonally wet. Lower area soils with permeable substrata, rarely wet. Alluvium in valleys. Catchment is largely grassland with hill farming in upper catchment, some livestock and dairying at lower levels. Some forest cover, significant concentration along NE margin.
description-flow-regime: Llyn Brianne reservoir (catchment area approx 88km) in headwaters regulates flow down to major DCWW PWS abstraction d/s of station. It is also used for some winter Hydropower. The reservoir began to fill in March 1972 and it was full by December 1972.

name: Cothi at Felin Mynachdy
description-summary: Velocity area station; straight reach and natural rock control. Natural flow regime.
description-general: Velocity area station. Straight reach and natural rock control. Channel width: 20m.
description-station-hydrometry: Stable section. All but very extreme flows contained. Single peak flow rating applied over period of record.
description-flow-record: PoR max was on Oct 1987; bypassing occurred on right back so recorded flow is likely to be underestimation. Flows from 1 Jun 2007 to 31 Dec 2012 reprocessed in 2014 due to rating change, increasing GDFs below approx 5 cumecs. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in October 2018 (WINFAP Files v7).
description-catchment: Impermeable strata, mainly Silurian with Ordovician along SE boundary. Mostly grassland; upland pastures. Livestock and dairy farming below. Significant forest cover.
description-flow-regime: Natural to within 10% at Q95.

name: Taf at Clog-y-Fran
description-summary: Velocity area station. Natural flow regime. Station used for flood forecasting and drought trigger.
description-general: Velocity area station. Channel width: 13.9m. Site used for flood forecasting and drought trigger.
description-station-hydrometry: Left bank steep with berm for recorder - recent signs of erosion. Right flood bank at approx 3.2 - 3.4m; considerable overspill during flood events. Channel prone to build-up of silt. Gauged from bridge u/s which can also become constriction at high flows. Flood rating change in early 1990s; exact date of change is estimated. Rating fits gaugings reasonably and allowance is made for bypass flow. Remedial works to stabilise the riverbank downstream of the gauging station and the bank to the rear of the gauging station began in July 2022 and finished September 2022. During this time a temporary site, was positioned in the river channel using a stilling pipe approx. 30m upstream of the station.
description-flow-record: Flow record from 60002 Cothi at Felin Mynachdy used to infill various short periods of missing data (principally in 1986, but also 1991, 2001, 2004). Flows from 01/01/2010 reprocessed in 2013 due to new rating, with main effect of lowering low flow GDFs, and from 01/0/1982 in 2025. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2020 (WINFAP Files v9).
description-catchment: Mainly impermeable strata, Ordovician with some narrow bands of igneous rock, Old Red Sandstone in S. Alluvium in valleys. Soils have permeable substrate. Largely grassland, mainly dairy farming. Very small patches of arable and woodland.
description-flow-regime: Natural to within 10% at Q95.

name: Dewi Fawr at Glasfryn Ford
description-summary: Velocity area station, constructed in opening of railway embankments where railway bridge crosses river. Ford 10m d/s. Runoff affected by effluent returns.
