description-flow-record: 1990s flows under review. Some monthly naturalised flows available (1970-74).
description-catchment: A very wet (mean rainfall may be underestimated), steep-sided, mountainous catchment developed on ancient metamorphic formations - some overlying superficial deposits. Mainly moorland with significant commercial forestry. Loch Eck dominates catchment. No significant catchment changes known.
description-flow-regime: The catchment contains Loch Eck, a major PWS reservoir.

name: Carradale at Dippen
description-summary: A velocity-area station on the Carradale Water draining into Kilbrannan Sound.
description-general: Velocity area station with natural control.
description-station-hydrometry: Natural control. Rating in use from Oct 1995 - 01/12/2007 was based on ultrasonic time-of-flight high flow gaugings between 1996-2003. Recalibration in 2009 (due to drift in low flows) suggested rating shift around 2000; new rating was thus created and has been applied from December 2007. Data from 2000-2007 are therefore based on older rating despite possible shift. Both ratings are suspect at high flows (probable underestimation) but the reason is unknown; more gaugings are required.
description-flow-record: NA
description-catchment: Low-lying catchment predominantly forested (~70%) with impermeable bedrock.
description-flow-regime: Responsive catchment.

name: Linne nam Beathach at Victoria Bridge
description-summary: A velocity-area station in a very wet, rural, upland catchment draining into Loch Tulla.
description-general: Velocity area with a spillway crested weir. Initially installed as part of hydro-electric power programme.
description-station-hydrometry: Calibration good at low flows.
description-flow-record: NA
description-catchment: Very wet, rural, upland catchment draining to Loch Tulla. Dalradian metamorphics with igneous extrusions; over half overlain by Boulder Clay. Moderate forest cover. A couple of small lochs in the catchment.
description-flow-regime: No artificial influences on the flow regime.

name: Orchy at Glen Orchy
description-summary: A velocity-area station upstream of the confluence with the River Lochy, initially installed as part of a hydro-electric power programme.
description-general: Velocity area station with low flow control (broad-crested weir). Initially installed as part of hydro-electric power programme.
description-station-hydrometry: All but very high flows contained. Calibration does not extend to highest flows - may result in overestimation of runoff.
description-flow-record: NA
description-catchment: Very wet, upland, steep, and rural catchment with some forest. Predominantly metamorphic rocks with local occurrences of Dalradian L'st; over 60% overlain by Boulder Clay.
description-flow-regime: Very responsive natural flow regime.

name: Strae at Glen Strae
description-summary: Compound broad crested spillway weir, initially installed as part of Loch Awe hydro-electric power programme.
description-general: Compound broad crested spillway weir, about 8m wide. Initially installed as part of Loch Awe hydro-electric power programme. Removed from peak flows dataset in September 2019 (WINFAP Files v8).
description-station-hydrometry: To date all flows contained. Rocks which stand above bed level immediately downstream of the weir are likely to result in rapid drowning of the weir in floods. Low flow ratings derived using meter gaugings up to 0.7m (about 0.2 QMED). High flow rating unconfirmed. Medium to high flow rating taken from theoretical rating inherited from hydro-electric power (which was the first edition rating for the site).
description-flow-record: The nominal 'normal maximum' flood is 144.7cumecs.
description-catchment: A very wet, mountainous, often snowy in winter, linear catchment draining to Loch Awe. Bedrock geology: predominantly Dalradian metamorphics with local occurrences of Dalradian L'st. Almost half the catchment overlain by Boulder Clay. Landuse predominantly rough grazing; some woodland cover. No significant catchment changes known.
description-flow-regime: Flashy response. No significant artificial effects on the flow regime during the early record. Generally natural regime. Possibly some water abstraction.

name: Lochy at Inverlochy
description-summary: A velocity-area station upstream of the confluence with the River Orchy, initially installed as part of a hydro-electric power programme.
description-general: Velocity area station with low flow control (broad-crested weir). Initially installed as part of hydro-electric power programme.
description-station-hydrometry: Rocky bed makes gauging difficult, particularly at low flows, reducing rating confidence.
description-flow-record: NA
description-catchment: Linear catchment draining westward from Lochan na Bi. Predominantly Dalradian metamorphics with local outcrops of Middle ORS. Upland rural catchment with forested slopes.
description-flow-regime: NA

name: Avich at Barnaline Lodge
description-summary: A station downstream of Loch Avich and upstream of Loch Awe, initially installed as part of a hydro-electric power programme.
description-general: Compound weir: broad crest low flow notch set in level rounded crest weir with wing walls. Initially installed as part of hydro-electric power programme.
description-station-hydrometry: Relatively few gaugings have been taken and all at low flows, down to c.0.3 cumecs. Only a single rating has ever been used and generally low flows fit the rating well; accuracy lost progressively with floods above main crest.
description-flow-record: NA
description-catchment: Predominantly Dalradian metamorphics with intrusive and extrusive igneous outcrops. Forested catchment (>50%) draining into Loch Awe. Catchment dominated by presence of Loch Avich approx. 2km u/s.
description-flow-regime: NA

name: Abhainn a' Bhealaich at Braevallich
description-summary: A station in a steep catchment draining into Loch Awe.
description-general: Compound weir. All but highest flows contained. Initially installed as part of hydro-electric power programme. Hydro-electric power station installed November 2005 with turbine flow bypassing the station.
description-station-hydrometry: Low flows measured over a broad crest notch; high flows over a long rounded crest with decreasing accuracy. No gaugings have been taken above 2 cumecs and high flows should be therefore treated with a degree of caution.
description-flow-record: Apr-Sept 1991 flows and runoff are anomalously high and should be treated with caution. The bypassed flow is accounted for in the flow record except for Aug 2007 - Mar 2009, where offtake data unavailable.
description-catchment: Predominantly Dalradian metamorphics with igneous intrusions; approx. 40% overlain by Boulder Clay. A steep catchment draining into Loch Awe. One of the most afforested UK catchments (>60%).
description-flow-regime: No other artificial effects on flow regime.

name: Eas Daimh at Eas Daimh
description-summary: A station with a small upland catchment.
description-general: Crump weir (originally installed for research purposes, now operated by SEPA).
description-station-hydrometry: Good low flow calibration. Access problems create difficulties in establishing medium and high flow rating; accuracy at high flows considered poor.
description-flow-record: Missing data 25/08/14 - 08/20/2014 due to weir construction work.
description-catchment: A wet, mountainous, catchment developed largely on Dalradian metamorphics (mainly schists, some slate and phyllite). Peat in upland areas. Small upland catchment, partially forested.
description-flow-regime: A very responsive, natural regime - no abstractions or loch storage (but snow pack storage can be considerable).

name: Eas a' Ghaill at Succoth
description-summary: A station with a crump weir in a narrow ravine.
description-general: Crump weir (installed for research project, now operated by SEPA) in a narrow ravine, all flows contained.
description-station-hydrometry: Calibration good at low flows but poor at high.
description-flow-record: NA
description-catchment: A wet, mountainous catchment developed on metamorphic formations - mainly Dalradian schists with some phyllite and slate. Peat in upland areas. Small, partially forested upland catchment.
description-flow-regime: Very responsive, natural regime - no abstractions or storage (excepting seasonal snow cover).

name: Nevis at Claggan
description-summary: Velocity area station draining the southern slopes of Ben Nevis.
description-general: Velocity area station; about 20m wide river section with boulder control.
description-station-hydrometry: All flows contained. Difficulty in gauging low flows results in a scattered low flow rating. Ratings derived from current meter gaugings up to 118 cumecs (about 0.95 QMED), simple extrapolation beyond.
description-flow-record: Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in October 2018 (WINFAP Files v7).
description-catchment: Wet, steep-sided, high altitude catchment draining southern slopes of Ben Nevis. No storage. Largely impermeable bedrock with approx. 1/3 overlain by superficial deposits. Predominantly Moinian metamorphic with limestone and granitic intrusions. Prolonged winter snow cover. Moorland, rough pasture, and some forestry. No significant catchment changes known.
description-flow-regime: Very responsive regime. Flows are largely natural although runoff from 6.7 sq.km of the headwaters diverted to Loch Trieg for hydro-electric power and further downstream around 5% of Q95 is abstracted for public water supply.

name: Lochy at Camisky
description-summary: Velocity area station gauging a rural catchment with a complex regime.
description-general: Velocity area station 60m wide.
description-station-hydrometry: Fully contained river section with stable gravel bed calibrated to 644 cumecs. Gauged to 105% above QMED.
description-flow-record: Staff gauge observations from Feb 1977 to Jul 1979.
description-catchment: Catchment is mainly rough grazing and moorland with some afforestation. Predominantly impermeable bedrock with approx. half overlain by superficial deposits. Significant snow cover during winter.
description-flow-regime: Abstractions for power generation and flows in Caledonian Canal regularly bypass station. Complex catchment with three large reservoirs controlled for power generation and transfers from the R. Nevis, Mashie and Spey increasing the natural catchment by 17%.

name: Allt Leachdach at Intake
description-summary: Compound weir measuring flows draining the north-eastern slopes of the Ben Nevis massif.
description-general: Compound sharp edge weir with a flat 'V' set in a sharp edge rectangular notch (6.7m long).
description-station-hydrometry: No drowning due to the steep gradient d/s, but at low flows the nappe in the V-notch is not aerated. The stilling pool is unlikely to be entirely effective at high flows. Freezing occurs in winter. Theoretical rating.
description-flow-record: NA
description-catchment: Mountainous catchment, often snowy in winter. The catchment lies on the north flank of the eastward extension of the Ben Nevis massif. Land cover is rough grazing, pasture and bare rock. No significant catchment changes known.
description-flow-regime: Natural regime.

name: Shiel at Shielfoot
description-summary: Velocity area station gauging a wet mountainous catchment. Natural flow regime. Downgraded to level only end of 2021.
description-general: Velocity area station d/s of Loch Sheil.
description-station-hydrometry: Cableway present. Gravel bed but relatively stable rating and sensibly a full range station.
description-flow-record: Low flow periods during July/Aug 2011 thought to be a true representation of discharge at the time and due to the installation of coffer dam at u/s outlet of Loch Shiel during bridge works.
description-catchment: Wet, mountainous catchment with grassland and some afforestation in the glens. Impermeable bedrock with some superficial deposits.
description-flow-regime: Natural flow regime.

name: Allt Coire nan Con at Polloch
description-summary: Station operated from 30/12/1969. Daily flows held from 1986, peak flows from water year 2001.
description-general: Pillar Box hut with stilling well. New station with cableway installed 2018/2019, first cableway gauging recorded September 2019. Station added to peak flows dataset in October 2018 (WINFAP Files v7).
description-station-hydrometry: The station has a pillar box hut with a stilling well and a natural channel control. Added to the Peak Flows dataset in October 2018 (WINFAP Files v7) with QMED indicative suitability status. This was updated to Pooling suitability in 2024 following a flood measurement in 2023. One peak flow rating across period of record.
description-flow-record: The wading limit for gauging is around 0.6m and high flow gaugings have been carried out using ADCP instruments upstream of the station. A cableway has been available since 2019. One peak flow rating is applied through the period of record. A stationary upward looking acoustic instrument was installed for a period in 2023 and this measured a large flood on 21/08/23. This measurement validated the flood rating and improved the confidence in the estimation of higher flood events. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in August 2024 (WINFAP Files v13).
description-catchment: NA
description-flow-regime: NA

name: Strontian at Ariundle
description-summary: Compound crump weir gauging a small flashy catchment.
description-general: Compound crump weir with fish pass. Station added to peak flows dataset in August 2026 (WINFAP Files v15).
description-station-hydrometry: The station between 2000 and 2006 consisted of an open natural channel with a simple gauge post and pressure probe. The construction of a Scottish Water crump weir resulted in a gap in the record until the works were completed in 2008. The current SEPA station records stage over the weir, which has facilitated improved flow calibration and station performance from 2008. The weir structure incorporates an abstraction offtake behind the right wingwall. The channel profile opens out above 2.2m with a steep natural bank above the left wingwall and a concrete stepped profile beyond the right wingwall that includes the raised foundation for the gauging station hut. There is good confidence in the flow calibration up to the top of the vertical concrete wingwalls at 2.2m above gauge zero, informed by gaugings up to 2.190m (measured flow of 29.9 cumecs). Flow estimation above the wingwalls (2.2m) is based on simple extrapolation of the in-channel calibration resulting in the underestimation of higher flood events, albeit less than 10% from the true value.
description-flow-record: NA
description-catchment: Small catchment, natural to gauging station. Some forestry, rough grazing, moorland and peat bog.
description-flow-regime: Flashy catchment with no storage.

name: Aline at Craigendarroch
description-summary: Velocity area station gauging a natural mountainous catchment.
description-general: 15m open channel section with gravel control.
description-station-hydrometry: No cableway. Gauged to around QMED; high flow gauging carried out by ADCP boat. Good confidence in high flows.
description-flow-record: NA
description-catchment: A natural mountainous catchment with few small lochs. Mainly pasture, rough grazing, moorland and peat bog with some forestry.
description-flow-regime: NA

name: Carron at New Kelso
description-summary: Velocity area station, 70% of catchment drains through Lochs Dughaill and Scaven.
description-general: Velocity area station, 40m wide with floodbank on right bank.
description-station-hydrometry: The unstable gravel control requires regular calibration in the low flow range. The channel became very unstable around early 2002 and subsequent years of channel scour reduced the gravel control, resulting in levels falling below gauge zero. This issue was corrected with a new ramp, installed on 20/04/2011 and with an associated drop in datum of minus 0.84m, applied back to 01/01/2010 in the stage record. Nearly all flows are contained except for the most extreme events where some bypassing may occur over the left bank in the 30m wide floodplain. Flow calibration is based on gaugings up to around 150 cumecs where after there is a declining confidence in the simple extrapolation of the rating. The flood calibration pre 2010 is under review and Peak Flow data before this date is excluded until the review is complete. Two peak flow ratings across period of record.
description-flow-record: The flood calibration pre 2010 is under review and Peak Flow data before this date are excluded until the review is complete. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in August 2026 (WINFAP Files v15).
description-catchment: Mountainous headwaters, often snowy in winter. Impermeable bedrock catchment with little superficial deposits. Typical mix of rough grazing and moorland; some forestry and lochs. Increased forestry over last 15 years.
description-flow-regime: Flows are 100% natural. 70% of catchment drains through Lochs Dughaill and Sgamhain with little additional surface storage. One of the wetter Highland catchments currently gauged.

name: Ling at Killilan
description-summary: Velocity area station gauging a natural mountainous catchment.
description-general: Open channel section with gravel control; 30m wide section.
description-station-hydrometry: Pressure transmitter initially until the full site was built in 2006. No cableway. Control is subject to change during major flooding events. Gauged to below QMED.
description-flow-record: Very high coastal tides evident on stage trace when river is low. Stage edited to remove tidal spikes.
description-catchment: A natural mountainous catchment with little storage. Mainly rough grazing, peat bog and moorland with some forestry.
description-flow-regime: Hydropower schemes on River Attadale divert water out of the catchment.

name: Ewe at Poolewe
description-summary: Velocity area station in north west Scotland. Flow regime dominated by Loch Maree.
description-general: Velocity area station, 50m wide.
description-station-hydrometry: Stable (rock armoured) control which has been modified infrequently resulting in re-calibration of low flows. Right bank has been modified by fisheries proprietors (about 3 times) without affecting the control. To date all flows contained. Rating from current meter gaugings, simple extrapolation beyond. Peak flow rating revised in 2016, with one rating applied across period of record.
description-flow-record: Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in April 2017 (WINFAP Files v5). Chart data between 1972 & 1982 was digitised in 2016.
description-catchment: Mountainous headwaters, often snowy in winter. Very wet, mountainous catchment developed largely on ancient metamorphic formations (Lewisian Gneiss and Torridonian Sandstone). About a third overlain by superficial deposit. Typical Highland land use with rough pasture and moorland and some tree cover. No significant catchment changes known.
description-flow-regime: Slow responding. In excess of 95% of the catchment drains through Loch Maree (surface area 30 sq km) which dominates the flow regime. Low to medium flows from 3% of the upper catchment diverted to Conon hydro scheme.

name: Kerry at Faich Bhiorach
description-summary: Velocity area station gauging a Highland catchment. Regime influenced by power station and impoundment dam. Station downgraded to level only and closed on the NRFA in Sept 2021.
description-general: Open channel section around 15m wide with gravel control.
description-station-hydrometry: No cableway. Gauged to below QMED.
description-flow-record: NA
description-catchment: Highland, mountainous catchment. Moorland, bog and rough grazing. Significant storage in upper catchment at Loch na h-Oidhche.
description-flow-regime: River heavily modified due to power station and impoundment dam. Agreement for compensation flows to protect freshwater biota - flow regime never extremely low or extremely high. Small Hydro scheme about 2.5km upstream at Loch Bad an Sgalaig.

name: Inver at Little Assynt
description-summary: Velocity area station. Low flow regime can be affected by Loch Assynt gate operation.
description-general: Velocity area station, about 30m wide.
description-station-hydrometry: Completely contained river section with adequately gauged stable calibration in excess of MAF. Rock control. To date all flows contained. Rating derived from current meter gaugings, simple extrapolation beyond. Peak flow rating was revised in 2003 and a new single rating for peak flows only was judged to be suitable for the whole period of record. Rating reviewed in 2016.
description-flow-record: Very low flows in May/June 1998 and April 2002 due to gate operations at Loch Assynt. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in April 2017 (WINFAP Files v5).
description-catchment: Mountainous headwaters, often snowy in winter. Predominantly Lewisian gneiss with Lewisian basic rock intrusions; some superficial deposits. Catchment is rough grazing and moorland with many lochans, of which Loch Assynt dominates (surface area 7.9 sq km). No significant catchment changes known.
description-flow-regime: Flow regime completely natural except for occasional operation of gates for fisheries purposes which mainly influence low flows. The gates are immediately u/s at outlet to Loch Assynt (surface area: 7.9 sq.km) and can result in very low flows.

name: Broom at Inverbroom
description-summary: Velocity area station gauging a typical upland Scottish catchment. Diversions of water in the upper catchment. Station downgraded to level only and closed on the NRFA from Sept 2021.
description-general: 25m wide river section on gentle bend d/s of bridge.
description-station-hydrometry: Floodbank on lb protects a wide cultivated floodplain; heavy tree cover on steep rb. Unstable gravel/cobble control, significant low flow gaugings scatter. Slightly skew velocity in high flows. Adequately calibrated to bankfull (150 cumecs).
description-flow-record: NA
description-catchment: Catchment typically Scottish upland except for a very narrow cultivated band on the lower valley floor. Impermeable bedrock with >60% overlain by superficial deposits.
description-flow-regime: 20% of natural catchment diverted (except overflows) via Loch Droma to Conon hydro-electric power scheme. 25% of upper catchment drains through Loch a' Bhraoin.

name: Langwell at Langwell Lodge
description-summary: Velocity area station gauging a natural mountainous catchment. Station downgraded to level only and closed on the NRFA from Sept 2021.
description-general: Open channel section 12m wide with gravel control. Hydro-electric power scheme installed in upper catchment during 2016 and began operation in Jan 2017.
description-station-hydrometry: Cableway present. Left bank is artificial flood bank.
description-flow-record: NA
description-catchment: A natural mountainous catchment with small loch in upper catchment. Mainly rough grazing, peat bog and moorland with some forestry.
description-flow-regime: HEP Scheme began operation in January 2017 - flows are not natural, particularly at low flows.

name: Abhainn a'Chnocain at Elphin
description-summary: Velocity area station gauging a natural catchment with some small lochs.
description-general: The station was built in 2008 to improve the network coverage of catchment typologies. The catchment type was identified as being poorly represented and is a relatively small catchment with a natural flow regime. Station added to peak flows dataset in October 2018 (WINFAP Files v7).
description-station-hydrometry: The station is built in a straight reach that runs through flat peat bog after descending from the steeper uplands. The flows are nearly all contained. There is a modern concrete lined road bridge 60m downstream that acts as the control and although higher events will be out of bank at the station, all flows pass though the downstream bridge section. A constant flood segment is applied to all ratings though the period of record. Low end rating shifts are caused by episodes of deposition and erosion of bed material in the reach of the bridge control. No cableway. Gauged to 1.060m with a measured flow of 7.508 cumecs. This is now supplemented by continuous velocity measurement which captured the event in December 2023 of 1.566m, providing calibration up to 14m3/s.
description-flow-record: Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in August 2024 (WINFAP Files v13) and in August 2025 (WINFAP Files v14).
description-catchment: Natural catchment with small lochs. Mountainous with rough grazing, moorland and peat bog. Partly limestone geology.
description-flow-regime: Natural flow regime.

name: Laxford at Laxford Bridge
description-summary: Velocity area station gauging a natural mountainous catchment with significant Loch storage.
description-general: Open channel section around 20m wide with rock control.
description-station-hydrometry: No cableway. Gauged to below QMED. More gaugings are needed to have confidence in high flows.
description-flow-record: Occasional very low flows e.g. Feb 2021, occur as a result of a ice.
description-catchment: A natural mountainous catchment with significant storage in Loch More and Loch Stack. Mainly rough grazing, peat bog and moorland with some forestry.
description-flow-regime: NA

name: Rhidorroch at Rhidorroch
description-summary: Velocity area station gauging a natural mountainous catchment with some small lochs.
description-general: Open channel section 15m wide located in a narrow rock gorge.
description-station-hydrometry: No cableway. Gauged to wading limit with plans to extend using ADCP boat.
description-flow-record: Missing data periods (2011, 2015) due to data logger issues.
description-catchment: A natural mountainous catchment with few small lochs. Mainly pasture, rough grazing, moorland and peat bog with some forestry.
description-flow-regime: NA

name: Halladale at Halladale
description-summary: Velocity area station in upland catchment. Predominantly natural flows.
description-general: Velocity area station, about 20m wide.
description-station-hydrometry: Natural control. Adequately gauged to bankfull. Two peak flow ratings both derived from current meter gaugings up to 62 cumecs (about 0.6QMED), simple extrapolation beyond. Peak flow rating was revised in 2003.
description-flow-record: NA
description-catchment: Upland catchment. Predominantly Torridonian sandstone with intrusions of metamorphic gneiss. Largely overlain by superficial deposits. Largely moorland with a peat based cover. Extensive afforestation from late 1970s. A few small lochs within the headwaters.
description-flow-regime: Flows predominantly natural apart from during very dry periods (e.g. Jun 2010) when there may be minor influence from augmentation (for fishery purposes) using sluices on a few small lochs.

name: Naver at Apigill
description-summary: Velocity area station; approximately half of the catchment drains through Loch Naver.
description-general: Velocity area station; 40m wide river section with narrow 6m floodplain on rb but otherwise completely contained.
description-station-hydrometry: Gravel control - regular need to reassess low flow rating. To date all flows contained. One peak flow rating across period of record based on gaugings with simple extrapolation beyond.
description-flow-record: Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2019 (WINFAP Files v8).
description-catchment: Mountainous headwaters, often snowy in winter. Impermeable bedrock with a large proportion overlain by superficial deposits. Predominantly Torridonian sandstone with granitic intrusions. Typical Highland mix of rough grazing and moorland; some forestry. No significant catchment changes known.
description-flow-regime: Flows 98% natural with small interbasin transfer to the Shin hydro-electric scheme. Half of the catchment drains through Loch Naver. Several small high level lochs within catchment in addition to the total surface area of Lochs Coire, Meadie and Naver of 13 sq.km.

name: Strathy at Strathy Bridge
description-summary: Velocity area station in north west Scotland.
description-general: Velocity area station, about 15m wide.
description-station-hydrometry: Stable pitched river bed control with gabion mattress constriction to increase sensitivity (installed on old bridge invert upstream of new road bridge). Bypassing on the right bank during extreme flood events above 1.65m. Adequately gauged to bankfull. Ratings derived from current meter gaugings up to 40 cumecs (about 0.5QMED), simple extrapolation beyond.
description-flow-record: Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2023 (WINFAP Files v12).
description-catchment: Upland headwaters. Predominantly Moinian metamorphic with small areas of sandstone and granite. Largely overlain by superficial deposits. Gently sloping peat-covered catchment with moorland and rough pasture. Extensively afforested from the late 1970s.
description-flow-regime: Natural regime. No significant surface storage but several small hill lochs on a low altitude.

name: Strathmore at Allnabad
description-summary: Velocity area station in natural and very responsive catchment. Some headwater storage.
description-general: Velocity area station, about 30m wide. Station removed from peak flows dataset in August 2025 (WINFAP Files v14).
description-station-hydrometry: Boulder and gravel control, can be subject to change in big events. Gauged down to 0.15 cumecs. Extreme low flows measured 2 km d/s at a more suitable site for wading (catchment area increase: 7 sq.km). All flows contained to date. Scatter in gaugings through the flow range due to the instability of the control and the turbulence in the gauging pool at medium to high flows. Two peak flow ratings, both derived from current meter gaugings. Maximum gauging for pre-Oct 1994 rating of about 0.7 QMED; for post-Oct 1994 about 0.8QMED; simple extrapolation beyond. Peak flow rating was revised in 2003.
description-flow-record: NA
description-catchment: Very wet, rugged, upland catchment with mountainous headwaters, often snowy in winter. Predominantly Moinian metamorphic with schist intrusions. Less than half overlain by superficial deposits. Moorland and rough grazing dominate land use. No significant catchment changes known.
description-flow-regime: Natural and very responsive flow regime; moderate storage in headwater lochans.

name: Dionard at Dionard
description-summary: Velocity area station gauging a natural mountainous catchment.
description-general: Open channel section 20m wide with gravel control.
description-station-hydrometry: No cableway. Rating extended using ADCP boat but not high enough to allow accurate extrapolations of high flows.
description-flow-record: April 2010 - April 2011 data is suspect due to instrument fault.
description-catchment: A natural mountainous catchment with little storage. Mainly rough grazing, peat bog and moorland with some forestry.
description-flow-regime: NA

name: Borgie at Borgie Bridge
description-summary: Velocity area station gauging a natural mountainous catchment with significant Loch storage.
description-general: Open channel section with croy control, 14m wide.
description-station-hydrometry: No cableway. Gauged to around QMED.
description-flow-record: NA
description-catchment: A natural mountainous catchment with significant storage in Loch Loyal. Mainly rough grazing, peat bog and moorland with some forestry.
description-flow-regime: NA

name: Thurso at Halkirk
description-summary: Velocity area station; 50% of the catchment drains through Loch More.
description-general: Velocity area station, about 30m wide.
description-station-hydrometry: Stable rock bar control. To date all flows contained. Two peak flow ratings across period of record derived from gaugings with extrapolation beyond.
description-flow-record: Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2019 (WINFAP Files v8).
description-catchment: Upland headwaters. Mixed bedrock permeability with about 1/3 impermeable, largely overlain by superficial deposits. Blanket peat cover. Land use is moorland and rough pasture with some tree cover. Extensive afforestation of upper catchment from late 1970s. Catchment characterised by small lochs.
description-flow-regime: 50% of catchment drains through Loch More which is used for river regulation (mainly freshets for fishing). Public water supply is taken from Loch Calder - this loch would naturally drain into both the Thurso and Forss catchments, but the outlet to Forss to the North is blocked by a barrage. Average net abstraction from Loch Calder 5% of long-term average runoff.

name: Eastern Yar at Alverstone Mill
description-summary: Station closed in 1997.
description-general: Compound thin-plate weir. The archived 'gauged' flows incorporate an adjustment to allow for an upstream public water supply abstraction - the record is thus partially naturalised.
description-station-hydrometry: NA
description-flow-record: NA
description-catchment: A largely permeable catchment - the Eastern Yar rises as springs on the Chalk of St. Catherine's Down but Lower Greensand dominates the lower catchment. Very rural.
description-flow-regime: NA

name: Medina at Shide
description-summary: Ultrasonic station (at road bridge) installed in 1996.
description-general: Ultrasonic station, superseded trapezoidal critical depth flume, width 2.4m (with broad-crested c/m rated overflow weir for stages > 0.6m). Upper Shide site closed since 2005, replaced by station 300m downstream at Shide; data from either side of transition considered homogeneous.
description-station-hydrometry: Springline accretion between the two sites may impact on the homogeneity of the overall flow record. Nov 2000 peak under review. Flow reduced in 1985 by groundwater pumping tests. From 1989, low flows augmented by Isle of Wight Conjunctive Use Scheme; also transfers to the Eastern Yar.
description-flow-record: No data Sep-Dec 1996.
description-catchment: Entirely rural, arable catchment. Fairly steep slopes in southern headwaters. Predominantly permeable: Chalk and Lower Greensand with some Gault Clay.
description-flow-regime: Small abstractions for irrigation.

name: Lukely Brook at Carisbrooke Mill
description-summary: Compound Crump weir. Site formerly known on National River Flow Archive as Newport.
description-general: Compound Crump weir. Total crest width 3.2m (upper crest: 2.4m wide; lower crest: 0.8m wide). Data quality improved since installation of fish pass. Site formerly known on National River Flow Archive as Newport.
description-station-hydrometry: Minimum in 1986; 1999 minimum under review.
description-flow-record: NA
description-catchment: The Lukely Brook drains the Bowcombe Valley - mostly Chalk with some impervious Tertiary formations near to the catchment outfall. Rural land use, but increasing urban development around Newport.
description-flow-regime: Groundwater abstractions upstream affect flow regime, water mill immediately downstream.

name: Eastern Yar at Burnt House
description-summary: Flat V weir, a rural, largely permeable catchment.
description-general: Flat V weir, 1:10 cross slope. Limited head for long periods. Peak flows truncated at around 7.9 cumecs.
description-station-hydrometry: NA
description-flow-record: NA
description-catchment: A largely permeable catchment - the Eastern Yar rises as springs on the Chalk of St. Catherine's Down but Lower Greensand dominates the lower catchment. Very rural.
description-flow-regime: Runoff reduced by surface and groundwater abstractions. From 1989, low flows augmented as part of the Isle of Wight Conjunctive Use Scheme, but also regular abstraction upstream.

name: Eastern Yar at Budbridge
description-summary: Flat V weir, runoff reduced by surface and groundwater abstractions.
description-general: Flat V weir, cross-slope 1:10, 2.98m wide. Limited head for extended periods. From 1988, low flows augmented as part of the Isle of Wight Conjunctive Use Scheme.
description-station-hydrometry: Regularly subject to weed growth.
description-flow-record: NA
description-catchment: The Eastern Yar rises on the Chalk of St. Catherine's Down, below the permeable headwaters Upper Greensand and Gault Clay dominate. Very rural, Godshill is the main settlement.
description-flow-regime: Runoff reduced by surface and groundwater abstractions.

name: Wroxall Stream at Waightshale
description-summary: Station level-only since 1994, runoff reduced by groundwater abstractions.
description-general: Station level-only since 1994. Flat V weir (2.90m wide, cross-slope 1:10). Limited head for extended periods.
description-station-hydrometry: NA
description-flow-record: Extensive periods of missing flows between July 1992 and December 1995.
description-catchment: A rural catchment trending N-S from the Chalk of St. Boniface Down. Some Upper Greensand and Gault Clay below the headwaters.
description-flow-regime: Runoff reduced by groundwater abstractions especially after the commissioning of the Isle of Wight Conjunctive Use Scheme (in 1989). Very artificial low flow pattern.

name: Scotchells Brook at Burnt House
description-summary: Station decommissioned, long periods with negligible head.
description-general: Station decommissioned. Flat V weir, 1:10 cross slope. Peak flows truncated at just below six cumecs. Long periods with negligible head.
description-station-hydrometry: NA
description-flow-record: NA
description-catchment: Chalk headwaters thence Greensand and Gault formations (largely impermeable). Land use: agricultural in upper reaches, more varied below (some runoff from Shanklin/Sandown).
description-flow-regime: Runoff reduced by groundwater abstractions.

name: Cefni at Bodffordd
description-summary: Weir structure. Domestic property discharges may impact low flows.
description-general: Rectangular thin-plate weir.
description-station-hydrometry: Weir rated at medium to high flows by current meter. Full range station. Weir susceptible to blockage and accumulation of debris which may affect the intake, particularly in the summer/autumn. Some gravel accumulation and clearance. Domestic property discharges maximum of 1.2 cumecs per day upstream of station; may impact low flows.
description-flow-record: Missing data 12-23/09/2009 due to repair work on weir; in-channel work minimal but downstream banks reinforced. Theoretical rating curve applied subsequently.
description-catchment: Typical low-lying Angelsey catchment of impermeable rocks overlain by thick Boulder Clay. Mostly grassland, minor patches of forest and arable.
description-flow-regime: NA

name: Snizort at Skeabost
description-summary: Velocity area station, the only one on the Isle of Skye.
description-general: Velocity-area station opened in 2001 as the first representative gauging station on Skye. Station added to peak flows dataset in September 2020 (WINFAP Files v9).
description-station-hydrometry: Deep rocky channel with semi-artificial rock control in channel roughly 25m wide. No cableway at site for high flows, gaugings are carried out ~600m upstream. Gauged to around QMED. Multiple peak flow ratings across the period of record.
description-flow-record: Dec 2009-Jan 2010 and Dec 2010 flows considered suspect due to extended period of freezing in the stilling well. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2022 (WINFAP Files v11).
description-catchment: 80.6 km2 High moor land to 400m, rough pasture and some forestry. Small loch in headwaters 0.5 sq.km. Tertiary geology, mainly ovaline-basalt and dolerite.
description-flow-regime: Moderately flashy. Small fish farm abstraction, with discharge immediately d/s.

name: Creed at Creed Bridge
description-summary: Compound crump weir gauging a mainly natural catchment near Stornoway.
description-general: Asymmetrical compound Crump weir - 8.6m main crest with 0.6m low flow crest on left hand side - immediately d/s of sharp right hand bend.
description-station-hydrometry: Theoretical rating. Structure capacity: approx. 15 cumecs, overtopped by flood peaks. Levels monitored by pressure transducer - monthly offsets applied, based on dip-flash readings.
description-flow-record: NA
description-catchment: Gently-sloping peat-covered (>75%) catchment near Stornoway. Heather moorland developed on ancient metamorphics, mostly Lewisian gneiss. Many lochans in South of the catchment. Some afforestation; current land-use mostly sheep-grazing.
description-flow-regime: Small fish-hatchery abstraction immediately u/s - can influence low flows (amounts unknown), causing both prolonged periods and single days of low flow - otherwise an entirely natural regime.

name: Laxdale at Laxdale
description-summary: Velocity area station gauging a natural mountainous catchment on the Isle of Harris.
description-general: Open channel section 5m wide with gravel control. Station added to peak flows dataset in September 2020 (WINFAP Files v9).
description-station-hydrometry: Flood gauging is challenging at the site due to its remoteness and there being no permanent cableway. However, a flood gauging has was obtained on 17/09/18 using a ADCP boat and temporary cableway set up. The gauged stage was 1.786m and the measured flow was 23.5 cumecs. Although the river was out of bank on the right during this gauging, there is confidence that the measured flow was close to the actual flow. One peak flow rating across the period of record.
description-flow-record: Low flows in June 2012 verified by gaugings during the event, therefore thought to be reliable.
description-catchment: A natural mountainous catchment on South Harris with little storage. Mainly rough grazing, peat bog and moorland with some forestry.
description-flow-regime: NA

name: Abhainn Roag at Mill Croft
description-summary: Velocity area station gauging a natural mountainous catchment on South Uist (Outer Hebrides).
description-general: Open channel section 7m wide with gravel control. Station added to peak flows dataset in October 2018 (WINFAP Files v7).
description-station-hydrometry: No cableway. Gauged to around QMED. One peak flow rating across period of record.
description-flow-record: NA
description-catchment: A natural mountainous catchment on North Uist with little storage. Mainly rough grazing, peat bog and moorland with some forestry.
description-flow-regime: NA

name: Durkadale at Durkadale
description-summary: Velocity area station, the first opened on Orkney.
description-general: Velocity area station installed on Orkney mainland. Record from August 1999. Regarded as a secondary site by SEPA (but first station on Orkney).
description-station-hydrometry: NA
description-flow-record: NA
description-catchment: NA
description-flow-regime: NA

name: Weisdale Burn at Weisdale Mill
description-summary: Velocity area station opened in 2002 to record data for Shetland.
description-general: Velocity area station, opened in 2002 to obtain continuous flow data for Shetland. Station added to peak flows dataset in August 2026 (WINFAP Files v15).
description-station-hydrometry: The control is a natural riverbed consisting of gravel and small boulders. Weed growth in summer can be a challenge for accurate low flow calibration. Flood flows are largely contained within steep banks up to 1.25m where after there is a gradual slope up to the grass field on the right bank. The highest conventional gauging is at 0.763m, with a measured flow of 2.096 cumecs. High flow calibration has been extended up to 1.6m (10.37 cumecs) using an IQ+ fixed acoustic velocity meter and from LSPIV processing of video surface velocity data acquired from the downstream footbridge.
description-flow-record: Issue with the level recorder caused gaps in the stage record between 07/08/2010 to 08/09/2010 and between 15/11/2010 to 06/10/2011. These gaps coincide with the largest rainfall event in the respective water years and so the AMAX events are missing for WY2009 and WY2010. There was no significant rainfall in the 6 missing days at the start of WY2011 and so there is confidence that the published AMAX event for WY2011 is correct.
description-catchment: Quartzite and Pelites with some metamorphosed limestone and dolomite. Overlain with peat and till. Mainly moorland and rough pasture.
description-flow-regime: Fish hatchery nearby abstracts and discharges - amounts unknown.

name: Fairywater at Dudgeon Bridge
description-summary: Velocity area station opened in November 1971.
description-general: One of the earliest stations in the Northern Ireland hydrometric network. A velocity area station comprising a wooden hut housing a stilling well. Main and backup instruments both present using shaft encoders with float and weight. Channel width approximately 15m at station.
description-station-hydrometry: Channel too deep to wade gauge at station, but during low flows in-channel gauging is undertaken at road bridge downstream. The last gauging over 10 cumecs was on 07/08/86, the highest gauging flow recorded since this date was on 18/04/96 when the flow was 8.3 cumecs. Rating derived from current meter gaugings. One peak flow rating across period of record.
description-flow-record: AMAX1 in November 2015 exceeded the previous long-standing highest flow on record from October 1987. Daily flows from 1977 onwards reprocessed in 2002. POT threshold revised in 2017 using entire period of record data up to 2015 water year. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2023 (WINFAP Files v12) and in August 2025 (WINFAP Files v14).
description-catchment: Solid geology - Dalradian schistose sandstone and shale form generally impermeable basement in the south. Much of the area is underlain by Carboniferous, generally indurated conglomerate, Claragh sandstone, mudstone and limestone. Prominent Palaeogene dolerite dykes cross the area. Drift geology - river alluvium overlies glacial sand and gravel deposited on drumlinised glacial till. Rock near surface and post-glacial peat extensive on high ground. Restricted development of river alluvium in valleys. Predominantly grassland with some shrub heath, bog and coniferous woodland. No significant urban development.
description-flow-regime: Natural regime - no water abstractions or significant returns.

name: Camowen at Camowen Terrace
description-summary: Velocity-area station with cableway opened in April 1972 as part of the original core network in Northern Ireland. Flow regime impacted since 2011 by hydro-electric power downstream.
description-general: Velocity-area station with cableway. Masonry hut housing stilling well and cableway winch situated on top of floodbank on left bank. Camowen River is one of two major watercourses flowing through Omagh that join to form the Strule River. Station located 750m upstream of confluence with Drumragh River. Main and backup instruments present, both using shaft encoders with float and weight. Channel width 22m at station. Channel too deep to wade gauge in all but the very lowest of conditions. Access steps into channel installed and vertical Post Gauge upgraded to more accessible and secure 30 degree pitch on new steps in 2024.
description-station-hydrometry: Informal broad-crested weir c.240m downstream originally constructed for mill use acts as control. Full range of flows contained within channel. Ratings derived from current meter gaugings and there are a good number of both low and high flow gaugings providing a good rating fit. Simple extrapolation used beyond the maximum gauged flow at 2.16m. Hydro-electric scheme opened in 2011 which is affecting (particularly low) flows. Two peak flow ratings across period of record.
description-flow-record: AMAX1 2011 event extent captured by aerial photography area to left of gauging station shows an area of inundation rather than bypass flow. Daily flows from 1975 onwards reprocessed in 2002. POT threshold revised in 2017 using entire period of record data up to 2015 water year. POT threshold subsequently reviewed in 2025 to include data up until 2023 water year and POT threshold remained unchanged as average was still exactly 5 events per water year. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in October 2018 (WINFAP Files v7), September 2023 (WINFAP Files v12) and August 2026 (WINFAP Files v15).
description-catchment: Largely upland given over mainly to grassland or heath. Solid geology - Dalradian schistose sandstone and shale form generally impermeable basement north of the Omagh Thrust. Moinian and Ordovician igneous complexes from generally impermeable basement south of the Omagh Thrust. The rest of the area is underlain by Devonian and Carboniferous conglomerate, sandstone and mudstone that are generally indurated. Drift geology - Extensive drumlinised glacial till with sand and gravel in valleys. Extensive rock near surface and post-glacial peat cover on high ground with restricted development of river alluvium in valleys. No significant urban development.
description-flow-regime: Records indicate a sensibly natural regime since the station opened in 1972 until hydro-electric power scheme downstream started up in 2011. This has had a noticeable impact on summer low flows in 2013 and 2014 when levels dropped to new minima below the bottom end of current rating equation. Given operational constraints of hydro-electric power in high flows, peak flow data remain unaffected.

name: Drumragh at Campsie Bridge
description-summary: Velocity-area station with cableway opened in July 1972 as part of the original core network in Northern Ireland.
description-general: Velocity-area station with cableway. Masonry hut housing stilling well and cableway winch situated on right bank. Drumragh River one of two major watercourses flowing through Omagh that join to form the Strule River. Station affected by backing up with confluence with Camowen downstream. Removed from peak flows dataset in September 2019 (WINFAP Files v8).
description-station-hydrometry: Main and backup instruments present both using shaft encoders with float & weight. Channel width c.16 metres at station. Top of the berm is 6.08m. Flow is out of bank above 100m3/s however the station is not bypassed. Well rated at low and high flows. Single peak flow rating across the period of record derived from current meter gaugings. Simple extrapolation used beyond maximum gauged level of 3.82m. Daily flows in late December 2010 considered suspect due to likely freezing in stilling well but this is very much an exception rather than the norm for winter conditions.
description-flow-record: Highest station flows both recorded in the month of October in 1987 & 2011. Latter event extent captured by aerial photography. Daily flows from 1975 onwards reprocessed in 2002. POT threshold revised in 2017 using the entire period of record data up to 2015 water year.
description-catchment: Approximately agricultural grassland and upland heath. Solid geology - Dalradian schistose sandstone and shale form generally impermeable basement north of the Omagh Thrust. Much of south is composed of Devonian and Carboniferous conglomerate, sandstone, mudstone and limestone that are generally indurated. Prominent Palaeogene dolerite dykes cross the area. Drift geology - Extensive drumlinised glacial till with some sand and gravel in valleys. Extensive rock near surface and post-glacial peat cover on high ground with restricted development of river alluvium in valleys. No significant urban development.
description-flow-regime: No water abstractions or significant returns.

name: Burn Dennet at Burndennet
description-summary: Velocity area station with cableway and natural control opened in May 1975.
description-general: Velocity-area station with cableway. Masonry hut housing cableway winch situated on top of floodbank on right bank. Main and backup instruments present both using pressure probes. Channel width c.11m at station. Instruments re-sited directly in channel in December 2017 as inlet pipe to stilling well is now sitting up out of the water in low flows as channel bed has lowered in recent years.
description-station-hydrometry: Natural in-channel control. Major bed shift in recent years has rendered lower end of rating equation as inadequate and in need of review. Bed also prone to movement at high flows prohibiting accurate ADCP gauging at the station. Ratings derived from traditional current meter gaugings with recent check gaugings using in-channel electromagnetic current meter. Highest gauging to date (45 m3/s) in 2009 was c.1 m below top of floodbank. Simple extrapolation used beyond 65m3/s. Two peak flow ratings across period of record.
description-flow-record: Daily flows from October 2013 are not available as a result of a shifting bed effecting gauging at low flows. Peak flows unaffected. Water year 1974/1975 rejected because AMAX from partial water year at start of station record. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in August 2021 (WINFAP Files v10) and in August 2024 (WINFAP Files v13).
description-catchment: Predominantly improved grassland, some bog and heath rising to above 500 mAOD. Solid geology - Dalradian rock types form a generally impermeable basement composed of metamorphosed, schistose sandstone, shale, limestone and basic igneous intrusive and extrusive lithologies. Drift geology - upstream, glacial till is overlain by significant sand and gravel and more restricted river alluvium. Downstream, sand and gravel may be absent or hidden by laterally more extensive river alluvium. Rock near surface and post-glacial peat cover extensive on high ground with restricted development of river alluvium in valleys.
description-flow-regime: No water abstractions or significant returns. Discharge through the underlying gravels may be significant.

name: Derg at Castlederg
description-summary: Velocity-area station with cableway opened in October 1975.
description-general: Velocity-area station with cableway. Masonry hut housing stilling well and cableway winch situated on top of floodbank on right bank. Main and backup instruments present, both using shaft encoders with float and weight. Channel width c.32m at station. New access steps into channel installed and vertical Post Gauge upgraded to more accessible and secure 30 degree pitch on new steps in 2024.
description-station-hydrometry: Natural bed control downstream of station. One peak flow rating across period of record derived from current meter gaugings. Low flow gauging conducted from upstream road bridge as bed is too rocky to safely wade gauge despite shallow depths at station. High flows gaugings conducted using cableway. Top of flood bank 3.72m. Simple extrapolation used beyond maximum gauged level at 3.04m. Daily flows in late December 2010 considered suspect due to likely freezing in stilling well but this is very much an exception rather than the norm for winter conditions.
description-flow-record: The two highest flows on record took place within 3 weeks of each other in November/December 2015 both surpassing the previous long-held Peak Flow record from 1985. Daily flows from 1975 onwards reprocessed in 2002. POT threshold revised in 2017 using entire period of record data up to 2015 water year. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in October 2018 (WINFAP Files v7), September 2023 (WINFAP Files v12) and August 2026 (WINFAP Files v15).
description-catchment: Solid geology - Dalradian rock types form a generally impermeable basement composed of metamorphosed, schistose sandstone, shale, limestone and basic igneous intrusive and extrusive lithologies. Moinian and Ordovician igneous complexes form generally impermeable basement south of the Omagh Thrust. Carboniferous conglomerate, sandstone and mudstone are generally indurated. Drift geology - Extensive glacial till with sand and gravel and lake alluvium in valleys. Extensive rock near surface and post-glacial peat cover on high ground with restricted development of river alluvium in valleys. Predominantly upland heath, agricultural grassland, coniferous forest. Castlederg is the main settlement.
description-flow-regime: There is a large water abstraction plant downstream. Loughs Derg and Mourne are in the headwaters; Lough Mourne is used for water supply in Co. Donegal. Aside from this, there are no significant water abstractions or effluent returns upstream of the station.

name: Owenkillew at Crosh
description-summary: Velocity area station opened in 1980. Steel cabinet kiosk installed in February 2018 to replace original wooden hut and cableway destroyed in August 2017 flood.
description-general: Velocity-area station comprised of steel cabinet kiosk on right bank housing main and backup instruments both using pressure probes. Station replaced that at Killymore in 1980, because of mobile bed problems. Killymore, about a mile upstream, was part of the original core network from the early 1970's. Wooden hut housing stilling well and cableway winch at Crosh destroyed during 23 August 2017 flood. New station sited c.60 m downstream of original station on higher ground although pressure probes are located in same position in river channel inlet pipe to stilling well used in previous station location.
description-station-hydrometry: River gets out-of-bank at high flows. The rating is derived from current meter gaugings. Simple extrapolation is used beyond 3.458m (maximum gauged level). Gauging and rating is good but some gaugings at higher flows would be useful. One peak flow rating across period of record.
description-flow-record: Highest flow recorded in August 2017 eclipsed previous, long-held peak flow recorded in October 1987. Flows for full period of record reprocessed in 2002. Data in late 2010 suspect likely due to frozen stilling well. POT threshold revised in 2017 using entire period of record data up to 2015 water year. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2023 (WINFAP Files v12) and in August 2025 (WINFAP Files v14).
description-catchment: Catchment of grassland, heath and forest with substantial agriculture. Solid geology -Moinian and Dalradian rock types form a generally impermeable basement composed of metamorphosed, schistose sandstone, shale, limestone and basic igneous intrusive and extrusive lithologies. Drift geology - glacial till extensive and overlain with sand, gravel and river alluvium. Rock near surface and post-glacial peat cover extensive on high ground with restricted development of river alluvium in valleys.
description-flow-regime: No water abstractions or significant returns.

name: Mourne at Drumnabuoy House
description-summary: Velocity-area station with cableway opened in June 1982 on Mourne River which holds record for highest flow recorded in Northern Ireland.
description-general: Velocity area station with cableway. Masonry hut housing stilling well and cableway winch situated on top of floodbank on right bank. Main and backup instruments present, both using shaft encoders with float and weight. Floor of station raised up following major inundation during 1987 flood event. Channel width c.47m at station. New access steps into channel installed and vertical Post Gauge upgraded to more accessible and secure 30 degree pitch on new steps in 2024.
description-station-hydrometry: Station location selected to be outside tidal influence of Foyle and influence of Finn River which joins Mourne c.3km downstream to form River Foyle. Natural bed control. Low flow gauging conducted by wade gauging. Electric cableway historically used for high flow gauging however this was destroyed during high flows in winter 2015. Last high flow gauging undertaken in 2002. Rating derived from current meter gaugings. Simple extrapolation used beyond maximum gauged level of 4.27m. One peak flow rating across period of record.
description-flow-record: AMAX1 in August 2017 exceeded the previous long-standing highest flow on record from October 1987. Defences constructed post-1987, when Strabane was flooded, protected the town in 2017. No gaps in record. Daily flows for full period of record reprocessed in 2002. POT threshold revised in 2017 using entire period of record data up to 2015 water year. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in October 2018 (WINFAP Files v7), September 2023 (WINFAP Files v12) and August 2026 (WINFAP Files v15).
description-catchment: A mainly rural catchment (grassland and heath with limited afforestation), with urban development at Omagh and Castlederg. Solid geology - Moinian and Dalradian rock types form a generally impermeable basement composed of metamorphosed, schistose sandstone, shale, limestone and basic igneous intrusive and extrusive lithologies. Moinian and Ordovician igneous complexes form generally impermeable basement south of the Omagh Thrust. Ordovician and Silurian greywacke sandstones and shales form some of the ground and are generally indurated. Much of south is composed of Devonian and Carboniferous conglomerate, sandstone, mudstone and limestone that are generally indurated. Drift geology - Extensive glacial till with sand and gravel and lake alluvium in valleys. Extensive rock near surface and post-glacial peat cover on high ground with restricted development of river alluvium in valleys.
description-flow-regime: There is a slight effect of water abstractions. The station has the largest catchment of any in Northern Ireland that has a natural flow regime, and has a relatively small urban percentage.

name: Roe at Ardnargle
description-summary: Velocity-area station with cableway opened in January 1975. Very flashy flow regime in spite of large catchment and reservoir in headlands.
description-general: Velocity-area station with cableway. Masonry hut housing cableway winch situated on top of floodbank on left bank. Main and backup instruments present both using pressure probes. Channel width c.17m at station. Channel stabilisation work completed in October 2010 saw bank protection and concrete bed installed and control established.
description-station-hydrometry: Control comprised of tiered rock olives established in October 2010 as part of bed stabilisation work. Multiple ratings apply to period of record with differences at low flows due to bed movements. High spring tides intrude up to the station. Very large range in water level (6m) although fully contained at high flows by extensive floodbanks.
description-flow-record: Daily flows not archived on the NRFA since October 2010 - pending rating review to account for bed stabilisation works. Highest flow recorded on 16th August 2008 when 3 inches of rain fell in 12 hours on already saturated ground during what the Met Office termed "Awful August". Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2019 (WINFAP Files v8) and in August 2024 (WINFAP Files v13).
description-catchment: Predominantly grassland headwaters with some shrub heath, bog and coniferous woodland. Intensively cultivated alluvial plain. High upland headwater area sloping fairly steeply onto an intensively cultivated alluvial plain. Contains towns of Limavady and Dungiven. Solid geology - bedrock is very varied with metamorphic, sedimentary and contemporaneous igneous rocks. Dalradian rock types form a generally impermeable basement composed of metamorphosed, schistose sandstone, shale, limestone and basic igneous intrusive and extrusive lithologyies. Carboniferous conglomerates, sandstones and mudstone are generally indurated. Permeable Triassic sandstone (Sherwood) overlain by impermeable Triassic mudstone. Thin Cretaceous chalk is indurated and overlain by Palaeogene basalt lava flows. Drift geology - glacial till covers much of the area with extensive sand and gravel at the northern end of the catchment. Post-glacial peat cover extensive with restricted development of river alluvium.
description-flow-regime: Flow regime characterised as flashy despite relatively large catchment area. Headwaters contain Altnaheglish reservoir yielding 32Ml/d.

name: Faughan at Drumahoe
description-summary: Velocity-area station opened in August 1976. Steel cabinet kiosk installed in December 2017 to replace original masonry hut and cableway destroyed in August 2017 flood.
description-general: Velocity-area station comprised of steel cabinet kiosk on right bank housing main and backup instruments both using pressure probes. Original masonry hut housing stilling well and cableway winch destroyed on 23 August 2017 when floodwaters eroded right bank and undercut station hut which fell into the Faughan. New station sited c.20 m upstream of original station. Channel width c.22m at station.
description-station-hydrometry: Natural control c.50m downstream of station altered in 1985. Floodwall constructed on left bank in 1995. Ratings derived from current meter gaugings. All low and high flow gaugings prior to August 2017 were conducted using cableway as channel is too deep to wade gauge even during low flows. Simple extrapolation used beyond maximum gauged flow at 2.998m. Multiple peak flow ratings across period of record.
description-flow-record: Highest flow recorded in August 2017 eclipsed previous, long-held peak flow recorded in October 1987. Daily flows not shown after this event as channel changes necessitates rating revision. Peak flows not affected. Flows for full period of record reprocessed in 2002. POT threshold revised in 2017 using entire period of record data up to 2015 water year. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in October 2018 (WINFAP Files v7), September 2023 (WINFAP Files v12) and August 2026 (WINFAP Files v15).
description-catchment: Drumahoe is a suburban development near the coast - some light industry; otherwise agricultural, upland basin. Solid geology - Dalradian rock types form a generally impermeable basement composed of metamorphosed, schistose sandstone, shale, limestone and basic igneous intrusive and extrusive lithologies. Drift geology - Extensive glacial till with sand and gravel and lake alluvium in valleys. Post-glacial peat cover extensive with restricted development of river alluvium.
description-flow-regime: No significant abstractions or returns.

name: Blackwater at Maydown Bridge
description-summary: Velocity-area station with cableway opened in June 1970. Flows influenced by major arterial drainage scheme between 1983-1995.
description-general: Velocity-area station with cableway. Masonry hut housing stilling well and cableway winch situated in steeply-sloping field on left bank, just downstream of a twin-arched bridge. Main and backup instruments present both using shaft encoders with float and weight. Channel width c.27m at station. Flood bank built on right bank in 1990 constraining all but the most extreme flows - aerial photograph from AMAX2 event in November 2009 (187m3/s, 4.051m) shows overtopping of floodbank directly opposite station.
description-station-hydrometry: Natural in-channel control. Historical flows between 1983-1995 impacted by major arterial drainage scheme. Approximately 50% of catchment is in Republic of Ireland where some groundwater may be abstracted but its hydrological significance is not considered to be significant. One peak flow rating across period of record based on gaugings. Gauging close to 2009 AMAX2 event lends credence to rating equation.
description-flow-record: Peak flow data are only presented from 1990 onward since the construction of flood bank constrained the majority of high flow events. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2019 (WINFAP Files v8) and in August 2024 (WINFAP Files v13).
description-catchment: Solid geology - indurated Carboniferous limestone, sandstone and mudstone are exposed upstream while permeable Sherwood Sandstone Group occurs downstream. Drift geology -downstream, drumlinised glacial till is overlain by river alluvium. Extensive rock near surface and post-glacial peat cover on high ground with restricted development of river alluvium in valleys. A predominantly rural catchment - largely improved grassland with limited afforestation. Monaghan Town - in the Irish Republic - is the only significant urban centre.
description-flow-regime: Second largest catchment size (behind 201010 Drumnabuoy House) of NI stations in Peak Flows dataset at 970km2 with a correspondingly high average T-rise of 29 hours - nearly twice the average for NI stations. There is evidence of abstraction activity in the instantaneous data however the scale of the impact is not considered to be significant.

name: Main at Dromona
description-summary: Velocity area without cableway, controlled by a weir of capped sheet piles.
description-general: Velocity area station comprised of standpipe with metal box atop. Station upgraded in May 2023 to include telemetry, solar panel and backup instrument. Main and backup instruments both use pressure probes. Channel width c.13m at station.
description-station-hydrometry: Major arterial drainage scheme, channel deepening and bridge replacement, was implemented in the 1980s from the confluence with the River Braid to the headwaters. During river works the cap was removed from weir leading to site moving upstream at ID 049 090 on 1/11/80. New location retained same station name while previous location now referred to as Dromona (Kenneways). Multiple rating curves, derived from current meter gaugings. No cableway, traditional (pre-ADCP) high flow gauging carried out from gauging bridge. Simple extrapolation used above approx 51m3/s. Weed growth during summer months may create seasonal impact on accuracy of lower end of rating. High flow gauging in 2002 confirmed validity of rating. Vertical post gauge in channel prone to damage during high flows.
description-flow-record: Water year 1969/1970 rejected because AMAX from partial water year at start of station record. Instrument failure lead to missing daily data during water year 2010/2011. Peak flow for this year rejected because the true AMAX may have occurred during this period based on nearby gauges. Additionally, peak flows rejected as unrepresentative post-2015 because of uncertain changes due to which the low flows are likely underestimated. Rejected until further investigations and amendment to rating. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in August 2021 (WINFAP Files v10) and in August 2025 (WINFAP Files v14).
description-catchment: No significant centres of habitation. Solid geology - the area is underlain predominantly by Palaeogene basalt lava flows. Drift geology - Extensive drumlinised glacial till with sand and gravel concentrated around the River Main and other major valleys. Extensive rock near surface and post-glacial peat cover on high ground with development of river alluvium in valleys.
description-flow-regime: Water abstracted from Dungonnell Reservoir in the Clogh catchment (12.5Ml/d) is predominantly returned downstream of station.

name: Ballinderry at Ballinderry Bridge
description-summary: Velocity-area station with cableway and natural control opened in June 1970.
description-general: Velocity-area station with cableway. Wooden hut housing stilling well and cableway winch situated on top of floodbank on left bank. Station located c.60m upstream of a multi-span road bridge which supplements natural bed control slightly further downstream. Main and backup instruments present both using shaft encoders with float and weight. Channel width c.20m at station. Channel too deep to wade gauge in all but the very lowest of conditions at the station but comfortably gaugable in-channel at road bridge.
description-station-hydrometry: Stable bed. Flows contained in channel beyond QMED, however highest flows do overtop floodbanks on left bank. Simple extrapolation used above 71m3/s. More high flow gaugings would be advantageous to confirm assumption that station is Suitable for QMED essential to upgrade station to Suitable for Pooling. Three peak flow ratings across period of record.
description-flow-record: Highest two flows on record in water years 1987/1988 and 2007/2008. Daily flows for full period of record reprocessed in 2002. New rating applied in 2007 to take account of raised bed caused by underpinning of Ballinderry Bridge, data reprocessed back to Sept 1995. Late December 2010 flows considered suspect due to likely freezing in stilling well. POT threshold revised in 2017 using entire period of record data up to 2015 water year. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in September 2023 (WINFAP Files v12) and in August 2025 (WINFAP Files v14).
description-catchment: Solid geology - Ordovician igneous complexes form generally impermeable basement overlain by indurated Ordovician and Silurian greywacke sandstones and shales. Much of south is composed of Devonian and Carboniferous conglomerate, sandstone, mudstone and limestone that are generally indurated. Permeable Triassic sandstone (Sherwood) occurs to the east and is overlain by impermeable Triassic mudstone (Mercia). Thin Cretaceous chalk is indurated and overlain by Palaeogene basalt lava flows and Oligocene clay and lignite. Drift geology - Extensive glacial till, sand and gravel particularly in the west. Extensive rock near surface and post-glacial peat cover on high ground with variable development of river alluvium in valleys. Mainly rural catchment (grassland or heath) with significant upland area. Cookstown has cement manufacturing works.
description-flow-regime: NA

name: Upper Bann at Dynes Bridge
description-summary: Velocity-area station with cableway, natural control opened in August 1970, closed in June 1991.
description-general: Velocity-area station with cableway, natural section control for low flows, channel width c.15m at station.
description-station-hydrometry: Cableway present. Natural section control for low flows. Channel capacity is large. Main road bridge 100m downstream gives partial control at medium and high stages. Simple extrapolation has been used beyond 3.08m. Two peak flow ratings across period of record.
description-flow-record: 1978 peak estimated (flood banks overtopped). Flows from 1979 onwards reprocessed in 2002. Upper one third of the drainage area is regulated with a minimum prescribed flow of 18Ml/d at Bannfield (203033). Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in August 2021 (WINFAP Files v10) and in August 2025 (WINFAP Files v14).
description-catchment: Impermeable quartzite and granite overlain by superficial deposits mainly till. Significant upland, predominantly grassland or heath, limited afforestation. Urban area at Banbridge, no major industry.
description-flow-regime: Upper third of the drainage area is regulated with Spelga Dam located in the headwaters of the River Bann.

name: Six-Mile Water at Antrim
description-summary: Velocity-area station with natural control.
description-general: Velocity-area station. Station originally located in masonry building on right bank moved directly across channel to left bank in 2011. Current station comprised of steel container with main and backup instruments both using pressure probes. Channel width at station c.18m.
description-station-hydrometry: Control at old bridge downstream. Channel has changed at the station over the years due to channel works and new bridge upstream. There is probably no better site on the river for the station. Multiple ratings applied to period of record. Rating derived from current meter gaugings. Simple extrapolation used above approx 3.5m.
description-flow-record: Exceptionally low flows in May/June 2008; however high degree of uncertainty (recession pattern not observed upstream). Flows from 1975 onwards reprocessed in 2002. There is a lack of data July to August 2010 due to vandalism at the site. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in August 2021 (WINFAP Files v10) and in August 2025 (WINFAP Files v14).
description-catchment: Solid geology - the area is underlain predominantly by Palaeogene basalt lava flows. Drift geology - extensive glacial till with sand and gravel concentrated around Six Mile Water valley. Lacustrine deposits might be present below river alluvium. Limited rock near surface and post-glacial peat cover on high ground with restricted development of river alluvium in valleys. Significant proportion of upland - predominantly grassland or heath, limited afforestation. Urban area: Antrim has substantial light industry and Ballyclare is a small market town.
description-flow-regime: The net effect of industrial abstractions and effluent returns is minor.

name: Claudy at Glenone Bridge
description-summary: Velocity-area station with cableway and natural control opened in December 1970.
description-general: Velocity-area station located on right bank. Masonry hut housing stilling well and cableway winch. Main and backup instruments present both using shaft encoders with float and weight. Channel width c.12m at station.
description-station-hydrometry: Cableway present. Rock bar with boulders 8m downstream of gauge gives low insensitive flow control. Three arch-road bridge 50m downstream gives medium and high flow control. Three peak flow ratings applied to period of record. Rating derived from current meter gaugings from cableway. Simple extrapolation occurs beyond 2m.
description-flow-record: Uncertainty in POTs between water years 1976/1977 and 1979/1980, AMAX unaffected. Flows from 1980 onwards reprocessed in 2002. Flows for 20-27 December 2010 considered suspect due to likely freezing in stilling well followed by rapid melt event. Need more high flow gaugings. Full period of record peak flow data reviewed and released in August 2021 (WINFAP Files v10) and in August 2025 (WINFAP Files v14).
description-catchment: Catchment is predominantly grassland with no urban areas or major industry. Solid geology - the area is mostly underlain by Palaeogene basalt lava flows. Dalradian occurs in the west forming a generally impermeable basement composed of metamorphosed, schistose sandstone, shale, limestone and basic igneous intrusive and extrusive lithologies. Carboniferous sandstone and mudstone also occurs in the west and is generally indurated. Drift geology - extensive glacial till with sand and gravel around the River Bann. Rock near surface and extensive post-glacial peat cover on high ground with restricted development of river alluvium in valleys.
description-flow-regime: Natural catchment with no major artificial influences.

name: Moyola at Moyola New Bridge
description-summary: Velocity-area station opened in January 1971.
description-general: Velocity-area station located on right bank. Masonry hut housing stilling well with main instrument using pressure probe and backup using shaft encoder with float and weight. Channel width c.21m at station.
description-station-hydrometry: Gauging section at the station always too deep for in-river gauging. Traditionally gauging carried out with cableway (now defunct). At high flows, river overspills minimally on left bank. Multi-arched bridge just downstream of station, between the piers, the inverts act as informal, horizontal controls.
